Ok so the trick here folks is to sit at the sushi bar.  You get so much attention from the sushi chefs that you'll never be empty handed while enjoying your meal.  Our sushi chef was super attentive, friendly, and extremely creative.  He kept asking the people next to us what they wanted...the couple responded by saying, "surprise us." I have no idea what he made but the rolls/nigiri were beautiful.  

We started off with 2 special scallop handrolls, a Titan roll, a mt. Rose roll, and 2 quail egg shooters.  Ah-mazing!  Ok, obviously this isn't going to be that melt in your mouth fresh from the ocean sushi...but it was really good for what it was.  I was not expecting the quality that I received from this place.  We then went on to order another scallop handroll, some sort of unagi handroll, tobiko with quail egg, and hamachi nigiri.  Good stuff...above par for an AYCE sushi bar.  We finished everything off with a happy ending.  Ok folks, get your mind out of the gutter.  "happy ending" is the name of the dessert...some sort of fried banana concoction.  Yummy status!  

Btw, appetizers and desserts are included in the $21/person.  You can't beat that!

Wanna know how awesome our sushi chef was? He made a fountain out of oranges and a rose from a strawberry.  Super talented.  And not once did I feel like he was getting irritated with us ordering...he kept asking if we wanted more and kept offering more items...not stingy whatsoever.  

The ambiance was super cutesy...great date place...before we left, our sushi chef said, "see you tomorrow." he just might be right.  Haha.

Most thorough wax I've ever had.  Go and see Shealynn, she has only been at this location for about 4 weeks but I'm not joking when say I've been waxing for over 3 years and I have never had such a thorough wax.  She was really sweet and told me when to breathe and made me feel really comfortable and not awkward that I was practically naked in front of her.  Seriously if you're looking for a very high quality wax, I hands-down recommend Shealynn!

We found Record Street on a recommendation while in town for UNR graduation.
Awesome food and very fair prices.  Great pizza options, best crust you could hope for.  The burger and philly cheese steak absolutely crush it and the fries are perfect, right amount of salt, perfect crunch and flavor and they don't get soggy.  Plus their beer and ciders are very good.

I grew up in SoCal so I'm very picky about tacos and this place gets it right! Great food, reasonable prices, really nice staff and responsible recycling. If I lived in Nashville I'd be back here regularly!
Went with my family of 4, all of us have never been there. Burgers were all super good, way better than average bar food. Stop by if you're here, the Mac and Cheese Burger was soooo good!

Fritzel's is a nice jazz bar. Quick service. The people who are complaining about drink prices must not come from big cities. $7.50 for a beer in NYC is typical - and you don't usually get a show included for that price. Fritzel's did not even charge a cover charge during Mardi Gras, so I ask these people who complain about prices - would you rather a $20 cover charge or a 1 drink minimum? Did you expect to see a great show for free? Stop being a cheapskate and spend your money. The performers and the bar need to pay their bills somehow. If you don't want to pay for service, then stay home. For the record, often jazz clubs in New York charge a cover AND a two drink minimum.....so you might not want to visit my state if you are a cheapskate. Happy listening y'all!

This is my second time trying Shake Shack in KoP. It's just ok. The food is good... but definitely over priced. My burgers each time were small and greasy with not much flavor, and the shakes were pretty small but very tasty. The line to order was long both times I went, and the food seemed to take a long time to come out. I'd much rather go to Five Guys. Better food for a better price. I doubt we'll eat at Shake Shack again any time soon. So many better eateries in the area.

This was our New Orleans experience. I went outside the general Po Boys every meal and had Jambalaya! Absolutely loved it ! If you like sausage the one they too on the Jambalaya is the best I ever had.

Absolutely horrendous! Never again. I rather pay more at another rental location because the extra cost will be worth my sanity. The wait is outrageously long to obtain your rental. Nickel and dime you if you let them and make sure you get a copy of your receipt to ensure no ridiculous add-ons that was not discussed and/or agreed to. Not worth it. The cars are fair - they run.
Great service, told us differences between different flavors and beat combos. Its always so fun watching them roll the ice cream

Overwhelmingly underwhelming. After hearing many rave reviews, I was so looking forward to dining at Peterson's for the first time after moving to Indy 7 years ago from Chicago. As a former employee of Sullivan's Chicago and patron of Capital Grille, Morton's, Chicago Chop House, David Burke...etc., I've been able to enjoy some very delicious and well-prepared meals. This was not the case tonight. While our server was knowledgable and mostly attentive, our birthday party of 6 was very disappointed. A prime rib ordered medium-rare came out well done. Why it left the kitchen in the first place is a wonder. Where are the standards?! The manager comped a ribeye to replace which came out at the proper temp but without seasoning and a baked potato that was hard and raw inside. Two "dry-aged" ribeyes at the table were also at the proper temp but not seasoned and did not have the flavor of a properly aged piece of meat. One also was one-third gristle and fat. Not marbling. Fat. My wild boar Wellington was cooked well but went downhill after the first bite, even after adding a generous sprinkle of salt to every piece. Bacon-wrapped shrimp was overcooked and dry. Out of twelve oysters, every one had pieces of shell (not grit) and mangled by a seemingly first-time shucker. We also didn't know which oysters were which as two different servers gave us different explanations of what was presented to us. The table beside us also sent an entree back and left soon after. The lobster bisque was the only food item that I can recommend, as the lobster flavor was very prominent and indicative of a well-made stock. While we took our time ordering and enjoying our apps, we were not served our entrees until well after the two-hour mark after being seated. The manager was apologetic and receptive of our criticisms, but with the timing issues, inconsistent food, and under seasoned everything, I am shocked at the number of positive experiences at this establishment. Perhaps the time to dine at Peterson's is in the past, for after nearly 3.5 hours and $550 (with a comped entree), we want our time and money back.

Update: Upped to two stars. Joe Peterson followed up with our party and sent some gift cards. Not sure when we will be back but his attention to the matter earns another star in my book.

To me Jay's is another version of Vic's (or conversely, Vic's is another version of Jay's).  They are both less traditional sushi joints that offer such things as tuna dumplings.  Overall, like Vic's, I think the quality of the fish is not stellar (it's okay), but it's a great value, particularly with their 3-roll special.  For around $10, you can get 3 rolls of decent quality--that's a deal to me, so I think the value that you get out of this place makes this a 4-star joint.

Try the spicy tuna sandwich if you stop by here.

I think compared to Vic's, Vic's is ever so slightly more expensive, but has better quality rolls (though Jay's are a tad bigger--slightly).  Some of Jay's rolls fell apart when I picked at them so that was a little annoying.  

But anyway, if I had to choose I'd pick Vic's.  But they're both great values and I see myself ordering takeout from both.
Fan-friggin-tastic sandwiches! Customer service and cleanliness leave something to be desired, especially at the price you pay.

By far the most delicious restaurant I have ever been to! The staff is always so accommodating. They greet you at the front door and ask you if you would like a complimentary glass of wine. I always make sure to get drinks too because they always seem to have something new on their drink menu. Unfortunately, parking is always a disaster since it is such a busy area, but I am still giving it 5 stars because the restaurant staff is so great.

We came in for Saturday lunch. We were promptly greeted by a very attentive and professional staff. This facility offers inside and outside seating and we were offered either. The prices were a little on the high side and the food was prepared differently than I would of expected. We order a blacken fish sandwich and crab melt sandwich. The crab sandwich was okay, but the blackened fish was literally burnt to make it blackened. It seems every fish establishment I visit and ordered blacken fish it comes back charred and dry. I guess it's a St Louis thing.

Food isn't bad, but not worth the wait for delivery. Several times now, I have ordered and waited for well over an hour. The food was cold by the time it arrived. There are better local options for delivery.

It doesn't take a brain surgeon to know what hits the spot! You have got to try GYRO SPOT!!! This spacious restaurant is a gem and such a welcomed addition to South Nashville. Their menu is large and is served with the reliability of plentiful portions and a friendly smile! Don't try to wrap your head around all of this - just go to GYRO SPOT today and wrap your mouth around one of their succulent Gyro sandwiches and a side of their Persian Rice! That would be a great place to start! You will enjoy an out of the ordinary eating experience and GYRO SPOT will become your new favorite place to go!

Wonderful 4 might stay here.  The room was very clean and came with complimentary bottled water and Goo Goo candy bar.  When we mentioned that it was our anniversary the management sent up a bottle of champagne and a plate of chocolate covered strawberries.  At the front desk Justus made sure our dinner reservations were made and arranged our transportation to and from the restaurant.  In fact the entire front desk staff was extremely friendly and helpful.  As our daughter lives in Nashville with her family we will be planning on many more stays at this hotel.

Arancini are a little small and gooey on the inside... but decent taste. The pizza could be a little thinner crust to be true Neapolitan style and the prosciutto a little thinner sliced, but overall satisfying pizzas and the wine list is good.

Mandina's is a neighborhood staple that generations of families have enjoyed. We went on Lundi Gras night, so it was PACKED. That being said, we only had to wait for about 15 minutes for a table. Granted, it was a table tucked back in a crowded corner, but it was a table nonetheless.  

Their menu is quite large, and other than not really being very descriptive of menu items and sides, is well organized. I like how it tells you if a menu item is going to take a particularly long time (like the broiled chicken and it's 45 minute cooking commitment). 

I ordered the boneless, fried chicken breast. It came with green beans and a boiled potato as sides (listed only as vegetable and potato in the menu). The chicken was good, the green beans were fantastic, and the potato was just ok. I would have preferred if the potato side would have been mashed or au gratin, but I get the boiled potato being culturally significant. We had onion rings to start off the meal, and they were quite tasty. I hear the crab fingers are delicious as well, but cannot speak to that personally. 

I love that this place is such a staple to Mid-City. I mean our waiter was probably 137 years old and has, most certainly, been there his entire adult life. People talk about how they came here with their parents and grandparents. I hope it never changes!
I live in Seattle now, well for the past two years, and I gotta say the coffee at the Hub is better than anything I have had here so far.

I'd give this a 2.5 if I could. 
Kitchen Kapers has a nice selection of kitchen items and  going to their stores is a great way to support a local chain. That said, I had quite a negative experience with a purchase I made for Christmas. I ordered a teapot and "stainless steel salt and pepper shakers". I picked up the order from the downtown location(as directed from their website online) which was quick and easy. When I had the chance to double check the products, it was clear that the shakers were not stainless steel. They were plastic and had a stainless steel look to them. Definitely NOT what I wanted. I live closer to the one in Ardmore so I went there to return the salt and pepper shakers. 
When I got to the counter, lady at the front desk was annoyed, rude, and very negative. She asked for the packing slip which I don't remember getting (maybe I did have it somewhere idk) and also in the return details it didn't say that an online receipt didn't count. In the end they were able to give me store credit, which I was fine with. But they didn't have to be so disgruntled and angry-- I approached very peacefully and willing to figure it out but the negative energy left me feeling confused and unhappy with my experience there. It was definitely a damper on the day. I'm the one who got something that did not meet my expectations, why can't I have a pleasant return experience?

We come to Reginellis on Magazine often and my go-to is the Uptowner sandwich but we decided to mix it up when at the downtown location and tried the Chicken Salad to start but they forgot the blue cheese and then we had the Smokin Chicken pizza which was fine but nothing compared to their other pizzas. Oh my gawd.. The good absolutely the worse. EVER in all of Indiana. The tortillas are  made with sugar eww.  I am completely surprised they are still in business with lousy food and higher than average for holes in wall mom and pop shops.

Mama Nita's Pizza is the third pizza shop in a row to inhabit this relatively small strip center location on Allisonville Road in Fishers. 

For about a year, Brother Doug's Pizza tried to survive here. You couldn't help but love Brother Doug's, but the pizza shop seemed to never attract an audience and nearly every single time I went to the place I was one of the only customers. He eventually tried doing a lunch buffet, but it wasn't long before Brother Doug's disappeared as did the pizza shop before it (that I can't remember by name). 

The truth is this is a weird location. It sure seems like it would be a great spot, but I've seen multiple businesses go in and out of here including Wyliepalooza's ice cream shop. So, I'll confess I was a bit surprised when I saw the Mama Nita's sign pop up indicating another pizza joint in a spot that had already seen at least two. To be fair, Mama Nita's is not only pizza and that may help it find an audience in a neighborhood that has multiple pizza shops already (though mostly chains). 

I'd been anxiously awaiting the opening here and was pleasantly surprised when I saw a couple reviews pop up. It's actually been a week since my first visit - I've really been wrestling with my review and decided to give it some thought. 

As noted, Mama Nita's is located in a strip center. I've always had a mixed relationship with this strip center. It's not really that old, but it's not particularly accessible with the parking lot at a slight slant and curb cut/ramps being shy of ADA requirements. There's one at the end of the building I use most frequently - it's next to an accessible parking spot, though both the spot and the ramp are a bit awkward. They do have some better parking spots available. 

Mama Nita's is about halfway down the building, a double-sided glass door entryway leading you into the interior dining area that is mostly wooden booths along one side and a couple of tables toward the front. The ordering counter is along the side on the right. They mostly utilize chalkboard menus, though they do also have some print menus. 

If there's one way that I think Brother Doug's was hurt, it was in their price point. While I understand that indie shops are usually going to be a bit higher, when you're surrounded by other pizza shops you simply can't afford to go significantly higher. Mama Nita's, on the other hand, serves up a nicely priced buffet that can compete with the big boys. The lunch buffet is $5.99, dinner buffet is $7.99 with kids from 4-10 at $3.99. The buffet price doesn't include drinks, but it's relatively easy to eat here for under a ten spot. The set up for the buffet is a bit awkward - it's essentially counter space that allows for 3-4 pizza types at a time along with breadsticks and maybe another item. If the crowd picks up here, they'll probably have to figure out something else. 

The buffet includes multiple varieties of pizza, breadsticks, and there's even an ice cream option. 

Mama Nita's, which started out in the New Palestine area, also serves up subs/hoagies, salads, and wings. I believe the New Pal location has a broader menu - it's unclear if they plan to expand the menu here. 

They carry the usual soft drinks, though they do have both sweet and unsweetened Gold Peak Iced Tea. So, yeah, I was happy with the drink situation. 

This location of Mama Nita's only recently opened and you can tell they're still giving the interior some personality. The layout is pretty much identical to Brother Doug's and the chalkboards for kids right next to the menus have stayed in place. The interior has a bit less "personality" than it did with Brother Doug's, but that could be planned in the future. 

The booths don't work particularly well for wheelchairs - the aisle is simply too narrow and if you sit in your chair at a booth, then you'll likely block people and/or be bumped during your meal. The tables are a decent option, though, as long as they are available. 

While Mama Nita's is local, it's not quite up to the "gourmet" pizza types that have been so prevalent lately. You're not going to confuse it for Jockamo or Bazbeaux or WB. However, it's a good quality pizza at a terrific price with a staff here that was absolutely super friendly and helpful even when they got busy. 

I will admit I seriously contemplated a 3-star rating and would likely go a 3.5 if it was available, however, the positive and family friendly pricing and top notch customer service are what really allow me to push this up to a 4-star rating. While Brother Doug's felt like a splurge, Mama Nita's feels like a place I could justify going rather consistently. If you're in the area, it's a definite choice (especially if you have kids). If you're not in the area, but you're in the mood for a buffet I'd have no problem picking this over Cici's Pizza in terms of a decent buffet option.

I have been seeing Dr. Halle for several years. This is not just a doctor this is a family. Dr. Halle has helped and my family so much. I love seeing Cindy and Julie his staff. Another anniversary marking 7 years since I underwent a horribly botched surgery at St. Luke's Meridian Hospital.  Instead of experiencing a carefully and cautiously executed surgery, the Meridian employed general surgeon expanded the targeted surgery as he ran amuck removing normal body parts and destroying nerve(s).  Impossible to forget given the result, the permanent loss of my voice, the cause of a surgically induced and permanent rare disorder, and the unrelated removal of yet another normal body part.  Whereas, I went into the surgery a very healthy whole person, I am now disabled by the loss of my voice, and while once an extrovert am now reclusive due to my loss of the ability to communicate.  Instead of sound my voice produces mostly air due to the paralysis of my vocal cord.  I suffer from and require ongoing medical care for the irreparable surgically induced hormone disorder.  I replay my mind the experience of a horrific extended and painful recovery from massive surgery, knowing that with experienced capable hands I could have had minimally invasive surgery and minimal recovery.  Later, in conferring with experts I learned that my injuries should never have happened, they were clearly due to incompetence.  The physical suffering made indelible by the fact that the general surgeon and hospital never acknowledged their mistakes and resulting injuries, there was no accountability and no apology.  My message is this:  your doctor and your hospital will never reveal their past mistakes, and the legal system will not protect you, and even the Medical Board will never reveal your complaint to the public.  Your only defense is to do your research and seek out the very best qualified surgeon, and in fact question the need for surgery.  General surgeons are among those who are least likely to be the most qualified.

Great place but very pricy!!!! Went here for restaurant week once and one time for apps and drinks. Food is very good and the points of service are on point. Out of my price range and I do think it is somewhat overpriced for what it is

The lessons on Sunday are relevant to our daily lives and are a true inspiration each week! The Student Ministry is awesome. My kids have been able to experience God at a whole new level. I ordered the fried chicken with fried okra. I personally wasn't a fan of the fried okra because there was very little okra and lots of batter. Would have preferred okra fries or something. 
The fried chicken was incredibly oily and salty. It had plenty of flavor, but I prefer it to be less oily. 

Portion size was meh as most people were still hungry after eating.

I went here with a large group and we were well accommodated. The service was a bit sparse but friendly enough. 

We enjoyed the Siam platter; I especially liked the rangoon and the shrimp. The Thai coffee, however, tasted oddly like cigarettes to all 4 people who ordered it. My Oriental Rice with beef was just average and in need of soy sauce. The soy sauce they offer has a tiny ladle to serve it and doesn't smell or taste like the soy sauce I grew up with. The rice was much better once I took it home and was able t season it appropriately. 

The restaurant is very nice and clean, though the bathrooms are quite a hike away and the immediate neighborhood is questionable.  Not a bad choice for dinner, but I think I would opt for take out if there were ever a second trip.

Went here for a birthday hibachi lunch on new years day. The food was good, the prices were fair and the chef was the most entertaining and funny that I ever experienced with hibachi! Kudos for the ambient chill music they were playing. I will be back and plan to try their sushi.

4 Stars!

I'd go back to have it again, but I definitely wouldn't risk going on a weekend.

The food here is really delicious.  Really expensive, but really delicious.

We had dinner here on a Friday evening and although the concierge at the hotel told us we wouldn't be likely to get a reservation, we managed just fine.  The place is really huge, with lots of old-style wood decor and big hefty booths.  The wine-rack that takes up a wall behind the entry area is pretty impressive (ok I'm a little jealous actually).

Our servers were attentive although a little awkward....they seemed like they were kind of confused although I'm not sure why.  

They do have one of my favorite wines available here for a hell of a deal.  Apparently the Ferrari-Carano winery has some kind of partnership with the Silver Legacy and therefore their wines are all over the place for way cheaper than anywhere else.  At Sterling's, you can get a glass of their Fume Blanc for $5.25 -- that's happy hour pricing all the damn time.  Woohoo!  Me gusta.

The bread basket they bring out before your meal is amazing....but let me warn you, the bread that has some kind of smoked cheese baked into it is evil.  Why?  Because you will not be able to stop eating it and by the time your entree arrives, you will be close to stuffed already.  I mean, I wouldn't know....I'm just guessing.  ;D

I had a seared ahi for my entree and my husband had a porterhouse steak.  Ok, let me just say that the portion sizes here are the embodiment of the gluttonous American stereotype.  Holy ass, that was a lot of food.  It was delicious, don't get me wrong, but if I'd have known how huge it would be, I'd have asked to have a half-order instead.  Holy balls.  So be forewarned....the insanely high prices are reflective of the insanely high portions.  Tasty but very unnecessary!

We didn't have any room for dessert, but at the end of the meal they brought us some chocolate-covered Grand Marnier-soaked strawberries.  Pretty goddamn good indeed.

Sure, I'd come back again, but I would definitely ask for a half-order (or make sure my hotel room has a damn fridge in it).

Nope, not worth it.  Really wanted to like this restaurant as its former incarnation was always a favorite, but the "new & supposedly improved" version is definitely NOT!  Let's start at entrance where the hostess? greeter? whatever?  did not acknowledge our presence until she had finished her private conversation with a server.  We did not have reservations for our party of two, but there seemed to be numerous empty tables.  We were asked if we would be willing to sit in the "cellar bar," to which we replied "sure."  We were told we just had to wait for the "hostess," who would seat us.  Okey dokey.  Nearly 10 minutes later, after we reintroduced ourselves to the young woman at the podium, an even younger woman, (who I mistook for a customer's teenage daughter), walked past us, grabbed menus, and said, "Two?" in our general direction.  We followed.

We were then directed to a table in the dining room.  When my dining companion inquired about the "cellar bar" seating, she was ignored.  Ok, no problem--the dining room it is!  We took our seats and picked up the clipboard menus.  Before a first glance, a gentleman arrived and began congenial banter with us regarding the specialty cocktails.  We would later surmise that he was the manager or owner.  It was a bit odd and awkward. Then our waitress arrived.  Let's just say, she clearly wasn't thrilled about being there.  She was quite terse and kept mumbling things under her breath.  She took our drink order and fairly quickly brought our "cocktails," which could more aptly be described as "mocktails," as there was barely a hint of alcohol.  Ok, not the first time we've had drinks that were a bit weak in the alcohol department.  We were still excited about the menu, so onward.

Ordered a salad to share, a burger and a ravioli dish.  The salad came out, but then made a bit of a journey around the dining room before actually winding up at our table.  (Maybe a bit more training of waitstaff is in order) Before we had a bite, we were asked how it was.  Well, gotta taste it first, don't we?  Two forkfuls into the salad, our entrees arrived.  Now normally fast service is a good thing, but this was a bit excessive and rushing us through the salad felt more like harassment than attentiveness.  While we awkwardly tried to make room for the oversized plates at our table for two, the plates were unceremoniously set down, nearly toppling other items on the table.  Wow!  Really? Our cries of "Excuse me!" were ignored.  Then again, before one bite of our entrees, the query of "How's your food?"  I appreciate that they want feedback and are trying to be obliging, but please, settle down a bit.  BTW, the aforementioned waitress was the one person who didn't actually seem to care about our dining experience.  She mumbled, "Everything ok?" as she breezed by our table, not even awaiting a response.  As a matter of fact, she mumbled and grumbled through every encounter with us.

Now the food was decent.  Solid burger and fries, cooked rare as requested, ravioli with ratatouille had great flavor--veggies were yummy, ravioli decent, but unfortunately the brown butter was a little too abundant and somewhat drowned the ravioli; still, a tasty & satisfying dish. Yes, we were accosted a few more times regarding our food, and we answered honestly that the food was good, service, not so much. When our entrees were finished, we decided to cut our losses and asked for the check.  On our way out, we noticed that the original young woman who barely greeted us, the server with whom she was speaking previously and the "hostess" were all still chatting at the entrance, and surprise, surprise, yet again, did not acknowledge our presence. Yup, bye-bye to you too!

Sooooo, disappointed.  There's such potential here and it is literally 5 minutes from home.  Some suggestions--don't make inexperienced, barely teenagers the first point of contact.  You need someone attentive and professional at the entrance to greet customers.  Don't employ servers that are surly and disgruntled.  Ours was clearly seasoned, but also clearly miserable.  Even great food can't overcome poor service.  The bartenders might also need a refresher course in proportion of alcohol to mixer ingredients.  The chef obviously has talent and with a little finesse could gain a following, but the rest of the establishment and the operation thereof needs some attention.  Fingers crossed they can get it together. Won't be back unless I hear future good things from the community.

Best baked beans ever! You could taste the peppers in the beans. 

Probably better than central bbq in Memphis, even. 

Ribs were tender and perfect. Brisket to die for. 

Mac and cheese ok... Didn't try other sides. 

Also, everyone is so friendly and the vibe is great.

I work near this place and always wanted to try it as I had never had, or even heard of, bubble tea. Even though there are multiple bubble tea places on the loop, this one is the most popular so I knew it had to be good. It turned out to be true. This was so delicious on this hot day. Can't wait to try the other flavors!

Great place and donuts are amazing!!  Awesome variety so the kids always try something different.  Owner was super nice and even gave us a free donut when we left and came back because my little son ordered the wrong type and was sad.  Again, just a great place with service to match the quality of their product. Great!!!!!

Never deal with this store again. TV I bought was great and installation person was great. Problem is the salesman signed me up for Geek Squad that I didn't want. He told be the first year was free. I told him I didn't want it. Then a year later I automatically get billed for the geek squad. I had changed my email address last year so I wasn't getting any bills. Then I get an automated call. I called Best Buy, since I can no longer get into my online account. I had Geeks cancel my subscription. Even though he told me I would not be charged, he didn't cancel it totally because it was now over a month. May hours on the phone and many hangups by the inept people at Geek Squad, Best Buy Billing and Citi, it is still not resolved. I have paid part of it and they did away with the other part. But, I have 4 complaints outstanding. Now they have turned it into the credit bureau even though I am fighting with them about it. Please be careful. If you see TTS on your receipt you are signed up for the geek squad. Plus I can't even get into my account because I can't give them the last 3 digits on a credit card I cut up last year. All of these are terrible companies.

Don't know if I'd count as a regular but I tend to visit every 1-2 months for the all you can eat during lunch time. My last 2 visits were a bit disappointing. My previous visit, the fish didn't seem like its usual freshness. The salmon nigiri, which is my favorite nigiri, had a borderline fishy taste and looked as if it was getting ready to go a touch slimy. The wasabi must have been old too. Piled it on because the fish wasn't it's normal freshness but wasn't getting the flavor or "bite" from the wasabi and kinda gave up. 

I ended up trying a couple new places due to this experience but came back 5/23/19 to give them another go. The fish quality and wasabi freshness had definitely improved but I was a bit disappointed with the service this time. Took a while for my nigiri to arrive but I was ok with it as I only saw 2 behind the sushi bar and it was the tail end of the lunch rush. That changed as I sat there with an empty plate and holding my order in hand as I kept seeing my waitress walk past and disappear. Not sure how long it would have been if another waitress had not seen me and I think took pity as she cleared my empty plate and got me another drink. I ended up ordering too much since I wasn't sure how long it would take if I chose to order again. I then sat there for a good while and watched the couple next to me get roll after roll served. 

Finally got my rolls to be disappointed again. The rainbow and shrimp tempura rolls were loose and several pieces fell apart as I tried to eat them. Often a problem especially when all you can eat rules state you'll be charged for leftover rice! The philly roll had more cream cheese than I seem to recall as well. Felt like eating cream cheese chunks instead of a sushi roll. At least the check came promptly when I threw in the towel....

I purchased a custom order dress online and it arrived way too big with no time to reorder the dress, Maria came to the rescue. She had to disassemble the entire top of the dress  in order to fix the oversized bust and sleeves.  She got sick and she still finished it in plenty of time for my daughters wedding.    The price for the amount of work she did was more than fair!  Thank you Maria

The food was okay. It's what you would expect at any Applebee's. The service  however was incredibly slow. The waitress was very nice. She continued to apologize for the delay however, it took over an hour to get our food. The restaurant didn't appear to be super busy so I'm not sure what the delay was.

I had the sandwich, upgraded to lamb meat. Overall, it was good; however, I thought the lamb was dry and overcooked. I was also disappointed that it did not include taziki sauce. I asked for a side but didn't get it. The zucchini fries as a side (for $1) would've been good if they were crunchy but by the time my late delivery arrived they were soggy and cold. I did order a side of the spicy feta and it rocked! 

I would try this again but I might call-in to verify my order instead of relying Yelp since clearly they don't read the notes.

I was looking for lunch with outdoor seating to soak up Santa Barbara's amazing weather and walked by this place. Started out with the bread basket - loved that it came out with fresh Parmesan cheese! I ordered the shrimp Caesar salad and a glass of wine. The salad was great - dressing was on point, shrimp was perfectly cooked. Quick service and just absolutely loved the outdoor seating!

In my humble opinion the most legit raspado spot I've been too outside of South Tucson.  The fruit is ripe which is crucial to a great raspado. I add vanilla ice cream and creama because it's delicious.

Just got a 2019 Chevy Silverado I love the truck. A&T by far has the best service and sales team. I bought multiple vehicles from them, every time they go out of there way to make sure your happy. Always professional and they cater to your needs. They explain everything and will do everything possible to make you happy. Jeff Leven and Joe Fost are great assets to A&T. Highly recommend them for your vehicle service and purchase of a new vehicle.

By far the best meal I have had in months. I was visiting the city for business and was recommended to come here by a bartender at Beast and Ale the night before.
We waited until the first available reservation at 9:15pm and even then it was still crowded. The vibe was warm, dim, and vibrant, the service was great, and the food was outstanding.
I ordered the prefix meal because according to all the servers, everything on the menu was their favorite. You get one appetizer, two small plates, one dish grilled over coals, and dessert for 42 dollars. It's the best way to go to sample the menu.
The Tehina Hummus was the best melt in your mouth hummus that I've ever had and the flavors in all the dishes were so unique and bold. The kitchen sent out some complimentary samples so by the time the Chestnut Konafi came out for dessert, I couldn't take another bite.
This place is a must, especially if you're stay in town is short! I highly recommend it.

Let's start this review by saying that Bluebeard tied my favorite restaurant of all time on our most recent visit. The short list of why: well balanced cocktails, delicious plates of all sizes from the shareable to the hoardable, and worthwhile desserts (some places sooo leave us hanging on the dessert -- not the case with Bluebeard).

We opted for sharable. Started with the bread appetizer, enjoyed the glass noodle salad, and ended the savory portioned of our meal with the Bolognese featuring (in my opinion) fresh cut pappardelle. Seriously delicious from start to finish, but the Bolognese was my favorite. You could definitely eat the entire dish on your own, but we were in graze mode so it worked well for us as a share. 

For dessert, we opted for two picks (these are full size desserts but we couldn't decide on just one). We went with the bread pudding and the chess pie. The bread pudding was good, but not particularly memorable to me. On the other hand, the chess pie -- velvety, vanillay, dreamy -- rivals the salted caramel budinos at Barbuzzo in Philly (fave restaurant, fave dessert). Just perfection!

And the cocktails! Did I mention the cocktails?! Well balanced, bright, and the right amount of boozy! A dream! Endless Summer and Gold Rush were my picks of the evening, but I'm guessing anything that suits your fancy would hit the spot. 

To top it all off, we shared a moment with our server who was expecting his first baby, a darling boy, in a few weeks. Our trip to Bluebeard was our first night out (courtesy of my parents) since our baby boy was born. He even humored us as we scrolled through a few photos of our little man on a phone. Bless his heart! 

Bluebeard is our "it" restaurant in Indy! Can't wait to head back on a date night in our near future.

I've been wanting to try this place for awhile, what time better than when I'm helping my sis move. 

I love how though they are a restaurant with vegan and vegetarian options they don't try to shove it down your throat by only offering those options. They also have meat options for you carnivores out there! But given that I was at a vegan restaurant, I was down to try the vegan and the carnivorous options. 

Bread. With Olive Oil and Balsamic Vinegar Dip. The bread was nommy. I liked how they had two different choices of bread, one white and one with poppy seeds and sesame seeds. The bread was fluffy, light and nommy. I liked how green the olive oil was too, what I learned in Italy, green EVOO is legit and bomb!

Raw Spinach Mushroom Lasagna. Chilled Zucchini Noodles with Marinated Mushrooms, Red Bell Peppers, Spinach, Raw Nut Ricotta, served with Raw Marinara, topped with Fresh Sprouts. This was soooo nommy!!!! THE best vegan dish I've ever had! The veggies were really fresh and it was delish! This is coming from a major carnivore too. It was so good! I loved the taste of all the ingredients and the textures of everything definitely made it a lasagna. 

Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb. With Grenache-Pomegranate Sauce, Wild Mushroom Melange and Potato-Spinach Croquette. This was well grilled and pretty damn good. And if ya know me, ya know I can make decent lamb chops. If it's good enough to impress me, it's pretty damn good! The flavors of the herbs on the lamb were delicious and it was grilled to medium-well perfection. I do normally prefer my lamb chops more on the rare or medium-rare side but they tasted so nommy I forgive the chef. 

Tuscan Fusilli Brown Rice Pasta. With Zucchini, Squash, Leeks, Mushrooms, Cherry Tomatoes, Chicken, Parmesan Cheese served with Marinara Sauce. This was bomb! I don't usually eat rice, but I think this brown rice fusili might just be changing how I feel about rice. This was oh so very nommy! The marinara was delicious and all the other ingredients were fresh and yummy. You can order it with tofu instead of chicken and vegan mozzarella instead of parmesan to make it vegan. 

French Lentil Walnut and Wild Mushroom Pate. Sautéed Mushrooms in Herbs and White Wine, puréed with Lentils and Walnuts, topped with Sprouts, drizzled with Balsamic Reduction, and served with Rice Crackers. This was so good! We actually got this on the house because all of our entrees came except for my sister's fusili pasta so our server let us choose any appetizer on the house and we got this one. This was a lot better than what I was expecting, it was really flavorful and delicious. You could definitely taste the flavor of the herbs and wine in the pate. I've never had such a yummy vegan dip before! 

The service was surprisingly formal for a more casual establishment as this, but I enjoyed their service a lot. Our server was really nice and made sure we were taken care of. It was extremely nice of him to offer us the appetizer on the house because shortly after we put in the order for the appetizer the fusili came out. 

Note: We came on a Sunday night and it might be a good idea to make reservations because we saw people get turned away. We only made them because we were making a long drive from the Bay and I'm so glad we did. 

This was THE best vegan restaurant I've eaten at to date and I'd gladly come back next time I'm in town. Can't wait to try more of their menu!

Hands down the best hurricanes in town!! Not only were they fantastic, but they were cheap too. Drink em from the bottom and they get stronger as you go. Do not stir or drink from the sides. Would have given 5 stars but really not a fan of smoking establishments. Good thing you can take your drinks to go. Pretty neat to be at a bar thats as old as the U.S. Customer service was pretty decent.

WORST SERVICE EVER!!!!! We waited for our food for over an hour (which we never received). Coffee cups remained empty. Waitress was inattentive. THREE tables who were seated after us were halfway through their meals while we were still waiting for ours. I had to ask another waitress to check on our order. When we asked why we haven't received our order, the manager spoke over me and kept repeating that my son's burger was ordered well-done and "it's the first ticket but it takes a longer amount of time to cook a well-done burger"!?!?!? For real?!? Over an hour for a well-done burger?!?! And trust me, it was not busy. Many empty tables and only about 12 people in the whole restaurant. For Sunday brunch when most restaurants on the same block have lines extending out the door? I guess I know why. Needless to say, we paid for our appetizers and left. There are many other choices to eat in the French Quarter, unfortunately CURIO  is not one of them. Disgusting service! 
Might I suggest Tableau, Muriel, Stanley's or Felix? All awesome restaurants with the most amazing food and outstanding service! Skip CURIO.

Best pizza I have ever had! My favorite pizza is the American Pie. Great service, quick to pick up after order is received and really unique combinations for the flavors of pizza. Reasonably priced as well.

Everything from the classic Cajun cuisine (i.e. boudin balls) to the Vietnamese flare to their homeade pickles (Giardiniera on many of their sandwiches). Beyond the delicious and flavorful food across the menu, the service was incredible. The owner and chef had a 15 minutes conversation with us about his love for food and roots in the New Orleans Vietnamese community. While they said that they close at 9pm, there was a Saints game on so they said they would stay open until it was over. They are putting effort into connecting with the Mid-City community which I appreciate with their location being right off of Broad St. Check out this restaurant for its unique cuisine, interesting location, and wonderful staff.

Who doesn't love the Heritage festival.  I have been to "cultural celebrations" in other parts of the country and in other countries, and none hold a patch to what goes on in Edmonton of the August long weekend.  It's like a tour around the world in one day.  Every year a few new countries are added, plus you can go see the old favorite sites.  I have a couple of food that's I count on each summer and then I plan on trying out one or two new tastes.  The food, the dancing, and so many people from so many places all getting along just makes me hopeful for the future.

While it's done for this season be sure to stick it in your calander for next year!

The hubs and I have been here twice and each time I leave with a feeling of indifference. 

The first time here, we both had the cilantro cream wet burrito and while the cilantro cream was delicious, the chicken inside was dry and bland. Oh and it only comes with chicken. The ability to order other proteins would be great. Service was alright. Not over friendly but not negligent either.

We tried visiting several more times after our intial visit but the line was always out the door which should be a good sign. On our most recent visit, I figured out why there is always a massive wait. No one buses the tables. We watched four tables around us go untouched throughout our meal while there was a steady stream of people coming in. At one point, a server picked up all the dirty dishes from one table and moved them to another dirty table just to be able to seat a family. As for the food, it was kind of bland and forgettable.  

There are too many mexican options in Fishers to waste one more disappointing experience on this place.

Been here a few times. Service and food is always great! Seared Tuna is a must try!! Also can't go wrong with the sushi. Definitely worth stopping in and trying. Menu has many choices for even the picky eaters.

Wife and I stopped by after a Dr appt on Wed, ordered the goat cheese appetizer wife liked it I thought it was ok. Daughter ate the garlic bread, san goat cheese (she's 2.5 what do you expect) settled on the parma pizza, prosciutto, parmesan, mozzarella with arugula on a white sauce. Order was relatively quick 15 min or so crust could have been just a little more crunchy but maybe that's my personal taste. Pizza was light, nice mixture with the arugula hadn't planned on getting a white sauce but that turned out to be a good selection. Waiter was helpful, prompt. Overall a good experience.

I finally went here a few weeks ago and while I was glad I did, I was a little iffy in terms of reviewing it.  It was huge...way bigger than the city market, statehouse or Broad Ripple farmer's markets, yet the produce stands were lacking (only saw two) and the art vendors (several) didn't have much that caught my eye.  Yet, if you want to go to eat and get lunch, it is perfect!!  The BBQ vendor had an amazing pulled pork BBQ, the ice cream vendor had outstanding ice cream and Nicey Treat always rocks!

Based on my keto diet, I can only eat one thing at Popeyes -- their blackened chicken. You typically don't see it listed but it's available and it's always cooked to order so you never get cold/old chicken. Pair it with ranch or their mardi gras mustard for a nice meal. 

The reason I felt compelled to rate this location is I've eaten here 2-3 times in the last couple months and every time the staff has been super friendly and helpful. That is a rarity at most of the Castleton area quick serve places so obviously their management or hiring is doing something right. I'm taking one star away because they don't offer unleaded iced tea... and I require unsweet iced tea. Make it so, Popeyes!

Best mid eastern restaurant this side of Dearborn MI.  So many great selections on the buffet from which to choose and they are all good.  Love going here, despite it being quite a hike from downtown St Petersburg.

And now they have BEER?!?!  

There really is no reason to go anywhere else.  

Except maybe Trader Joes to get dog food.

It was awesome having BJ's cater our lunch. Their staff was set up early. There were three staff members: one on mac n'cheese duty, meats, and a backer in case refills were needed. 

The mac n' cheese Ma'am was obnoxious about the plates/utensils. BJ's had the plates set in a basket separated by official heavy duty napkins embossed with the BJ's Barbeque logo. As wonderfully stacked as these were, the napkins and plates got stuck, and picking them up was not easy. I accidentally grabbed two napkins caught in the front and behind a plate. As I handed my plate to the mac n' cheese lady, and she stalled and stared at my two napkins. She stopped to tell me that each plate allows for one napkin. I placed the napkin back and said I only grabbed the extra because I had already touched it. She uncomfortably giggled as she handed me my plate. The person after me seemed to have grabbed two plates and she grabbed the extra plate while remarking "...I am going to run out of plates!" Perhaps future caterers could grab the plate first, instead of micromanaging utensils!!

The meat options were shredded brisket on a hoagie roll and grilled chicken. The portion was perfect for the shredded brisket, just enough to fit the bun. This was not dry, and was filling.The chicken was a bit flat, but pretty juicy overall! The sauces caused confusion, probably because the caterers allowed our HR generalist to help, and she described each sauce as medium or mild! Mild was good.

The mac n' cheese was creamy!! I think it is what got me really full off of just half the plate!!

Overall I was happy to finally try BJ's barbeque! What a way to make my workday, minus the meticulous plate police!!

By far the best supply store in town for nail techs. Chuck, (I think that's his name) the owner is AWESOME. He is always great to ask for suggestions on new products and is very knowledgeable. 
I see a lot of reviews on here with people and confusion that this is a professional store, but that shouldn't be something that determines how great the store really is for us licensed professionals!! 
I could spend all my money here if I wanted! Love it.

on our 2nd visit, the food was good (especially the fresh tortillas and the green tomatillo sauce) and we enjoyed attentive service from someone who offered strong knowledge of the products.  it wouldn't have taken but a bit more 'sauce' to make it a great experience instead of just a good one.   giving a party of two a tiny bowl of salsa and then asking to charge $1.25 more for more tiny portions is just plain rude.  if you want to charge for chips n salsa, fine, then have a $5-10 portion or something. don't try to nickel and dime me by giving me a sample and then asking me to buy more.   it feels fast food and it simply makes me want to go somewhere else.

I saw Mothers on a famous unnamed food show and was excited to visit on my trip. However I was extremely disappointed in the service and the food. After waiting in line for 20mins outside the establishment you get yelled at on how to enter and where to stand. The yelled at to ordered and rushed through without explanation of the system. The food was only so so....The red beans and rice were meaty good but lacked seasoning completely. The ferdi special was only okay and nothing like what was shown on tv. I would try it again to see if maybe I just went at the wrong time. I however thought the menu was over priced.

The curries are off the charts.  Fresh veggies, coconut, and spices mixed in a bowlful of love.  Pad Thai is also a favorite.  Not much to look at from outside - normally pick up.  Add this one to your list.

Always a pleasure to stop at Backatown! Such a cool vibe and space filled with tasty art. The food is equally good. I've tried so many things and have never been disappointed. My fav is their avocado toast. 

Today I'm just doing coffee and working on some photos. Catch my photo art @sun_shine504.

this Popeyes like the location and Lebanon Tennessee which closed has fallen on a little hard times a lot of staff is no longer here and sometimes you will find the quality of the food is still good but the dining room can be sometimes slightly messy and it's still in the TA truck stop it's still quite busy they do a good job on the food I'm enjoying my food currently although the dining room is a little messy they mentioned they lost a lot of help so I'm not going to really put up pictures of that cuz I can understand the quality of the food though is still great currently having the two piece mixed mild leg and breast with a biscuit and a red beans and rice which makes something combo at the meal and it's perfectly fine they brought two employees from the TA truck stop in Effingham Illinois are the try to get things in line I guess apparently they put them up in a hotel or something but they're doing what they can but good news though is the quality of the chicken is still good I'm eating in here now and they came out and I just checking you wiped out at Avon they did so it's okay I understand but the main thing is to consistency of food is hot it's not cold it's not uncooked that's the good thing

Place has a great location and easy parking.  The food has changed over the past 2 years from great to average and portions were cut in half.   Dinnertime seems the best time to eat here, I was served a spoiled ceasar salad at lunch and the waitress didn't offer to replace it or even take it off of the check.

I liked everything about this office. First impression when I walked in was a welcoming environment. Second thing I liked is that I didn't have to wait long to see Dr. LeMay. He is highly competent, professional, knowledgeable, and really tries to help you with your hearing problem. He has the latest equipment and thoroughly tests your hearing: frequency and volume, understanding of words with no noise in background, and understanding of words with noise in the background. He is also up on the latest software for each hearing aid. I highly recommend Dr. LeMay.

I lost my car key and the spare was 150 miles away. After I called AAA it only took a few minutes before Robert from Bob Holzer got in touch with me to confirm my location and shortly after he was there. He was able to unlock the car swiftly and without leaving so much as a scratch and a few minutes later we were on our way, towing my car to the dealer. 
Great service, can only recommend!

Celina will give you a sob story of how one of her 9 puppies just died, and there was a few puppies that I wanted to look at however she kept blowing me off and giving me excuse after excuse on why I couldn't see the pups, then she told me that 2 of the 4 puppies on the website was gone (they are still on the website even days later after I brought it to her attention). Then today, I was going to go look at one of the other 2, and she just told me blatantly "Sorry the pup passed away."

I brought my broken headlight Chevy truck at Ticos located in Sparks. I am very amazed how Jose fixed faster of the time I told him to finish. He finished the same day, he gave me a complete diagnostic with my car as well.I will definitely recommend Ticos for Auto Repairs.

This place has probable the best happy hour options. A GF and I met here to check out the happy hour and were not disappointed. The bartender was young and fun and the appetizers are 1/2 off! Between the two of us we had 4 beers and the mandu poo poo platter (which we took over half home) and the bill was under $25. Can't beat that. If your looking for a fun vibe and cheap thrills during happy hour highly recommend this place!

I have insomnia, but not the regular "cant fall asleep" kind. I suffer from maintenance insomnia, where I will fall asleep just fine but then only sleep a couple hours at the most and wake up then not be able to get back to sleep. I'd always heard commercials for 20 Past 4 but had never been to one. When I was reading online about fixes for insomnia, CBD repeatedly came up. Knowing that CBD is now legal in Indiana (finally) I researched CBD retailers and they were the first listing to come up. Seeing as how they weren't far from where I was staying, I decided to stop in and ask questions.

The guy that helped me was very knowledgeable and friendly and actually listened when I explained what I'm dealing with, and he recommended multiple things that would help, based on what others have purchase for the same reasons. Being completely new to CBD, I didn't know up from down, and while the stuff was a bit pricey, I bought an affordable option to "get started" with.

I'm very grateful to 20 Past 4 right now, for taking the time to listen to a new customer and offer recommendations as to what could help them the most. A lot of places just want your money and for you to get out, but the guy that helped me cared, and it showed. Great Place, lovely people! This place is my new favorite. Thanks to Monique, who btw is also the owner of MOKO. She is so professional and yet very welcoming and comforting! This was the first time I visited MOKO with my wife. We both got our hair done and we absolutely loved it! The vibe of the place is so fresh and relaxing with so much space and natural sunlight. Loved this restaurant and have recommended to friends. Great for a date night. The food is really good. The whipped feta is amazing. Showed up at 4;45 for my Guaranteed room reservation only to be told by Ron at the front desk that My room (suite) had been given away to someone else. I was the last one to show up! Major problem with brand new 328 bought in October 2012 (powertrain warning.) Called Otto's as have to go out of town on Monday--WITH THE CAR.  No diagnostics on weekends--okay. Arrived 4 hours late.  Called at 1:30 to say they would arrive at 3pm instead of 2.  3PM no-show.  Called the office, was told they were finishing up previous job and were only 30 minutes away--would arrive by 4PM.

4PM no-show.  Tried calling again, office closed left message.  Owner called back and apologized, said they would arrive by 5.  About 5PM I received a text saying they were on their way and showing tracking information.  Tracking showed the truck was nearly an hour away.

These are not professional movers.  They were awkward and careless.  One guy did most of the work hence the awkward and alarming handling of the furniture.  One guy was on the phone in the truck and did not help carry many of the items that could have been carried more safely with 2 people.

Pizza Plus has all-around good food. Their wings and chicken tenders are tasty and the medium sauce is good on everything! I enjoy the pizza as well, but usually just end up ordering a platter with the battered and fried veggies, wings, tenders, and fries.
The lunch buffet is also a great value...

I've lived in Radnor for 2 years and until recently have I seen the quality go down and the prices go up. Yes, I understand that living on the main line will guarantee higher prices, however their produce always disappoints. I can honestly compare some of the fruit to the fruit you would buy at Wal Mart (bruised or mushy). Like I said, it wasn't always so, just something I noticed in the past few months. Very delicious food. Egg sandwiches are great and coffee is solid. Lots of other options like yogurt and pastries that are wonderful highly recommend

Horrible customer service and rude employees.  We come back every so often to give it another shot and are always disappointed.  It's too bad as the food is good.

I love min moon. It's the best Chinese food in the hood. Family owned and operated. Quick service great food. You can watch them cook it if you come inside so it's not sketchy.. I only gave it 4 stars because it's definitely a hole in the wall place. If the appearance of this restaurant doesn't scare you off try their food it's worth it.
Average Mexican food, nothing spectacular.  Food was made fast, efficient service, no major complaints.

Perfect for takeout but dining in is another story 

I must confess first by stating that I have actually eaten at this location before. This time however, my wife and I decided it would be best served by getting the order to go. While we waited on the order we split a large sized Taj longer while sitting at a booth. Unfortunately, my reasoning for wanting to write this review has mixed feelings. First, let's start with the bad. The Clay oven is actually a retrofit of the previous Italian restaurant that had a salad bar. Currently, they utilize the old salad bar for an Indian buffet that is served during lunch time. The lighting above this display area is comprised of florescent office lights which unfortunately bleed over into the first row of booths and outward throughout the rest of the restaurant. The restaurant lighting is equally unappealing as it is comprised mainly of lights that are attached to the ceiling fans. There are two large HDTV's on either side of the rectangular shaped restaurant dining area. The picture on these is quite clear but unfortunately, they keep the volume on which in turn clashes with both your conversation and the overhead music. They should enable the closed captioning and mute the volume altogether. They are able to fix the lighting however, they could choose to use individual table lamps on each of the booths which would create an intimate atmosphere and provide better lighting. Additionally, they could put up some sort of wall partition or overhang that would prohibit the bleed over of the florescent lighting into the main dining room. While we are on the subject of lighting, we need to talk about the restrooms. The lighting concerns continue in the restrooms which are so stark white that you feel like you're being watched even though you're not, it's simply horrible.

Of a small concern and yet still a concern in today's times, is the company website or lack thereof. In doing a Google search you will find that www.ClayovenofTampaBay.com is listed on as this restaurant's website. Going there you will quickly discover that that is merely an ad for printing company with Web services, probably attempting to gain this company's business. If anyone in management from this organization wishes to do so I will be more than happy to design and host their website in exchange for a small fee and food bartering!
Now let's talk a little bit about the positive items, which are the food and the service. Starting with your entry into this establishment you are always greeted by a friendly young woman who abstains from the boring and traditional methodology of simply asking how many people in your party to asking how she could help you. I like this because it's not presumptuous. As I stated earlier on this particular outing we opted for our food to go. We started with Dal soup which, on the menu, is described as a lentil-based soup with herbs spices and a verge of lemon. For those of you unfamiliar with this type of soup it's basically an Indian form of split pea soup although considerably more flavorful and probably better for you in the long run. As it is with all Indian foods, you can get this dish served from mild to extremely hot in our family I always choose a mild soup and my wife chooses medium. To change the textures most Indian restaurants serve some papadum, which to me is a cross between a cracker and bread. It is typically accompanied by some mint chutney, tamarin and a spiced onion mixture that I always forget the name of. My favorite thing to do is to mix all three together and eat it that way, delicious! For our entrée, we ordered butter chicken at medium temperature. Butter chicken is always accompanied with basmati rice and for me the entrée would not be complete without Onion Kulcha which is naan, perfectly stuffed with spices and chopped onions and perfect for cleaning up any extra butter chicken sauce. The Clay oven does a fantastic job of keeping the temperatures correct, having a good proportion of meat to sauce and having perfectly cooked rice every time. In addition, the kulcha is never burnt. Again a word about the customer service, we were given plenty of sauces and breads as well as napkins to accompany our take-out order. Each item is meticulously packed after being carefully prepared in a large paper sack with handles making it easy to transport.

In conclusion you'll notice that my rating suffers a bit as a result of the aforementioned decor and lighting issues, however the Clay oven should not be discounted if you're looking for great Indian food with pleasant, caring service. My only hope is that someone in management will read reviews such as this and potentially make corrections within their dining room so that I can make it a regular stop.
These folks are awesome. We ordered five different things and everything was great. Then they gave us some free candy. Will definitely be back.

Great local spot to get a really good burger without the feel of a franchise! We love stopping after little league games, and they are great for a good sized group of kids and parents, or for anyone looking for a game night spot that is a local best kept secret! We had burgers (of course), and the kids had chicken tenders and fries. The different burger choices made it really hard to decide but gave us reasons to try something new every visit!

I can see why people love this place. It's a nice space, clean and we'll-organized, and the food all looks fabulous. Everyone working here was pleasant and friendly as well. For me, though, the prices were a deal-breaker. Again, the food was beautiful, and I'm sure well worth the price. However, the selections just did not fit my budget. This may also be a reflection of what I was looking for this week. I was hoping for some good-quality seafood, and they did not have seafood specials this week. They do have some specials on pork and poultry that are very reasonable. So I'll keep an eye on the specials and visit again for the great customer service.

Overall a good stay!

This place is older but huge!! I stayed in a suite for business and the room was pretty awesome!

If you are looking for something to do at night do not stay here.  Down town was quiet and the bars at this hotel were empty.

Overall a good stay for the money would def come back again!!

We had an event here a couple days ago and at me tell you about customer service! The manager was phenomenal! She was patient and caring ... she was informative and attentive to our big group.  Her serving staff,even though there was a lot of us, made sure our drinks were filled and our food was served right.  I'm all about the quality of service and food and for a steak at 6 bucks... it was pretty good! Late night eats... especially after clubbing and drinks....  instead of tacos, come to Bonanza.

I was in panic mode when I noticed a wet spot on my ceiling!  After narrowing down the issue we contacted Cornerstone Pros.  The very next day (it was late when I called) Quenton came out and after climbing around in the attic he figured out what the problem was.  Quenton was very professional and very helpful.  He turned a very stressful situation into a very positive experience.  Thank you Quenton and Cornerstone Pros for taking care of us with the best customer service experience I have had in years!

Excellent service and great staff! Very knowledgeable and professional. Took both my cars in for repair and the wait time was as expected. Comfy little sitting area while you wait. Would highly recommend this place for all your service needs.

Without a doubt, the "Cadillac" of painters in Center City Philadelphia. On time, professional, and they do an outstanding job. I have used them countless times over the past dozen years for my home, and various projects I have built.
Not cheap, but worth it!

These are some of the best bagels I've had. I prefer them over Philly Style. It's like eating a cloud. The cream cheeses are delicious as well. Best of all, the people are super friendly and really passionate about their craft. I'm not surprised that Delish rated them best bagels in PA!

I love Tulip Nails! I stopped coming here for a while, but only because I was looking for a place closer to home. However, I will soon be returning! Everyone here is very friendly and professional, the salon is always clean, and I have no problem being seen quickly even as a Walk-In.

I have been helped my several different manicurists for both pedicures and gel and I have always been happy with the outcome!

Food is bomb!!..If you want really good chinese food without spending and arm and a leg this is the place to eat.Their lunch/dinner combo meals are really great! Comes with soup,1 eggroll and 1 crab rangoon at a decent price along with good portion sized meals.

On our return trip from Sturgis 2015 that included a stop at the Harley Museum in Milwaukee ... the clutch went out on my 97 Police Road King in St. Luis.
Numerous phone calls to local Harley dealerships proved disappointing because they refuse to work on older bikes.
I found Flying Tigers on Yelp ... talked with Brett on the phone, he offered encouraging possible solutions.
Once Tim had a chance to assess the problems ... he quickly ordered parts, opened the housing, found the extract problem and even worked through his lunch break to get us back on the road in just a couple of hours.
I highly recommend this shop for any repair ... very honest people here!
Thanks to all at the shop that helped get us up and running.
Tom from California & Wes from Hawaii

The food was really damn good. I got the fish n chips. My issue tho, the bathrooms are not wheelchair friendly. Not even close. You can't even get a wheelchair in the door. My chair is not very big. Been drinking beer and need to pee. Not at this location.

I love it! Always reviewed good service and the food comes out on time. Everything I've ever ordered taste delicious. The setting is perfect for friends and family. Sometimes loud. But great place for all kinds of foods. Their dessert has never disappointed. It's amazing all the way when I eat here. A little pricey but so worth it!

Really great food serviced up by a lovely group of people.  My wife and I eat here at least 3 times a month.  I have never had a meal here I didn't love.  Best burgers around, amazing sweet potato fries, unique tasty salads ... Can't say enough.  Don't be afraid to try the specials, I had an amazing prime rib there :)

I really like Mangia-it is very close, the food is always  good, as someone said it is pretty veggie-friendly, the creme brulee is just so delicious, as are the pbr's. I recommend the smoking section because it is just so much more relaxed and better (even if you don't smoke I recommend it).  
Their homemade pasta is available at the farmer's market in Tower Grove and is very delicious.

Great Juniors Cheesecake choices at whole sale prices.  Best part is no line and the cake dispeners were very nice and attentive.  Great place to stop as a break off the highway. I live on west coast now but will be back if I am ever in the area.

Lovely Bride was the first bridal salon I went to, and I almost regret that because the other stores I went to were so disappointing in comparison! 

The service was great. My consultant, Aleza, asked me about my wedding and what sorts of dresses I liked, and when we walked around looking at the dresses she made suggestions. Then, as I tried on dresses, she made adjustments to what she had me try on according to what I liked and disliked. She definitely listened and I felt like we were on the same page. When I tried on the dresses, she took care to clip them properly so that everything was aligned and I could get a sense of how the dress would look in the proper size. (As I said, I was spoiled by going here first. The other places clipped in a much more haphazard way.)  I didn't feel pressured at all (either of the two visits) to make a purchase. Also, they let you take pictures and give you the name of the designer and dress so that you can think about it with a clear head if you'd like. 

The selection was great and definitely different than the other shops.They have many dresses with an indie/modcloth/romantic/demure type of vibe (they also have other styles but that's what I paid attention to). I went to two other stores (Bijou and Nordstrom Bridal) that had nothing that I liked. I came back to Lovely to buy my dress. 

As for prices--I think everything I tried on was between $1600-2500. They told me that they have about 15 full length gowns under $1500.

I definitely recommend Lovely Bride, especially if the aforementioned styles appeal to you or if you're having trouble finding dresses in your style at the other stores.

Poor concept of this type of beer service. I've been to many pour your own bars, and this was by far the worst. To start, there is no bar. This is a restaurant that has added pour your own beer service. Catch is-- you have to get a table and be seated to have beers. We went on a Saturday night to have a few beers before dinner, except that wasn't possible due to the fact that there was a 50 min wait to be seated. Upon asking if we could just have drinks we were promptly told no and that this wasn't even an option. Two thumbs down. If you're going to advertise yourself as a beer bar, be a beer bar, not a restaurant where you're forced to sit with wait service to then serve yourself. Will not return.

Customer service is not their strong point. Trying to make an appointment was a daunting task. I was transferred to three different  customer service reps, placed on hold, and untimely had three conflicting appointment times. When I arrived their computer system "was down" so I waited an extra 30 minutes for my service to begin. My facial went pretty well,  very nice personable woman. After my facial, I checked out and once again the badgering to obtain a membership began. " why don't i want to join", "what are your concerns" ect ect. Ultimately, I won't be returning because I don't like feeling pressured to do anything plus subpar customer service!

Whomever made the decision to make Nashville the second location for this wildly popular Chicago based restaurant, I SALUTE YOU.  The food was fantastic. You will love the ambience and the location is perfect. We valeted out front but you can also park in any Gulch parking garage. 
We started with edamame, tuna poke and an Escolar. All great. But promise me you will order the Escolar. The flavor combination is incredible. The truffle shavings on it are a special treat. The Miso Cod is perfection. Then we also sampled numerous rolls. All 5 Star. The crunchy pig was again a tremendous flavor combo. The only miss on the menu for us was the Pad Thai. I actually can't recommend that one.  If you are in need of a Vegan or Gluten free menu, they have you covered. 
One service faux pas... the server spilled a full dirty martini down my silk jacket... unintentional... but not ideal. They did send over a few complimentary menu items to apologize. 
I suggest starting with a few cocktails across the street on the rooftop bar at the Thompson Hotel, then walking across the street for your Sunda reservation. Made for a fun night out with friends!

The ginger drinks were were very gingery, the way I like it. The food was very flavorful. We got the lamb shank and red snapper. They were amazingly good

There steaks are ok pretty much just like genos which is really not that good. Steves is better than genos but the best in town would have to be Tony lukes. Steves has a good system for ordering but that's about it.
delicious food. nice people. great salsa beats. what more do you need?
i like this place.  quick delivery and good service.  delicious rice bowls, panini, pita, and hummus.  will definitely be ordering from here more often.

We stopped here for an early breakfast yesterday.  The menu hasn't changed much since my visit in the winter.  I was disappointed that they have fallen off in terms of quality.   My dining partner's breakfast was the eggs Benedict but the home fries were deep fried frozen potatoes.   Maybe they were always that way but the other details made me sit up and take notice.   I ordered the Frankie Jr. which included the two pancakes with two eggs and a side of meat.   When I asked about what kind of meat they have, the waitress said "everything" rather than bother to list them for me.  I also asked for real maple syrup as they have had it in the past.   This was no longer available, so suffice to say I had to use what they have in the squeeze bottle on the table.   The bottle was sticky on the outside and clearly no one bothered to clean it.   The meal here is OK, but not something that would draw me back. It is just another breakfast and lunch joint.
I got to feed a f-ing giraffe. A giraffe ate lettuce out of my hand. Need I say more?
