Had time to kill while waiting on the amtrak so I took a stroll to Peddler Coffee. It was a sin day late am so they were pretty much out of food but has tasty biscotti to nosh on. I am a latte fiend and the latte here was just so so. after reading the reviews I though I was in for a treat and while better than many not a top end latte. I should come back to check out the pour over coffee. If you are in the neighborhood it is definitely worth a try just not the best I've had.

I have been a Ray Skillman customer since 2010 when I purchased my first 2011 Kia Soul at Ray Skillman Westside. It had a manual transmission. After having that almost 5 years I traded it for another Kia Soul this time a 2016 automatic transmission. I happen to be flipping channels and stopped on The Price is Right of all things. The prize at this moment in the show was a 2018 Chevy Trax. I hadn't even heard of a Chevy Trax. The Trax concept came out in 2012 but only in a few countries. It wasn't till 2015 when it came out in the US. I like the AWD and the Premiere is loaded with frankly too much stuff but I wanted the AWD with 18in Wheels so had to go Premiere. My Dad retired from GM after over 30 years so I knew I got the employee discount. Ray Skillman Chevy gave me a great price on my 16 Soul and with the employee discount and rebates my monthly payment went up very little. Kevin Lortz and Dakota Whitmer were very easy to work with. They had to find the Trax I wanted at another dealer and trade something they had on their lot for it. My Trax was driven from a dealer not far from Chicago. They installed my cargo kit and followed my instructions not to put dealer stickers on the car. So far very good experience. Just waiting on my paperwork so I can transfer tags and my first payment.

Decided to try em out again in the chicken wing department. Like holy crap!! Their chicken wings are freaking great!! HUGE wings i forgot i was eating chicken! Very well done, not dry. Very nice n tender and the sauce? Amazing! I went with the honey barbecue ones, side of rice n beans. New York style Cheese cake dessert. The rice n beans where great to, nit to salty n beans just nice over the rice. I couldn't believe they managed to put that much in the container. The cheesecake was heavenly to. Tasted home made to me. Had real pie crust not that cookie crumble one I'm not a fan of. Nice n near foamy. Had a soft texture, the taste was real good not to sweet n the strawberry sauce was just on point. Will definitely order more wings from them. I usually get bad luck ordering pass midnight but they did me in great! It was a blessing from the food gods. 

Major heads up! If you get the saucy stuff? They gonna nuke it. DO NOT tilt the bag! It will drip! I had so much sauce left i had to take a picture of it! U can easily fill up a nice small bottle with it n just reuse it.

I went to see Gabrielle for a private acupuncture session last week to address my issue with teeth grinding. She spent a long time checking in with me, talking about my concerns and asking me questions. She even demonstrated the path that energy takes through a few meridian lines that run through my face - neat! The highlights for me were: the amount of one on one time I got to with her, the calming and deep caring energy I felt from her,  the knowledge she held about acupuncture and the meridian lines for the jaw, the quick relief of the tightness I had in my jaw, the deep relaxation I felt after the session AND the cold that was creeping up went away (yay!). I totally understand the value of a private acupuncture session over a community session now (until now I have only received a community session). Both are super healing, but the private session offers time for deep inquiry into health issues and concerns, asking questions and more time to be cared for one on one. As a mama, being taken care of like this is such a treat! Thanks Gabrielle! 

I highly recommend Gabrielle and getting a private session from her at least for your first session!

Horrible service last night.  My tennis friends have been coming here after playing for years, but will probably not anymore.  Our first clue should have been that there were plenty of empty spaces in the parking lot at 7pm on a Saturday.  That never used to happen.  We stood at the "please wait to be seated" sign in the bar area for about 5 minutes with no one acknowledging us.  So I walked back into the dining area and came across 6 waitresses standing around the server area, chatting.  I noticed that the dining room was practically empty.  I said "we've got a bunch of people out here waiting to be seated."  No one moved.  One of them stopped talking long enough to say "yeah, the hostess is coming."  So I dutifully went back to the door to wait.  Ten more minutes.  Finally the 5 of us sort of stormed the dining room and complained to the waitresses again and someone finally seated us.  

I have heard that there is new ownership/management.  I just know that when several of our party ordered sandwiches, our waitress said "that comes with chips now, not fries, is that okay?"  No, really, that is not okay and we probably will find a new spot to hang out.  Pity.  I liked the outdoor tiki bar area in the warm weather.

Growing up in Tucson, going to Pat's was always a treat reserved for dad's payday. I liked it then and I still like it today. The chili is the same as it always was, don't fix what isn't broke. (I recently learned that you can buy Pat's famous chili by the bucket, if you're so inclined.) And the bag o' fries...yum - In n' Out's got nothin' on Pat's! It's fast, cheap and greasy! Word of advice, take cash because they charge $1 per credit/debit transaction.

I thoroughly enjoyed my visit here.  This is a tiny shop in Narberth, close to the wine store (priorities!).  They have coffee, baked goods, and lots of jams and spreads in addition to cheese.  Staff was friendly and offered me multiple free samples.  I found a wonderful bleu and a great triple cream brie that literally melted on my tongue!  Staff also helped me pick out the best cracker to complement my cheeses.  Much better selection and service than at a regular grocery store.  I'm sold!

Happy Maki is okay, I suppose. It comes off as a hole-in-the-wall sushi place, and it is small and cozy inside. The staff is very polite and endearing.

The food is meh. The bowl that contained my miso soup smelled like dish soap. This can be interpreted two ways: at least they're cleaning the bowls, but apparently they aren't doing so well enough. The smell, by proxy, made my brain think I was tasting said soap. I couldn't finish it. Their sushi was pretty good. Lackluster, really. I also got chicken katsu in a bento box - I had never had katsu. This was good in the scheme of chicken, though the other components of the bento box, not so much. I think the soap smell really set my tastebuds off. I'd be willing to try it again, as this was probably a one-time thing.

Um.. so my Southwestern tomato soup said to be served with tortilla strips did not have tortilla strips.  Not only was that missing, but also the soup was just so unbearably oversalted that I could not eat more than 2 spoonfuls.

A complete, disappointing waste of money.

Traveled to Nashville TN and recommendation from locals was to have the "hot chicken." Found this place 1 block from my hotel. I was warned that the line would be long - it was - approx 30 people waiting in line at lunch time AND at 9pm at night it was close to 15-20 people).

Place does offer online ordering and you can bypass line to get your chicken order.

The wait was well worth it. The chicken is probably the best I have ever had. You have selection on spice level (none, mild, hot). With most orders you get two sides (recommend the Pimento Cheese and macaroni and Red skin potato salad).

Was on a 3 day business trip and ate at this place twice. Highly recommend. Staff is courteous. Limited seating area - but that is because lots of customers come to eat here.

The westbank location is the only location I ate at. I must say that food is amazing and the service is A+. Everything is fresh and prepared with care. No complaints on my end. Just wish they did law enforcement discount like they do military.

YESSSS!!! PHILLY HAS AN ALL YOU CAN EAT HOT POT AND BBQ! An 5 star full review right here! Get the scoop! 

APPEARANCE: Very mordern, elegant and simplistic design. Its got a nice authentic color scheme and get atmosphere for family, friends and more! anyone you bring will be impressed and its almost always very busy! Its a formal resturant that is also casual! Good for anytime morning, afternoon and late night! They also have huge party rooms, which my family always uses when we come to celebrate for birthdays or just party! 

SERVICE: first im going to point out that the staff is very cute and good looking.. i have no shame in saying that, plus they are super friendly and easily crack jokes with you if you like! They gladly bring recommend food options and help your grill the BBQ! Exceptional service all the way! The servers even went out and got beers and deserts for us!

FOOD: With a fantastic appearence, atmosphere and service tbe food is of course on par and if not better! The options seem endless from meats to seafood and vegetables and oriental drinks! They have it all! I recommend Hot Pot for is variety of vegetables and seafood and the BBQ for its mouth watering smell and meat! Watching the food cook infront of your eyes is soo satisfying and makes your mouth just drop and water! Sooo good, you really cant go wrong anywhere! Also BYOB

PRICE: Its extremely  reasonable for ~$22 Hot Pot and ~$27 BBQ and $32 for both! For the amount of food you can eat as much as you want I was all in for this! This is definitely the place to go. Around the area the other similar style resturants are over price this place is where its at! 

Overall, I'd recommend this place whenever with whoever because it's just that impressive and good! HOT POT AND BBQ ALL THE WAY!

With one week before a private memorial gathering in my home, and in the midst of a three day holiday weekend, my caterer was forced to cancel my bought and paid for order, due to the need to temporarily close the business because of a shortage of personnel.  I tried to stay calm as I started calling around town for alternatives.  Some businesses were closed, others not taking large and/or online orders.  Several were closed for a week, during the time I needed, to give their overworked staffs some time off.  Others were limiting their menu choices and options due to personnel shortages.  Shout out to the woman at The Clover and the Bee who took my call, on a very busy Saturday morning, and to her manager, Alfonso Aceves, who in a matter of hours, got back to me with offers to help.  Though I had already made arrangements with another establishment, my faith in humanity was lifted by the goodness of those willing to help on such short notice!!!!

By the way, I have ALWAYS enjoyed the food, service, and delightful surroundings at The Clover and the Bee.

We came here last week and man oh man. Whiskey Joe's aims for the vibe that every riverside restaurant aims to capture, yet they hit the target in every aspect! The outside was designed as a beautiful beach with tiki huts and fire pits. I did not go inside but my friends said it looks great inside as well. 
Parking was a bit confusing, there's valet parking for $5 or do it yourself parking with a short walk, the $5 is worth it however. You may want to carpool if you wish to limit cost. 
I got wings, others got burgers, still others got nachos. Everyone agreed it was incredible food and a great atmosphere. I loved the wings, they were the best I've had and I've had A LOT of wings! 
I cannot recommend this place enough, it's the toast of the town if you will!

This pizza was delicious.   I had a personal chicago style pizza and mozzerella triangles,  and they were both bomb.    An hr is a bit long to wait for food,  but i cant complain if i want my pizza cooled right.

This was an unusual place, but glad my husband and I found it! Even though "the Hill" is known for Italian food, ChaCha Chow has succeeded at Mexican/Latin food there. They have a small menu, but it was still hard to decide what to get - it all sounded good!  We tried three of the five kinds of tacos - bbq pork, beef short rib & fish tacos...finally a good fish taco in St. Louis!! We also tried the cha cha burger & fries - not typical Mexican fare, but still had that "flare" since it was seasoned nicely then topped with peppers, onions, cheese & spicy ketchup - pretty delicious in my opinion! The fries were also good & spicy!  
We'll definitely go back since it's so close to work...still need to try the chicken verde taco & pupusas! (They have a curried sweet potato taco too for veggie lovers...not sure if I'm game for that one)
4/5 stars just because it was a little pricey for the quantity we received $25 for 2 @ lunch, no cocktails - service & taste were excellent!

My cousin got married here and while I didn't stay in the hotel it would be a cool place to have any kind of outdoor party. It looks like an old plantation. It's quite an experience although I enjoyed being on the front porch, or under the tent rather than inside the hotel lobby. It was spooky how much I felt like I was back in the old school south.

Was so looking forward to this experience after visiting a Peruvian restaurant in London and waiting for a place in Philly to pop up! The Pisco Sours were delicious, but getting them took forever (even though we ate early at 6:15 and the restaurant wasn't full yet). The dishes were lackluster--not enough flavor and the seafood was rubbery and tasteless. I'd go back for drinks but wouldn't recommend the food, especially for how expensive it was.

We love Brandon. All of our clients have a great experience with him! Brandon and his team are so professional and our clients always rave about how helpful they are! We are so thankful to know and work with Brandon everyday!

This is a very nice apartment in a very nice location - close to regional rail, restaurants, and river trails.  

And that's where the good stops.  

Parking is a disaster.  If you plan to get home after 8pm on any given night, you will not find parking.  There is absolutely zero enforcement of cars without parking permits.  The office recently decided to switch from parking permit tags to parking permit stickers and has lauded this as solving the parking problem.  The rationale here is unclear, but what is clear is that nothing will change without enforcement, which the management company seems unwilling to undertake.

Reaching anyone in the "management office" is often an effort in futility.  They do not answer the phones; often the office is empty during business hours.  Even though it was already difficult to reach someone, they decided to end Sunday hours.  Unfortunately the management's concerns seem to end once you had signed on the dotted line and become a resident.  I recommend copying the regional manager or calling corporate headquarters when you have an issue.

The maintenance team seems very nice.  Unfortunately they operate completely independently of the office.  You might put in a maintenance ticket and if they decide they don't want to deal with it, they will simply close it and not notify you.  There doesn't appear to be grounds staff; there is often broken glass left on the ground after recycling is picked up, for example, and on multiple occasions I have come across dead birds in the parking garage areas.

Be very careful before renting a top floor apartment.  If like me you are lucky enough to live under all the building's compressors which sit on the roof, you won't sleep and will get migraines.  I'll be happy to update this review if the management company ever solves this issue, but to date, I've gotten nothing but empty promises (going on a year now).  I'm typing this email at 3am as I sit here listening to the compressors run.

They do not enforce rules about dogs being on leash, leading to a dangerous situation for other residents and dogs.  Again - the office staff is concerned with leasing, but once you are here, their concerns appear to stop.

The elevator situation is disastrous.  Over the winter, the elevator in my building was out intermittently (more often than not) for several weeks.  It was also dangerous, periodically shuddering to the ground rapidly when it was supposed to be going up.  During this time, maintenance told me the office had decided efforts to fix the elevator were costing too much money.  Additionally, the elevator was not connected to an answering service, so if you did happen to get stuck during an incident, there was no way to reach assistance.  Just a few hours ago we were notified that the elevator in another building was out of service.  When I first moved in the elevator in the last building was out of service.  It's a constant problem, and one the management seems to have no interest in fixing.

A few months after the management company changed, they switched the vendor billing for common utilities.  This led to extra charges with no information from management, whose response was to "Call the new company with questions."

The office gives less than two days notice when having to enter your apartment for routine building wide maintenance.  Most recently, they gave less than two days notice for checking the fire alarms of the buildings.  People with pets had no opportunity to make plans for them to be out of the building, resulting in serious issues for some pets due to the exceptionally loud noise and flashing lights.  The inspector told me my sprinklers were painted over, but I have heard zero follow up from management about this issue.

After a work assignment in town ended early, I had some time to kill and decided to check this place out rather than wander around the airport.

I got there around 3 pm on a weekday, so it was fairly empty except for a few other people hovering over laptops. This is a very casual place with a vintage feel- equal parts coffee house and bar. The barista was super friendly and took my order quickly- even opened a new bottle of wine instead of serving one that was previously opened. I had the spinach dip with chips, and though the dip was served chilled (rather than the hot kind I anticipated), it was flavored well and the portion was a good size. Just the kind of snack I needed to make it through the afternoon. The menu isn't huge but it's got enough interesting things on there to make it worthwhile.

Next time I'm in town I will check out some of the coffee offerings as well- watching the prep of other patrons' drinks, I could see the time and skill put into each one.

Stopped here for a quick breakfast.. which wasn't quick at all. To start there was only a few bagels left which is fine, but after I had ordered I over heard the cashier saying there were more bagels in the back. Thanks for telling me that. On top of it it took about 15 minutes or so to get our bagel order. Nothing fancy just needed the bagel toasted.. by the time we got our bagels they were cold and on top of that had to put our cream cheese on it. Really strange place.. wouldn't recommend it again.

First time going to this location with some friends. The building itself is beautiful and spacious. Old church into a brewery/ restaurant was a success in my opinion. Parking was bad and went on a Sunday night. The restaurant was very slow w very few guests. The server never asked how we were and it took food a very long time to come out. There was no acknowledgement of how long things were taking and a quick check in or apology would have been nice. Appetizers and dinner took a long while. I ordered the pork chop and it was very dry. 2 of us ordered that and we liked the sauce (bourbon glaze) and the sweet potato tots were good. We had asked what temp they recommended and he said anything over medium. With that we said Med well but it was very well done and hard to swallow. The waiter did not return to ask how the food was. He did fill up water and drinks though. Another friend ordered the lobster risotto. She said it was very bland (another friend tried and he agreed) and some of the mussels were raw. She did not eat them after discovering that.  
When we left an  employee was near the door and no one said anything to us when we left. The employee was not with any guests and it was very vacant at that time. 
The highlight for food was my friends bison meatloaf. That is what I wished I had ordered.

One of the best Mexican places I have tried by far! Great taste!! Totally reccommend the carne Azteca! It's amazing! I would give it five stars if I didn't have to wait in line to order my food like a fast food chain and sit in a very small table! Regardless , it was Totally worth it ! A must try while in SB!

I went at 2:30 pm on a Monday afternoon, absolutely no line. I went past on a Sunday and the line was almost out to the main road. Try to go during off times. I paid for the $7 was but I'm curious how the machine knows if u pay for the $3 or the $15  one. I mainly went for the free vacuum! Trick is you still have to buy a car wash in order to use the free vaccuum. Next time I'll probably just pay for the $3 wash. Anyway, the vacuum strength was so strong it sucked off one of my stereo buttons of my car!! I sat there debating if I should just let it be or try and find help getting it back. There was a guy walking around nearby so I flagged him down. I asked him to help me and he was eager to help!!! We found my button and I tried to give him a tip but he wouldn't take it. I'm so happy I have my button back:) Just be careful bc those vacuums have a really strong suction!!!!

The best Sicilian pizza I have ever had.  Very consistent....always a winner!  White pie is great, and regular cheese pie is one of the best around!   The staff  are wonderful....friendly and efficient!  Love, love, love this place!
worst food ！ The "tasty creamy mashed potatoes" is not testy or creamy，it tastes funny。My friend doesn't feel well after eating over there, and diarrhea。
Love this place. Delicious and GREAT artistic atmosphere. 5th star if they had more SOL (Sustainable, Organic, Local) AND/OR if they were some kind of a cooperative organization.

Service was unfortunate, food was ok not exceptional. This place is highly overrated in my opinion. Having lived in Spain I had higher expectations considering this place is suppose to have authentic Spanish tapas. My gambas al ajillo is better hands down.
It's at your own pace. Has a great view. It's really high. Has entertainment for the little ones while your up there. The one reason why we went here was for the penny machine. Happy they had it.

Overpriced, subpar, bland food that is not authentic at all. No flavor! Meat portion was so small, not characteristic of Arab food. Sampler appetizer was decent but we have had better. Also service is slow and inconsistent. We do not recommend.

Hands down best massage I've had in a long time. It's really a unique experience now a days to get a high quality massage for an affordable price. My boyfriend and I had Tina & Coco and they were both fantastic! We both have pretty bad muscular issues and for the first time in a while we felt tension dissolve. Highly recommend!!

Went out Saturday afternoon & wow! It's worth the drive to Geiger Grade.  Plenty of parking, carts by the entrance.  And so many plants!  We walked all around, through greenhouses & the shop.  Good prices, and happy to support a local business.  Loved the shop & all the things we don't need, but want.

I have mixed feelings about this place.

When I booked my room several months in advance for my 1 year anniversary, the lady I spoke to was very accommodating and I had no issue with the reservation. I asked a lot of detailed questions knowing how important this weekend was for me and she answered all of them without issue.

I also received a text from someone named Paul in the morning of my arrival just confirming if I had any needs or questions. I responded about the anniversary and basically just to make sure I have a nice room due to the occasion, but I didn't require anything in particular as I already knew I had booked a Junior Suite and I expected to get something worthy of the $1,600 total I was paying for two nights which included valet and service charges.

When we arrived, the Valet was very attentive, the front desk was very friendly and attentive, and a couple of phone calls I placed to the front desk were handled by friendly and attentive individuals. This includes the checkout. For Service, I give this place 5 stars. However, I will say that I was a bit disappointed that there was nothing in the room waiting for me for the 1 year anniversary, again, especially for the price I paid for everything. Other folks have commented on receiving something, but for us, not even a happy anniversary when we arrived or a nice note in the room. Anyway, it is what it is and no biggie, but as I normally stay at high end places, most other places would have taken that extra step.

Though our Junior suite, the room was spacious and a corner room, the balcony is tiny. It's only their for the look, you can only stand on it and it felt dangerous to me, so I stayed away. You can't open any windows to let any air in at night except for the balcony door which has no screen. The room itself was very clean, so we were happy about that. I appreciated the fact that the bed was comfortable, the TV worked, except for the one in the bathroom which had maybe 3 channels that came in with a lot of interference. I read about how someone wrote that the water pressure in the shower isn't very good. For the rain forest shower head, very true, but for the handheld one it was fine. The shower was very spacious and there was more than enough bathroom counter space. There was a magnifying  mirror next to the sink.

The room itself though feels very dated, from the couch which had stains to the colors of the wall, to the furniture, just everything kind of looked dreary to me and in need of a major upgrade. Many may like this dated neutral look and may even call it charming, for me, well, I didn't. It was the first $1600 two night stay room where I didn't want to share with my mother via WhatsApp like I normally do a live video of the room because it wasn't anything special to look at. For that kind of money, whether I'm in San Francisco, Palm Springs, or Miami, I get stunning views, huge and/ or pretty rooms, modern amenities, etc, but this really felt like you are just paying for the location.

I did appreciate that the room was quiet. We didn't hear our neighbors or anyone above or below us. That would have been great except for the fact that every few minutes, the A/C which is in the closet made a loud noise. When we first heard it from across the room, I actually thought it was someone blow drying their hair in the next room. Then it happened again and I looked at my husband and said, wow, this person really likes to work on their hair. Then when it happened again, that's when we traced it to the closest where the blowing high pitched sound would occur every few minutes. Fortunately, I brought with me one of those sleep machines with white fan noise so I placed it on the floor between the bed and the direction of the closest where with the help of my melatonin, I was able to mostly ignore it and fall asleep. 

We didn't order any food, they did provide us a $10 credit against the bill since apparently there was a credit we could have used as part of our package for the food, but there are so many great places within walking distance, we didn't succumb to the laziness of the overpriced menu. 

We did LOVE the fact that the hotel was dog friendly as we brought our Toy Poodle with us. Our dog seemed to enjoy the room and behaved herself the entire time. Just be aware that it may not be able to find grass to walk the dog if your dog is accustomed to grass. To save yourself some time, if you leave the front of the hotel and make a left, just go one block and there is a Jiffy Lube. That entire area has grass. There is also in the other direction, if you make a right out of the hotel and then a right on State Street, go about 2 blocks and on the left about 100 feet up the street there is a large grass area behind some restaurants. 

So in summary, great service, clean hotel, fantastic location, dog friendly, great roof top with pool, overpriced, ridiculous $78 service fee that doesn't include the $38 per night valet, dated.

Wow, incredible value. Huge steaks with all the trimmings for $25-$30. Steaks were awesome and cooked perfectly. I had the ribeye, my GF had the porterhouse both were exceptional. It's not fine dining but the food and service are amazing. We'll be back!

I live on the second story of a beautiful, but impractical, New Orleans home. The high ceilings and zero insulation on the roof lead to extremely hot temperatures during the summer. On a good day, my house would reach to the mid 80's. When searching for solutions, I found spray foam. I met with several companies and felt most confident and comfortable with Sunlight. 

They have been nothing but courteous, professional, timely, and most importantly, pay close attention to detail. We are only halfway through the project, but I look forward to the final results.

My favorite place in New Port and I do t even like
Tacos. :) Mongolian beef and jerk chicken tacos are amazing. Their deserts are off the chain too!

My husband is fairly obsessed with Hawaiian food.  Peg's Glorified Ham and Eggs has been a staple for him since he discovered their Hawaiian dishes and he's pleased to have L&L just a couple doors down with a later closing time to get his fix.  

So far he's had the Kalua & Lau Lau Combo and the Loco Moco and I've had the Kalua Pork Sandwich.  We were both pretty pleased with our orders though the Kalua pork was pretty light on the flavor; this might be a one-time issue, future visits will tell.  

The restaurant itself is a bit awkward and could use some attention.  During both visits, the trash can outside was beyond overflowing with piles of trash littered around it and the interior is a bit cramped.  There's no clear way to know where you should line up to place your order meaning people were lumped into awkward groups in the small spaces between the (too large?) tables.  Also, the service at the front was a bit cold both times and on my second visit, the vibe was very stressed out.  Of course, all of this is likely due to growing pains and I'm hopeful they get worked out.  I'll absolutely be back and I will be updating my review appropriately!

Bottom line, the food is pretty good and worth a shot!

Lindsey always gets me through the correct steps to take action on my legal needs. She is professional, courteous and experienced. I would say call and talk to her and you'll see yourself!
Anthony

Rick Ross the boss sent me here. lol  I was in the area for my job and my coworker suggested this place.

The fries were good. Almost as good as Penn station, in fact  I'm going to say Wingstop fries and Penn Station's are cousins.

I opted for the garlic parmesan and the mild wings. The mild wings were the better of the two;  saucy just to be saucy, but it worked. The garlic parmesan was a little too salty for my taste. 
I probably would only go back if I couldn't think of anything else to eat.

This little park is actually a 10 foot-wide sidewalk which starts on the north at Columbus Statue Park and ends at Gandy Boulevard to the south. That makes this 4.5 mile-long hunk o' concrete the world's longest continuous sidewalk. 

The park hugs the perimeter of Hillsborough Bay, and follows Bayshore Boulevard around South Tampa. Most of us know this area because of the awesome scenic views of the Bay, the spectacular homes along Bayshore Boulevard, and that big ol' honkin' pirate ship. Whatttttt ?!?!?!?

Bayshore Park is a popular spot to see people walking, jogging, running, pushing strollers, riding bikes, inline skating, and dog walking, as they gaze over the sea wall and watch for signs of manatee and dolphins and pirates! Trail amenities include benches, a water fountain, bicycle parking, a city marina and fitness stations. The sunrises and sunsets are world-class, and just another reason why I'm glad that I live in Florida.

In late January this section of Tampa is home to the legendary Gasparilla Pirate Invasion and Pirate Parades. Any good student of Tampa history will tell you that the name of Tampa's traditional Gasparilla Carnival comes from legendary pirate Jose Gaspar, "last of the Buccaneers," who terrorized the coastal waters of West Florida during the late 18th and early 19th century. Gaspar, given to calling himself "Gasparilla," served as a lieutenant in the Royal Spanish Navy for five years until 1783 when, upon seizing command of a Spanish sloop-of-war, he with his fellow mutineers set sail for the Florida straits. And so the young Spanish aristocrat-turned-pirate began an adventurous life as outlaw of the sea.

The story of the swashbuckling Gasparilla was unearthed and his memory revived in 1904 when Tampa's social and civic leaders adopted the pirate as patron rogue of their city-wide celebration. The Gasparilla Children's Parade comes first with hundreds and hundreds of pint-sized Johnny Depp look-alike swashbucklers taking to Bayshore Boulevard and cheering on all of the floats, marching bands, and dance companies. Most everyone is in costume, and hoping to snag some pirate's booty (strands of beads) to take home and show Mom and Dad.

The following weekend is the raucous and outrageous Gasparilla Pirates Invasion and Parade. This time the pirate ships sail up through Hillsborough Bay to the Convention Center where the pirates demand the keys to the City from the Mayor. From there the costumed pirates lead the parade floats, marching bands, dance teams, along the same route as they cheer for grog, beads, and wenches!

No matter when you come to visit Bayshore Park you're guaranteed to have a great time. Enjoy the view, the warm weather, the sunsets, and let loose with a mighty "Arrrggghhh!"

I usually sit in the bar because the restaurant seating can be a zoo and very loud
The food is ok for a chain I like their burgers and my wife says the steaks are a good value. There are always coupons around so you can get some money off the bill
The blooming onion is good but usually way too salty. I like the dark bread and butter its best when it is hot
I've had them mess up my order several times and well well done does not sound like rare but I once got a burger that way
The staff is always nice and they keep the place clean

My boyfriend and I love this place! It's one of our favorite treats and we love the loyalty card that gives us a free yogurt after every 9 bought. Our one wish would be for captain crunch to reappear in the topping bins! :)

This place was really close to our hotel which made it a great first stop. The waiters were very friendly and over all I had a good experience here. 

The first time I went I had a chai tea latte which was delicious. Highly recommend it. 

My second visit I had a problem. I ordered an English Breakfast, and one would think tea, duh. Instead I got this vile latte drink that was more mixture of syrup then coffee and I had to throw it out because it was too sickly. I guess next time I need to say tea. 

Overall although good prices and good selection. I would go back, just be careful how you order.

My favorite ice cream place in Brandon. I've been going here since I was little and now take my own kids. The kids really enjoy the play area outside as well. You can't go wrong with ordering anything here. The inside is a little tiny but it's Florida, go sit outside. Drive thur is always fast.

Hmmm. I was really not sure what to expect. I am in the market for a new washer (see my review for the Southern Plaza Laundry & Tan). I think I was hoping for better deals. I did find a Maytag washer that I may end up purchasing-has a dent on the front. However, I saw a Kenmore I was interested in. Everything here is not "scratch and dent" per se, some things are on "clearance" or maybe another word I am not familiar with, because I looked up the Kenmore on the Sears website, and it was cheaper at the store, than at the 'outlet'. Same model, etc. Yeah. IDK. 
They do have lots of interesting things, such as clearance furniture, large and small appliances, and clothing. And lots of other random things you would find at Sears. 
Final comment: do research before you buy. That is always the best way to go.

Could not have had a better experience! Josie & Allison were amazing teachers and Josh made setting up our off site event so easy.  It was like having your best friends come over and teach you how to paint,  seriously.  If you're thinking about trying a class,  do it.  If you're thinking about hosting a party,  host it. You'll love it.

Found this on YELP and went last night for the first time.  This is a little pub located in the heart of Oreland.  There is plenty of parking and the bar gives a great first impression as it is sleek and immaculate.  The service was great.  The menu has a good variety.  We tried the triple sliders (one bacon, one blue cheese, one American cheese with fries), the fried red bliss potatoes topped with Parmesan cheese and side of blue cheese and hot sauce for dipping, mac' n cheese and wings.  Everything we ordered was delicious.  The food was prepared very well and served promptly.  We will definitely return and spread the word.

Honestly this place was better than many Mexican restaurants I have been to. I've never heard of this restaurant before, but was excited to try when I saw it while walking through the mall. 

Mystery man and I had gotten Carnitas Verde burrito bowls. Let me tell you this place was better than chipotle. It was like the CAVA of mexican fast food restaurants. We also got the chips and Queso. 

The mystery kids had cheese quesadilla kids meals. They came with chips, queso, juice box, and a cookie! 

I liked it here and would certainly come back to try other things on the menu as well.

I found this nail salon over the summer and I am never going anywhere else. I have had my nails done by Linda during all of my visits. She is fast, professional and very talented. When she does my dip powered nails they typically stay nice for 3+ weeks! The place is clean and the service is efficient. Lots of colors to pick from and you have the option of a glass of wine with your service.

Ate here tonight for the first time.  It is a byob.  My husband and I were enjoying some vodka when the waitress came over and poured water in it.  We explained that our water glasses were full and attempted to drink our vodka a second time from a second glasds. AGAIN, the waitress came over and poured water in it again.  They did not seem REMOTELY sorry but rather laughed at their second mistake.  The food was average and we will definitely never go back.  There is a better sushi restaurant between 17th and 18th on South ( a few doors down).

JDog Alpharetta/Roswell area in Georgia did a fantastic job helping me and my son clean out the basement and load a truck for travel to storage. Michael and Devine were first class guys and hard workers. Before beginning, I was a little concerned about the cost, but at the end of the day I was very pleased with quality of work and the cost. Highly Recommended!!!!!

First off, Very friendly front staff with a clean admission area.

 Once admitted the techs in the back kept me up to date on my position in Que to see the doc and the anticipated wait time. All the equipment was clean and modern and I felt they were very well organized and well staffed. 

 The doctor was super friendly and knowledgable and made my procedure fast and virtually painless.

 I HIGHLY recommend this facility with anyone with a work place injury.

I love this resturant.  Its one of my favorites because everything is affordable and good.  You can see they take pride in what they serve.  If you can get there on one of the few nights that they serve the primerib it is the best in boise.  They use a lavender rub and cook it to perfection.

We were really excited about this restaurant and anticipated its arrival for months!  We looked at the menu once it was posted and couldn't believe--pad thai for $18 for dinner but were excited when we saw the price at lunch was 1/2 the cost.  It was a generous lunch size (veggie pad thai) but was just ok, pretty dry actually, I kept putting lime on top.  My friend had the coconut soup which she said had a big layer of oil on top and she didn't eat.  We will go back in a few weeks and try it, we want it to work things out and succeed!

This is place has one of the best happy hour menus in Tampa .  The staff was super friendly and very attentive - quite honestly a rarity these days . A special shout out to Frank and his outstanding service . The Lobstah Mac n Cheese was extraordinarily delicious - I savored every bite . The lobster tacos with a splash of siracha was a 10 + !! This place is a must and most definitely a great happy hour meeting place ...

Gotta support the local, ya know. The staff is incredibly friendly for a start. Love that. It's local and neighborhood based--love that too. Also, nice selection of teas, and I presume coffee (I won't touch the stuff unless Hagen Das is in the title). They do have a few quick grab bakery items, but not as much as I wish. Cute little off-the-beaten path place to go grab a cuppa and a catch up or meeting. Long may they reign in Chatham Arch.

I attended my first hockey game last night at the TCC Arena. The Roadrunners beat the San Diego Gulls 4-1. It was fun. I could have done without the noise from all the cowbells in the audience. Next time I'll bring earplugs.
Horrible customer service! Paid for several volleyball games..when we came in, the court was take by basketball players. Refused to give us a refund and didn't apologize. Never coming back!

We are happy with this car wash and are glad to have this new location in Eagle!

As with any mechanical car wash, it never gets all the books and crannies but they provide towels to finish off the job. The towels are clean, soft and absorbent. There are dual vacuums, one for each side of the car. Staff is friendly and wash prices are comparable. 

They have a monthly fee for unlimited car wash that's roughly 2-3 times the single wash price, depending on the wash package you select.

We will be back!

Both the food and drink were delicious and reasonably priced when we went on a random Monday evening. They have specials, but you need to ask. The house maragaritas were only $2 and good-sized. The menu is pretty extensive and everything seemed freshly made. Parking lot is right next to restaurant.
This is a amazing place.I have been twice both time were after a funeral and both times they knocked it outta the park Friendly staff and very professional...I highly recommended this place.

My sandwich and soup here was good, and the service was excellent.  I was a little disappointed by the volume of contents hiding between the bread of my $8 "half sandwich" - I expected more, even for a half sandwich, and concluded that it's a little pricey for what you're served, when compared to other lunch options.  All three of us left lunch hungry after spending $11 apiece (and drinking only water) with tip.

We LOVE Choolaah. It's definitely an Americanized version of Indian food, but it's delicious. Service is great and the flavors in the food are amazing. I love their paneer and veggie bowls. The veggie masala, tikka masala, lentil daal, all sooo good. We always order extra naan because we love it, but they give you a big piece so probably not necessary. Love their fire and lava sauces that you can get at the utensil counter to add more heat to the dishes. Ordering online and picking up is also super convenient! The decor is modern and simple. Clean and beautiful. Love the hand washing station out in the dining area because you will get your hands dirty if you eat this food the right way!

I'm from DC, Atlanta, SanFran, Detroit, Bath, ME, WV...I've lived around.  Steak and cheese, cheesesteak, (whatever you want to call it) is part of my constitution.  This is my version of comfort food plain and simple.  I've made my own and I have tried countless varieties from more places then I can care to remember.  I've had allot of versions, some memorable and some not so much.  

Here is what I will tell you about Mamas.  It's a warning actually....This place will ruin you on all other cheesesteaks anywhere-ever.  I can tell you about the bread, I can tell you about the meat, I can tell you about  cheese, (secret blend of 5 cheeses I think) and I can tell you about whatever.  I'm going to save all of that and just tell you this sandwich will make you not want to order another cheesesteak anywhere else again because any other cheesesteak would simply pale in comparison.  It's on another level, plain and simple.

I've tried many Thai places in the New Orleans area, and not one even compares to Equator. The lunch specials are out of this world...so much for around 10 dollars an entree! Their pad Thai is absolute the best. I love asking them to add veggies to it, but it really doesn't need it because it is already so filling. Soups and appetizers are delicious, as well as their specialty teas. If you do go here, don't be surprised if you start craving it...A LOT.

Mike and Justin just finished cleaning our windows and they did a fabulous job!  We're glad we used Alpine and will call them anytime we need their services.  They were recommended by friends and we'll pass the recommendation along without hesitation.  They were careful while working inside our home and cleaned the windows and storms inside and out.  Great work!

If it's "last call"... 2 hours before close,  than tell your customer... don't ignore them. "Oh the owners want us to stop serving...."  Unbelievably same experience on 1st visit which was your GRAND OPENING!! Last visit.

This is an absolute must for people who enjoy art & sculptures! This beautiful garden is located with in NOLA city park. They have more than 60 sculptures!! 

You can walk around the whole park or take a trolley on warmer days. I suggest walking because you can then take your time admiring the art. There are some really beautiful Spanish moss trees! 

Some of the cool sculptures include the Love sign (awesome for lovers!), the giant mosquito and the upside safety pin. 

There is also a huge spider and you can walk underneath it. I was mesmerized by everything!!

We were passing thru Nashville and literally checked yelp for "best restaurant near I-24".  It was sheer luck that we found Tasty and Delicious. It's definitely worth the stop!  If you like a good burger, these are SO GOOD and the guys are super nice!!  Don't let the outside fool you - it's small but packs amazing taste and service!!
This is my favorite McDonald's in the area. The employees are wonderful, the food is always hot and my order is always right. I will go out of my way to eat here if I am craving McDonalds.

This is a great hospital, one of the best in the Middle Tennessee area. I've had a number of surgical procedures and hospitalizations here and have found the staff to be both skilled and professional.

The menu here was very unappealing to me. Everything was pretty heavy and lots of red meat which i dont care for. I opted for a salad and the ahi appetizer. I have never had a worse salad i dont think. The dressing tasted literally like they spritzed water over the whole thing, it was really strange. The ahi was very mediocre and if i recall it was around $12, too expensive to be mediocre. The service wasnt good and it wasnt because it was busy, it was a monday night and there were only about 6 other people in the whole place. We had a party of 8 and the only people satisfied with their food were the ones who ordered burgers. We unanimously agreed though that the overall experience due to the service and prices we felt were too high wasnt good enough to want to come back.

Nothing special, this is your typical main drag of a touristy area style bar/restaurant. The drink list is definitely massive and the tap list is great.

The service was friendly and inviting as well. It did take some time to get refills but nothing to seriously complain over.

The mozzarella sticks are what we were told they are known for. They are huge and homemade but nothing that amazing.

The so cal chicken wrap definitely wasn't my favorite but it seemed fresh. The chicken was a little burnt which left that taste lingering after each bite.

I have been wanting to try this place for some time so yesterday we went for our anniversary lunch! It was not bad. The beers I tried were good, the service was okay, and the food was tasty but my order was incorrect. Our server would disappear for large chunks of time, our order took a while considering how few patrons I could see both inside and out, and I asked for Pork on my nachos which wasn't present when my food came out. By the time I had a chance to look at my plate once she set it down she was already gone and wasn't seen for some time so I just ate them as they came. I was surprised that a brewing company doesn't offer traditional fare like burgers and felt the menu was a little bit limited unless you love salads or mac and cheese, which is fine it just is not my jam. I felt like we waited for a while for the check so we scrambled to give her our card before she disappeared again. 

Pro: The patio was nice, the food we did get was pretty tasty, the beer was also tasty. 
Con: The service was slow and our order was not correct. Very limited menu in my opinion.
We ate there for a surprise birthday about two months ago.  Great vegan restaurant.  My food surprised me with the flavors and quality.  Service was good and a great time with 10 of my best friends.

I stopped by Capdeville.... Actually, no. I walked past Capdeville 3 times before I found it. A sign on the door would be handy.

Anyways, I stopped by Capdeville for lunch and ordered the black and blue burger with fries. The burger was phenomenal: generously sized without being obscene, perfectly cooked, and nicely topped. The fries we ren't perfect, but they were damn close -- fresh cut, lightly crispy on the outside and salty. Thankfully, I'll be back in NOLA next month, and I look forward to visiting again.

We went here for a birthday as my brother-in-law had heard good things.  We were very disappointed.  Four of us ordered the Chateaubriand (mine medium) and it was absolutely terrible.  I like a nice crust on my steak but it was burnt to a crisp, tasted like charcoal and raw on the inside.  It also cost $90 (for a couple).  My wife ordered hers rare with her brother and same, burnt to crisp on outside, raw in the middle.  It included dessert and our table ordered cannoli, carrot cake and flourless chocolate cake. The carrot cake and chocolate cake both tasted stale and I recognized the Hershey's chocolate syrup drizzled over the cannoli and chocolate cake.  A desert from TGI Fridays would have been better.

And the price.... I paid for dinner and it was $450 (party of 6).  I could have had a better steak at Outback for far less.  I don't mind paying for good food  and could have dined at Bern's, Capital Grille, Ruth's Chris, etc. for the same money and actually enjoyed the food.

I didn't want to make a big scene bc it was a birthday and my in-laws chose the place.  I ended up taking the steak home and feeding it to my dogs.  I didn't eat lunch prior to dinner and was absolutely starving if that says anything on how bad the food was.

I can't fathom where the positive reviews come from, they have to be fake.  You've been warned.

Solid Seafood. Love that they use fresh seafood and that the menu changes constantly. Started with the Lobster Dumplings. For entrees, we had the Wood Grilled Grouper(with a pineapple glaze) and the New Bedford Sea Scallops(also Wood Grilled atop some mushroom risotto). Ended with the Crème Brûlée.  Our server, Ricardo, was excellent. Loved that he was very attentive and wasn't so pretentious. Great experience. Would definitely come back.

I had a phenomenal experience ordering a custom cake from Sophisticakes this past weekend. I went in a week prior to get a quote. I can't remember who helped me but she was so friendly and helpful. She asked me what I had in mind for my friend's bridal shower cake, showed me pictures of cakes they'd done before, and figured out a solution for my budget and number of guests. All this took only about 10 minutes. They're very flexible with opening early if you need the cake before opening hours, and the whole process was totally seamless. The cake was exactly what I was hoping it would be. I chose the chocolate chip pound cake with buttercream icing, and the guests were thrilled with it. Everyone kept asking where it came from and couldn't believe it was my neighborhood bakery. Several guests were literally smiling as they savored every bite, and several also went back for seconds. Many wanted to take home a leftover piece for someone at home to try. Everyone agreed the cake was an absolute highlight of the party. Basically, there was nothing but rave reviews. This cake only cost us $80, and it was estimated to serve 24. We had 22 at our party, and there was plenty leftover, so I guess we cut the slices a little smaller. I would order a custom cake again from them in a heartbeat.

This company is very reliable worth every penny,  the owners are very responsive and make sure the customers are happy before they close out the jobs they do. For Florida they blow out the competition... thank you for everything.

We drive 95 often as touring musicians and were so pleasantly surprised by this find. We ordered the mushroom soup, which our three year old loved, the short ribs on pozole appetizer (tender, flavorful and filling) and the mushroom pizza. The food is simple, elegant, fresh, flavorful and not a greasy salt bomb like so many restaurant meals. The music was awesome (Wilco, Joni Mitchell, Edward Sharpe and the Magnetic Zeros), service was friendly and the decor simple. We will definitely be back!

I got takeout with the fresh spring rolls and #13 chicken pho bowl. It was amazing. My order was neatly packed with care and the presentation was very appealing.  I am looking forward to dining in the next time.

My husband and I love it here! There are so many options to pick from, no matter what your dietary restrictions are. The dessert is incredible, we tried the Belgian waffle sundae and we definitely recommend it. It's the perfect place for a date night. The service is great, the food is delicious, and we can usually find parking in front, despite being in Mass Ave. Try it out, you won't be disappointed!

Always clean, friendly staff.  My only complaint is that it's like a sauna in there.  There is no air flow, it's stifling.  Other Planet Fitness locations have really large ceiling fans.  I wish this location could improve on that.

Nice little chill spot..I went for a going away party and a little karaoke. The drinks and food are both reasonably priced and tasty. The bar is full operating but if you're sitting at tables they constantly come around for customer checks. There is also a pool table and dart board on location. The Dj has a pretty good selection of songs so that made the night fun

Stopped in here for lunch. The place had a good lunch crowd but we were seated right away. Service was all prompt and very friendly. We split the Best Friends platter, which stuffed both of us even eating just half. Both the chicken and the pork were tender and delicious. We got the mac and cheese and the potato salad for sides, both expertly made and also tasty, and it came with a popover, which I thought was the best part. The atmosphere was clean and laid back, bright. As any bbq place should it smelled amazing. On top of all this mouth-watering food, the price was incredibly reasonable. I'd return any time I'm in town.

Amazing street food!

If you're a fanatic of cheese steak sandwiches this is your place.

Among the variety available at the City Market this place has a distinctive offer.

The options for cheese steak sandwiches have a unique garnish and sauce that differs from a regular Philly cheese.

There's one that adds Ají which is a not spicy sauce originally from Peruvian culture, there's another that has chimichurri who's sauce was originated in Argentina and two other varieties from Uruguay and Peru.

It's consider a cheap lunch, the combo is roughly 12 dlls and that includes fries and soda.

There's usually a line but the service is pretty fast.

Once they are about to finish your order you can ask them to add more Ají, sauces or a variety of garnishments.

If you're starving near downtown stop by, you won't regret it!

We just left here after eating tonight. We made a reservation over 24 hours in advance knowing we were going to have a large party of 14. We made our reservation for 5pm. When we arrived, 5 minutes early and checked in, we were told we could sit outside to be seated now or it would be awhile before they could seat us inside... even though we had a reservation. We had 6 kids so we opted to sit outside to not wait (which shouldn't have happened since we had a reservation). We then sat by 5:05pm and promptly ordered drinks and appetizers. Prior to apps arriving we ordered our food (4 medium pizzas, 1 kids macaroni and 1 side of apple slices- not an outrageous amount for 14 people).  20-30 minutes after ordering our waitress came out to say that it would be an additional 20 minute wait to the normal wait. After over an hour wait since ordering we were told it would be about another ten minutes and the waitress said she was going to make sure they took care of us. The manager then proceeded to come out 5 minutes later and tell us that the restaurant was busy and everyone was having to wait, rather rudely. No apology. No offer to make anything right. No matter of sympathy whatsoever. It is a Saturday night at dinner. I'm sure the restaurant is busy, but that should be expected. It always is. Over an hour and a half after sitting down, around 6:40pm, we finally received our food. We felt rushed to eat after being there for so long. We finally asked for our bills (and received them in full) with no other mention of our extreme wait or an apology for it. After arriving at 4:55 we finally were able to leave at 7:10. We love mellow mushroom but we probably won't come back to this location. Having to spend over 2 hours at a restaurant when getting there at 5 for a reservation is insane, but the poor poor customer service from the manager is what did it. I would recommend retraining. I would be happy to share his name, but he wasn't even polite enough to introduce himself when coming by our table. Not good etiquette.

Edit: the owner and assistant manager reached out to me and went above and beyond to right this poor experience. We appreciated the fact that they did care and it changed our whole thought about the location.

Arrived in Tampa for a convention and every step of the way to get there was hellish, delays, missed flights and whatnot. We finally get to the hotel we had reservations at only to find they had been canceled by someone who was not us. Not only were they canceled, but the hotel was sold out. They were kind enough, however, to find availability at the Westin so they tossed us back in a cab and sent us over that way.

The first person from the hotel we encountered was a lovely woman named Cindy, whose warmth and enthusiasm made it impossible for me to hang onto my bad day. She told me anything I needed, to let her know and she'd see if she could make it happen. 

Getting up to the check-in desk, we explained to the man (the ever so helpful Alan) that we had been sent over from a different hotel, with the understanding there was only availability for that evening but not beyond. (Which, by no fault of theirs, would leave us without a place to stay for another 2 nights.) We asked if there was anything he could do, please....

And he did. Somehow, someway, he magically saved the rest of our trip to Florida by finding some availability for our whole stay. Thankfully, cleaning up the mess we were left in by the 'other' hotel.

The stay there was wonderful. The room, sure, it probably could use a little bit of updating, but it was white-glove clean and had an incredible view. The restaurant downstairs, we ate there 3 times during our stay and each time, the food was delicious. The breakfast buffet, the only thing I didn't like about that was the potatoes were a little too garlicky, but that's ok because I stuffed myself on everything else they had, which was a LOT.

Convenient to the convention center, a clean room, awesome customer service, delicious food and a beautiful view. I loved the stay I had there and won't hesitate to go back again.
Great place drove out of our way to to find the spot after being at the casinos all weekend. The food was awesome just what we were looking for. Great service good food.

Excellent all around - went for an early Fathers' Day brunch which was also celebrated by Lacroix with a custom dessert even though they have a whole room of amazing desserts! The Foie Gras smores and beef broth/quail egg shooters were spectacular! Top notch service - thanks Darryl!

Cute Irish pub located in the Seven Gables Inn. Having been to several pubs in Ireland, this U.S. version has pretty much captured the ambiance and décor - felt like we were in Doolin, Galway or Dublin! Nice selection of Irish whiskeys and ales, and the Irish coffee is sure to warm you up on a chilly day. 

In addition to American favorites, the menu does include some traditional Irish fare and daily special. For lunch we had the wild salmon and mash special plus the chicken pot pie. The pot pie had the biggest puff pastry crust I'd ever seen!! Both dishes were very good - only comment was the pot pie could've used more pepper, but that was an easy fix!

Great customer service, and friendly staff. We took advantage of the nice weather every time we stopped in and sat out front! Lots of locals appear to make this their watering hole of choice - another great recommendation.
This place is a great go-to shop right around home. Nice selection and very knowledgeable about the sticks in store and in general. Fun bunch of people and great atmosphere to sit, chill, and smoke.

My Boss and I work right by this place & although there are lots of other places where you can purchase "Antojitos" "Mexican Snacks" this place is within walking distance from our work. With that said we rarely ever go to this place, maybe once in a blue moon when we are craving it but today happened to be that day. I ordered us "Duros" "Pin Wheel shaped chips" with out any Chile, Limón etc. just by themselves a "Chamango" which is an "icy drink with chunks of mango, Chile etc." "Ezquite" "Toasted Corn kernels with lime juice, mayonnaise, grated cheese, chili powder, butter, and hot sauce etc" and last but not least I ordered a "Fresa Raspado" "Strawberry Icy Drink" long order short...I paid and walked back to the office. Then about 5-10 minutes go by & My Boss and I are enjoying our drinks. While talking about how they guy that served us did a really good job and despite problems with this place in the past we were glad we came back. A moment after that my Boss looked down at his "Fresa Raspado" "Strawberry Icy Drink" and low & behold to his surprise guess what he saw in it...... a COCKROACH! My Boss was really UPSET and I don't Blame him! We were both completely and utterly Grossed Out! We Immediately stoped drinking our drinks! I packed everything back up and brought it back right away! When I got there I told the guy who served us that we had a problem with our order. We  just wanted to return the whole thing and get our money back. The employee didn't speak much English and I only know the bare minimals when it comes to Spanish but he gave me my money back right away. I told him I needed either a business card or the owners name as well as business information as I would be filing a "formal complaint" with the Health Department! He didn't understand me and ended up having to call his wife to Translate. I told her the exact same thing and All she could do was translate between him and I. They both blamed it on their "Distributor" in California and said the Cockroach came from them as he had opened a new package of Flavoring for the "Raspado" I told them it doesn't Matter if it's the "Distributor's" Fault or if the cockroach came from the uncleanliness of the place.. I told them both I would be calling the Health Department as it's a "Health Code Violation"

Jax Kitchen is one of my favorite restaurants in Tucson and one of the first I recommend to people looking for delicious food and a fabulous experience. I've been to Jax quite a number of times and have never once been disappointed. More often than not the experience exceeds even my high expectations. The food is always delicious whether one of the salads ( the duck confit is always a favorite) or the delicious salmon. I also love that their menu changes so there are always new exciting things to try. 
I have to give a quick shout to their cocktails. I had the most amazing Raspberry Gimlet there that has become my new favorite drink. They converted me to a gimlet drinker and I will forever be thankful!

7:30 reservation. Table not ready. "Give us 20"
8:00. Table not ready. "We are going to get you the next table I swear"
8:30. Table not ready. "It's not our fault. Opentable just accepts reservations."  
8:31. Table turns to me and says "we've been here since 6 still waiting on an entree". 
8:32. I walked out.

I had a great experience with the Tulane Dermatology Clinic for injectable lip filler. 
Every time I called I spoke with Garrett, when I had questions I would give them a call and he'd always be quick to get back in touch! It is a learning clinic, so the discounts are great, but you may wait a few weeks for an appointment, it's really no big deal. When they had a cancellation, I received a call and had my appointment moved up a whole 2 weeks! 
The doctor in residency and physician came in and did a little mini consultation, applied numbing cream, and then did the injections all in about 30 minutes. I felt totally comfortable the whole time and my lips look great. This was my first experience with lip filler and I was impressed with the whole thing. I will be returning to the clinic when I'm ready for a touch up!

I'm giving it a 2 just because the food was pretty good and I can't give a zero for the abysmal service we received. Also, I at least used a Groupon for part of the meal so that made it a little less disappointing as well.

If you're looking for a quick dinner before going out for drinks, this is not the place to achieve that.

Ugh, woooooow.

We recently stayed at The Chase for a little staycation during some questionable winter weather, and while we originally had our eyes on The Preston, I am so glad we ended up at The Tenderloin Room. This cozy, old-school steakhouse was so perfect for a cold winter night, and the food was just outstanding.

Service here is great, but a little stuffy given the old-school, formal nature. We started with a bottle of Catena Malbec which was great, but should have been a little chilled (I get sad when restaurants serve warm red wine.) It still was really wonderful and perfectly accompanied our appetizer, the smoked atlantic salmon (served with capers, olive oil, red onion, and cream cheese.) The salmon was done perfectly and it was a great way to start the meal.

What you really care about: the steak. I really wanted the pepperloin a la tenderloin, but it just seemed way too big. I settled on the 8oz filet, and oh my God it was so delicious. It was cooked to a perfect medium, and was served on top of twice-baked potatoes and next to some expertly prepared green beans. When your server asks you if you want the optional steak sauce on top, say yes. 

When we were almost too full to move, we decided to order the cheesecake. Say yes to this as well, and enjoy it with a strong cup of coffee

I'm not sure when I'll be back, but I am so grateful we were able to enjoy such a beautiful dinner in our great city.
Biscuit Love? More like Biscuit Friend Zone. My grits were room temperature and a poor display of what grits represent (Girls Raised In The South duh). Chic fil a has better biscuits.
Fantastic. The service was perfect. The food was amazing. The fish was incredibly fresh; probably the best sashimi I have ever tasted.

Weird s* happens here.  First time: these old, er, "older" men would not stop hitting on my friend after she basically said my friend (that would be me) is here, I'm going now...  the dude proceeded to ask me about my friend and what her "problem" is.. uh, the "problem" would be YOU since you are nearly twice our age and won't stop talking about what a bitch your last gf was.  smooth move, loser. 

Second time: scary dude siting in the corner says he wants to kick one of the guys that we are with in the face!  wtf.  I don't care who you think you are mr. ex cop now bailiff or whatever person.  You don't go around threatening people for no good reason a*hole.  
The bouncers seemed to think it was all ok that the guy was a jerk.  

anyway, whatever, this place is eh.  they draw an older crowd but when when a Jamison on the rocks is $5, you know why.
Wonderful Indian food, not your typical fare. Indian with a twist. Great wait staff, attentive and knowledgeable. Loved it!
This is by far our best Chinese restaurant in Clearwater area. It's New York style Chinese. We use takeaway and they never make a mistake. Prices can't be beat - check it out.

I am a busy person, but still wanted to have a somewhat traditional, but intimate ceremony and reception. Cj's was just the place. Their first rate planning team takes you from beginning to end and all the details in between. The day of the wedding was flawless and beautiful. Jennifer (our wedding planner) made me feel very special. She and the staff took great care of my guests and family members. I would highly recommend Cj's Off the Square to anyone looking for a classy and beautiful venue to hold any event.

Terrible. A soon as I said that I wanted a short dress for my summer wedding, the consultant completely lost interest. She only pulled two dresses off the rack. As my mother and I were about to leave, we spotted a handful of short white bridesmaids dresses that would have been good to try on. Somehow David's Bridal managed to make me feel simultaneously unwelcomed and guilty for not buying anything. Gee, sorry I broke your secret rules about what is acceptable bridal attire and what isn't. As a side note, I went down the street to a discount clothing store and found the exact same dress as one that I had tried on for hundreds of dollars less. 

Their fake enthusiasm is irritating and I have received spam email from their partners.

We walked in, without a reservation and were immediately seated. As expected we were sat in the bar area. The table was right under an AC duct and way too cold. When I  commented about this, the hostess, Kim, immediately took  us back to the lobby and talked with the manager, who immediately found us another table. 
 
Our server, Daniel was amazing.  When asked about wine paring for our entrées he suggested the perfect wines.

I had the Broiled Chilean Sea Bass. When it came to the table, it looked great. My first bite told me that this was no ordinary seafood dish. The taste was out of this world. The bass was melt in your mouth done to perfection. And it was HOT, not just warm, but hot. The wine was perfect. So much so that when I took a sip, it "popped." This doesn't happen very often. 

After dessert Daniel had a very nice conversation with us, about our plans, for the next day.

Even the manager stopped by our table to see if it was a warmer location for us.

This was one of my top dining experiences ever. Highly recommending this restaurant is not enough. "Fantabulous!"

I had walked by La Fontana often during the summer months and saw all the tables outside, thinking I should try it. Finally I went last week with my girlfriend and the words mediocre and average stand out. It took a few minutes for anyone to greet us once we sat down, and when they did come over there was no introduction or sharing specials from the waitress. We ordered the bruschetta as an appetizer and I could have made that myself, it was large chunks of tomatoes with some oil on top. I brushed that off and was looking forward to my entree of chicken parmigiana. The piece of chicken was the size off my hand with maybe ten strands of spaghetti on the side. Once we were served, the waitress came over to ask if we wanted fresh Parmesan; she proceeded to bring a bowl of parmesan cheese that looked like it came from a can. I wasn't impressed by anything and will not be dining again here.

The windows are great, but whoever designed the screen removal and installation should be fired. The absolute worst system I have ever had to deal with. If you don't mind having to feel your way around to install a screen and if you'd like to open your window without completely removing your screen, than Andersen is for you.  I wouldn't again.  

John G Philadelphia

Christopher, the Operations Manager, at Canyon Ranch is amazing.  If you are fortunate enough to visit Canyon Ranch, this man will make your stay even better.  Thank you Christopher for your superb hospitality and for all you do!!!!

Great hometown Coffee shop,rustic ambience with Modern Coffee house staples like Caramel Macchiatos and Mochas,skillet Tenderloin sandwiches and of course lots of Muffins,cookies and the like. Try a pumpin spice latte!

Oatmeal (made to order) with slivered almonds and bananas that they'll even heat-up in a skillet for you.... BRILLIANT after your morning workout before heading to Van Pelt to study!!!

But I wouldn't eat anything else in this place if you paid me.

My friend and I were greeted by the nice Japanese workers and the Japanese style seats which made the whole experience more amazing! I would recommend the seafood tempura platter. Roll seemed small for the price. Even though everything was a bit pricey, they compensated with their customer service and the great food
Fantastic!  This is great Vietnamese food.  Fried oysters app is super.  Fried chicken vindaloo is vinegary as it should be.  The lamb is a must

I came here yesterday before doing some shopping between three and four o'clock, and I was alone so I just sat at the bar expecting to drink a little and get some food. I was promptly asked what I'd like to drink, but when I produced my ID-not my driver's license, but still a state issued ID-I was refused alcohol service because the bartender was unfamiliar with the form of ID. That did not bother me too much as I was just hungry and wanted food, so I waited for her to come back and offer me a nonalcoholic drink and a menu. I sat there for about five minutes, and when the bartender began washing dishes directly in front of me, it was clear I was not going to get service. I will not be returning to this establishment.

What a friendly gym. I just love it here. The kids classes look like so much fun. The DUT and boxing classes are fantastic.  Plus, everyone is SO friendly, not just the staff but the members too. Best gym ever!

Traveling for work the drop in class option has been the best bet for me and the welcoming environment makes this the only choice for my home away from home gym.
Chris and Laura have outdone themselves with this place. Some of the best cocktails and ambience in town.  Food is perfectly cooked and served with a smile. All day happy hour is oh so Nola.

Food: overall, yummy! Not the best ever in NOLA, but very close to it. Highly recommend the pasta NOLA. The fried green tomatoes were truly disgusting. 4 star on taste. 

Price: incredible. One of the cheaper dining restaurants with good food. 5 star on price. 

Location: great! 5 star. 

Service: great! 5 star. 

I will return here!! Enjoyed this place.

There's a reason Sylvia Segress shot this place up in 1985.    It's a pretty crappy mall, which is suprising in an area full of white people who like to shop.  The problem is these white people also like to drive and go to KOP or other malls like that leaving this place really crappy.  There are loads of empty stores including one of the Anchor shops.  It is accessible on the route 101 trolley and 4 bus lines tho.

This is a surprise hidden jewel in Montecito, Santa Barbara. I had a wonderful lunch in this heavenly, exclusive and spectacular setting. Unfortunately, this is not a "Every Joe" club. In order to get into this restaurant, you need either to pay an astronomical membership fees to join the club first, or find a super rich sugar daddy to take you there. 
It was a life experience for me.

Delicious food at this hole in the wall. All the comments about its nickname "the choo choo" are dead on. Their neon train sign helped us out of towners find the place a boy are we glad we did. Very affordably priced! My friend and I each had an entree, shared an app, she had a beer and I had a Thai tea and then I'll came in under $25! I even walked away with a nice sized portion I left overs for lunch the next day. The chicken curry was delicious and perfect texture. Peanut sauce is on point. Will return again!

The WORST HAIRCUT in my entire life!!!  Do NOT GO TO JENNIFER or frankly to this Supercuts!!  First off, she is extremely RUDE!!  Doesn't care about the customers at all.  My hair was uneven, left long in some places and way too short in others.  IF YOU CARE ABOUT HOW YOU LOOK AND WANT A DECENT CUT DO NOT GO HERE.

Simple but a very clean restaurant. 
The man at the register was very nice and courteous. An added bonus that so many places forgo. 
I ordered the lamb kebobs that come with basmati rice and grilled tomatoes. 
I was also given some pita bread. 
Also includes a side selection. I chose a side salad with balsamic dressing. I gotta admit the plastic container the salad comes in is a bit cheesy but hey it's lunch.
At $17.89 with a fountain drink it is a bit steep but this is real lamb not some processed meat and filler.

I'm not a cigar aficionado by any means. In fact, I've never even smoked a cigar in my life, in my opinion it's kind of a "guy" thing, but I came to Thompson Cigar this weekend in order to bring my Grandpa here so he could restock his never ending cigar supply. This place is a bit hidden and took a while to find it. Although it's located near Hoover and Hillsborough, it's down a little side street on the left, but there is a sign out on the fence if you look close enough. We arrived around 1:30 on a Saturday, just a half hour before they were set to close, but there were still quite a few people inside looking around and plenty of staff to help. The selection here is huge, one of the biggest cigar shops I've personally ever seen.
