They had a wide variety of different levels of cigars and different brands, as well as options to mix and match in sampler packs. The prices ranged widely from cheap ($3) up to high premium level. They also offer a variety of lighters, cigar cutters and other accessories. Many of the items were on sale, especially if you bought in bulk, they gave a good discount. We had to ask a few of the guys that worked here to help us pick out particular items and they were all very friendly and helpful (and as one of the few female customers who has ever stepped in here before, I will say they were pretty easy on the eyes too hehe. 
As we went to go cash out, they even gave us a discount for having a membership card and they offered my grandpa a veteran's discount as well, which I thought was a nice extra step. I would recommend this to others who are looking to find a wide selection of cigars all under one roof. Keep in mind they are open 6 days a week, but on Saturday only until 2 PM and they are closed on Sundays.

There was no one at the door when we arrived. We waited about 5 minutes before someone helped us; which was not the hostess. No idea where he/she was??? After we were seated we wanted 15 minutes when we left because the waitress had still not bothered to show up at our table!!! I will not be going back!!!

Went for Restaurant Week in January and the food was just so-so.  Maybe that's because it was Restaurant Week, but based on the reviews I really had expected better.  On the up side, it was the site of the first date between me and the love of my life, so that's something.

From all the positive ratings I see around here, I would say maybe my experience was just a fluke... but truth be told, I would have gone lower on my rating if this wasn't a school. I wasn't very satisfied with my haircut, but it's most likely my high expectations that are to blame here.

The student was trying her best, and I appreciate that. When push came to shove, though, my hair was cut at different lengths, my sideburns were left almost untouched, and the back of my hair was cut asymmetrically. I went back home and did my own touch-ups afterwards.

On the up side, the student and I talked about different ways to style my hair (which was fun), and the shampooing was very pleasant.

All in all, I'm probably not coming back... but that's mostly because I prefer paying more for a professional cut than donating my haircut to science.

It's really difficult to work with this group if you have anything with them because they have 40+ min wait times on the phones and their website is limited.  They don't provide tools that you need to manage what you might have and if you need to do a transaction you have to call.  I'm very disappointed in their service.
Nice assortment of menu items. The food is different than anywhere else we've been. It is tasty, presented well and the service is first class. It's one you should experience.

Second time here for brunch so can say the place doesn't disappoint!  We were seated in the bar room by the window over looking the park and the high ceiling added to the Art Deco glam. Service was excellent and food came out fast given how busy it was!

We started with the cheese plate - which had away bigger portion a few years ago, scones - must get these, fruit bowl which is super fresh, and single pancake.  The grits are some of the best I've had and that's with spending 4 years living in the South. The beets were just ok IMO. 

My mushroom omelette was delicious with plump mushrooms and fluffy eggs, tastes like French onion soup as described. Hubby enjoyed his crab Benedict. 

Go here!

Overpriced and Underwhelmed about sums it up for me. $40 for 2 burgers, 2 fries (one order had 3 greasy onion rings that crumbled when touch), and 2 small drinks was much more then I anticipated spending. The cashier was nice but the service slow. The food itself was just okay.  Nothing to rave about. Could have gone to Wendy's for half the price.

Visited this Applebees with a group of co-workers for dinner. I haven't been to any Applebees in forever, mostly due to the same kind of issues we experienced tonight. Service was slow, despite the almost empty restaurant when we arrived. Our server needed constant reminders that we'd like drink refills, or that we would like to order food. Things did improve after mentioning to another server the problems we were having. Still, some of the food arrived to the table cold, I ordered my steak prepared medium and it was cooked well done. I'm glad my employer footed this bill, as I could've prepared a better meal at home.

Taco Bell.......... What do you expect??

Stopped by to get some late night tacos. I was only the second car in line, so it didn't seem all that busy. Ordered 2 party packs and was told to pull into the parking lot to wait for the order. Didn't mind since I know it's 24 tacos in all, but should be fairly easy to assemble. Waited a good 20 minutes for it to be done. The worker was fairly nice, but did not say or ask for much and was fairly quick. Gave me my tacos which I checked to make sure I have all 24, and I did, but was given a small amount of taco sauce to suit each taco. Didn't feel like driving around to ask for more, so I went home. Tacos were made very skimpy with very little meat which were probably half filled with the cheese and lettuce combined. Come to find out, they were made like that because they ran out of ground meat because half of my other tacos were made with chicken! I just find it funny they had to do that and not tell me about it. Got me to realize why the worker was very quick to give me my order.. I am thankful, I got my tacos, but definitely would have like to have known that they were made with chicken..

This is one of those places that has somehow escaped my radar, yet Yelp! came to the rescue once again.

When I first walked in I have to admit I was preparing myself for a bad experience.  I didn't realize it had taken over an old O'Charlies location, so to see what looked like a large chain restaurant environment didn't bode well to me.  Then I opened the menu....Mole's? Tacos with chicharrone, al pastor, etc, etc.?  Hmmm.  OK, not your standard tex/mex fare.  But still concerned.

Then the food arrived.  Rustic food (a good thing), but prepared and presented with a class above my expectations.  Fine.  But still concerned.  First bite? All concerns obliterated.  WTF?  Where's this place been hiding?  This place is nowhere close to me, but you can bet your sweet culo I'll be back.

p.s. - lunch for 2, including non-alcoholic drinks was  $20  even

These grounds are very tranquil and beautiful the temple beautiful open to he public. 

These a ton of picnic tables and they also serve food here I did not eat here we arrived to late.


There's a entrance to the Hillsborough river you can drive up with your boat or just seat an take in the view

Have been here twice now. First experience was fine, would have rated it 4 stars, but last night's was poor service, very poor. So - am not sure what to make of it. I love the decor, the authenticity, and the flavor of the food (sushi and other items). I love that it's quiet. There is no music playing, which is almost impossible to find in a restaurant these days. The sushi bar is really cute, the owner/chef works away steadily and happily and that's where my love and reverence ends. 

There are two waitresses, one who seems to just bring out food, and was silent and the other (who was our server both times) is clearly very new to her profession. Last night, we went with friends. I ordered two sushi rolls (vegetable and the shiitake mushroom) and they ordered chicken teriyaki, salmon teriyaki and ramen. My husband and I also shared the veggie gyoza and I had a cucumber salad as appetizer. Got the cucumber salad within about 10 minutes, and my sushi in about 20 minutes. Didn't start eating right away because I wanted to wait for others to get their food, and figured that would be 5 or 10 minutes. Time passed, more time passed. After about fifteen more minutes (because I was hungry) I slowly ate the sushi. Ten minutes later, the veggie gyoza arrives. Naturally, my husband (who is very hungry by now) and I share it. Over a half hour (more) passes before finally get the rest of the food. 

Our waitress did not come to check on us once during this time, except for delivery of the food, which was dropped off without a word by waitress (deliverer?) #1. No refills on our green tea, no apology for how long it was taking - and the restaurant has give other tables full. Five.

About 45 minutes into this debacle, manage to flag down our waitress, "we've been waiting an hour, where's our food?" She said - let me check. She comes back five minutes later -- and it's not a long walk from the kitchen - and says "they're preparing it now." Fifteen minutes later we ask again. She goes into the kitchen, comes back five minutes later and says, as she's walking by, "they're about halfway through." There was zero apology, no attention to the fact that this is not normal, nor any attention to us at all. I understand lack of training in waitressing, but it seems like common sense to APOLOGIZE when customers have been waiting a really long time. The food finally comes out, literally over an hour after it was ordered, again no ability to acknowledge the problem. When I ask for more green tea she gets snippy, but finally brought a pot out in some sort of act of conciliation, I guess. Needless to say, we couldn't leave a tip. It was just too absurd. The food is delicious, but that level of bad service makes it hard to return.
Had a wonderful lunch. Sabrina stopped by our table to say Hi. The key lime dessert with oatmeal cookie crust was fantastic.
Best non-touristy dive bar within a very touristy area. Great Sazeracs, friendly staff. Definitely stop by when in the French Quarter to get away from the hustle and bustle.

Nice atmosphere. Moderately slow service. The chow fun is delicious, though the meat isn't very good quality. A bit tough and rubbery. The broccoli beef was bad. The lemon chicken was okay. I suggest the chow fun.

I was here, for the first and last time, about 2 weeks ago (5/29). I have thought long and hard and agonized about writing this review.   I am a small business owner and realize that feedback is very important so I am unhappy to post a bad review which could harm a business.  Posting a poor review should be a second (not first) step.  I prefer to contact a business via email or phone first so that they have an opportunity to hear about my experience with them which gives them a chance to mediate or explain.  Unfortunately this company's website is not an English based site so finding an email is difficult (if not impossible).   I understand and fully support cultural diversity but since they are doing business within the USA there should be a language option.  Now that my motivation is clear here is my review - 
I entered the restaurant with only about a 1/2 hour to eat and then had to leave for an appointment.  The restaurant had very few patrons and was, essentially, mostly empty.   The young lady behind the counter was courteous but less interested in taking care of a customer than she was with what was on her cell phone.  At 4:14 pm I ordered a small chicken meal, paid, and was told to wait.  I waited patiently for more than 20 min with no indication that my order was ready (or even being prepared).   During this time there was one pickup of an order that was either phoned in or ordered via an app.  I say this because the excessive time to prepare and complete my order wasn't caused by high volume.   Through the parted curtains leading to the kitchen I saw several guys talking and joking but didn't see them preparing any product.  After I waited patiently for almost a 1/2 hour I inquired about my order.  The counter person went into the kitchen, asked a few questions, then came out and told me it would be about 10 minutes more. I got the feeling that her talk with the kitchen staff was basically that they'd not even put my order in yet.   I told her to make the order to go because I couldn't wait any longer and that I was rather upset.   It took another 10 minutes for my order to come out and I told her to put it into a container... which she did... I was handed my meal with no apologies... and I left.   To be fair, the product was good.  It was hot, crispy and tasty, however, almost an hour for 6 pieces of fried chicken in a business that isn't incredibly busy is utterly ridiculous. I am a regular at many of the Chinatown establishments but can't recommend this one and I will NOT return.

Literally the worst McDonald's I've been too. My chicken nuggets and chicken snap wrap were hard as rocks being left in the fryer too long, all the workers are rude as hell and I was the only car in line of the drive thru. All the workers were standing around laughing + joking with each other like hello..... just so frustrating. I understand it's a job and like many others it has its stressors and can be busy but you weren't busy... at all.. terrible terrible terribly.

This is different. I don't think Hilton has it right. Looking for hip crowd. Parents with little kids, my age group (60s) in abundance. But it didn't live up to my expectations. 4 day/5 night starting Feb. 19. The rooms are small. We got quite good at moving to get by each other, reaching into cubby holes for things. If sitting on beds, knees touch. Beds are great - comfortable and not too high or law. Choice of pillows. Possibly the stupidous things is have unmarked outlets on a switch which lead to the clock to be wrong. Stupid #2 - can't reset clock; maintenance has to be called! Bright side - Ray the maintenance guy is a real gem. So the second day, housekeeping didn't touch the room. Called front desk, some new policy? No just error. Next day beds made, trash emptied, floors untouched. Fourth day, room again untouched. Okay, it's new, BUT opened in December. Isn't that time enough to get organized?? Shares with suites hotel down the hall. Shares staff, laundry, etc. Can eat breakfast  on either or both sides! Maybe that has something to do with problems. Tru has no portico. Arrived in downpour. Use the other sides portico - works great but further to room. Upshot - if the rate was significantly lower than others, I'd use a Tru again. But cancelled the reservation at the next destination and stayed elsewhere. Make up your own mind, try it or skip it - maybe they'll get it together. Hotel Impossible TV host stressed checklists. Hope verifying time is an item!

John was very responsive, interested in obtaining the sale and truly understood our moving needs. Martin and Arnold were extremely professional, efficient and took great care of our items. HIGHLY recommend! VERY competitive pricing with "no hidden fees."

Unfortunately I was not impressed with this place.  Maybe it's because I've had tapas in Spain and several other cities in the US but the tapas were heavy, overcooked and two of the dishes we ordered had different ingredients than stated on the menu. The beef with green peppercorn sauce had no green peppercorns and a few items were missing from the rabbit dish.  The Pulpo (Octopus) was prepared well and tender but was so overpowered by the heavy handed salt and smoked paprika that we couldn't eat it. 

This is an example of a place with too many things on a menu so they really cant excel at anything.  The sangria was the only redeeming thing we had here.

We've been to Kavanaugh's twice since they opened. The first visit was shortly after their opening and we were disappointed during that visit with both the food and the service. But in an effort to give them a fair shot we wanted to try them again now that they have been open a while. We chose St. Patrick's Day (today) to go for lunch. We figured, you are going to get the "best of the best" of an Irish restaurant on St. Patricks Day right? No. I will say that the decor of the restaurant is wonderfully done. And the staff really did it up with a Kid's corner (coloring and art projects, etc) and Mardi Gras beads to hand out. And everyone was very festively dressed head to toe in green. 

But the tables were so crammed together that once you were seated you literally could not leave your table unless other people stood up from their chairs to let you get by. 

I know they were probably planning on a big crowd and so limited their menu to 4 selections. And the kids menu was either PB&J or ham/cheese with a bag of chips, a Capri Sun juice box and a Chips Ahoy cookie. For $5.50 each. - Which I thought was steep for what it was. Done up either on old/stale bread or the cheapest of the cheap bread available.

I ordered fish and chips. My fish was just OK and there were no chips just regular frozen/deep fried french fries. And for $8 I felt like the small piece of fish I received was not a good value. 

My husband ordered corned beef and cabbage. The corned beef appeared to be sliced deli lunch counter corned beef not the real corned beef brisket you slow cook for hours with savory spiced cabbage and maybe a carrot or two. The corned beef was dry as a bone and in crumbles. I needed a spoon to scoop it up. The cabbage was tasteless and also dry. Again not a good value for $8.

The adult entrees were served in paper baskets with plastic utensils in a plastic wrapper (like you'd get at a picnic). I'd have prefered real silverware and plates. I am sure again due to the crowds they were expecting they must have been trying to keep their clean up easy. But this just did not sit well with me.

My other two older children decided that nothing on the limited menu was anything they were interested so we ordered a SINGLE side of french fries for them to split to tied them over. The server brought out a double order and charged us $8. When I said that seemed like a high price for french fries the server did go back to the manager who corrected the price to just under $4.

I am sorry to say that for me it is two strikes and you are out. This is the last time I will visit Kavanaughs. I wished I had a better experience. I hope that they will seriously consider learning how to cook. I want small local businesses in Mt. Juliet to survive and thrive but they have to put out a product that is worth my money.

Good food, friendly and helpful staff, excellent beer selection on draft.  I had the gumbo, yummy and spicy, but not so spicy as to overpower the other flavors.  Nice location down towards the river, there's enough people around to be lively and fun street scene, but not the mobs of Bourbon St.  Atmosphere is dive-y friendly and comfortable, noise level is normal for a dive bar.  Music is fairly loud, but you don't have to yell to have a conversation.  It was all together a fun place to spend time with friends.
I'm CJ STAGGS  i'm NOT affiliated with this company but I highly recommend them. Best prices and services in hillsboro county.

I'm going to keep this short and to the point. The food here is excellent. Everything taste, portion size, presentation excellent.  The customer service was polite,and attentive, but not annoying. One of my biggest gripes when going to Caribbean or West Indian restaurants is the poor customer service and rudeness that I receive. 48th st Grille's staff was friendly and professional from start to finish. The prices are reasonable for the quality of food that your getting. I strongly recommend giving 48th Grille a chance.

Ps. Can't remember the exact names of what we had in the pictures attached. One was a salmon dish the other was a tilapia dish. I'm sure they can tell you if you show them the pictures.

Omg. Excellent brisket tacos!  Everything is freshly made and you can tell. 10 Stars!
The people who work here are super nice!

If I could rate this place any lower, I would. This business is listed on GrubHub, so I ordered through them. I picked out some dishes/appetizers that seemed appealing and fairly hard to mess up. I got a call from the business saying they didn't have half of the things I ordered. I ordered at 2:10am when the website listed they take orders until 4am. My account was charged $34 for food I never received and was treated disgustingly by the person who was somehow allowed to answer the phone. They spoke to me harshly and told me in a quite rude way, "this is a day time problem, call back in day time."  Excuse me for being concerned that my account was charged and I did not receive what I paid for. Avoid this place at all costs. Horrible customer service. I have never been treated this way by any member of the service industry in my life. This place ought to be shut down as it is a sham of a business. Everyone knows customer service should come first. Shame on Mama Rosas.

A solid 3.5. App was beet shrimp salad. Very very good. But I LOVE beets. Husband was ok with it. He had blackened sea bass was "very good" and tasted better than our favorite La Stalla. I had the the chicken Marsala. It was what one would expect. Nothing great but not bad either. Nothing to stand out of the Italian crowd. All in all, pretty decent

Worst service ever, party of 13, waiting 2.5 hours.... Still no food...still sitting here....hungry.
Never come here!

They were not even apologetic :(

I was in last evening for my first time at this establishment, and I must say that I was very impressed from the staff, ingredients, proper Preparation, Very skilled chefs and I'll be back probably one of the best meals I've had in a very long time. Very very good I recommend you come here

I've been on a 20 year quest for authentic jerk in the Tampa Bay area and sadly my quest continues. I should preface this review by saying that I spent nearly half my life in the Caribbean, and as such am familiar with many of the cuisines, especially Jamaican and jerk. 

I decided on a whim to drop in on a weekday around 5:30 or so. The place was pretty empty. Just me and two other couples in a pretty good-sized dining room. Upon grabbing a seat I immediately noticed how sticky the table was. Come to think of it, so was the floor. I'm not sure why the staff didn't notice this, but it doesn't make for a good impression. 

Stickiness aside, I decided to go with the most common and popular dish in any jerk restaurant - jerk chicken with a double order of rice and peas (you get two sides with each entree). It's not a good sign of authenticity when you're served whole pieces of chicken. True jerk is hacked into chunks (usually by a meat cleaver-wielding Jamaican), but whatever, this is a common occurrence here in Tampa Bay. The first bite revealed the chicken to be under-seasoned. This is a major no-no for me. Jerk is not subtle. It is supposed to jump out at you and slap you in the face. And to add insult to injury, there was very little meat to be found on these chicken pieces. The rice and peas was on the dry side, so much so that I left some behind. I'm a lover of all things rice and beans/peas. I never leave rice and beans/peas on my plate. 

The best thing about my outing was that I discovered a new love - alcoholic ginger beer in the form of Royal Jamaican Ginger Beer. This is the real deal! Made with real ginger with a little alcoholic kick to it. I ordered two and promptly drove to my local liquor store and bought more.

In closing, if you're already familiar with jerk cuisine and looking for authentic Jamaican fare, you're probably going to be disappointed. If you're not so familiar with jerk, then this might suffice as it seems their target market is the "jerk newbie", so to speak.
Great Mexican food.  It is always busy but worth the wait.  Sangria margaritas are a must have.

The food was great. The staff didn't honor Happy Hour. What was supposed to be $1 was almost $3. What was supposed to be $2 was almost $5. The staff was very helpful up until we asked to order off the Happy Hour menu.  The cashier said she was unable and unwilling to help us. We left and went across the street to a company that honored their menu prices.

Having been coming for a few years and still love it. The owners work really hard and put everything in to this place and shows in the consistently good food they serve. I often bring friend and colleagues and all enjoy. Can't go wrong in my opinion. Just remember- cash only - pain but there you go.

I was once a huge fan of shake shack. 

Then it seems like everything went down hill. 

The burgers became really greasy and it seems Like they are pushing them out too quickly as they have been way underdone. 

The fries are still good especially with the cheese sauce. 

I was never a fan of the shakes so I won't comment on them.
Great pizza! Friendly staff. Nice environment. Wish they had chicken wings. We will be back for more pizza and to try other items.

Holy amazeballs. Boyfriend got the buffalo chicken sandwich and I got a burger and we both left so full and satisfied. The portions were huge and the price more than reasonable. Our server was super friendly and attentive. She was training a new girl and I judge people a lot by how they treat those "beneath them" in a business setting. Even when I saw them away from tables, she was patient and nice and they both were so charming. I will go back as much as possible. Definitely my new burger place.

Went their for the first time. I order the steak and egg and oh boy it was bad. I order it medium rare got a cold over cooked steak that was of the lowest quality possible. You get eggs with no bread.  The home fries were just ok. Oh and that was after a 45 min wait time. The owner was nice she did not make us pay for the food. We tip the server and left hungry...

We stayed here during spring break 2016 and were very disappointed in the actual room. Clearly, there were attempts made to update the room but it still felt very antiquated. Our microfridge broke and was replaced, the shower backed up after two showers, and the toilet broke our second day there. Sofa bed was a joke- huge divot in the middle. The breakfast buffet was terribly overpriced at $18.95 per person for eggs. The pool was not overcrowded but it did not have a ton of area to walk around. Just lounger after lounger with a race that begins at 7am to get a decent spot. There are also no towel hooks, bars at ALL to hang bath towels in the room.  There is a drying line in the shower but it can't hold enough towels for a suite full of guests. I ended up buying command hooks. The elevator was SLOW AND OF THE 3 one was broken down. Best things were the polite and attentive staff, location, and kind housekeeping staff. For the $$ hugely overpriced even for spring break

After the plumbing company accidentally flooded our kitchen they sent Simple Solutions. Started out professional then it all went wrong. Were told they have one"floor" guy to put down replacement floor and took over a month to put our floor down. End result we now have a hole like dip in floor and places where planks don't even touch. They sent him back to fix first plank we saw sticking up but after time more planks have moved and sank. We no longer have faith in their work and don't care to have them back. So now stuck with this horrible flooring job

Food arrived ice cold. 
Chicken park is from chicken fingers.  
Awful.  This place really went down hill

Extremely good coffee beverages in a large, comfortable setting with plenty of places to set up with a laptop, etc. In my experience, some of the best espresso in town.  They also sell pastries (see photo of Kouign Amann) from the esteemed, nearby. Possibly the best straight-up coffee shop in town, as it happens.

Long waits, recooked food from previous days (jerk wings to be specific...) they use old leftover cooked wings. Bland flavor, nasty interior. This place needs help, Save yourself the trouble and just to the other Jamaican restaurant down the street! Better flavors & Better Service!

Long ago, I had one of their burritos and was not terribly impressed.  Then, on a recent weekend I was back here with a friend who wanted a burrito, so I figured I'd get one, too.  

There is a large selection of burritos to try, both meat and vegetarian.  You can eat in -- at the bar or a table -- or get it to go.  I got a fajita burrito in a spinach tortilla for eating in nearby Rittenhouse.  It was tasty, with a good balance of meat, veggies, rice, beans, and sauce; the wrap was heated to have a nice hint of crunch.

The orders were cooked pretty quickly.  The bar tenders were friendly.  Prices were reasonable (about $8 for a burrito).

We thought the place across the street looked much better once we were actually inside here.

Outside looks like a classy place. Inside has a confusing decor of cross funeral markers and random paintings, with a somewhat awkward layout. 

$7 for a vodka and tonic. Meh music.
Really liked it. Hidden. Basement entrance. Great strawberry cider. Nice low key vibe. Really comfortable couches. Will go back. Make it an evening, with several other bars at this corner.
Amazing breakfast.  The breakfast burrito and huevos rancheros are a must try. Great service and a fun atmosphere.

This is a solid choice for soup and a sandwich downtown. They are super friendly and the food comes out pretty quickly even during the lunch rush. I had the Cuban sandwich and a cup of the beef and Guinness soup yesterday. The soup was stellar and the Cuban sandwich was good, but not the best I've had in Indianapolis. I'll definitely be back to try another soup and sandwich combo.

This was a great dinner experience.  We started in the front bar for cocktails about an hour before our reservation.  It was a really cool atmosphere with table games and a table top arcade.  The bartender was very nice and the drinks were great.  Our experience in the kitchen was even better.  Each course had an enormous amount of flavor and the description of each dish by the chefs added to the experience.  It's almost like you have your own personal chef and bartender in the back.  If you're not full when you leave grab some nachos from the front bar and that will seal the deal.

Cute place!  Picked up some souvenirs for friends and family to take home from New Orleans.  Loved the stuff here because it was more local and handmade items that were special which was definitely more of the vibe I got from New Orleans than the trinket shops that just sold beads and whatnot.

Visited Manhattan Nails on January 24, 2021 for 2 pedis.  In addition to having to wait about 20 minutes for a tech to service us after previously scheduling a Noon appointment, the one tech (an older lady) did a TERRIBLE job.  She didn't even pick up a file for my nails (I had to ask her if she could file the corners down).  And on top of all this, I witnessed her grab tools from her cart (not in a baggy), spray them down with solution from a spray bottle, wipe the tools off with a towel & begin using them on me.  This was not my 1st visit to Manhattan Nails, but definitely will NOT return.
This food has no flavor it's like they took most of it out just to be appealing to people who don't understand real Jamaican cuisine. Taste like they use a pinch of seasoning just no

You'll probably miss Mike's unless you know where it is since its hidden by a Checkers. A Checkers with a dining area, mind you, that may occupy your thought process for the moment - I didn't know Checker's had dining areas. But once you get past that, both mentally and physically, you can get to Mike's.

Mike's is a dive-y pizza, sandwich, Italian joint usually filled with an odd mix of blue collar, white collar and police collars all enjoying lunch. They usually have a few specials of the day, nothing more than $7 for usually a few slices or something new with a side salad, garlic knots and pasta.

Flavor-wise Mike's isn't the best of anything - pizza, subs, calzones, stromboli, etc.. But the slices are large, the service fast and again you're getting out with less than $10. They also have Bubba's Buffalo Chicken Dip pizza, which is a stand out (although it also has mushrooms, that I spend a good 5 minutes picking off).

To any BTLS Fans: Mike's has tubs of Bubba's Buffalo Chicken Dip for sale.

Note: if you're a cute blond woman, chances are you may be given a free brownie (which in turn will be given to a male co-worker back at the office).
Poor service and bad prices. I found the whole experience rushed and the prescription they gave me hurt my eyes. This place reeks of the kind of greed that flows from a large pile of student loans.

I had pretty high expectations going into my dinner at Cochon last night, it's been getting so much praise. And it was a good dinner, don't get me wrong. if you like french food (heavy heavy HEAVY) you will like Cochon. But a couple aspects of the dinner just bugged me all night, and that combined with a hefty price tag has left me with 3 stars for this BYO. I'll just run through the dinner...

Before we even ordered, the first disappointment happened: no specials. I can't even remember the last time I went to any restaurant that didn't have SOME special. I'm sure this is not the norm at Cochon, but we were pretty unhappy, especially because we heard they had very creative specials.

Apps: I had quail stuffed with foie gras, she had rabbit ragu on some pasta with a fancy name that I can't remember (on some level, isn't it all just pasta? Where do all these weird names come from...) My quail was very good, cooked well, quite tasty. I'm not even a big foie gras fan, but this was goooood. The rabbit ragu went over well, but we totally had the exact same dish at James not too long ago. Not sure whether chicken or egg came first on that one.

Main course: Probably the biggest stumble of the night. I had 36-hour short ribs. I fancy myself a bit of a rib connoisseur, so I was excited. These were most definitely subpar. I mean, not bad ribs I guess, but they were not very tender, certainly not 36 hour tender. I can make ribs more tender than this in 6 hours on my Weber in my back yard. I also had some 36 hour short ribs at Daniel Boulud's restaurant in Vegas not horribly long ago, and they were 1000 times better. My fiancee has the pot-pie of the day which was made with boar. I think more than anything this was just a poor choice for her, not that it wasn't necessarily made well. The boar was quite gamey, a little too much for her. The pot pie was also steaming hot for like 15 minutes, which made it kind of hard to eat. The whole main course was just "meh." 

Dessert: Best part of dinner. I had an apple-cinnamon bread pudding which was awesome, and she had creme brulee which was also incredible. A nice rebound after a subpar meal.

Overall, I don't know ... maybe my expectations were too high. I think if this meal hadn't cost 100 bucks, it would've definitely been 4 stars, but the steep price tag is forcing my hand on the 3 stars.

The food here is always good. In fact it is so good that there are usually long wait lines. They have a great 10 great breakfast meals under $10 that are perfect for a budget. Great worksheets for young children as well as a nice food selection for kids.

My friends and I were visiting New Hope for the day and we came across this place. We have had Indian food before but this place just blew us away. The owner was so friendly and greeted us with such a smile. We got the onion bhaji as and appitizer and it was delicious. As a compliment he brought out this rice nut dish. Im not sure what it was called but it was fantastic. Something nice to nibble on while you waited for food. We had the chicken and the shrimp tikka masala. This was amazing. I wanted to lick my bowl of the sauce. And the great thing was he brought us as much rice and we needed, which by the was was delicious by itself. Ive been to more expensive places and this place is just as good and cost less and I got a lot more for my money. This was better serive than other places I've been. I would 100% recommend this place. I would go back to New Hope just to eat there.

If I could give this company less than one star (or negative 5 stars) I would.  Joe Cool called me for my $39.00 spring service (they do the spring and fall maintenance) and I scheduled the appt.  My unit was working fine prior to them coming out to service it.  The tech tried high pressure tactics to sell me a new unit when he arrived for the service,  and I refused.  A few days after the spring maintenance service, the house started getting warm and wasn't cooling properly, and a few days thereafter the unit froze up in the attic and the water from the thawing unit caused a ton of damage to my son's bedroom below.  I called a different company to fix the issue (because I have a home warranty plan and used their a/c service contractor for the repair) and the tech said the unit froze because the valves were left loose when the recent maintenance was performed by Joe Cool which caused the R410 to leak out and the unit to freeze.  The company that fixed the frozen unit and added R140 and noted on their invoice that the issue was caused by the loose valve caps.  I provided copies of the invoice to Joe Cool, along with photo of the highly damaged bedroom ceiling (located below the a/c unit in the attic) the damaged walls, and the damaged mattress, and they have refused to pay anything.  Worst company ever, and I am highly suspicious they intentionally caused the R140 to leak out to make me think my unit was broken and sell me a new unit.  I am a single mother, and this company took advantage of me and cannot be trusted.

I used to go here all the time for family dinners and Sunday morning dim sum. The food was always delicious and I loved that you could choose between authentic and westernized Chinese food. One this that has always been a problem was the staff. They always rush out like REALLY REALLY bad. The worst experience though was the last and final time my husband and I went here about two or three years ago. There was a fly in my husband's rice. He pointed it out to the waitress who said it was not a fly then called another waitress over who told us it was obviously a peppercorn. We pointed out the wings then she stormed back to the kitchen with it. She returned less than a minute later with a terribly plated dish and did not say a word. My husband went to take a bite and to no surprise saw a fly in his spoonful... And two more in the mound of rice. They said we didn't have to pay for my husband's dish but demanded I pay for mine despite me having taken only a couple of bites then leaving it behind in fear of all the flies... I tell everyone who bringa this place up about it. I'd feel terrible if someone wasn't so thorough and actually ate a mouthful of flies!

This was a really neat experience I love hard cider so it was right up my alley. I couldn't believe with every booth being mead or cider how different they all tasted and how many flavors they had. I absolutely love la Margherita and they had a good truck at this event!! Definitely made me happy we also tried the pierogi love buffalo chicken and it was ok my mom liked it a lot more than I did. One thing I was really looking forward to to get me in the fall/ Halloween spirit was the tarot card and palm readings but unfortunately they didn't show up to the event. Kind of a bummer. Overall we had a great time the samples of cider were large and lots of options food was good and the cute souvenir glass was great.

Papa John's cured my constipation... Oh yeah, I wasn't constipated but it sent me to the bathroom anyway. I can't eat it. My wife can't eat it. Better ingredients?  Is laxative an ingredient? If it is, then it's premium stuff I'll tell you that. Really, when I first had Papa Johns in the early 90's I thought it was pretty good for delivery pizza. At least better than Domino's (back then) but it seems the bigger "papa" got, the worse he got. I'll never buy it again. My colon needs a break.

I enjoyed my dinner at Luke.

Our table of eight shared the chicken and rabbit pate, mussels, salad, and foie gras. Everything except for the mussels were great. I have to remind myself to avoid molluscs in New Orleans, they really do not agree with me.

For mains, I had the shrimp and grits and discovered that I love grits! Although the size was on the smaller size for the American and NOLA palette, it was perfect for me. 

From what I heard, the chicken and duck confit were wonderful as well, but the fish entree and the fries with the mussels were salty.

Overall, the meal was a little pricey for the ambience and serving size. Service was good and timing, for New Orleans was almost fast. (So average speed for any other city.)

I would visit again, and would order any of the appetizers, cocktails, and would ask them to go easy on the salt on the mains.

Tried the Hawaiian Classic- really enjoyed the fresh vegetables and taste. They do have a choice of brown rice or white rice but the ingredients cannot be substituted. It was little hectic and chaotic there as sometimes the servers would take orders from people in line and then switch up to taking orders from people who order d online which made the wait bit confusing. The bowl itself was delicious and I would recommend them.

This is my favorite place to get delicious food. I ordered at 8 pm on a Friday night last week and I expected to wait an hour like I have before with other pizza places but it came just within 25 minutes. The delivery boy (he drove a red car didn't get his name) was really courteous and one of the sweetest boys I've met in his generation. This is now my go to food place and I can't wait to order again and try their famous calzones and I will make sure to get extra cannolis this time for my kids- yum!!

Came for Christmas set prix dinner menu. They forgot a dish. Duck was cooked to a cinder, salad was excellent, carrot cake just ok, fried oysters were lovely. Excellent atmosphere and service. We sat at the bar. A  decent time.

Every now and again, I'll place a delivery order with La Scala's Pronto. It's not too often because I'd rather be sitting at a restaurant enjoying a nice meal for the price they charge. I can say, however, that whenever I do order from them, I'm almost always guaranteed a great, hearty, well-crafted meal.

My most-ordered dish has been the chicken and spinach cannelloni. At $14, it's certainly a splurge for delivery, but it comes hot in a strong microwavable container -- filled with gooey cheese, smooth sauce, cooked spinach and an ideal mixture of chicken bits.

La Scala's also offers stellar Italian hoagies (comes on a fresh seeded roll) and chicken fingers. 

Most recently, I ordered the caesar salad topped with breaded chicken (I subbed grilled for breaded and there was no upcharge). I loved, loved, loved the creamy dressing -- and it was even better that they provided a fair amount for the massive salad size. I will be ordering this again, no doubt!

Delivery is generally fast. I had to run down two flights of steps the other day because they were 20 minutes earlier than GrubHub's estimate. I'd count that as a positive!

Basically: Top-tier for delivery on couch-bum nights, but eating at a restaurant often wins.

The best salads ever...large portions with fresh, delicious veggies. Their chef salad with Albacore tuna is my favorite. I always add an avocado to it. Their fresh fruit and pasta salads are amazing as well. Love them!

AJ was very Insightful on the food menu and drink menu. He was the highlight of our entire trip that we spent in New Orleans. He was very knowledgeable on the drink menu and recommended us the Blueberry Hill. Let me tell you, BEST DRINK ON THE MENU. if you find yourself in this amazing bar, ask for AJ!!

This place deserves 5 starts for sure! It was late in the night and we didn't know where to go because all places were already closing so we found Noble Crust which was 10 minute drive from our hotel and we got surprised. The ambience was so cool, the pizza was so delicious and the server was so helpful, dedicated and happy. I had the mushroom pizza and the marguerita, and they were perfect.

I use this laundromat every two weeks. I typically need 4-5 washers and 2-3 dryers, and have never once had to wait for either. The prices are very reasonable compared to what you would pay at a full-service laundry. I use their in-house wash-dry-fold service for my cotton shirts because they are so meticulous about folding that my shirts don't need ironing. They also offer drop-off service for laundry and dry cleaning and both services are fast and excellent. If every business was run with the integrity that Gloria and Wilburt put into this business, the world would be a lot nicer place...

And did I mention that detergent, bleach and fabric softener are all FREE?

I met my friend for breakfast this morning at Los Altos Breakfast Lunch & Dinner and it was delicious. We arrived at 9am. No reservations needed, it was slightly busy but not crowded. Inside is very bright and clean. When I walked in the first thing I smelled was chorizo and it got my tummy grumbling.

I was pretty hungry so it was very hard to decide what to choose. The menu includes most of the breakfast classics like French toast and Waffles and a couple of skillets as well as Eggs Benedicts. All of my favorite breakfast options were available so I had to decide my meal based on what I could just have at home. I decided the biscuits and gravy were gonna be my meal. The biscuits and gravy come with: eggs, choice of meat and choice of starch. I chose bacon and hash browns along with scrambled eggs. For my beverage I had black coffee and water. The coffee was Farmer Brothers. I've been asking who the coffee roaster is when I eat out because I love to hear when it's a local company. Farmer Brothers is not bad by any means and may be more cost effective for them to use.  I just like the warm feels I get when local helps local. I like Blind Dog and Wood Fire Roasters. The cup given was very large and also for sale at the counter. I may just get one next time. 

My food was delicious as stated before. The biscuits were very cake like and held the gravy well. Breakfast gravy is easy to mess up. If the pan is too hot you get a scalded milk flavor. If you don't mix it just right it's clumpy. This gravy was terrific. It was flavored perfectly, did not taste milky and did not taste like flour.  My scrambled eggs were cooked just like I like them and had a light and fluffy texture. The bacon was crispy and my hash browns were golden brown. 

The service staff was polite and efficient. We didn't have any issues on this visit. I am already planning my return visit with my husband.
I was there 1/26/13. My bartender (dark hair with glasses) was amazing and made a great drink. Food was delicious. Service was good. Overall feel was excellent. Great night out in Nashville.

Would have bumped this one, maybe two, stars if they had put me in the room type I requested (non-smoking 2 queens for family of 4).  Instead they put me in a single-king which smelled like it had the same amount of leftover cigarette smoke in that one room as the whole casino had downstairs.  It was pretty gross smelling, and that's considering I have a terrible sense of smell, plus lived with a couple smokers without issue.  But my wife and daughter hated it, and let me know it...not that I could do anything about it.  Also, the shower was pretty pathetic...meager water pressure when set on the narrowest spray.

Good things were the view from the 26th floor and the connections to the other two hotels, especially Circus Circus, where the kids spent a lot of time with their friends.

The food was so-so.  Compared to Vegas buffets, the buffet at SL was lacking, but still not terrible.  They had plenty of selection, and the price was OK for a buffet.  The restaurants we ate at had decent food which wasn't as outrageously priced as I feared it might be.

Parking was an absolute nightmare, but I think that's the peril of staying at 
a large casino over a weekend.  I could have opted for the valet.

Oh yeah, I know big casinos now charge a mandatory resort fee (what a scam -- if it's mandatory, don't call it a fee, just bake it into the room price, but whatever).  But the Wi-Fi that comes with it is for only a single device. WTF is with that?

Use to really love this place! The food was great and they have interesting options. However, the last couple of times the same items have been different (smaller in size from $11 dinner to what looks like half an appetizer, cold, unseasoned) and also an instance where I ordered a wrap dinner and received... just a wrap. Not sure what's going on but I love supporting local business and they're a staple. Hope something changes, would love to eventually return!

I don't give the Hollywood Grill enough credit. It's an incredibly reliable diner with some of the better breakfasts in town and a full bar. What's not to like?

Well...the ambiance, for one. Hollywood Diner feels exactly like it is: a former Howard Johnson's. Posters of movie stars are nice, but they don't make the place feel any less generic. And dining at peak hours means a long wait and lotsa noise.

But if you want good, solid diner food (and that harried-but-friendly service unique to larger diners), you can't go wrong here. Breakfasts are yummy and huge...I don't know how they make their egg n' ham sandwiches so tasty, but wow. Every lunch sandwich I've had has been totally enjoyable - club sandwiches taste like they should, and if the grilled chicken isn't spectacular, it's certainly big and receptive to mayo. And the fries are big and fat and exactly what I want from a diner. I haven't tried many of the dinners, but there are tons to choose from, and for the most part they look tasty as they are carried past my table.

So it doesn't have a lot of character, and too few of the waitstaff call you "hon." But if you want a solid diner meal with good coffee, you could do a lot worse than Hollywood Grill.

I have been here before and always enjoy the food.  I happened to be looking in an old sauce magazine and saw the shaved duck featured in there and saw a picture of the sausage sandwich and thought I had to try it.  So I went there last night and tried it and was amazed the complexity of all the flavors of the sandwich.  The sweetness of the dried mango with the spicyness of the sausage was a great combination.  I also always order the house fries because they are my favorite fries of all time......sorry mom.  Hand cut and cooked to perfection.  I wonder what the fries would taste like with a light seasoning of the dry rub they use on the meat.   I asked for the chefs name and have to say chef kat has her act together.  Kudos to holly, the waitress that works there too.  She is always very friendly and knowledgable.  I highly recommend this place who wants a great dining experience.  Don't forget desert.  The brownie is awesome and the peanut butter pie is pretty terrific too.  Make sure to order it with the chocolate sauce.
Awesome!!!! Brunch is my favorite. They nail it here!!! Coffee and desserts are also delicious and decadent! Definitely a place to visit!
Cool atmosphere, good food. Wasn't much for vegans, but wasn't a big deal, vegans are used to having to eat fries. I personally loved the pretzel and dips!

Worked with Craig Mutchnick after a huge tree fell on the house. 3 months later we still are negotiating with the insurance company. He did not order the appraisal when he said he did, and I cannot honestly say that I feel he was on my side throughout the transaction. It felt like he just took my signed contract, called it a day, and waited to make commission on my loss.
Service is amazing!! The trout blew my mind..I don't even like Mexican food..have the trout please

This is the best pizza I've ever had, and I'm a girl who lives on pizza. I had the Old World and added pepperoni. I was nearly brought to tears upon the first bite. Everything was so fresh and the crust was buttery perfection. The beer selection was decent, and the service was quick. Just thinking about how good the pizza was is making me so hungry. I think I'll go here for lunch. And dinner. And every meal for the rest of my life.

Amazing business conference hotel perfectly laid out with exceptional restaurants, shops and located close to all the action.  Service is exceptional and my wife and I would jump at the opportunity to come back.  Well done Omni owners and staff!

I am addicted to hot wok after a friend suggested it. I have gone at least 10 times in the last 3 months. 
The crab wontons are crave worthy, giant golden fried and fluffy triangle cream cheese filled goodness with a hint of crab. 
The teriyaki chicken is 4 pieces of thigh roasted on skewers, enough for two meals and always my go to with white rice and hot chili oil. 
Shrimp Lo mein has honorable mention. Medium sized shrimp, enough to have a piece with almost every bite.  Container is always stuffed to capacity.

I joined Chuze when I moved to the north side of Tucson, and quickly found out how good this gym is. It is a great place to work out and do cardio, since they have the cardio cinema. In January I joined the 3 month challenge in which I won the 1st price for body transformation. All of this was possible with the hard training from the instructor Randy. Randy pushes you to the limit and knows how to encourage you for those final reps. He has taught me discipline and makes working out a constant challenge to better yourself. The training sessions are to the point and make you work hard, which is why are recommend him as a trainer

The service was good...nothing to complain about. Food was okay also. We tried the seafood platter and the crab cakes. It was too much batter. But saw the couple dining next to us having shrimp Po boy ... It looked good. THe waiters were pleasant and checked up on us from time to time.  It was a pleasant lunch. Out :)
Our favorite stop before the Blues game. Amazing smoked wings and pizza to die for.  Love Lacey the bartender. Always so friendly. Highly recommend this place.

The food here was horrible. The wait staff was not horrible but they weren't exactly friendly nor accomadating. The wait was long and the food was not good. We had a large party so we pretty much ordered everything and everyone was completely unsatisfied. The food was extremely overpriced and extremely underwhelmed. I would never eat at the blind pelican ever again.

This is my favorite place to eat out. The owners are attentive and friendly, and the food is outstanding. If you have never eaten Ethiopian cuisine, give it a try. If you love Ethiopian food, you will be happy you came. The restaurant is kid friendly, with a warm and pleasant atmosphere. They offer a formal coffee service. We have also used them to cater a meal for our church. Great prices, seamless pick up, fabulous food. I cannot day enough good things about this place!

Umm...if I could give them negative stars I totally would. Service HORRIBLE. Food HORRIBLE. Management HORRIBLE. Order not right. Waitress not found. Manager finally located, could care less and then went in the back and mocked my accent and mannerisms. Seriously?? Ummm...dumba** I CAN SEE YOU!! AVOID THIS ESTABLISHMENT!!!!

I had never tried Sports Clips before so I decided since I am new to Tampa I would explore some new things.  First thing I want to mention is this, when I walked in the door to this place all three of the girls working turned and simultaneously welcomed me with big smiles on their faces..So I was instantly impressed and knew they cared about their customers.  I only had to wait about 5 minutes for a cut which was also great because I am not high maintenance and I don't like to spend a lot of time at the barbers.  I should also mention, there are flat screens everywhere with sports on, and the magazine selection is completely geared towards men including hunting, fishing, golf and fitness so your wait is entertaining for sure.  I was called for my cut, and before we went in my stylist Robin explained to me that because it was my first time there, I would be upgraded to the top level service which includes a hot towel face steam, scalp massage, and neck and back massage (all of which were amazing! And for the middle price of only $17!).  So onto the haircut...I have to admit I went in assuming I would be getting the regular SuperCuts style haircut where the girls rush through you because they want to get in as many people as they can during their shifts, but this was not the case.  Robin took the time to figure out exactly how I wanted my hair to look, then she assured me that in the future my details would be saved so if you come back and see a different stylist, there is no need to explain what you want because she has that information in the system.  I also want to mention, they use new clipper guides and combs/towels on every client so it is a super clean experience!  Anyways, when my haircut was finished, I was completely satisfied.  Robin was careful to check with me throughout the cut to make sure things were looking exactly how I wanted them, and it resulted in a perfect cut.  I usually have to deal with girls not being able to cut around a cowlick on one side of my head, but this cut came out perfectly even!  I will definitely be going back to this Sports Clips again, and while I will try and continue seeing Robin, I am extremely confident that you will get the same experience from any one of the stylist working there.  Check them out!!

The worst Pizza that I never had! Unfortunately I am banned from a pizza place that I was never able to eat at.  I called in to order a pizza (8:26)  large Chicago style sausage and pepperoni and unfortunately had to call immediately back to cancel the order (8:32)  "I was told it was too late the pizza was already in the oven I could not cancel it" I said I just called it in that was fast, I am a sorry  I cannot make it.  
The Owner "Ron" called me back and left a message to say I am banned bfrom his restaurant in my phone number will be blocked from now on. 
I called him back immediately and asked him to explain why and he said it's a $26 pizza and I just wasted it. How can that be Ron? I called you right back to cancel it and there is no way that that pizza was going to cost you $26 to make. I even said I would happily come in and pay for it, but he said that it doesn't matter I'm banned from a store. .. I will never recommend this restaurant to anyone just because of ownership and staff.
Good beer selection, and that's it. food was extremely bland, cooked wrong, and just plain bad...and overpriced.

I called to get a quote for a set of rims I saw in the flyer for my car, when I talk to to guy in the proper department i'm told that those don't fit my car and the ones that do are $5 more a rim. I'm not to upset. When I call to see if they have a set of tires in stock the associate says something that is muffled and puts me on hold for 10min comes back on the phone and hangs up on me.
I liked it here. My chai latte with oat milk was GREAT. Nice decor too. The main road it's on has tons of restaurants and cool shops to explore. I went on a Sunday morning and it was perfect.

Amazing breakfast in the city with attentive service. Finally, I've gotten the chance to eat at Green Eggs after years of hearing how awesome they are. I also absolutely love how their motto is being environmental especially since I'm trying to be more environmentally conscience. 

The food was awesome and the portions are generous. We absolutely loved the Chicken and Waffles entree we ordered as well as the stuffed waffle that was on their specials menu for the day. Also the dishes are all very photogenic which is a big plus in my book!

Service was also great and we were extremely lucky to have gotten a seat without any wait time! This is definitely a restaurant that I would love the revisit and wouldn't mind doing the wait if I have to.

I have been to Firebirds three times now and every time our experience has been nothing but perfect. The hostesses, the servers, and Tom the manager are so nice and personable, and they truly make my time there enjoyable. The food is amazing every time and the wood fire grill adds that extra flavor that you're looking for. Such a fun environment as well. I would recommend Firebirds to everyone!

Tuesdays Texas Holdem Poker Tour's Llc free poker and food in the way at the bar are really fun and food is good and drinks 
Chicken tenders are good and they're huge prices are unbelievably reasonableAnd the people that run the place are super nice if you get a chance try the Texas Holdem Poker Tour's Llc Tuesday night at 7 PM or Thursday afternoon noon to 4 PM

Owners/proprietors Hemphills' offer fabulous assistance for customers.  Last week had to get several natal day and Mother's Day cards to various obscure addresses.

Also had to mail our grandson a very special teenage gift for his birthday...brought it in [a 2-sided glass frame]..it required special safety packaging.  Bill helped me find the right box and fillings.

Off it went, arrived in NY two days early.

Their staff is also terrific.

Do not expect customer service here. Ever. From the management all the way down they refused to locate the ID & credit card they held at the bar for my tab. You would think after spending the type of money I did for a table for my birthday they would be more accommodating to give me my personal property back. 

It took almost a MONTH for me to get someone there to locate my property & then find someone to open the safe. Because they are only open Thursday-Saturday & refuse to answer voicemails it has been the biggest ordeal.

I am beyond excited that I finally ventured into this place after hearing about it for months. I'm sugar, dairy and gluten free and have been craving sweets for months. This place was a little too amazing. I can see doing some damage here, both financially and to my sugar habit.  I tried a red velvet cupcake and a mint cookie sandwich. They taste gluten free, but that is not a negative thing. I thought the treats were delicious and I was ecstatic to be able to indulge my sweet tooth.

Great atmosphere and views. But that is really the only reason to go. Went a few of months ago in July and had a good time up until the time the hostess came over to our group of 20 and asked if we needed anything else, trying to get us to leave. The waitress was was not happy with the hostess and was very nice to us about the situation. And I get it, they were newer. So we'd figure we'd try them again today, and were very disappointed. The wife's entrée chicken salad was the size of a side salad and the chicken was completely dry. The fish tacos I had were so overly stuffed with everything else but the fish, which was also very dry. Then, the Pina Colada I ordered was halfway filled with chopped up fruit, I thought I ordered a drink, not another meal. All in all, probably won't return, at least not for the food.

Simply amazing food, can't wait to come back. Finally a place for us vegans/vegetarians to flock to and eat beautifully crafted food that isn't the typical one pasta dish on the menu. The service was superb.

Salt roasted gold beets- 5/5
Roasted maitake mushroom-5/5
Braciole- 3/5
Fingerling fries-5/5
Carrots shwarma style- 5/5
Chocolate uber chunk- 5/5 simply amazing if you like peanut butter. *little bit of heaven*

A bit pricey and small portion plates but completely worth it.

Was driving by and saw the signs.  We thought "a brew and a burger?  Hot damn."  Didn't read  the Yelp reviews and wish we had.  I mean do not all brew houses sell burgers?  Apparently no.  This one doesn't.  They have Hawaiian bar b que.  I didn't even know Hawaiians bar b qued.  Oh well we're here so why not eat?  My wife had the wings and I had the bar b que chicken breasts.  Both were so so at best.  Macaroni comes with about everything as does slaw.  Both were so so.  Quite a few people there, but just didn't do it for us.  In addition we had to explain wine to the server.  We won't be going back.

It's places like these that make me appreciate folks who take the time to do Yelp reviews. We wanted to grab breakfast before getting back on the road to California, and we were looking for a cafe.

We went to Peg's, and we saw the line out the door. That's enough to convince us to try a restaurant - along with all the great reviews.

My country fried steak and eggs was the best I've had in quite awhile. My wife said her huevos rancheros skillet was the best breakfast she'd had...period. And portions were quite generous.

Our waiter, Martin, was also naturally enthusiastic and attentive.
The ice cream was underwhelming. Ordered coconut chocolate almond and it was coconut with chocolate chips, did not taste any almonds.

Really delicious Southern breakfast. Cheap and easy and yummy greasy. The biscuits and gravy were oh-so-yummy and authentic. The gravy is totally homemade (which I hear is rare)! The owner even came and sat down with us to ask how it was. Great place to roll into late morning and replenish after a long night. I will be back on my next visit to Nashville!

Well my friends, in honor of my 100th yelp, I decided that I had to review a hands down five star institution. DiNic's serves as just that. If you are a fan of roast pork, it doesn't get much better than this. To get the full experience, order a roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone. All of the flavors work soooo good together. It's a match made in heaven. I am extremely lucky because I can walk to DiNic's from my office. For those of you who can't make it to Jersey, the original location is in the Reading Terminal Market in Philly. However, the lines can get quite long over there around lunch time. Stop into DiNic's for a good old fashioned roast pork sandwich, that you won't be sorry that you broke your diet for!

The food is very very good! Very cool atmosphere and big points for the Frank Zappa fandom! The service is generally very friendly but totally inefficient!! Waiting in line to place an order when they're busy reminds me of the hellish pains I get at the DMV.

Do you know how to breathe? Oh yah? Ok - Then this is for you! 

Are you open to the possibility of having your body and your sense of self transformed? Yes? then this is for you. 

Hang up your coat, ego and expectations at the door... because Jada goes beyond all three when you're on the table. 

This is THE best body work I've received in 15+ years, quite possible the most powerful ever in my life! 

I'm going back often. 

This is the real deal Holyfield, folks! Strap in!

This place used to be one of our favorite little treats, for a good brunch or lunch. It was a little pricey, but we were always satisfied with our food, so well worth it. I'm not sure if they changed owners, but our last visit there will definitely be our last visit. It used to feel like a little bistro. They had good service and greeted you with a little sample of baked goods. Now you go to the counter and order and they bring your food out. Not much different than McDonalds. The food has definitely gone down in quality as well. There was another disappointed family sitting near us, complaining about the same issues we were having. Tasteless food, that still costs too much. Such a shame, because this place used to have a certain home cooked charm that kept us coming back.

$3 for basic car wash. Convenient by Broad St. Fast service and friendly.

You pay at the entrance of the wash.
Amazing service and great beignets! I also had the cafe au lait and my husband has a vanilla latte, both were fantastic. Easy to get to and plenty of parking outside and nice seating area inside.

This venue is AMAZING, it's been a month since the wedding and I keep getting compliments on how beautiful and perfect the wedding was. I am so thankful that everything went so smoothly, we both had a very stress free day nothing went wrong at all. Kelly was very helpful with planning everything, my husband is very particular of getting things done right; dot every "i" cross every "t" kinda guy. Kelly was able to accommodate everything he asked for and kept us both calm when planning was getting stressful. We hired a firework company to come out and the communication between Kelly and the company was great, I was able to keep them a surprise until the firework show started. 
  John Gibbons market place catered the wedding, I have a million different allergies including gluten, dairy, tomatoes and red meat; they accommodated for me with an amazing chickpea stuffed acorn squash. We had ordered the bacon wrapped meatloaf and prickly pear chicken, let me tell you we had managers from 5 star restaurants as guest at our wedding and they were very impressed with the food. With that note we also hired Genevieve to make our cake...AMAZING, again compliments are coming all the way from Iowa STILL. The biggest compliments are coming from my special ordered gluten free dairy free vanilla with raspberry filling cake, it seemed like everyone took a small taste of my special ordered 30 person cake. You can bet I will be calling Genevieve for ALL my event cake needs, especially for that GF DF cake. 
  Mark was our DJ, we share wedding anniversaries now. My sister is getting married in Phoenix September and was asking how to get ahold of Mark to be her dj, I told her he is with Che's dj company. I met with a couple of the DJ's with this company Mark was the best there was to have! He was very lively and fun, played music from my list and didn't try changing my music selection. 
  Shela was our bartender, she made an amazing virgin pomegranate margarita. From what my guest where saying she did an amazing job on the alcoholic drinks as well. She didn't have to cut anyone off. 
  Jona was the BEST investment of ALL when it came to my wedding. She set up my decorations, moved them from the ceremony site to the cocktail hour and reception areas! At the end of the night she took everything down put it away then swept through the place to make sure nothing was missed. 
  Overall we had the perfect wedding, and would HIGHLY recommend anyone to get married here. Kelly was very helpful and answered our one million and one questions promptly. She allowed us to use everything we wanted without hesitation; the florist, string quartet, mariachi and cocktail hour caters had no issues at all. My photographers and videographers loved the venue as well.

In rating this restaurant, you have to consider whether to base it on the food or the service (or both). The food is typical and I don't have any issues with it; it serves a need for basic stuff.

The service is third world quality. Use the drive up window and you are as likely to be frowned at as not at the payment window. Do not expect any version of "please", "thank you" or ,to quote another fast food place, "my pleasure". Is it recently so hard to hire young people with sufficient skills to indicate to a customer that they have not made a serious error in their food choice? 

Spare me; my money spends elsewhere just as easily.

Spoke  with Ashley the manager here at Publix she was very helpful and super empathetic when I told her about my apples being bruised. She offered me a new bag of apples.  Great store and nice people!

This is what a sandwich tastes and looks like if you're lucky enough to have an Italian Mom who can cook her ass off. Sad to say, my Mom is gone. But the sandwiches at George's are so close and so delicious that I find myself licking my chops and crying for Mom simultaneously. The T and T is my favorite. I know most of you don't care for tongue OR tripe- more for US! I brought my husband his first T and T without his knowing what it was or who made it. He FLIPPED! So incredibly delectable- perfect, mellow seasoning, the ingredients tender and succulent but still distinct. If you eat in the car, I hope you have a towel, even thought they wrap everything perfectly. Oh, man, I'm dyin' for a T and T.

Highly recommended by many folks, I took my family of five adults and we loved it!  I'm not a golfer by any means, but I had fun. The smile on face lasted hours. Fun golf games, great food, and a nice bar. There is so much to review and comment on, so, here it goes.

As a hack (having played only 2 par 3 courses in my life), this old timer (62 years old) with a bad shoulder, I had a lot of fun with one of those golf sticks in my hands. There are targets to aim at, each at different distances. Electronics are built into the ball, which scores you.  So I would toddle up with a pitching wedge and aim at the target 25 yards away. My son is much more experienced. The thing is that I was competitive score wise. Even though I was a hack, I did not feel like one.

You can come here just for the restaurant and bar. You do not have to golf. They also have concerts in their own 300 seat "theater". They get good bands, from what I could tell.

Servers bring food and adult beverages to a table behind the tees in each bay. The food was excellent. We ordered a lot of appetizers and shared them, so I will review each.

For a limited time, they had a Farmhouse Flatbread. This was a crusty bread with all kinds of great stuff piled on top of it. Arugula, tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, sauce and cheese were perfectly balanced. Wonderful.

From the standard menu, we ordered the Macaroni and Cheese with Bacon Spring Rolls. I'm used to Spring Rolls that are not fried. These were like fried egg rolls and were yummy. Nice cheese sauce and it was easy to pick up and eat.

Grilled Chicken Wings were probably the least favorable. While having a great flavor, they were a tad dry.

The hit of the food was the Jumbo Pretzel Platter! This was a pretzel that was about 10" in diameter. Inside the pretzel was all kinds of other yummy goodies. Prosciutto, sausage, alcohol marinated fruit, cheese sauce, coated pecans and cheeses were wonderful and a lot of fun to pick at.

Waitstaff was friendly and professional. They even all held their serving trays the same way.

One drawback is that the place is noisy. It is a party venue. Serious golfers would require quiet to concentrate and develop their shot.
Beautiful restaurant and friendly staff!!! Delicious food... I suggest the OM Yellowtail Sashimi and the Honda!!! We'll be back in the near future!

Use to love this place. Grab a double walk around. What's not to love. Stopped in today a Thursday needless to say slow. Wife grabbed a cocktail off the wall $9 I asked for a double of shine rocks $26. Wtf. A triple tasting was $8 needless to say I'm not gonna go back. I'm not one to ask why so much. But think for $2 more I coulda bought a bottle. Sad day.
I love this place! The food is phantastic! Where else can you eat lunch for $10 and leave food on the table because you were too full to finish it!  10/10 will be back!!!

Came in because the pizza looked great. I sat at the bar and ordered a glass of wine, pizza, and a side of pasta. I don't know what the food is like because when I was served the wine in a dirty lipstick stained glass, I canceled my food order. I told the server about the dirty glass and I watched her transfer the wine from a dirty glass to another "clean" glass and handed it to me. After this I saw the server pick up a pizza on the crust with her bare hands from the window. She had just finished handling beer bottles and dish rags. I think a cleanliness isn't a priority here.
Average ice cream and a bit pricey. 3-5 ice cream flavors were out and it was definitely a 3 star ice cream place. The sitting area and building was very clean.

Fantastic find... Soup Nazi best describes this man... he is definitely passionate about his food art and will not sway from his way. Every ingredient in the meal is fresh. Also do note that this a "get what you get" place. There is only one item on be menu each day,and the item changes everyday, the only consistency with this place is that it serves Grilled Chicken and falafel everytime. Expect a long wait, got there at 12:30p and didn't get food until 1:20p. But while waiting in line , got to chatting with some regulars and the food is said to be fantastic everyday. 

Happy Eatings! CASH ONLY spot and bring your own fork. Oddly they don't provide utensils nor napkins just a styrofoam box and the food inside of it

Was rescheduled THREE times. I had to take time off work to wait for the technician on three different days. When you make an appointment with them, DO NOT EXPECT THEM TO SHOW UP. Extraordinarily unprofessional. Never going to reach out to them again and I would recommend anyone who values their time to also avoid.

I've been waiting a long to time to have a ramen place in Nashville and Chef Gavigan has been promising this for quite a while. I've been here several times and overall a good bowl of ramen. This is not the knock your socks off ramen I think it should be, considering the hype, but still a decent bowl. I always get the same kind and it is never consistent, good, but not consistent. Sometimes the noodles are cooked to perfection and sometime under-cooked. I would agree its a bit pricey, but hey supply and demand right? A little stingy on the veggies and eggs, only half an egg, unless you shell out an extra $2 for the other half (lets see thats a $4 egg, hmmm) never seen that before. You can make it stretch with the extra noodles for another $2 though. 

The real beef I have is they are only open, occasionally, so just make sure you are only wanting ramen Tuesday - Friday afternoon and evening. 

I actually prefer the Miso ramen at Hanabi in Brentwood, for the same price you get a huge bowl, full of veggies and a whole egg :). Yes a whole egg...

I was completely disappointed with my visit with Dr Weinstein 
He seemed uncaring and in a rush to be done with the appointment 
I would never recommend anyone to see him

Wow...this place was unbelievable. Seriously 5 stars all around. Smelled fantastic, people were super friendly (except the woman cashier who was texting while we were paying for our food, definitely uncharacteristic of everything about this place.) The rest of the staff was genuinely friendly and cared about taking care of you. I mean genuine. The food was sort of like a flashback, going thru the cafeteria line at school and while ordering the food I was kind of taken aback. BTW the guys putting your plate together were extremely nice as well (just that dang lady texting at the register? wtf are you doing there?) I had read reviews before coming and was prepared for a good meal but all I could think about was the cafeteria line at school. NOT THE CASE ON THE FIRST BITE! Holy smokes this is grandma's cookin' with fllllaaaavooor! Yes probably the most flavorful meal of down home cooking I have ever had. Mac and cheese, green beans, mashed potatoes and meatloaf. Pops had the fried grouper and it was unreal too. Super light crispy batter, again tons of flavor! Unbelievable...You must go, seriously. Treat yourself.

WAY to expensive for what you get. 9.00 for vodka on the rocks 5.00 Heineken. 4.50 for a side of chili and a 14.00 hamburger. I've paid 14.00 for a hamburger before but it was excellent. ( lamb burger at midtown eats)

I happened upon this store last year and was interested in a table with 2 chairs.  When I went back a month later to purchase, new owners had taken over.  I went ahead and ordered the items.
