I searched all over NOLA and this place was the best I had hands down.

We always go here after chiropractor treatments next door! #26 and #40 are our go to's every time! So amazing! always full! always good! always hot and fresh! You should try it for yourself! I always look forward to dinner here! and this soup is the cure all for any cold you may have! its soul food!

Wow!!! It was first visit and it was absolutely amazing.  The waitress was so pleasant and welcoming.... The atmosphere was nice and I will definitely return.  

The only thing for me was the fact that I was cold.  It wasn't warm enough for how cold it is outside.  Other than that it was a great Sunday outing with the children.  Oh BTW they eat free from 12-4!  Bonus!

Holy Smokes!!!, Stumbled upon this place killing time waiting for Wifee to get out of a rehearsal.  Hit the H-Mart downstairs and started to feel a bit hungry.  I've done a lot of Korean but have never seen anything like this.  It was completely alien to me.  As you walk in the door, there are many tables.  On the left wall there are 4 windows w bars across them and I guess each window is about 15 feet apart with a corresponding piece of kitchen and a bell, the type that you ring w your finger tip.  In the corner to the right near the front door is a cashier with photos of menu items on the wall in addition to descriptions and prices.  The prices were very inexpensive which made me a bit suspicious.  I ordered a spicy seafood noodle dish, the woman gave me a receipt with a number and she pointed at a window.  In about 10 minutes a bell rang and my number appeared on a screen above a window.   Included with my profoundly delicious bowel of noodles and assorted seafood were small dishes of kimchee (the cubed radish style), regular kimchee, rice and potato salad.  The total price of my dinner was $6.99 and I also purchased an iced tea for $1.50.  I studied the dishes others were munching at the surrounding tables and everything w/out exception looked delicious.  We'll return with a vengeance (and friends) in the very near future.

I stayed here for 2 nights for my brother's wedding. It is nice for a Holiday Inn and reasonably priced. We had two rooms (one for the bride and groom) and another room for a couple other people and me. The room I was in had two double beds which I didn't find all that comfortable. I used the exercise room which was clean with good equipment. They have the typical Holiday Inn breakfast with a buffet of eggs, bagels, bread, cereal and yogurt. There is plenty of parking.

My only gripe is that we had issues with the door. The door to my brother's room didn't work well the entire time we were there. The first day, we went down and complained about the key and had to get a new one several times. Then at 2am, when my brother and his wife were coming in after celebrating their wedding and still in their wedding attire, I found them in the hall not being able to get into the room as the door just didn't work. The employee wanted to put them in another room but all of their stuff which was a lot of stuff due to the wedding and various items left by people in the bridal party were in the room. Finally after some time, he was able to get the door open but it remained broke. They did end up giving them a free night but it was kind of annoying that it happened on their wedding night. But I think this may just be a fluke (or I hope).

Worst moussaka ever had , dry salad, and stale gyro . Worst part is that it's priced high.
Must be a tourist trap . Drive further away if you can

Well, Lenny's isn't the best sub place I've ever been to, but it's close to my house, is very different and it's enjoyable. 

I honestly can't pinpoint where Lenny's can improve- I just know that it can. I always get the Italian, which I think is the best sub that they make. Bread is fresh and meat is cut right in front of you for each sub that's made. They have a great hot pepper relish that comes on a lot of the subs, but I would recommend asking for it on the side and/or very light on the sandwich as they tend to slather it on. 

Staff is never super friendly, but they are nice enough.

Great food, service and atmosphere! Calamari and scungili salad was very fresh and tasty. Chef came out to check on us several times. Not only did we walk in late, but we didn't realize it was BYOB.  Not only were encouraged to take our time, but they were also kind enough to share some of their wine with us!

Be prepared to wait a long time... But worth it!

The best Ortho docs in the Tampa area.  It's so nice to meet a doctor who is not in a hurry to "put you under the knife",   I have arthritis in my knees, pretty badly, and they are doing everything they can to buy me time without having to do a knee replacement.  Staff is friendly and kind, and the PA and residents they train here have all been awesome.  I would highly recommend Dr.Bernasek if you are having trouble with your knees.  He's extremely kind, calm, and compassionate,  He also takes the time to talk to you and explain things, sometimes even leaving with a little hug,  And he does not order unnecessary testing

Now, this is a HUGE practice with several locations.  And for some reason always run behind time.  When I saw Dr. Bernasek in December, I waited over 2 hours.  This time I had an appointment with his PA who gives the injections "so I won't have to wait so long". Well my appointment was at 11:00am but I was not called in until after 2pm.  That is ridiculous.  The PA was very apologetic about the wait, but I still gave him "what for" about it.  How can you get 3 hours behind in the morning?  This is definitely the biggest drawback of this practice.  I  do have to say they did bring around bottles water and packets of peanut butter crackers for us, which was a nice thing, but still did not make up for such a long wait

But, I have great confidence in my PA and Dr.  They don't rush me when I'm with them and they genuinely seem to care.  When it comes to my health, I want the best, and even with these long waits, I have the best.  

Minus a star for waiting time.

I love the juices here very tasty and freshly made! I ordered their Caesar wrap and it was very disappointing, very garlic-y and also not the best portion, it's more like a snack. If stay away from the food and stick to the juices!

Craft distillery in Nashville with a great vibe.  The tour was very entertaining. I have been on multiple tours and no tour guide has been as knowledgeable and entertaining as Kolby was.  I will visit this distillery every time I come to Nashville!  Oh yeah and a quick shout out to Kyle who poured all of my samples at the tasting.

I will never, ever eat here again. And I suggest you don't either. I went a few months back based on the reviews I see most places.

I dined with my boyfriend and a friend of ours--all of us agreed we'd never had such bad service in our lives. After waiting--no joke--at least 30 minutes, we finally got up and asked the hostess if she could please at least bring us some water. You may be thinking this place was packed, and I'm complaining...but you are wrong. There were only a few other patrons and we were ALL complaining to each other. Another table told us we should just get up and leave, but silly me, I decided we should sit it out because maybe the sushi was just that good. Wrong again. Mediocre at best. 

The evening continued just as it began...with us continuing to have to go find someone any time we needed anything. The hostess was probably tired of seeing us by the end. 

There are much much better places to get sushi in Tampa with much better service.
Their selection had gone downhill since covid-19 hit unfortunately unless you want to buy their house brand, that they have a ton of

Only giving this place two stars because a good service and prompt attention to our table. The food is terrible from the appetizers through to the sushi rolls there's nothing with good about this place. Stay away-- there are totally so many better sushi places in Saint Pete to go to.

Right in the middle of the city, you could almost miss this one. It's between several buildings but has a nice uptown sign. Not as much space as some of the others and really only has giant jenga for entertainment, still the location is super central and convenient.

The most amazing seafood! Everything was delicious! We started off with a crab soup. It was creamy, flavorful and full of crab chunks. We then had the baked octopus with feta cheese. It was probably one of the most delicious appetizers I have ever had. We also ordered the snow crab dinner and fried oysters. I could not have been anymore pleased with my dinner. Oh and the service was excellent!

Came here after coffee tasting at Counter Culture Coffee on a Friday morning.  We had heard great things, and it was only a few blocks away.  It kind of felt like a hole-in-the-wall kind of place.  There was a shop front where you could order pastries and drinks to go, and in the back were tables and seats.  We were greeted by the one waiter who was running the restaurant at the time and he told us to sit anywhere.  It was relatively empty, but expected for a Friday morning. We took a table in the back.

After reading some recommendations and browsing through some photos, we ordered the sweet potato fries, the eggs benedict, and the sweet potato hash.  The food portions were huge, and we definitely didn't need to order the sweet potato fries.

The sweet potato fries were thin and crispy, lightly salted with large flecks of sea salt.  I love sweet potatoes but what really made the dish was the side of sour cream and sweet chili sauce-- a dip into the sour cream and then the chill sauce was this delicious combination of sweet, creamy, and salty all at the same time.  We ate half the bowl before we started to realize that our stomachs were getting full (the bowl was that big.), and decided we still needed to save some room for the main course.

I had the sweet potato and sausage hash and it was delicious.  The sunny side egg perfectly spilled all over the sweet potato and sausage and made this gooey, sticky sauce.  It was delicious.  The sweet potato was a good alternative to the traditional potato, lightening the dish, which was needed after being smothered in the heavy yolk and mayo sauce latticed on top.  Served with two slices of bacon, too.  Although I didn't try the eggs benedict, it looked really good as well.  The poached eggs were perfectly cooked and delicately spilled over the english muffin. 

Like I said, the portions were huge, and I could only finish half my dish.  We took the rest home to enjoy later.  One nuisance was that Ants Pants is cash only--but they do have an ATM in store.  Service was very attentive and friendly.  Great place for brunch if you're in the area.

Beer and food is great but we were disappointed the last time we went in because we were told they didn't have any high chairs. Most craft beer drinkers in town are probably ages 25-40, the age at which many of us have young families. Every other brewery/restaurant in town has high chairs and kids menus, why can't RD accommodate young kids like Rec Room, Bistro, and others do?

I love this restaurant. I had previously met Chef Eric Kelly and he was really cool. Then i went for dinner here one night and it was amazing. Its not something you can eat every night but once in a while yes.

The service is horrible. The first time was 2 months ago. I was seated but no one bothered to take my order. I walked out. Now, I'm here but the food still didn't show up after 30 minutes of my order. Mind you this is the airport. It's all about speed.
Thank you Aaron your driver did an amazing job navigating a hard driveway to offload my vehicle. Your driver was on time very kind and courteous and I appreciate the great rate.
Delisous. Great service coupled with fulfilling soul good for lunch might take you out but well worth it! They also have lighter options like baked chicken and mixed greens as well!

Good hamburgers price just a bit to high
Employees they always seem bothered maybe under payed they need nicer people to work their employees with a welcoming smile  
Restaurant always clean that's a plus

The retro stadium fad is a great idea for baseball. Having never made it to The Vet, Citizens Bank Ballpark, just from my associates' opinions was such a good idea. 

To go with this new ballpark, there isn't a big premium price. You bleacher bum it for $10-15 bucks on a lot of nights from a scalper, and given The Phillies' growing wins and rising stars *cough* Ryan Howard, I don't know how long that deal will last.

I much prefer a day game here to a night game, as it's a great way to spend an afternoon. My only qualm, coming from a city with an architecturally pleasing view of bridges, skyscrapers, and rivers from its own famed ball park, is that all you have to look at it is South Jersey. What a downer.
A nice and consistent place. I have been here quite a few times and have been rewarded each time I went. Good place to meet a friend and catch up.

Save your money, time and effort. Happened upon this place to kill a few hours, figured I would play some Poker and stay out of the most miserable humidity known to man. Enter giant entrance after being dropped off by uber and ask first employee I see "where's the poker?" oh it's over a mile from here, you need to go to this end of the building and follow it for over a mile? You're kidding me right? No I am not, it's actually over a mile down the street. 

Moving on, ATM machine (they always pay at casino's) bad dad jokes. Not this one, ate my Applecard, not once but twice.... took a solid half hour for them to come and retrieve it by the way, no one gives a shit in this place about anything. so so florida..... 

On to the cashier, "sir this card has no numbers" my reply "it has a chip, and I can provide you with the numbers on my phone if you need them?" Their reply "oh we can't do that here" .... It's 2021 get with the fuck#ing times. 

Okay can I scan my bank of America app on my phone? No sir, we can't do that either.... I just cackled and laughed at this terrible place. oh It's dirty and smells too..... but hey a casino right? 

At this point I'm pissed, but we came all this way.... I took the measly $150 cash I had on me and bought chips at a black jack table. 1st hand boom black Jack, alright lets do this, chipped away made a couple of hundred, but more importantly tipped about $100 total, because this place certainly isn't paying well if they cant keep up with technology. 

I'll never step into this casino again, and I still have no idea where the poker room actually is...

much like florida, this place is a lawless swamp made up of people waiting to die.

This place is so close to my house I had high hopes that it would be awesome Mexican food, and I would never have to get on the highway again (for mexican food...)

I was extremely disappointed. 

This place has changed owners a lot since I've lived in my house, about 5 years, and I was never interested because it was always a bar, and I was guessing there was no food.

As soon as I saw the new name on the sign I wanted to try it!  We walked in, there were 8 other people there at 6pm.  The inside looks like a bar, there are a few Mexican decorations, a frame or two with the flag on them, but I did not feel like I was sitting in Mexico like with some other restaurants.  I was very impressed with the menus, they were very well made and I did not see any typos. 

I think my boyfriend was trying to stay positive, the service was okay.  I was also not a huge fan of the chips, and the food (both of our entrees) were way too salty.  I got a chicken chimichanga and it was chicken and chimichanga.  I'm used to onions and sometimes peppers maybe beans inside the chimi, I think lack of any other ingredients is what made the chicken super dry.  I was looking to the sauce to make the chicken not so dry and that's when I was attacked with salt.  

I will probably try this place again, like I said it is sooooo close to my house, but not with high hopes.

I went to Sufei for a foot massage, after 30 min I was told to turn over (normally I would think this was weird but my Mom had just gone there and she said they do your back after your feet). The masseur then started on my back, everything was fine until he started putting all of his weight on my spine as if he was trying to pop my back... not only that, he did it in a hurry starting by my neck down my entire back, popping happening the whole way. I said, "not so rough, softer" he just giggled and kept going. He went back up to my neck and was so rough I had to say "softer, softer" again- to which he just says "oh, ya, ok" and kept going SO HARD. 
I wish I would have gotten up when he started popping my back. I started having back pains last night (FOOT massage was at 10am) and I am still in pain this morning. 
If you are not a chiropractor you shouldn't be popping people's backs... you shouldn't even be working on people's backs for a FOOT MASSAGE.

Great little lunch spot with delicious bbq sandwiches and ribs. Had the tri-tip sandwich with a side of beans. Try all 4 of the bbq sauces, each offering great flavor. The meal was very good and a decent price for a tourist town. Wish the sandwich was a bit larger for the price but overall was very satisfied.
Loved the firecracker salmon (daily special).   The service was excellent.  Safety measures were in place. And everyone was super friendly.   I'll be going back.
Service was a bit weird....but the blackened salmon sandwich I got was GREAT. They have other good food options on the menu as well. My sister didn't like her mahi mahi, ended up getting what I had.

Service has been better last few times I have gone.  Sushi is the best! I Love the Sophia roll, cucumber hand roll, spicy tuna roll, spicy crunch tuna roll, screaming spicy roll. I don't believe I've ever had a bad roll.

Atmosphere is cozy and homely, not very modern. Felt like it was just a place to bum around. There's Jenga, cards, etc. on the side where you can play. I wouldn't sit around there to hang out. But the tea is better than the tea I had from tea do. Had the lychee green tea & mango green tea.

My boyfriend and I went here for dinner and we had Jo as our server. She was awesome. So down to earth and very friendly.  We defiantly will be going back and will be asking for her again. The food is very good also. He got a hot roast beef and I got a Harts burger. I really recommend going here.

Terry does a great job 1st time & everytime. I highly recommend his service. He sharpens at the following Farmers Markets -  Gulfport Tuesday's, Cory Ave. Sundays, & Dunedin Saturdays. Plus he accepts knives at his home just south of Gulf to Bay at 19, by appt.

There are a lot of things you can get here for parties, gifts or holiday decor.  The cards are reasonably priced.  There is quite a large variety with themes such as Spiderman, Pokemon, Disney, Hello Kitty etc.   I like going for Christmas stocking stuffers.  They have single candies that are 15 for a dollar as well as other inexpensive small items.  They have Christmas and Hanukkah cards, decorations and accessories.  Some prices are better than others.  They also do helium balloons for special occasions and cups, paper plates etc.  Personnel were helpful about finding things or answering questions.

We go to the Meridian Idaho Pizza location quite often, but our first time at this location. Not at all impressed. The buffet was terrible...salad bar was dirty with food all over, lettuce was out, ranch was out, among other things empty. When my 10 year old son asked an employee for more lettuce and ranch, she intentionally ignored him and waited until 5 other adults asked. She appeared to take her sweet time refilling as she liked seeing people get upset. The pizzas were made beforehand and stored in a warmer, so they tasted old...not fresh. We also saw several people using their dirty, used plates at the buffet. When putting their pizza on their dirty plates, I saw the pizza server touch the plates! Completely unsanitary and unappetizing! We heard other customers complaining about the same issues we had. Customer service is absolutely horrible. We were there for a sports party, thus the reason we went to that location. However, we will not be returning to this Boise location. We'll stick with the tried and true, awesome Meridian location!

First time at Sierra Cafe was good, and inexpensive, but let's not go overboard with the huzzahs just yet.  It's a prototypical last-chance coffee shop at a last-chance I-80 Nevada Casino (Gold Ranch) and gas station (Sinclair)--or first-chance for eastbound motorists--a stone's throw from the California border.

The Ranch House Ham & Eggs selected late one Thursday morning is pictured by fellow reviewers, and described in the menu, as a bone-in, half-pound ham steak.  Mine was served cut into three sections away from the missing bone.  Possibly aging more noticeably than I am aware, I do remain capable of cutting meat from the bone without aid.

Having chosen home fries well-done instead of hashbrowns, the potatoes were little, crispy cubes the size of Sonic (nugget) ice, and devoid of any frills one might prefer in a side of home fries, like onions and herbs.  Two eggs were faultlessly fried over/hard.  Service was prompt and excellent.

Two others' Sierra Cafe reviews mentioned the water tasting of chlorine, but it tasted fine on my visit, and coffee was satisfactory.  What a relief!  If you couldn't get fresh-tasting tap water at elevation 5000 in the Sierra, maybe the planet really has only 12 years left.

A friend told us that when we got tired of the craziness on Broadway to find this alley.  She did not steer us wrong.

On our first night in Nashville, Printer's Alley was just steps from our hotel so we landed here.  We found two great spots to listen to live music:  Alley Taps and Snitch.  The next night we landed at Bourbon Street Blues and then made it back to Alley Taps.

I would make this my destination for evenings (especially if you are into live music).

This place gives false advertisement on their percentage of their products. If you advertise 25% thc then I buy at a costly rate and get a 19%. That's a fucking rip off. Advertise what you really sell!!

The original problem was fixed promptly why an employee who was cordial and professional. Unfortunately, the lock broke again-exactly the same problem-within two weeks. The company was totally unresponsive, difficult to reach, and never seemed concerned about resolving the problem.

Been here twice now and both times experienced exceptional food, with so much flavor! Definitely have anything Makhani, or Korma. The cilantro mint chutney was super fresh and tasty too. Many options for all kinds of diets without any skimping. 

The service was also wonderful. I had to send something back once because of my own dietary restrictions and they handled it immediately and beautifully. The servers all know they menu well, and are great at making recommendations.  
Not to mention how beautifully decorated, and very clean everything is.
Can't wait to go again.

Very Poor performance  on their service department and their back-office!

I traded in my lease in March 2019 and the process was seamless, however, the weeks to come became very intrusive and a big nightmare. One has the perception once you get your car you are done! no not here, I have had to go back for numerous issues they cannot get correct: title, registration, vehicle turn-in, etc. I am still getting notices for a vehicle that was turned in  on March and they have not closed out the balance. I received a 3 month registration and never got a call back or update on why, and the service department... That has been the worst of all. I have been waiting over a month to get my vehicle checked for a fuel/gas mileage issue on a brand new 2019 equinox and they do not make the availability or  have a rental ready. I have been in contact with GM and they cannot get it together either. DO NOT GO HERE! They are nothing but headaches!
Great location, staff and food! We had the guacamole, salsa, queso and chips. Delicious and filling. We had the best time here thanks to Amelia and her suggestions!

Very yummy, great selection of rolls and very reasonable price! Picked up to go, service was great and very prompt. I also asked them to add slides jalapenos and lemon on the side, and they did! =) Will definitely order again.

Not bad, just mediocre. The food didn't have the level of flavor that I expect from Indian. I ordered takeout and it arrived quickly and the order was correct. Again, not terrible, but it's no Tiffin or Ekta.

A trip back to Tucson is not complete without a stop at Bison Witches. The $7.95 combo where you get a half of a sandwich and a bowl of soup in a bread bowl is the perfect lunch. 

A half sandwich from Bison Witches is quite large, particularly the ones served on Texas toast so be prepared. The soups are all great, I always struggle to choose between the clam chowder and potato bacon. Most of the time I get the cally for my sandwich but I sometimes change it up and get the chicken salad. I have never had anything bad here, ever.

Finish it off with $1 jello shots, and I have the perfect lunch. Someone please open a Bison Witches in Las Vegas?!

I like that Campo's has some variety to their cheesesteaks, so that it doesn't feel like you're eating fast food.  Plus, their drink selection extends beyond soda and water, so that's great!  I had the Works, which was pretty good.  Mushrooms, onions, bell peppers.  The bell peppers were interesting.  I didn't quite like the mushrooms they chose to use, but the sandwich was pretty good overall.  The staff was very friendly and attentive.

It's a nice place to sit and relax and watch all the tourists run around while you eat your sandwich.  I wouldn't say it's the BEST.  I've yet to find the best, I think...

I have been here twice and I have enjoyed each visit. My husband loves it above the normal Chinese I drag him to. Good prices as you get alot for what you order. I was skeptical about trying the Dim Sum but it turned out to taste great.

The wife and I eat here every couple weeks. The freshly baked chips are always excellent, and they have the best queso dip. The Tacos Al Pastor is probably my favorite meal of any restaurant in Indy - it's delicious! However, the best part of La Cabana is the service. Everyone is always warm, friendly, and eager to serve. Great people!

I went to this place and Prince's Hot Chicken on the same day to try each of the sandwiches. By the rating, you can see where I'm going.

Hattie B's sandwich contained a nice juicy chicken breast. That's pretty much it. The bun was subpar, the slaw wasn't as good as Prince's and the seasonings were not as prominent as Prince's. Hattie B's was also a but greasier than I was expecting.

Hattie B's makes a good looking sandwich on Instagram but the flavor department lacked a bit. Hattie B's is just insta famous.

The most amazing part of this little place was the sweet tamale. We ordered a pineapple tamale and it was downright amazing - warm, sweet, and delicious. That is the best thing we had here.

We tried a trio of tacos - beef tongue, beef cheek, and carne asade.  The tongue was our favorite - it was cooked the best and went with the toppings well. 

The cheek was a bit too watery and made the taco hard to eat. It was good, but not great. I would eat it again, but I wouldn't be like jumping for joy about it.

The carne asada was my least favorite - way too watery and impossible to eat as it disintegrated the tortilla. Not as great of flavor as the other two either.

The place is small and outside but has a fan so it's not unbearably hot if you sit in.

Overall, my family and I enjoyed our dinner at The Pelican.  I loved the seafood bisque and would go there just for that.  There were large chunks of seafood in a tomato base broth that was smooth and buttery.  That was a five.  I was disappointed in the Crispy Calamari because it wasn't crispy at all.  I think it wasn't cooked enough because it was very rubbery.  The dipping sauce was good though.  The bay scallops with a mushroom risotto was delicious.  I was disappointed in the chocolate mousse.  It wasn't creamy at all, very hard, like it sat in the refrigerator too long.  The taste was good but the texture was hard.  The waitress was fabulous and friendly.

Great restaurant in Yardley. I had the lamb gyro and Greek salad which was awesome. My hubs had the chicken parm sandwich with fries which was ok- gyro was better. It's byob so it ends up being very inexpensive. We sat outside by the canal which was nice. Service was super fast. It's great for a low key, casual restaurant in town.

Update :
We take out Greek salad here at least twice a week!!! We love it !!!!
My review is now 5 stars.

5/5 stars for amazing service -- I used the drive thru twice while in town and both times the person who took my order was extremely friendly and helpful. I had a couple questions regarding my coffee and the guy taking my order was helpful and patient. Once I got to the window, I was greeted by a woman who was also very friendly, asked how my day had been going, and if I had any fun weekend plans. It's the little things that make an experience memorable/positive, like just asking someone how their day was. I truly appreciate good customer service, so thank you Starbucks for showing a great example of that.

February 20th is National Sticky Bun Day and like many other things, the sticky bun originated in Philadelphia, hmmm, I wonder if Fritz's grandfather knew that when he came to this area from Germany with his recipe for German sticky buns?

Regardless, when you walk inside you will see more sticky buns than you have ever seen in your life! Plain sticky buns, raisin topped sticky buns, walnut topped sticky buns and raisin and walnut topped sticky buns and trays of sticky buns with thick cream cheese icing on them! They even have sticky bun rings, sheet cakes or layered cakes. I've found sticky bun heaven!

They claim to have the best sticky buns and have awards to back them up, we bought a couple of each kind and plan to freeze some, but we each had a sliver of each and they are good indeed, are they the best I have ever had, no. However they are moist, very sticky and loaded with toppings, if that is how you ordered them.

We also bought 6 Danish, again plan on freezing some, one cheese and one lemon filled for me, I had a third of each and they were buttery and flaky and had enough filling to even satisfy me. Hubby chose two cherry, one crumb and one apple. He ate 1/2 of one cherry and loved it and 1/2 of the crumb and was not thrilled. Got milk?

Cases of homemade fancy cookies, layered cakes galore, all kinds of brownies, cheesecakes, plain or filled with fruit, mini Danish and cannolies or you can buy the large size. Fruit turnovers, eclairs, cream puffs, pies, and cinnamon breads or pound cakes. They make cinnamon pretzels and a chocolate cheese dream cake, which we bought, it is loaf size and is a dark chocolate cake that was very moist and topped with both a rich chocolate fudge icing and cream cheese icing, excellent!

I must admit my favorite of all that we bought was one large macaroon covered in a dark chocolate. I'm anxious to return to try their gooey butter cake. The only thing calorie free about this bakery are the wonderful aroma's that catch you as you're walking in. They have three locations, actually one closer to my house that I had never noticed, but it's cool to know when my sweet tooth starts hollering! 

And yes brian, they sell "crummy" t-shirts...

We came here after seeing the reviews and the decent ratings however that is where it ended. Service was in attentive. Pizza was lackluster. You're not that far from Reilly's down the road which is overall significantly better.  Won't be a returning customer.

Excuse me while I fume. I took my iPhone 6s in for a screen repair. A simple screen repair. They told me the wait would be 2 hours (which already is ridiculous). So I wandered the mall and filled my time, I then went back after 2 hours just to be told that they won't fix it because it had had some third party work on it in the past. They say that because of the third party's repair job, replacing the screen would risk damaging the battery. So I tell them, "oh my battery is trash too since it's a 6s so let's just replace both." They refuse without explanation and I'm told I need to buy a new phone at full value. Only option. Were they courteous in tone and manner? Sure. But did Apple refuse to fix their own phone? Yes. This is absolutely mind boggling. This review is not simply for this Apple store, but for the Apple brand. Convenient and beautiful products are prized in this world, you got us there. But in every other category for technology, you fail. I'm cheering for Samsung to find a convenient way for iTunes lovers to switch to their phones. Maybe a deal with Spotify? This Apple lover and advocate is done making excuses for the big brand. Samsung just gained a new customer.

We used Yelp to pick a new restaurant to try while on the other side of town. We settled on this Egyptian restaurant. The murals on the walls were pretty cool. The staff was very friendly and attentive. 

The white tablecloth had black spots all over it, it may have been pepper from the previous customers I guess. We grabbed the Humus with Beef appetizer and it was very good. Plenty of pita bread and dip for 2 or 3 people and tasted great. 

My wife ordered the Gyro and it was a little different than other Gyro's we've had. It was closed and pressed flat. Tasted great and was filling. The onions and tomatoes were not as fresh as they could be. 

I ordered a Mansaf Lamb dish with Rice. The dish came out and was very large, but 75% of it was rice. For a $17 dish I would have expected a little more meat. Also, I've eaten lamb many time, it is one of my favorites. It was good meat but half of this lamb was a little fatty and it also tasted very "gamey" kind of like bear or elk.

I will return here to try a different plate next time.

I never even knew about this little gem of a restaurant until I was craving some really good tacos and an even better cocktail.  I decided to try out Lucha Cartel and I was not disappointed!!!! I am in the customer service business and I am really big on receiving great customer service so imagine how good I felt when the manager came over to our table to make sure that our food came out the way it should have and if we were enjoying our time at Lucha.  I believe the manager said her name was Johanna.  The night that we visited Lucha it was really crowded but that did not stop my food from being great and the service from being absolutely wonderful.  I felt like since I told the manager that it was my first time there she told the chef to make sure he put some extra love in the food.  To say the least Lucha has become one of my go to places for drinks and tacos.

Since my family brought over our pet chihuahua Luis in our vacation to Tampa, we ended up going to this park. The place is wide and the people and dogs we met were pretty friendly. Luis really seemed like he had a pretty good time running around and playing with the other dogs. Wish we could go here again if we had the chance to go to Tampa again.

We were visiting from CO; looking for a great place for breakfast near the hotel. Bobo's came up as #1 recommendation. I thought we would try it, most reviews said the pancakes and cinnamon rolls were amazing. Let's just say the food was terrible at best. 
First, the floor and tables were filthy, grease every where, on the menus, on the salt and pepper shaker and the cups. Ugh! The food: I ordered the Huevos Ranchero, the tortilla was greasy, the salsa tasted like jar salsa.  I also ordered the cinnamon roll hoping the reviews would be somewhat accurate. Disappointed again. The roll was dry, the frosting was flavorless. 
To sum it up- don't go! I would rather have McDonalds or Denny's instead of Bobo's.

I'm from Houston which has some pretty good Asian food, but this place was objectively good (despite being in the middle of Nashville)! I had the Chong Qing noodles which were legit, had a marinated tea egg with it as well. The soup was very well made, with strong meat flavor, and the noodles were perfectly cooked. Also got the peach oolong tea with milk cap, which was super refreshing and sweet! 

Ambiance is interesting: sticky notes on the wall from past patrons and rubix cubes/cards for people to play with if they're so inclined. More restaurants should do that.

Waitresses were really friendly and helpful, suggesting that I drink the tea with no straw to get the full flavor. I appreciated that! Keep doing your thing.

We did a jazz dinner cruise...not a cheep dining option by any stretch but we were celebrating. The main portion was reserved so the cruise took place back in the King room and was quite cramped. The food was okay not as good as most restaurants in the area. It is buffet style in chafing dishes. The drinks are not included and are not very reasonably priced. There was a lot of fog so it was touch and go for departure and there are no refunds. After dinner we had a lovely cockroach grace the walls behind the seating area and eventually the table. Do not recommend this experience for others.

I was immediately won over by butcher and singer by the matchbooks. Growing up my mother had an oversize brandy snifter full of the suckers. They were all neat and from all over Montreal to Cuba. They had neat designs and pictures and were bright and brilliant. Butcher and Singer's have a darling little design with two cute dogs on them. Open up inside and you see a map of philadelphia.


We started off with shrimp cocktail. The shrimp were sweet and succulent. Fresh and tender. They nearly melted in your mouth. The cocktail sauce needed a bit more oomph, but our darling server thought nothign of bringing me a little saucer of fresh horseradish! Perfection. I scarfed these pretties down. I think they brought us 3 or 4 a piece I forget. 

Then onto the meat. A perfect portion of filet mignon. So perfect it lasted for three meals. Great garlicky mashed potatoes. These are not the bland flavorless plate fillers of most restaurants. We ordered brussel sprouts and stringbeans almondine. Huge portions! Best string beans ever! I was dipping my fingers and scooping up the buttery stock goodness of the string beans. 

Then came the baked alaska. Heaven is a baked alaska. This was light yet decadent. A perfect circle of cake, with delicately flavored banana ice cream capped in a angelic swoop of meringue. 

It was restaurant week and a steal! Next restaurant week you will find me here maybe twice!

OK, I've tried Lulu's 3 different times now, and the verdict is: the food is yummy.  Seafood dishes are pretty darn good, and dim sum is good enough to take friends and go back for more.  

Lobster with ginger & scallions was delish.  We really liked the Seafood with Fish Maw Soup.  Not only was the flavor there, but they are generous with the scallops, shrimp, and squid in the soup.   We also got the Seafood in Nest dish - the seafood in the nest was good, but I would have skipped the nest part since it was just deep fried noodles that didn't taste good.  The Thai fried squid was yummy, and so was the steamed fish we ordered.  For non-seafood, we've ordered Mongolian beef, which was good, sauteed vegetable in garlic (they use a lot of garlic!), and vegetable clay pot.  If I were to do the clay pot again, I'd skip out on the all vegatable clay pot and order one with seafood or some other meat since the vegetables will probably be in there with the seafood/meat.

As for dim sum, they had all the traditional dishes you'd expect.  I love my har gow (shrimp dumplings), and their's didn't disappoint.  A couple dishes were not very hot (fried daikon cakes and fried taro thingee), but were good nonetheless.  They also had some non-traditional stuff being pushed around - like fried smelt fish in a basket, vietnamese spring rolls, and boba drinks.  Service was fine, but it helped to have a cute baby at the table because all the servers wanted to come by to look at him.  :)

Also, for Lunar New Year's they have special new year dishes that they serve (sorry, we didn't get any so can't comment on it).  Even cooler is that they have Lion Dancers that come to perform in the evenings for that week. However, they were super busy during this time (with lots of big tables) so service was pretty spotty.

Hamentashen.  You may not be able to pronounce it and you may never have heard of it, but you must eat it.  You afraid to try new things?  Not my problem.  Do it.

The hamentash is a Jewish pastry involving a triangular pie-style crust wrapped around some sort of filling(fruit, chocolate, poppy-seed, etc.).  It is delicious and I am perpetually insistent that you consume this dessert with milk.

It isn't a question.  If I pass within 5 blocks of this establishment at an hour they are open, I will purchase one for myself and at least one more for another person because I believe in sharing things that are great.  Now it is fair to say that I grew up eating these and my opinion is ridiculously biased.  

Bottom line - 4th St. Delicatessen creates the best, if not the only, poppy-seed hamentashen in Philly.  This would be a 4 star review if i didn't enjoy this dessert so much.

Now the food at 4th Street is served in portions that can only be described as masochistic.  Everything you order off of their menu is an affront to moderation.  Their corned beef hash w/ eggs is awesome and is not meant for one human being.  It isn't even meant for several human beings and I love it.   Some restaurants have food challenges where they serve you a ridiculous quantity and doubt you will finish it - well buddy at 4th Street Delicatessen they have a whole list of food challenges that they call their OUR ENTIRE MENU.

Quantity aside, the quality is always pretty good.  The recipes show discipline and high quality ingredients.  Sometimes the pickles are better than other times but whatever.  On the action-movie-satisfaction-parallel scale, this is Hard Boiled.

Fun fact: The triangular shape of hamentashen is attributed to the triangular hat worn by a villian named Haman in the story of Purim.

If you're expecting Italian cuisine and a menu full of authentic options - this isn't the place to go. That being said, what they have is still delicious. I ordered the garlic bread as a started ($3) and that was really good. Then I had the eggplant parm for my main. The jam at the top was too sweet but the rest was delicious. Personally, I think it could've used a bit more of a kick in terms of spice. For dessert, I ordered the warm chocolate budino. That was delicious - rich chocolate flavor with salted caramel in the middle and the cool whipped cream on top. Aside from that, there are very limited pasta options - it's definitely more of a pizza place with a few other options. Overall, pretty delicious experience.

Okay.  I absolutely HATE the dentist.  Childhood trauma . . . don't ask.  However, my parents kept pushing me to get my teeth fixed because I'm "going out into the world," was starting at a new job, etc.  I had tried another dentist, and she wanted about $15,000 to do eight veneers.  Yeah.  Right.  My friend had told me about Dr. Preston and how much she liked her, and since my insurance included Dr. Preston, I decided to go.  The office was beautiful!  Her staff was really kind too.  The hygienist, Danielle, was kind and really understanding after I told her about my fear of dentistry.  She was actually very gentle during my cleaning, but not so much so that I didn't feel "clean."  After my cleaning appointment, I met Dr. Preston, and she was super nice.  She recommended what I should get done, and when I talked about the veneers and what exactly I wanted, I felt like she actually listened.  Her staff quoted me for $8,000 for eight veneers, and my insurance was going to pay for some of it anyway.  Now, some periodontal therapy, three fillings (which really didn't hurt, Dr. Preston is really good with that Novocain, I barely felt the shots, and . . . yeah, okay, I had some nitrous too), and eight veneers later, I love my teeth!  I've gotten so many compliments on them.  Dr. Preston did a great job.  I highly, highly recommend her!

The food was delicious. I didn't give it 5 stars only because it is a "fancy" place and my gf and I walked in off the street because we heard the food was good and we were dressed in just normal street clothes and the staff kind of looked down their noses at us. Staff wasn't the friendliest tbh.

I was so excited to try Krēm! I'm from Sacramento, so I'm used to having a wide variety of unique desserts to try. But this - soft-serve and cake?! - was something I've never tried before! 

You can choose between set combinations, or you can make your own delicious concoction. I decided to try chocolate soft-serve, vanilla cake, strawberry ganache, and condensed milk. The verdict? Delicious! The cake was so fluffy and perfect.

They have other flavors such as matcha, chocolate, and taro. 

The environment? Small, but cute. The place is notorious for its "I licked it cause it's mine" neon sign - super Instagram worthy. They have games set out to play with like Jenga. It does seem to get hot in there, but I guess that just makes you scream for more ice cream. 

Why three stars? I'm not sure if this dessert is worth $7. For my first time there, the worker wasn't super helpful in helping me to understand the menu. Again, it is small and it gets hot.

Overall? Still a nice spot to try. Perfect place for an IG picture. Would I go again? Maybe.

Wondering if this store's COVID safety protocol includes no bagging groceries for shoppers: The cashiers touch grocery items to scan, why can't they go a step further and help you bag?
My cashier this morning basically stood at her post and watched me bag my items...just waited...waited...waited for me to finish while other customers stood 6 feet away and beyond. She thanked me for bagging at the end to which I did not bother to reply. If I wanted to limit my contact, I would've gone to the self check out lane. I bought a week's worth of groceries and waited at a cashier's lane to get help with bagging. There are other grocery stores in the area with better customer service.

I've recently had brunch and lunch here within two days. The food is good, different but good. It's pricey, which I don't mind paying but I had some flaws with this. Nothing too crazy, just ordered crab cake sliders for their lunch special, was $17 dollars and they were the thinnest crab cakes ever the buns were too much for them. They have a Reuben soup; which is interesting but not horrible. Also, when I went for brunch we ordered "old bay home fries" there was no essence of old bay at all. They have a very small menu so if you're a picky eater I do not recommend going here. They do have vegan and vegetarian options which is nice. It's just not consistent with food, that's my own downside.

This experience was SO MUCH FUN!! Seriously one of the most fun things that I have ever done in Tucson. It would also be extra fun for people who are visiting Tucson. Our driver was awesome, everything is laid back, and it literally is just like a giant party while riding a bike! They even had a little tablet with Spotify connected so you can pick exactly what you want to listen to. So awesome.

Jacamo's offers great pizza and a broad menu of sandiches, salads, etc. The pizza is the crowning glory of this restaurant. They have several locations. The quality control at all of the ones I have been to has been excellent. The crust is tasty, the variety of toppings is expansive, their attention to special orders is impressive. If you like beer, they have a good selection of that, too. Family friendly and able to handle large groups. Given the quality of the food and the friendly service, the prices are extremely reasonable.

First of all, I'm very surprised by some of the negative reviews on here.  I suppose no place is perfect and every once in a while they might make a mediocre sandwich... but I haven't experienced that yet!

I highly recommend Lenny's cheesesteak.  It's fantastic and, in my opinion, better than Pat's or Geno's down in the city.  I also love Lenny's regular hoagies, when I'm not in the mood for a heavy cheesesteak sometimes I'll split a turkey hoagie with someone.  The seasonings they add to the sandwich take it up a notch compared to other delis.  They use fresh Conshohocken Italian Bakery rolls, which are fantastic in and of themselves.

Bottom line -- take it from a local Conshy guy, Lenny's is the best sandwich place in town (and one of the best in the whole Philly area!)

On a recommendation from my son I took my 2020 Subaru to Cutting Edge for window tinting. 
The owner is knowledgeable and very nice. 
They were on time and did a fantastic job. 
Their office and shop were super clean too. 
I would definitely recommend their service. 
And what a difference the tint makes on my windows, love it!!

I find it difficult to rate a chain, but this location is one of the closest to me, although not much a coffee drinker, I do visit more than the others.  I have never had a poor beverage from this location, and recently they started serving limited gluten free treats.  I spotted a wrapped 2pk of chocolate cookies in the case yesterday. The USA menu is coming up here, just slower than molasses.

They upgraded a while back and added power outlets. Handy in a pinch!

Yes, I definitely come back. And you should get a Starbucks card and the app for the perks. So easy to pay from my phone if I forget my wallet - heck even if I have my card or wallet. Gold stars! Earn beverage upgrades, and freebies. Nothing wrong with that.

I went to the County Clothesline to find a dress that my daughter needed for a photo shoot.  I had only yesterday to find as I needed to mail it to her in Vancouver so it would be there before Saturday.  One of the ladies there said there was a dress in the back that might be exactly what I needed.  She wnet to see but was told they couldn't take it out.  So I went to ask the manager Freda if I could see it.  I was told there was not way I could see it or buy it.  They could not bring out till graduation season.  It's March and many people start looking for grad dress way before this and since when do you refuse to sell something you have in stock.  So I will never return to County Clothesline nor recommend anyone go there.  The ladies on the sales floor were wonderful but as a manager Freda you are lacking.  So much for customer service.  Extremely Poor Service on the part of the Manager Freday.

Rita Barrett

I purchased the Groupon for a Brazilian wax from here.  I then read some reviews after my purchase (I know, I know) and so I was a little hesitant about going.  When I first tried to call to make an appointment (in the middle of the day on a Friday) I called twice - and no one picked up either time.  I called a third time and finally got in touch with someone.  I wasn't sure how busy this place was, so I asked if  they had an appointment that same afternoon.  The gentleman on the phone said that he could squeeze me in, which I thought was nice.  

I arrived at my appointment time and everyone was very friendly.  I was offered water several times and people were attentive.  The owner was the one doing my Brazilian and apparently he wasn't there yet.  I had to wait about 20 minutes (but I figured I couldn't be that mad, after all they did squeeze me in).  He was apologetic for his lateness and was very professional and polite throughout the wax.  Now, I must say, this was my first Brazilian, so at the time I had nothing to compare it to.  It was very quick, with no tweezing or anything and when I got home I noticed that I still had a lot of hairs in some of the hard to reach places.  At the time I was satisfied with how it turned out, but like I said, no standard for comparison.  At the end he gave me a punch card where I would get a free service after I had five punches or whatever.  So, it was time for another wax, and I figured I'd go back.  I called to make an appointment - this time a woman took my phone call.  She was extremely rude, and seemed like she just wanted to get me off the phone.  It was very difficult for me to even make an appointment, she was less than helpful and just tried to rush me off of the phone.  

Since I needed a wax, I had no choice but to go to your average little nail salon on the corner.  After having had a wax there (for 20 bucks cheaper, I might add) I realize my wax at this salon was less than par.  She spent much more time removing the hair, and made sure she removed everything, and tweezed afterwards to get any strays.  

So my conclusion is I will never go back.  They're expensive, rushed and rude.  For 20 bucks less I can go right around the corner and get better service, more polite people, and I can walk right in and get a wax.

I had high hopes for Praline Connection, having been recommended it by a couple of local people I had met in New Orleans, unfortunately my experience failed to live up to the expectation.
Prior to arriving at the restaurant, I called ahead to confirm that they were still open and to check if they were still serving the full menu (it was memorial day and another restaurant had ran out of many dishes, so i wanted to avoid disappointment). Upon arriving, we waited 20 minutes for drinks and our orders to be taken, even though there was as many staff as there was tables. When our orders were eventually taken, I was informed that much of the menu was unavailable such as shrimp, fish and strangely, french fries..
I ordered the gumbo, which was ok and the fried stuffed crab which was nothing special. The waitress got our order wrong and brought out two of the same dish, which I refused to pay for. 
Service can be just as important as the food and ours was poor. The food wasn't great and I was restricted due to unavailability, as a result, im giving two stars.

Nice selection of stock for internet shoppers.  However, either extremely slow or non existent return of emails and phone calls.  I was looking to spend my money there, but they couldn't get their act together to make a sale.  Plenty of other stores in the sea . . . their loss and another store's gain.

Family run, home cooked breakfast. Can't beat it. Don't let the line outside scare you.  It moves quickly and you'll be glad you waited. The home fries are the best around. Huge pancakes made to share. We love the chance to sit at the counter and watch all the action going on.
Great tacos, very delicious. I gave it 4 stars because it takes a bit of cash to get full. Other the. That their food is great and their special drinks are amazing

Love love love this place ! Great prices for the amount of food they give... I have never edited more than .15mins for an order. Customer service is awesome. Just wish they had online ordering but you can call ahead!

Third time going there.  There won't be a fourth!  
Chef is really lacking. I ordered a different dish each time because, I wasn't happy with my previous choices. Tonight I tried the Pad Thai, I know it's not a Thai restaurant you say, but I've ordered it in a different P.F. Chang's and it was delicious. 
It was my friends 70 th BDay and PF Chang's was so cheap, to offer it complimentary.  Terrible !

One of my favorite places to study for many reasons: 1. solid coffee and quick service 2. relatively spacious and quiet 3. wifi and lots of power outlets 4. decent to-go food options but lots of other food places nearby 5. Washington Square park across the street if you need a break 6. big windows for people watching if you're bored. Fairly simple overall but you shouldn't be too distracted while studying anyways :)

This was the best Po boy sandwich I ever had and the staff was very friendly. Also try the chilli with cheese, awesome. I forgot to mention the price was also great for the frugal people. 

This place was simply amazing!

This place should be five stars. Great service low wsit times for how busy it is. And very very big food portions for the money.This is a little hidden gem here repeat that honestly should be getting more attention. Think of any breakfast place you've ever been to on steroids. That's what this place is. Whole family loved it.
This is seriously a joke! The worse so called pizza ever! The crust is so tough, just not good enough to try again! Not worth the money!

When Home Depot first opened they were awesome. That was then, times have changed. This location insists on having almost every customer use there self checkout lane. I was here on a Saturday morning, busy time of day. One cashier with at least six people in line. I go to customer service to get rung up. The lady there gets an attitude but does ring me up...  

All these retail establishments that are going out of business have one thing in common, THEY DON'T HAVE ANYONE TO RING YOU UP. 
If i have to ring my self up, I may as well stay home and shop online....?? 

I no longer use Home Depot, as Lowes is less then two miles away.

The nail salon is located in a shopping center, so there is plenty of parking. Customer service is lack-luster. Not good but not bad. Plenty of color options, so that's a plus. Received a mani/pedi and it was done well. Again, nothing spectacular. Everything was ok. The final test would be to see how long everything holds up. Will return again and see if it offers a better experience.

First time and won't be last. Good food even when I did take-out and it took me a while to bring it back home then had to reheat. If it's still good then, then ya know it's on point when it's fresh out the kitchen!

I highly recommend this location! Staff is very friendly, and the doctor is very personable and down to earth. I was in and out very quickly too. Neal helped me get the best deal on a new pair of glasses. 5 stars!

I can't believe this is the best we can do for a seafood restaurant. The Brandon area is so lacking in choices and having to drive to Tampa or Saint Pete is a drag. Too many thing to criticize about the food the bowling alley back home was better.

Great store.  Huge selection of Chinese medicine in powdered and whole form. Teas and dried fruit and candies.  Chinese medicine has helped me maintain my health for many years now.  I consistently refer people to this store.

Wanted chipotle and this is the closest location to my house since the proposed hermitage one seems like it will never be built. Got here 3 mins after the time it said to be here and my food was ice cold, I'm not sure it was ever warm. They were very skimpy on the toppings, the west Nashville one is not by the way. I asked for fajita vegetables and got two bell pepper slivers and 3 onion slivers... Wanted sweet tea but they didn't have any so got the lemonade instead and it tasted alcoholic like it was old and fermented. I don't think I would come back to this location, definitely not when ordering through the app, I'd have to be able to see what they're doing if I came back.

Update! We had a great time. Relaxing, fantastic bartender, Smokey delicious wings traditional with sauce on the side ( seriously, they brine their wings, then smoke them, then season and flash fry) a traditional blue cheese parm wedge salad with real bacon and cherry tomatoes! Lots of laughs and a fantastic view! Eat, live and play with heart! Enjoy

Impressed with everything our group ate tonight. The lamb biriyani was tender and the rice was perfectly cooked. The chicken Shawarma was tasty. The Mshakal (Iraqi meat) platter was outstanding with falafel and chicken. All platters were HUGE and had amazing rice, salad, and fries (which surprised me!). Very enjoyable and will be back.

I have been coming to Supreme nail for over 14 years. The customer service is always fantastic. And I have never had a problem with my nails. They totally reinvest to keep the shop fresh and new. I would highly recommend getting your nails done here.
Amazing food, super prices and friendly staff! Accidentally found this place and so happy we did!

1st time visit with my family because I saw a lots of positive reviews here. There's limited free parking lot in front of the restaurant. BYOB, Staff is OK but you needs to ask if you need to Order again or refill your tea ( Surprised that House Tea is not complimentary ). Clean environment ( Including Toilet).

The quality, tastes, presentation of the Sushi & Sashimi is not that good. Sashimi is not that fresh (Specially the Salmon & Tunna) & small portion, Red Clam sliced very small. Hot & Sour Soup was good, Shanghai Roll not recommended ( Tastes Like Vegi Roll ), Hot foods served hot. 

But for All You Can Eat less than $25 per person , what can you expect. At least my tummy was full:) However, I would prefer any others places better than here.

Don't too high expectations. At the end, I feel a bit disappointed.

Awesome flavorful food and fun location. My family and extended family went on a Sunday night and sat outside. Everybody else had been multiple times and I didn't know what to expect...

I was a little surprised by the Sauce self service vibe but didn't mind it. There was a smidge of atmosphere missing despite being about 40% full. 

Despite some functional and atmospheric quirks the food was top notch and I can't wait to go back. My kids and rest of the family all thoroughly enjoyed our meal and service.

I've only been once - the burger I ordered was good - but the pizza my partner ordered was burnt to where I can't believe they even served it. 
Waiter acted very depressed and not attentive. 
I would try it again still but I don't want that same waiter and hopefully the Food won't be burnt

Terrible service. The place also smells really bad. 

I could get over the bad smell if the server wasn't so rude.....go to Manny Browns down the street. They're a much more pleasant spot.
Great notary. Judith is absolutely wonderful, very personal and accommodating, willing to stay late. Prices are very reasonable. I won't use anyone else.

Ratchada is the most special restaurant in Philadelphia to me and my husband. They hosted our engagement party and catered our 11-person wedding during the pandemic. The food is always incredible and fresh and delicious, and the chef is so kind and generous. We are always referring people to Ratchada! It is far better than Kalaya, if you ask me!

The thing about living off of Magazine Street is I live dangerously close to a lot of super places. I've been here a bunch and if they have the Wedding Cake or Lemon Meringue flavors in the donuts - that's what you want. I can sometimes find it's too much donut and am grateful when I have a buddy to split another kind of treat with. Their chicken biscuit is tasty. The sliders would go great with a beer styled brew but the brew they serve here is of the coffee variety. You can go to Charcoal's and pick up an adult beverage if you like.

This is definitely a destination to consider whether you live here or are visiting here. It's popular so prepare for lines on the weekend. It's not cheap either as some donut selections are basically $3. It's clean, the staff is professional and there's a bunch of cool retail around there.

First. The good was great ! Especially for the price you pay.  Everything was prepared perfectly. Our server was warm and attentive .  


A little in the noisy side. If your looking for a nice date place and want to have a conversation not the best ambience for a dinner date. 

All that being said, I will be back.
Great place!!  Very nice atmosphere and tasty food. We ordered 3 types of tarts, they were really good!

DO NOT GET BREAKFAST HERE! NASTY NASTY NASTY!!  They use pre-mixed eggs from a carton- I suspected as much when I saw the only way to have eggs, which is 90% of their breakfast menu, is scrambled. When I asked about eggs to order, waitress said they were "pre-mixed due to airport health regs." Really? Eggs in shells are more dangerous than hamburger meat???
Even worse-- everything had the texture and heat of being PRE-MADE AND MICROWAVED!!  Eggs were tasteless and rubbery, too dense and dry like pre-mixed carton eggs tend to be; potato wedges were hot and crispy- and so bland that no amount of salt and pepper could make them appetizing; my bacon was cooked through- but served cold and rubbery- I suspect it was the middle-of-the-plate microwave missed area.  I'd have sent it back, but it's still bacon, and we had a plane to catch. Only good thing was the whole wheat toast- high quality bread, real butter and jelly in little packs.  Only problem- ONE FRIGGIN' SLICE OF TOAST PER MEAL?? How cheap is that?  Coffee was mediocre- and at 4 bucks a cup, very, very sad. The breakfasts were 8- one coffee equals half a full platter?
My wife had a cheese omellete- same thing- really melty cheese incased in a yellow rubber jacket. My son's egg scramble was same, only with warmed generic sausage patties.
To make it all worse- waitress kept upselling.  "Would you like a fruit cup with your stale microwaved overpriced crap? How about a jacked up bottle of water so you can keep feeling screwed as you sip it on the plane when they offer you free drinks??"
Next time- we brave the line at Starbucks. 
And Shulas- we will never, ever set foot in one of your restaurants anywhere, at anytime.  Every location reflects your chain- your chain must be total sh!t, based on our experience here.

We went in on a Saturday morning. My only complaint is that you can't book appointments in advance, but you can check in online or call to add your name to the waiting list. 

It was fairly busy. We were 3rd and 4th in line and we got there right at opening time. The family before us called ahead to be added to the waitlist. Definitely worth it to call ahead or check in online for the waiting list before heading in,

We waited about 25 minutes but could've left to shop at either Kroger or the stores next store and come back. About 10 more ppl came in while we waited and during our haircuts to check in.

My actual haircut took about 5 minutes but I was just getting a simple trim. We were both satisfied with our haircuts. I did catch the names of either stylist but they were both friendly.

I've gotten sushi from this location numerous times, it's always super fresh and delicious! They have numerous specials and too many rolls to count. Their miso soup is to die for, I always consider ordering a gallon to go. I'd recommend any sushi lovers to try this place.

Dr. Early's practice is the place to go when you need compassionate and experienced care. From the first interaction with Charlene, the office manager, I sensed she was a real person with empathy for patients' needs. I saw Dr. Dannenbaum and recommend her without reservation. She will put you at ease from the start and will listen carefully and provide the care she thinks will help you. This is an office with the highest standards for patient care and wellness. 
Good luck on your journey to get well and stay well.

The airport has  done away with short term parking and now you have to pay $22 for anything after 30 minutes. I complain to the Nashville airport authority and basically all they said is that we can charge what we want to

I really wish yelp would let us rate  businesses with half stars, as I would rate Gold-N-Silver Inn.  My In-laws really liked the place on a previous visit, and after hearing about DDD coming here (it's all on the walls and on the menu) I was really looking forward to seeing what the hype was about.

With all of the business that has seemed to generate for the place from DDD, I would think they would throw some money into improving the looks of the place.  It looks like old inside and out. But it's really the food and maybe the clientel that make people come back.  I thought the food was good, but not great, but that doesn't necessarily mean I won't come back.

I will come back because I'm the type that likes to eat breakfast at any time of the day and that is definitely what they offer and it's a huge menu.  Generous portions for all plates.  But after ordering ham instead of bacon on her plate, my wife still received bacon after stating it in her order twice made for a notch down. The rest of the breakfast food was good but not great.  The gravy for the biscuits was really good, but the biscuit itself was dry.  I went for the famous lemonade porkchops and they were different but also a bit dry.  The sauce was sweet and spicy to amend for the dryness of the porkchop, so they tried but it was more of a double into the gap, not a homerun.  My In-laws usually order bacon and eggs or ham and eggs so it's not hard to mess that up.  The waiteress did come around often to fill our coffee, so again the execution overall was really good, just not a big wow factor.

I wil be back for more breakfast items at all hours of the day and also for the tri tip sandwich that they are also famous for.

Don't go before 8 AM on Sundays.

Just had the worst diner experience here (and, really, how good can a diner experience be). Rude waitress who literally threw the plate of food at my mother after loudly complaining about how people are jerks, a cook who apparently has never seen what an omelette is supposed to look and taste like ( hint, you don't put 3 inch square chunks of onion in an omelette - I sent it back) and it took about an hour longer to eat the kitchen was so slow. The booth next to us broke a glass - they had to clean it themselves because no one else showed up to help.  On the way out, there was no one at the front cashier's desk - why? Both of the hostesses were across the diner chatting with each other. 

Guys  - hire a manager.
Stopped in here on the way to another restaurant. We turned around due to the smell! And so glad we did! This place rules! Brisket was awesome! Banana pudding.. ohhhh my Lordy!! Yesssss
I stopped in last night to have a drink with an old friend. We sat in the bar and had Kelly as our server. The food and service were both outstanding. I'll be back!

EDIT: 
I have to give this place props. My original review is below. I didn't voice my displeasure with anyone. I just went to eat my food. As I posted this, the assistant general manager came and sat with me. Heard my out. Genuinely listened and he got my dinner all taken care of! 

I enjoyed the food a lot. The environment is very hectic and stressful as a first timer. 
Staff and patrons make you feel rushed and you don't really have time to process the options available to you. The girls on the add on/sauce station are partially short tempered when you're just trying to match up the names to the items in front of you.

Ordered two beers and a gingerale from the bartender after standing there for several minutes without him acknowledging me.  He poured the two beers and then one of the people sitting at the bar had a problem with their bill so he stopped what he was doing to help them instead of finishing our order. When he finally got done with them he put the two beers on the bar and then brought over a glass of soda that looked like Coke. He said " We don't have gingerale so I mixed coke and sprite together which is what gingerale really is"?!?!?!?!?!?!. What kind of dope did he think I was?  I said I didn't want it and he didn't charge me for it.  The food was ok.  Got the Blood Orange grouper which was $28, it had a piece of grouper the size of a pack of cards.. kind of a ripoff. It definitely wasn't worth $28. My friend loved their burger and fries. The smoked fish spread was ok. Nice view from the outside seating and outside bar.
I have an appointment for next week, but  the girl on the phone was sooooo rude, putdown and snippy   I'm going to cancel..  don't feeling good about this place

Notice there are no review under 3 stars. Yep. The food is that good. Order a burger, order some fries, leave with left overs for two meals.

Not a girls place to eat so dont think date place.

The Cobb Salad is amazing! Had the blue cheese dressing and would highly recommend! The tri-tip sandwich is also great! Get the fries and add the bodacious fry sauce, it's totally worth it! The habanero bbq sauce is wonderful too. Spicy but full of flavor at the same time.
We were there for lunch. They were really busy with only one server, but you never would have noticed, she rocked it!
Delicious food. Awesome service. Truly enjoyed my Friday night dinner and the amazing bbq. I also got brisket egg rolls which was delicious!

My favorite craft cocktail bar in the U.S.  Seasonal cocktails that are so much more than the sum of their parts.  For example, the Jean Lafitte with Spanish moss lifted from trees in City Park; seriously?  Insanely good, tart, herbal, spring-infused, yet decadent.  Then our amazing and lovely bartender, Adrian concocted a few specials for us (it was our second night there and we admittedly were smitten), one of them was called the Green Door, a chartreuse-based cocktail.  Well, I don't know why they call it that because I renamed it Napoleon 1791 in my head.  Full of maniacal hope to take over the world, enforced equality under penalty of death, with the heaviness of the Gulf south in the summer, all cedar swamp, moss, mint, and citrus.  Truly extraordinary.  Go there now.

LOVED this place, but why no WiFi??? Took the star off for that. The coffees and pastires spectacular. They did charge me a $1 for a cut of plain hot water, which I thought should have been complimentary. 

If they got WiFi, would have been a top notch place.

If I could give this place a minus one star, believe me, I would,  don't know who is writing all of these "glowing" reviews but I must have been in some kind of alternate universe when I took my dog in there to see Dr. Samuels, what a fabrication specialist!
Just be very leery when going in to see this vet and whatever he may say that sounds a little off, do some checking, I did and we will NEVER go back

The food at Lung Wah has taken a nose dive over the years. When we first moved to the area 20 years ago, we would order at least once a week. Everything was prepared well and absolutely delicious. The food now is just a step above mediocre. Since the decline, we may go every few months as opposed to every week and stick to ordering the simple noodle dishes and the egg rolls. The General Tso chicken used to be out of this world many years ago. Now it seems like they use dark meat chicken instead of white meat and one piece of sautéed broccoli in an overly sweet and gelatinous sauce. So, try Lung Wah if you're in the area but don't go out of your way for it.

I am happy to say that my maintenance request was completed the same day it was entered. Our service technician Tom even followed up with me to let me know exactly what was done. He also said to reach out if my AC was not working up to par. You have a very great service partner in Tom. Congratulations on a job well done !

The voodoo museum was a great experience! We sat in and listened to one of the tour guides speak about voodoo history. He had so much knowledge and really helped me to understand parts I was confused about. It was nice to have someone speak on the history and meaning of voodoo. Would highly recommend this tour and the museum.

Oh, Nick's... It's been awhile since we've seen each other. Too bad it had to be on St. Patrick's Day :( 

I haven't been down to Dogtown for St. Paddy's day in quite some time and let me be the first to tell you that it made me feel, well, old! Did you know that if someone was born on/before 1989 can drink alcohol? Seriously? Ugh... 

Anyhoo, watching all of these young kids mill about the bar in their green getups made me want to go home to my sensible shoes and clean bathroom. Is that wrong?

I must agree with Stacey T and say that I can never get enough of the guy singing in the corner... And Nick's does serve as a good starting point for the St. Patrick's Day madness. But I doubt I'll be back anytime soon just to hang out. Sorry, I'm too old!

I went to Home Wine Kitchen last Friday with a group of girlfriends for dinner. 

HWK is located in Maplewood in the former home of Nosh. I LOVE what HWK did with the space. It has a homey, almost Farm House-like feel. Well...I've never exactly been to a farm, but it's what I would imagine one would look like! It was very rustic. I liked it. 

On this particular night, it was rather warm in the restaurant, but since I'm usually freezing wherever I go, it didn't bother me at all. I know a few of my dining companions were bothered by it, however. 

The menu at HWK changes every week or so. While there was a nice selection of appetizers, I skipped it since I wasn't very hungry. I just wanted an entree. 

I went with the Red Trout. It was accompanied by roasted red potatoes and spinach, and the fish itself was topped with pecans, sage, and brown butter. 

It was delicious. The potatoes were my absolute favorite; they were crispy, full of flavor, and had just enough salt. The fish was also very tasty. The portion size was more than enough; I could only eat about half before I was too full to continue. 

At $22 for my plate, it was definitely not cheap. I enjoyed my meal, but I don't know if I'd return for dinner. I noticed that they serve bread pudding from time to time, so I'll come back when that's on the dessert menu. 

HWK also serves brunch on the weekends. I have a feeling I'll be back for their chicken and waffles.

Veggie burger is beets based and a nice twist on this. Side salad with vinegarette dressing over seasoned but good sized portion.  Turkey pannini was delic bread was exceptional. Large seating area with minimalistic decor. Solid wood tables and very good, knowledgeable service. CASH Only so be prepared. ATM available up front.  Caesar salad kind of stingy on chicken and no croutons but otherwise tastee dressing and grated cheese.

This spot doesn't have the same hype as some of
the other spots in town, but it's possibly my favorite Mexican food in SB. Really, really good burritos. Tip: I recommend choosing only one of either sour cream or guacamole (or neither)- rather than both - in order to maintain the "bean density" of the burrito.

Pretty disappointed.  Got the double cheeseburger and super greasy and had a weird chemical taste. Fries were great but there must be 1,500 calories in them. All in it was like $17.00 for 1 person and a burger, fries and a drink. That's way too high-I won't be back.

Haha, why everybody is so negative with Southern Nights? Of course it's going to have some of the usual club headaches. Nothing new about that. Yeah, they have a cover charge after 9 or 10 or so. A lot of popular places do.

During COVID, they are trying their best at mitigating the spread. You have to have a seat and can't be standing for the drag shows. However, I'd consider it pretty crowded still so I'd advise taking precautions.

Every time I have gone, I have had a good experience. They always have good drag performances. There is always a crowd. And I think they are an essential part of the gay scene of Tampa.

#SupportYourLocalDragQueens
