We had a private party with a total of 22 kids, including our birthday boy.  It didn't matter how many parents came with the kids.  I added 4 extra pizzas for the kids and was asked if we wanted to add an extra pizza when we arrived.  I added it, but it was un-necessary since 4 would have been enough.  The drinks come with the party and there is an endless supply.  The cake was delicious and you can choose from a variety of choices.

The staff has everyone watch a safety video and then gets the kids pumped up before they enter.  Since the staff is young they have a lot of energy.  They needed it because they had parties all throughout the Sunday we arrived.  

The party is divided into 3 areas.  The first area  has a huge slide, a climbing apparatus, and a run and tag the flag inflatable.  The kids can also toss basketballs into a hoop.  However, they found the most fun in a hurricane booth.  This was not included in the cost but we were prepared and the other parents were happy to chip in.

The second area has a faux boxing ring and a bounce court with balls to toss into hoops.  You can toss foam footballs and balls into a large beanie bag type of box.  This area also has 2 large slides you can only get to if you climb up through a tall maze.  You'd think the kids would be scared of this in the dark but they all loved it.  Again, we had to pay for an air hockey table  but the parents all contributed if their child wanted to play.  There are Little Tyke cars and a massage chair in this room.  

Both rooms have benches for parents to sit but a lot of our parents liked watching their kids have fun and stand to talk with other parents.


When we got to the eating area it is nice, bright, clean, and decorated for a birthday party.  They add the balloons you requested and there is large birthday throne for the birthday boy/girl to sit in.  This is was a big draw for our son.  He loved the throne!  

They sit all the kids at one table and let the parents use the second one.  With 22 kids it was a tight fit but it was nice to have them together.  Anymore and I would recommend you use both long tables for everyone.

The place is expensive.  I scoured for a $50 coupon and I was glad to have found it.  However, it was a huge success.  Most of the kids had never even gone to a BounceU and the parents were really delighted with the experience.   This was an extra bonus to give everyone a unique birthday party.

Every child left with a gift bag, included, and smiles on their faces.  Great job BounceU!

This place deserves the 5 star rating because they really care about their customers and the time they spend.  I had two snafus...  I was promised they could blow up 30  special glow in the dark balloons but only got 10.  I think it was a case of money and title.  I was promised something from someone who wasn't entitled to give me free helium.   The 2nd snafu was that they forgot to put the all included (buy one bounce and get the second bounce free ) card into the gift bags.  I just don't think they make this mistake often so it was a little difficult getting my cards mailed to me so I could included them in my son's thank you cards.  They did eventually send them within a 7 day period.  

You'd think this would deter me from a 5 star rating but I just loved the way they handled things and their intentions are for you or me to just have fun and try to make it the best experience they can.

Because of YELP and the other amazing people who post on here I found my NEW FAVORITE RESTAURANT!!!!
I travel a lot for work and this was my first time in the area and the pictures of the food looked really good so I had to try. 
For dinner I got the Country Fried Stake Special and oh my gosh!!!! It had bacon jalapeño gravy with crawfish on top! 
I've never tasted anything so flavorful. 
The green beans and potatoes were SO good too!! 10/10 for sure. 
If I'm ever in the area again I will totally be back! 

This restaurant is not a chain and the people who work there are also fantastic!!

So incredibly disappointed with how my eyebrows turned out. It's always concerning when your esthetician says "it's so frustrating how eyebrows are sisters and not twins" I left in a hurry and didn't get a chance to look closely until I got home. My eyebrows are completely uneven and my right brow has a chunk missing!

Perfect location. Walking distance from our apartment in channelside. The wraps are yummy. My favorite is the grilled pork. They also have awesome smoothies. I got talked into trying the avocado smoothie and it's probably the best smoothie I have ever had. 

My husband and I enjoy going in there to just hangout and play games. I would definitely recommend this place especially if you live in channelside. The staff is great too.

Took the ebus from EDM to CGY on a sunday morning.

Pros:
Staff and driver were friendly
Cheaper option than red arrow
Convenient location downtown
Bus looks new, excellently clean and no smell
The one im in has power plugs on every row
Lots of space under the coach for the luggages
Has an overhead storage for your stuff but not so big
Ample leg space
5% discount when booked online

Cons:
Rough seats - like seating on a sandpaper sort of, had to wear my jacket for my skin not to touch the rough seat
Hard seats - like seating on a wooden chair
Refund/exchange policy seems unfair


Though this is not ebus' fault, my 4hr ride was not very pleasant due to a couple of inconsiderate passengers who were talking and laughing so loudly and watching videos without earphones. I tried to move seats but too late.

This place has a really good wings/beer combo. I got very hot and they were bomb! The beer is cheap too. It's close to campus so it's in a fun location. My friend got buffalo fries and said they were really good as well. I'll have to come back for more!

This place was recommended to us by a friend that found it on yelp. I'm usually a little apprehensive about all-you-can-eat sushi "buffets" because the fish is never as fresh and I can never eat my money's worth, but this was great. Everything was made to order. Food was always hot and fresh all at $21.95 a person, what a deal! 
Together my bf and I had 9 decent sized sushi rolls. We also had 3 hand rolls, one appetizer (the yakiton, a must get), and two tempura banana ice cream desserts (dessert was included). Everything was so tasty! I had to try everything, and now I can hardly breathe...but it was worth it. I would definitely go again if we ever came back Reno.

Disappointed of my Double Cheeseburger!!! My husband order Double Cheeseburger for me, for my supper, the tomato and vegetables are missing!!! He asked for ketchup, the lady told him they don't have ketchup. I feel so sad and the burger now taste so dry!!!

Beautiful ambience but unfortunately terrible food, have been there for both dine-in and take out, disappointed both times. Tried buffet lunch on a weekend, it was just an average food, the flavors and aroma was missing altogether.
Ordered their chicken biryani which was soggy n under cooked and again missing flavors. Chili chicken loaded with tangy, sweet gravy (btw, I ordered dry) not worth trying.
Btw, the food is not authentic at all, way too compromised in taste and quality.

We toured St. Louis Cemetery #1.  It was rushed, hard to hear, and gave us no time to look around.  As an American History teacher, I was a little disappointed.  The tour guide gave historical info in front of gas station with blaring music and traffic, he was hard to hear (and I have great teacher ears).  We had no time to learn about or take pics of or with historically significant tombs, such as the tomb of soldiers who fought the Brits in War of 1812.  He almost seemed inconvenienced giving the tour.  The tour was about 1 hr, with less than 45 minutes in the cemetery itself.

I've been to a lot of barbershops in Indianapolis looking for a place that compares to Jayuya barbershop in Chicago. Los Nitidos is hands down the best shop in Indiana. Anthony, Bori, Denny, Adrian, all of them can cut! It's a good shop with great barbers. You will always walk out with the haircut you want without a ridiculous wait. Even when it looks packed, it's not bad because they have so many barbers. There's always good music and sports conversations. Easily my favorite shop.

The food was amazing.  My first sonoran hotdog and it rocked! We had Jonathan as our bartender AND wait staff and we couldn't have been happier.  Come,  enjoy,  and ask for Jonathan and you will be happy.
No custimer service. Place is antiquated and if unhappy they do not even return a phone call, never again!

If you haven't done The Handlebar yet, you are missing out! This is a must-do in Indy! As you can see from all of the other reviews, it is clearly a favorite activity in Indianapolis. So, I am going to break down the top 5 reasons why I loved it: 

1. Our driver/guide was extremely nice and down-to-earth. He was very flexible with our last-minute stops (aka stopping suddenly at Monument Circle to take a group photo or at Mass Ave to take a bathroom stop)
2. You get to travel to all of the fun places located in Indy, such as Monument Circle, Mass Ave and more!
3. There is an aux cord where you can jam to your own music
4. Everyone walking on the streets/driving in their cars look at you with complete envy because they can see how much fun you're having!
5. And for all of you non-21 year olds, don't fret! You can actually be 18+ to ride it.

Tip/Reminder: You bring your own drinks and it cannot be glass! Be sure to bring cups.

I want to do this again ASAP- especially with the nicer weather coming this summer.

Called to set-up an appointment to get an est.for a new shower, sink repair and another repair. Was told that there would be a $75.00 charge for them to give me an estimate. I called two other plumbers and received free estimates. Picked the one that explained what he was going to do and why it needed to be done. Was very happy with the job they did very professional crew. $75.00 for an estimates. just aint right.............
Great ambiance if you are looking for food/bar/music. Had the hot chicken sandwich which was great. Not hot but you can spice it up. Also tried the green friend tomatoes which were good.
Really fantastic job! I always felt like my cats were in great hands. The communication from this team is spectacular. Highly recommend!

I'm giving them one star because of the dine-in service. We were seated, ordered... no problem. 40 min later still no food. Called our waitress over and set send a different girl over to our table. We couldn't get a straight answer on how much longer it would be. Finally, we just decided to leave.
I just adore Dr. Mat! His attention to detail and his ability to provide the best care imaginable keeps me coming back! The best of the best!

While at security check we were told the gate closed and plane leaves in 10 minute . We were directed to ticketing counter for accommodations. 
While at ticketing counter we were offered another flight three days later for additional fare of $119+. 

We left sad and disappointed

Later learned that our flight had been delayed by an hour. No one working at Frontier related this info to us. We could have made our flight ! Really.   

I called Priceline whom I purchased the ticket from and was put on hold for 45 minutes. No refund or adjustments made. This is terrible. We traveled two hours each way to and from the airport in Philadelphia. Ticket was purchased 1 week ago. 

Don't use Frontier airlines! They have young staff that are not trained and are very unprofessional! At the Philadelphia airport terminal. 

Update: I received a refund in Three days after Priceline called me at 12:40am. 

New flight purchased through Frontier on 11/16, lost bag when arrived in Dallas. Contacted the next day had bag in office. Note***Frontier is contracted with American  Airlines; they close at 6:00 pm; they don't tell you  this. There is bad staff , stood there picking her nails while passengers went through security line!

It's under the el. so what do you expect? my sandwich maker was arguing with the cashier for giving a fat 50 something customer a deal on 2 five hour energies. the man was relentless. all for a single dollar savings. anyway. they have falafel. the portion was huge. it was ok. what i expected considering the location. i also got a side of mac and cheese and the guy only charged me 6.50. the price was right. and the place was quick and near to where i needed to be. i'd go back for sure. the selection of sandwiches ranges from meatball parm to turkey club. they seem to cram it all in.

Totally impressed with this DMV. Sent my 18 year old in with a bunch of documents to renew her license and change her name (lots of paperwork) and get real ID. Lady was helpful, patient, NICE (is this a DMV???) and my daughter came out smiling. I highly recommend- and yes- make an appointment!

We have been to Oori about four times now and every meal and service has been exceptional. The wings are to die for, try every flavor you can! We also love the dan dan noodles and bulgogi lettuce wraps. Beautiful dining room too!

LOVE LOVE LOVE LOVE this place! I grab breakfast from here probably three or four times a week and calling ahead makes me able to walk right in and out and not have to wait super long for my food.  Bagels are amazing and the workers are all very nice.  Wish I could give more than five stars!

Every time I order at Nico's, I get huge portions, very careful considerations towards my dietary restrictions, and the chef is extremely accommodating to any additions I want to add to the food I order. On top of that, they have the best refried beans I've ever had.

And a special shout-out to all the amazing employees, especially Arianna, for all their patience.
The friendliest place here! We come here every time we're in the area. Must try the drunken shrimp!

Had the chicken ribs and chopped pork.everything was delicious.  Spicy sauce was delicious.  Greens kind of seasoned too hard with the rub.  Baked beans best I've had in years.  Will definitely be back

Stopped in at my sister's recommendation for a pedicure and to try the shellac manicure, and they were perfect.  Tony was nice, did a great job, and didn't rush through.  

I went in on a late Tuesday afternoon, and by 4pm it was getting busy, but the wait even then was only 15 minutes.  

The spa obviously has high standards for cleanliness, and I appreciated the individually sanitized and wrapped tools. 

Pricing was very fair, and I'll be stopping in again on future Nashville visits!
This is a decent local bar with okay food, drinks, and pleasant service.  Nothing extraordinary but a good place to grab a drink after work if you live close by.

This place is great! Brownsburg needed something beyond taters, burgers, and wings. I'm a serious pho fan and Jenny Pho did not disappoint. The service was excellent. The workers were prompt and friendly.

I highly recommend it.
Super Expensive. Don't waste your money. There's cheaper and better places. They think because your not getting out of your car they can charge more.

Wobbly One Star

As I brought my nieces in to purchase some candies for the road trip back this morning, we came in early in the morning around 11:30ish and the work stared us down as if we were going to steal a 10 cent piece of candy.. lol... 

We ended up getting some sunflower seeds covered in chocolate and 2 egg gummies. It totaled around $5.
Of course it'll be a little more pricey but that's not the reason I gave it a bad review. 

As we spoke in Chinese, our native language, she mocked us of it by repeating us and chuckling (a white lady who was looking over the store as the other went away). I don't find humor in what she did as she chuckled to herself so I proceeded to getting my card for payment. With her hands straight out in desperate agony of snatching my money, I took my sweet time. 

Lost stars because 
- Rude (racist if we may get into specifics) 
- Suspicious 
and we felt rushed.

The food is ok. Most you can tell is not homemade, just stuff from a restaurant depot. The real problem is customer service and cleanliness. The people here are RUDE. They don't know much about business. I called one time 5 minutes before they opened and the son refused to take my order. 

Worse - the father dropped his thongs on the floor, wiped them and still kept cooking with them. If he did that with me watching I don't want to know what they do when people aren't at the cash register. That's a healthy code violation!!!

Waited about an hour to get some cheesesteaks.. the gentleman at the cashier was very nice and personable. 

Cheesesteaks and fries were very good, great portion sizes, and enjoyed it. I don't like cheesesteaks that much but would try when in the area!
The closest to real Parisian French croissants in  NOLA.  It is all good.  Delish coffee too
Loud talking by obnoxious customers. Fox News on TV.  TWO STRIKES! Food is ok. Place needs a phone booth
They are always so nice and helpful! They spend the time to make sure you are happy with your new glasses and find just the frame you are looking for. I would definitely recommend!

Theatre and staff are great! They could deal with some better shows/acts though. But, I suppose that's an unfair statement from a New Yorker, what with Broadway and all. The theatre has great acoustics and there truly isn't a bad seat in the house. 

Oddly, their advertising is atrocious. I never know when they have shows unless I go out of my way to search. What's going on in their ad department? It's a theatre!

When I was a kid, Laser Quest was the absolute coolest place to celebrate a birthday or just spend a day shooting up your buddies with strange, blinding lasers.  I haven't been in a while, but I can tell you that this place remains cool no matter what age you are.

Sure, there are plenty of places to play laser tag, but Laser Quest is renowned for being the number one spot.  The course is pretty confusing, but that typically makes for better games, and (unlike at other places) I don't recall ever getting a gun or vest that was a dud.  The staff, though they always seemed a bit jaded about the whole thing, was typically pretty nice.  I like the fact that the course has randomly placed mirrors off which your lasers can ricochet.

Laser Quest is on Second Avenue, right in the heart of the tourist district.  This makes it a good spot for visiting families to pop in for some good clean war games.  The fact of the matter is that it's laser tag; as long as the guns work, you're going to have a good time.  They also have games like air hockey so you can kill time easily while waiting for the next match.  The place is also available for private events, so if you're a high roller who can afford to privately slaughter your friends with lasers, be sure to book this place.

Is there a Fresh Kitchen Addicts Anonymous group I can join? I eat here probably 3-4 times a week because it's just that good! It doesn't help that my office is within walking distance from FK, either. There's a running joke at my office that whenever we need a lunch location for a team or client lunch, everyone knows I'm going to suggest Fresh Kitchen! I'm not sure how something so healthy can taste so good!

Went here for restaurant week and thought it was a great choice. I brought an out-of-towner who is a bit of a foodie. She has tried some of the best NYC and DC has to offer, and it was nice to know Philly could stand up to her standards. Good food, wonderful service, and a great ambiance. They have a restaurant week drink menu which was nice, $6 for sparkling wine was perfectly reasonable and we couldn't resist. They also had bottles starting at $24, wine pairing courses, a huge book of drinks, and an option for a 7 course meal. We opted for the regular $35 RW deal.

FOOD.
-Excellent, but not the groundbreaking, life-changing meal I expected knowing how much they usually charge(maybe I should lower my expectations, knowing quality may suffer during restaurant week). For some reason I kept comparing everything to Pumpkin, which was my last really great meal, and Pumpkin won pretty much hands down.
-Everything was beautifully and artfully plated, and the waiter explained what everything was, which was lovely.
-The bread basket featured 3 or 4 different types of delicious fresh bread and came with french butter, and goat butter which was really good. It was hard to resist finishing the basket even though I knew we had 3 courses coming.
-Blue Crab Consomme-we didn't taste much crab, but the broth was good, the kale dumpling was really good and the pork belly was excellent.
-Japanese Sea Bass-the sashimi layered with pineapple was a great combination, very tender and fresh tasting, and the trout roe kicked it up a notch.
-Swordfish-perfectly crispy on the edges, but still tender in the middle, in a delicious broth, with hearts of palm, some greens, and other root vegetable cubes.
-Beef Short ribs- very tender and flavorful, went nicely with the mushrooms and the white chocolate grits were an interesting combination.
-The Apple dessert was sort of a deconstructed apple crisp and I really loved the thyme ice cream and crunch on top.
-Chocolate Coffee Mousse- really good, this was the only course where we thought one was better than the other. Light, fluffy, and with delicious crunchy cubes.
-They ended the meal with two tiny treats-a tropical chocolate, and some sort of gummy berry thing, both good.
-The portions looked small, but in the end we were very satisfied and not overly stuffed, just perfect.

SERVICE.
-Amazing.
-There seemed to be a lot of people waiting on us (several waiters taking our order, refilling water, bringing food, telling us, in detail, what the food was, taking our plates and utensils away without us even noticing like secret ninjas, etc.) but there was never any confusion or repeatedly asking us for orders like there often are at other restaurants when this happens.
-There was a bit of a long wait between courses, but not unreasonable, and it was nice to enjoy a long meal and work up a mini-appetite between courses. I think we took about 2 hours.

OVERALL
-Great experience and would love to go back for their 7 course, or raved over brunch, but not sure it would be worth the money if the quality of the food is the same. Maybe when I'm no longer on a student budget.
-Great view and ambiance, tables were not too close together.

Recommend for restaurant week or if you have money to blow, a date to impress, or have already tried a lot of other places for restaurant week and are looking for something new.

We love this place and go here pretty often when we are on the south shore. It's one of our favorite places. Everything I've had is good, and I always follow it with the waffle and green tea ice cream.

My 1 year old kitty had her first grooming with Keith. She is long hair and incredibly shy, and with Keith she did great! My first experience with a mobile groomer which is genius. I saved myself and my kitty a stressful car ride back and forth and all the waiting she would have had at a salon. I'm so very happy and shocked at all the fur he brushed out! Above all I'm just really happy my cat had a pleasant experience.

Terrible place, waste of time!!! After making us wait 2 hours for the banana boat, and informing us we were next in line, they lended all of the jetskis to people that had just arrived and told us we had to wait longer. Terrible customer service, evident that none of the employees enjoy working there. Avoid this place at all costs if you value your time!!!

I was taking a walk and happened upon this attractive building. 
Walking in, I was warmly greeted by the owner, Donny. 
We spoke a bit about when they opened and how nice it will be for all, when they can open fully for inside seating. 
I ordered a large coffee. I really hoped for some decaf as I had a couple cups earlier in the day, however that wasn't an option today. 
Well, I wish I had taken a sip before I left, as the coffee wasn't terribly hot. It was more than tepid, but not much more. 
I also think there should be more options for sweeteners, than just sugar. Also, disposable stirrers would be nice, since, cause of Covid times, it's all takeout. 
When able to stop in in the future, I will try this place again.

This is an interesting place for sure.   Part tasting room, part upscale dining.


The crowd is definitely of the middle-aged, well-to-do set.   It's also quite the cougar den.     40-50 year old women in high heels abound.

Food is decent, but not spectacular.   No real theme here.   Some Asian, some Italian, steaks, burgers, etc.    The only real standouts were the crab & lobster bisque and the complimentary pretzel bread. 

The tasting area is a bit of a mess, though.    It's Tony with room for only about 10 people to taste at a time.    Expect a wait.

There shouldn't be an option for a lower rating. This place is great. I ordered through Door Dash. I ordered a 1/2 sandwich and soup combo, a brisket sandwich, and a chocolate eclair. The 1/2 sandwich was pastrami. The soup was chicken noodle. Both were brilliant. The pastrami was tender, juicy, full of flavor. The soup best I've had. The brisket came with an onion jam and coleslaw on it. The brisket was pretty good. The eclair was a solid one pound. It took a couple of days. Overall this place is fantastic.

Tom is awesome as a carpet cleaner and the price is right. He uses a brand new cleaning system and truck, he's punctual and he's a nice guy. I'm not sure who wrote the bum reviews below but when I read them it seems like they wrote them below the wrong company because this guy is the truth.
Love this place, the people, and especially the Garden Calzone. I've even gor my coworkers hooked on this place DELISH!

Surprised to find a decent price offered for a great location; that's about where the positives end. The room is quite small yet functional (large bed, limited tv channels, good size bathroom but tub won't fill or drain right; walls thin; room has fridge and free WiFi. Keruig mini in room, too. Hotel room clean and acceptable; staff member at desk seemed annoyed at my initial questions at check in; a game was on tv in the bar/restaurant that the staff wanted to watch. Pool and spa CLOSED up, no business center, no gym, a boutique that's got few frills to speak of. Sigh. Staying here for work; average but overpriced for what you get--really you're paying for location. Would be cool if this place was haunted; would give it some mystique. It's just kind of mediocre. Pillows are nice and soft. Might or might not return. If they had a free breakfast it would be awesome; would make most people happy since NO pool. That's a bummer; I was planning to use it during off time for r and r.

OMG,  This made our vacation.  Our Captain Chip was fabulous.  He was funny, loads of information, grew up on these waters, has swam in the swamp , taught us so much about the alligators and when it comes to buying alligator products and last he is a fast and  fantastic driver.  He knows how to handle this beautiful airboat.  We we're blessed to have gotten him.  We saw 6 alligators, bald eagle,  turtle and loads of birds.  He took us in areas you can't even imagine  going down.  I highly recommend this family owned company.  Your not a number you're a guest.  Thank you Captain Chip and Captain Joey.  We will return.

It's in the Airport. It's as if your quality automatically drops due to inhaling jet fumes. The original is an Opus. A sweet dream of culinary greatness. TOP THREE meal of my life. That's how I sold it to my husband. The food at this location makes me eat those words and owe him "favors". His jambalaya was too tomatoey with no actual flavor but lots of heat. Plus he said the taste was of the burnt hard scrapings from the bottom of the pot. No Bueno. My neighbor who is 70 and dad was from NOLA makes better. Wayyyyy better and we can see actual seafood and bay leaves and it ain't burnt. Plus all we have to do is cut her grass or pull leaves or was her car to get it. The gumbo was good. Flavorful. A lil heat. I wanted a lil more in that bowl though. It was chicken, shrimp and sausage and each came through. The greens were spectacular to ME because they tasted like the West African style greens I make with tons of smoked meats and peppers. My husband didn't care for them, he was expecting southern style. I totally respect the flavor of the heritage coming through and served to the global masses. Ashé. Respeck.

My Bloody Mary was good as expected with the obligatory olives, green beans and celery. No horseradish but peppery flavor. Meh.

Some of the best wings on the planet. The pizza is great too. We live just a few blocks away and glad they took over where Tate's left off. They try very hard with customer service, but often struggle. I am sure they will get better and am excited for their future. Great wings!!!
Great place. Friendly staff and really good food. Everything tasted fresh and was cooked well. Good portions. Collards are some of the best in the area. Definitely will be back.

My boyfriend and I picked up Sandwiches from here traveling from San Diego to Big Sur and holy crap this did not disappoint. I highly recommend everyone stop in!! Also I showed up way earlier then I should've and was not mad because the atmosphere was so much fun! 10/10 would recommend

Relocating from a Dallas, Texas, I was referred by an orthodontist, as I was not pleased with any of the former dentists I went to.  I am truly grateful for the referral to Dr. Michell's practice for many reasons...the administrative staff is personable and efficient, the office setting is clean, up-to-date and appears to be state of the art...the dental team of Rhonda and Dr. Mitchell are FANTASTIC and put you completely at ease as they are gentle, competent and do REMARKABLE, QUALITY COSMETIC work.  Doctor Mitchell advises you exactly of the financials, what insurance pays and what my costs are prior to commencing work.  My next experience is for my dental cleaning and I just signed my husband up to be under Dr. Mitchell's care.  Whether you are a seasonal or permanent resident of Tucson, Dr. Mitchell is who I trust and recommend.

Me: "how many pumps are in that usually? 5?"
Barista: "I don't know, I just be pumpin'." 

Probably the worst Starbucks experience I've ever had. Baristas have very little knowledge of product and what's going on, everyone was very confused. They seemed adequately staffed in bodies, but not skill. Latte was marginal.

Awesome concept for a hotel. Motel setup redone with vintage pop look. Clean and well done rooms. Nice features like super comfy bed and big screen TV. Friendly, easygoing staff. They give you a free drink per guest at their bar by the front desk and offer free breakfast with good options and beverages. Dog friendly as well. Seemed very safe. Also they have a local version of Uber Eats that delivers to the hotel for free. Would definitely stay here again.
I love this place so much. The ambience is perfect & they serve Roberta's pizza which I sacrifice my lactose intolerance to eat.

Buddy Freddys is our family staple, when I don't want to cook, and the boys still want a buffet with breakfast options. A Buddy Freddys you can order the waffles all day long. If I order the waffle in the afternoon I want a piece of the french fried chicken.

The servers are always kind and responsive, they always get a good tip. The food is always good, and the fried chicken  is the best in Plant City hands down.

Buddy Freddys would be great for me if they could get new silverware and new plates. They also need a freshlook inside.

This place is great! It was crowded on a Tuesday night so you KNOW it's good. Service was decent and the food was PHENOMENAL. It definitely falls under the "new American" category. The atmosphere is casual. Families are welcomed and there is a kids menu. It's also a great place to get drinks with friends. There is a 21 and over section :)

THE. BEST. PIZZA. EVER!! I can't say anymore than this. I travel from 40 minutes away just to eat here w/friends after moving out of the area. 
To start: 
1.) Perfect crust - not too thick and not too thin, definitely not super chewy or gummy (which I hate); 
2.) Cheese! They have the BEST cheese mix - it's super melty and delicious; 
3.) Sauce - delicious! There isn't much sauce on the pizza, this is more of a cheesy type of pizza in the most perfect way.
*The cheesesteaks and buffalo wings are also really, really good.
Otherwise, the rest of the food is your regular pizza shop type of food. 

Grab a slice from here - you won't be sorry!

I was apprehensive about trying Mod Pizza the first time.  I thought 'just another chain offering crappy pizza.' Boy was I wrong!  Mod pizza offers personal pizzas and salads that are totally customizable to the customers' taste.  Their dough / crust is very hood.  The toppings are varied and of good quality. I'm very picky about pizza and so far Mod is the only place in town I find worth returning to.

My husband and I stopped here around 6pm on a Saturday night after deciding we had to try it, in spite of the poor marks on service fellow Yelpers had given Brugges. Unfortunately, we had a similar service experience, but the food was great!

We walked in and they were packed and there were people waiting.  The way it is set up we couldn't see beyond the main dining room- luckily I decided to peek around the corner where we saw there were 2 open seats at the bar and that's where we ended up for dinner since we didn't want to wait for a table. This place is seriously boho- it's almost dive-ey, but not in a fun way, more in a "lacking atmosphere" way.  

We had the Moules Frites for $20, where you get to choose mussels and 2 dipping sauces for your frites.  The mussels were good (had the Provencal), the fries and dipping sauces were outrageously good!  We got the garlic aioli and the sweet chili- I would eat this every day if I could- it is insane.  They had a good selection of beers when we were there- we had a flight and there were a couple of good ones.  We asked to try a sample of one of the beers that you can't include in the flight, and boy she did not like that.  She begrudgingly got it for us but was clearly not happy about it. 

As for the service, the staff comes off as a social club that you are not invited to.  They seem more concerned with their own conversations and jokes than anything else. I even heard one of the girls (not sure if she was a server or hostess) talking poorly about some people that had come in. The bartender warmed up to us after a bit, but still wasn't very welcoming.

If I lived in Indy I would probably come here to get the frites to go, but since I don't I won't be visiting again, was a one-and-done experience for us. Indy has such a rich culinary scene that I would rather go somewhere else with better atmosphere and service.

I have been a member here for many years, but did not realize the resourcefulness of this library until I was a teenager. 

First things first, the staff here are amazing. They are extremely helpful and always kind. 

The library has improved greatly over the years and I find it to be very organized compared to other library's I've visited. The sections are clearly marked and they have a huge selection of books, movies, video games, and other typical library items (including cake pans)! 

Unlike the other reviewers, I have never found the noise to be a disruption to my reading or studying.
It's really good and the prices are fair! The employees were really nice and the mango juice is to die for. A lot of vegetarian options too!

I particularly stay away from pasta restaurants mainly because they all taste like chef boyardee in a can    This place certainly lived up to that expectation    They were unable to handle our big party even though the menu was agreed upon a week in advance ....  bartender didn't show up to work    Took forever to get a drink and the food tasted like it came out of a can........ American Italian style restaurant continue to receive bad reviews from me cause they are just that..... bad...... if you love them then I can only believe you've never had great authentic Italian food...... cause this place is neither authentic or good

I've dined here twice (without giving them the courtsey of a reservation, for which I apologize) and each time the front-of-the-house has been very helpful and accomodating.  Very charming building and decor.  Good wine list.  Beef short rib with vegetable ragout was a great fall dish and was well prepared.  Had the seared scallop salad on my second visit and was equally pleased.  I would advise against dining on the balcony at night; the city installed an obtrusive floodlight that shines directly at the restaurant (quality service from the city of New Orleans...).  Indoor seating is intimate without being pretentious.

This place is unbelievable. Been in there a few times. Just moved to this side of town. Two days ago I buzz the door to get in and some black lady met me at the door with her attitude demanding my ID. Told me I had to let her see my ID else she would not let me in. I told her I had s Dotty's players club card. She with her attitude demanding my ID. So I showed it to her. Cashed in some change for a dollar. Played and lost. Not once was I offered something to drink. But I had to listen to her and her friend talk about her boyfriend the whole time. Thought about spending more but decided against it because of her attitude. Next day decided to back in there but got a message on my phone. Same lady moves up front and watched me while I was in the parking lot chatting with someone. Today I buzz the door I am let in. I choose aachine to play I see the same lady peaking around a door frame in the back like a couple crack head. Then I sit down she comes out questions about what I was doing the night before. Said I was acting suspecious. Said I could not talk on my phone out in the parking lot. I told her suspecious is not a crime and she can not tell me what to do. She said yes she could and she can have me thrown out. I informed her she hasn't rights to tell me what to do and get out. I left and I told her I would be contacting corporate today. All the other staff are really nice. Now I see why it is dead in there when she is working.

Food was great. Service was terrible. 

We made a reservation to have brunch at Willa Jean because we knew it would be busy. When you walk in you are greeted by the bakery which had a wide selection of pastries and breads. Deeper into the restaurant they have seating at tables as well as at the bar. 

We were seated promptly and we waited a couple of minutes for our waiter. When the waiter "greeted" us and took our drink orders, he didn't crack a single smile and did not make an effort to even make eye contact with us. This continued throughout our entire experience. A small bug flew into my friend's water and we asked for a new one and our waiter looked at us as if we had offended him. Lastly, if that wasn't enough, when he came back with our checked he literally plopped it into the middle of our table and just left... There was not a single attempt at "faking till you make it" with this guy. We looked around at the other waiters as well and noticed they were just all in a bad mood except for one probably one person. 

But the food was amazing and saves this place a few stars in my review.
Corn bread: YES! Extremely decadent and moist -- more like a corn pound cake. Perfect blend of sweetness and a hint of saltiness. The shrimp and grits were amazing as well -- they give you nicely sized pieces of shrimp and it was the perfect start to a busy day. 

Overall -- great place for food, not so much if you're looking for a friendly atmosphere.

First time at this Juan's location and I think I prefer it over the others. There's way less traffic, more parking, and it's a better place to just go to have a casual dinner.  We got seated immediately when we got there which was great. 

I ordered the Juan's Tacos with chicken. They were sooo filling which was perfect because I was starving by the time I got there. Our food came out really quick.  Our server was great with answering any questions and getting us what we needed. 

I definitely want to go try out their happy hour one of these days!

This is the perfect example of how simple some things should be. When I go into a doughnut shop I expect a lot from just a few things- great, fresh doughnuts, serviceable coffee, and a lack of judgement. Shipleys gets all of these right and I love it. Their cake doughnuts are second to none and should be tasted by any lover of fried morning cake. Their Apple fritters are also crunchy and satisfying. A friendly, non judgmental face stuffs these and other mouth watering treats into a box and charges me a criminally small amount for a dozen fresh shame-holes. The atmosphere is small town, no frills, and just right; it's the exact opposite of a Dunkin Donuts where those places feel like a Starbucks with diabetes. Shipley dispenses with formality, keeps the old school donut shop, and passes the savings on to me. They're open at five and stay open until they have no more doughnuts to sell. I would image that could be at 5:30. Better get there early.
Coffee wasn't very good. Doughnuts were on point. Line goes fast. Fun place that everyone has to go to.

they are unprofessional they hung up on me 3 times and put me on hold more than 4 times because they didn't want to accept the fact they messed up my order i pre paid with my card and they delivered to the WRONG ADDRESS and i clearly told them the right one i was called by two different numbers one telling me they were going to send one out and then later another one saying that they are not going to send anything at all they ignored me because they didn't want to hear what i had to say they are rude and i kept a calm tone the whole Time they said the money would be returned and i would like to speak with the manager but they won't even answer my calls very low place

Theses are my kind of people. Pizzas are wonderful and service is warm & friendly. 
I am a long time patron of both the Holy Tomato ladies and the curmudgeonly Alfred from legend. I like their style better. 
Go. Eat. Get the house salad and don't be afraid of a Chicago-Clam & Parsley. Trust me.

Two words: MOLE ENCHILADAS!....I came with a large group so we had a catered affair with limited items but everything we had was tasty. Those mole enchiladas, though? Mmmmm! Good stuff!...Get 'em. Go 'head. You won't be disappointed. 

What adds to this restaurant's charm is their decor. A little kitsch. A lot of Mexican art. A cameo by El Moz. What's not to like?

Best part? The service was on point! The gentlemen who work here were fast, friendly, and courteous. I appreciated them a lot (I'm just embarrassed I can't recall any of their names). Even when it was after closing and we still had a lot of people still chismeando, they didn't kick us out. Thanks, fellas.

Overall? Good food. Great service. Cool spot. I dig it.

Pointe Pest Control is a great company that we have had for years.  They use non-toxic sprays and methods to keep pests out of your home and off the perimeter outside.  We love Eric who takes care of everything for us and he is always through and smiling.  Eric and the company work with our schedule and we have complete confidence in them to keep any pests away.

Are you sick of Starbucks? Does the idea of a quiche make you feel like a million bucks? Get your butt to Lighthouse Coffee. This is a small town coffee shop that is locally owned. The inside has a hipster feel. They have wooden furniture, couches, coffee bar and a chalkboard menu. They also have a drive through which is convenient.

Not many positives to say about my experience at this dealership. I was pushed to make a deal and put a deposit down for two days and once I did I was left without contact for 24hrs before reaching out to finalize this deal. Being in sales, I first hand understand the importance of communication and organization in the selling process. This is obviously something they are dropping the ball on. Never in my life have I purchased something that is thousands of dollars and not had the salesman present to deliver the product. When I arrived at the dealership to finalize paperwork my salesman wasn't even there. In town on business and found this close to our hotel. If you are looking for authentic Tex-Mex, this is your place. 
They start you with fresh corn chips and salsa. It was good but we ordered the queso fundido as a starter. Usually you will get white queso with a little bit of chorizo, but at Chimi's they like to put the fun in fundido and it was loaded with chorizo, corn and fresh jalapeños. They give you a spoon to serve it out on the appetizer plates, but you might be better with a trowel and I mean that in a good way. The dip was good. 
Next I followed my rule of going with their specialty when I hit up a new Mexican place and as the name implies they offer a lot of chimichangas. I ordered the chipotle chicken plate. It comes with white queso, refried beans, rice,guacamole, sour cream and pico. I'm always interested to see what "chipotle" means. I've had some that tastes like warmed up salsa and sometimes ketchup, but I think Chimi's gets it right. It had the right amount of spicy and smoky flavor and I really enjoyed it. I would also note that it wasn't ridiculously huge. It actually came out smaller than I was thinking, but it was still plenty to eat. 
As per my rules, I can't give Chimi's a 5 star review because they serve Pepsi - aka - the Devil's drink. As much as I enjoyed the frosty anti-freeze colored Mountain Dew, rules are rules and 4 stars it is. 
If you're staying near the airport Chimi's is close by and worth the drive. 
Enjoy!

My Standardized Yelp Ratings
5 stars - This is for a place that I see as one of the best at what they do (steaks, sandwiches, BBQ, seafood, etc). 5s are for places I've been several times (typically) at least and never had an "off" experience. The food quality, service, price and atmosphere are all going to meet or exceed expectations.
 
4 stars - This is for a place that is good, I would drive a little out of the way to go, and the food and service is good, but maybe not amazing. Also for me, this could also be a great place that serves Pepsi products - automatic 1 star loss - bad management decision. 

3 stars - This is for a place that I view as standard. Nothing special, nothing lousy, not a place you'd avoid like the plague, but a place that is not one you really look forward to either. 

2 stars - This is for a place that had something go wrong or something perpetually wrong. The food and or service is likely consistently suspect here (they probably serve Pepsi too).

1 star - I can't see wasting time writing a review on a place that gets a 1 star. This is for a place that should consider closing.

This review is for the Ice Cream only since I did not try any of the Mexican food.

I found this restaurant with an unusual combination of specialties through Yelp!  Located in Nora just a bit west of North Central HS, I was able to grab a parking spot in the communal parking area south of the restaurant.  The big square dining/serving area has plenty of room and many tables for guests.  The ice cream selections on hand are posted on a board behind the counter.  

Several of the selections have names that were hard for me to guess the flavors, so I asked for a sample and that made a big difference.  As a result, I went with the White Russian and with the Mamey combined in a bowl.  

The White Russian is mainly a chocolate base but it seemed to have hints of mint and coffee as well.  When I asked the owner, he said think Kahlua and it made more sense (I have never had a White Russian cocktail, so it never hurts to ask.)  Very tasty and smooth.

I also had the Mamey.  This one reminded me of a creamy cookie dough.  Boy, were my taste buds off.  The Mamey is a tropical fruit that has a subtle flavor that I have read described as a baked sweet potato.  It was delicious too!  The texture was just a little different, so that is probably where I got the notion of cookie dough.  

When I discussed the ice cream with the owner, he mentioned that all the ice cream is made in house, not through some outside vendor.  Credit for that!  

For two large scoops in a bowl, I still spent less than $5 including tax.  Great price and even greater flavor!  Highly recommended.

Should I go out of my way to Nathaniel Reid Bakery? This is a question I asked myself for a couple years. I had friends that just raved about the place. When my wife and I moved to Crestwood were were close enough to the store that I decided to take the plunge. 

The first thing you need to know about the bakery is that timing is everything. Some of the more popular items will sell out so if you have your heart set on anything (e.g. Kouign Amann) you need to commit to going to early. There are often lines, but they move pretty quickly. I try and go on a weekday rather than Saturday when the lines are the worst. Note that they are close on both Sunday and Monday. 

The second thing you need to keep in mind is that everything is delicious. Don't lock yourself into only one or two things. To my wife's chagrin I tend to splurge a bit whenever I go. She initially protests, but I never hear a complain when we have an extra almond croissant or two left over for the next day. 

Okay, so the most important part of the review, what should you get when you go? I tend to go early in the morning so I buy items that can serve as a breakfast treat. This means I primarily get Croissants, Kouign Amann,  and Four Cheese & Honey Focaccia. For the croissants I like the almond ones more than any others. They have the right amount of sweetness and are delicious. 

Beyond the pastries I have tried some of the savory selections. The Prosciutto Sandwich and Roast Beef Sandwich are both very good. These tend to be rare purchases for me just because of how early I typically go to the bakery (8 am). I've never tied a quiche sandwich, but I have a friend that raves about them. 

I've also purchased several of the specialized cakes (Ruby, Guyana, etc.). These are gorgeous and make for a stunning visual presentation. The couple times my young son has gone with me he always asks for one of these. They are quite good, but overall I've enjoyed the bakery goods more. These make for statement pieces if you want something that is visually appealing or a small treat for a special occasion (e.g. anniversary) but I generally skip them in favor of more croissants or kouign amanns.

Yes this could be considered a dive bar but that is the kind of bar I like. Cold beer check, friendly conversations check a good bartender check plus the food is good. I went with the Sheppard pie very tasty and a big portion. The daytime bartender knows how to pour a perfect Guinness so go on over and enjoy.

Panera makes it easy when they have a long line. The food was tasty and healthy. you cannot go wrong with their broccoli soup. I also had a turkey club. They have a large assortment of teas that is serve yourself and fountain drinks. A fun little place to walk around and see some neat street art if you like interesting art.  Its free and nice on a lovely day.

Tried this place out about a month ago for the first time, and now I'm hooked. The late night happy hour is amazing. Chips, salsa and guac are a must. The portobello taco is my favorite. The ingredients are all so fresh, and the service is great.

Love this place! The great fruits and vegetables are amazing and the meat selection is on point! Want fresh ground beef? They got it. Want T-bone steak cut to your thickness? They got it. Get the app to save on weekly items, always includes meat items. Don't forget to stop in for the best tacos in Indianapolis, just head inside and turn right!

I didn't love the double chocolate cookie, but it wasn't bad at all. It just wasn't my favorite. The chocolate cherry scone was much better, though I could do without the American style of coating it with sugar. Even so, it was tasty and I'd get that one again.

This is a great little restaurant. If you can knock it for anything, it's probably the bread, which is pretty dry and plain. It's also a bit pricier than it probably should be... $18 for spaghetti and meatballs seems a bit over the top. All that said, the atmosphere is comfortable, the wait staff is excellent, and the food (especially the calamari app) is top-notch overall. There is a desert that has a cookie on top of a brownie topped with ice cream that is pretty, pretty, pretty good. Given how small the space is, you'd be smart to RSVP.

My husband and I were on our way back from Santa Barbara and found this place on yelp.

Read the reviews all the photos we said let's give it a try.

The sat us quickly ,we were there on a Sunday morning.

He got the veggie omelette and I got the Montecristo sandwich, which is probably the best breakfast sandwich I've ever had in my life.
Who would've ever thought that to French toast with eggs and ham and cheese powdered sugar and syrup would be so divine.

Everyone was super friendly ,our waitress was so nice and helpful and the food came out super fast & super hot .

I highly recommend this place to anyone that lives in the area or is just passing by or just wants a nice trip to Santa Barbara for a great breakfast come here, We will be back & hopefully soon

If it was up to me, they would get no stars. This is the worse company I've ever worked for. I've been working there for 4 months and they only paid me twice and haven't paid me yet for my mileage. When I call HR they always tell me I'm going to get my check but never received it. They had the audacity to fire me because I didn't show up because they haven't paid me. No one works for free this is 2019. This company needs to get shut down asap and if there was a petition to sign to shut this place down I would be the first one to sign it along with many others. If you're thinking about working here DONT

Alert the media...it's finally safe (and delicious!) to head back to The Hog Pit on Tanque Verde!  Amazing how a change in ownership can make a world of difference.  After steadfastly avoiding the place for the past couple of years, we decided to give it another shot (the Under New Management sign was calling our name, because after all...what's better than really great BBQ!).  Had to return the second day just to make sure the previous day was really as delicious that we thought...and I'm happy to say that  we were right!  

Have only tried the pulled pork and sliced brisket sandwiches so far, but I'm sensing the entire menu is going to be as good.   Had the same waitress on both occasions, and she was quite sweet (and organized, something I've always liked in someone in the waitstaff biz).

So a hearty welcome to the new owners and keep up the good work!

Every time there is a major TV event, this company can't handle it. First it was the Oscars. Total darkness for the first half of the broadcast. People in town with Charter said they had no problem with the broadcast. Now it's the Olympics.  During the day, no problem. At night, when large numbers of households are probably trying to watch, it cuts out for large periods of time. Good job, Direct TV. I'm sure nothing will change.

So much information packed into such a tiny space.  I wish I had more time to truly explore this museum.  I could have easily spent a day just really reading and exploring all of the artifacts.

I walked by on my way to brunch and I was immediately intrigued.  On my return, I decided to swing inside to see what it was all about.  

Fair warning:  If you get queasy or uncomfortable around blood, death, "ghastly" images, just the human preoccupation with serial killers, or are toting children with you, do yourself the favor and go shopping down the street instead of walking through here.

You cannot take any photos, but there are so many exhibits featuring different killers or incidents that you really could just spend all day absorbing it all.  Very informative, but quite tiny, so when there are lots of people, you don't always get the time you'd like for each of the exhibits.  The old videos definitely give you the sense of the macabre and add to the vibe of the place.  I only wish there was more space to really enjoy what's going on here, and give them more to elaborate upon.

Each time I go to Nesso, it seems they outdo the experience they provide my small group.  It's like they keep all the things that are great (food, ambiance, and SERVICE), and then add more.  On our latest visit, we got to check out the new patio (with a cover that opens and a fire pit!), try a new "Red Pop" that is house made and bottled with multiple kinds of booze (nothing else!), and were introduced to Chef Kawika Pieper who brought out a dish of Rabbit Terrine to try as a future item (Oh MY!!!)  Everything is first class and served with a smile.

Of course, we always ask for our favorite waiter in town, Brandon D who greets us at the door when we arrive and seats us on the quieter side of the restaurant because our group likes to talk and be able to hear without shouting.  That is greatly appreciated.

We started off with the Burrata with an extra side of buttered and toasted semolina sourdough.  After patiently waiting for my photos, Brandon then broke down the cheese ball so that it would be easier for us to spoon on to our sharing plates.  This was so delicious!  It comes with a cherry tomato conserva, red wine candied onion, and pesto.  (see photo)  We knew we were in for a special night when it started this good.

We ordered cocktails, my friend ordering a "Balanced Martini" that was excellent and smooth, while I got the Pearbarbaro which was sweet and like a pear juice with a bit of alcohol.  Very nice!  Our wives tried the Red Pop and were surprised at how easily they could sip that like a soda!  

We ordered a variety of antipasti dishes which we all enjoyed (see photos), and while waiting for our entrees from the Primi and Secondi, the chef brought out the Rabbit Terrine.  Only two of us had tried rabbit before but nothing like this.  It was served seasoned and deep fried with a light crust along with some prepared radishes (sorry I can't recall the type and procedure), some greens with little white flowers, and a spread of delicious flavor on the plate.  (no menu to look at for the details yet)
There were four small pieces maybe two bites in size.  I speared one with my fork and it was so tender, that the terrine fell apart.  It was literally fork tender.  And the flavor?  Wow!  Light and juicy like the best dark meat of chicken you've ever had.  Wow!  The radishes were cold and prepared so tender that I didn't have to chew them.  I could crush them with my tongue!  The meal with the exception of the greens, seemed to melt in my mouth.  I gave a resounding "Yes!" to adding this to the menu soon.  

For our entrees, I went out of my comfort zone and ordered the Calamarata (lamb sausage with noodles, Calabrian chile, labneh, pesto, and oil-cured tomato.)  Although I'm not a big fan of lamb, I had no trouble finishing my plate.  The complementary flavors seemed to carry the day as I got further into the dish.  

Of course, we had to get some desserts and since we were celebrating both couples' anniversaries and my wife's birthday, we tried a bit of everything.  Chef Hattie and the kitchen once again gave us the perfect ending to a night of delicious exploration.

If you come here, come to enjoy the experience.  We had a group of staff stop by to assist in water or removing used plates, bring out new utensils for every course.  We greeted each and were pleasantly greeted and served in return.  It's hard to say if we like the food or the people more.  Can I just say both?

Rev.  #43
Nice place to sit out and grab a bite to eat. Got a half kilo of mussels that weren't too bad
Amazing food! Great variety from enormous pancakes to delicious salads. Very friendly staff!

Ate here while visiting New Orleans. Great service and great food at decent prices for the area. I had the fried shrimp platter, a cup of gumbo, and a house salad. Very fresh and tasty. Would definitely recommend. 

Gumbo was some of the best I've had!

Ok, this isn't the best park that I've been to, but it has its perks. Let's start out by saying that the Phillies are having a poor year and there was ample parking around the stadium. We settled for the parking lot at the Holiday Inn next to the stadium for $15. Entry in to the stadium was painless and our seats were excellent for the price we paid for them. The price of adult beverages is on par with what I've experienced at other parks and the Philly cheese steaks are delicious. The trade up value is excellent at this park due to the year they are having and we were able to move up to the rail after the sixth inning. I would recommend going to this park and will probably venture back.

This review has little to do with COVID though the workers and management do not seem to be following health care  professionals and government advice. Nobody wears a mask regularly, not sure they have cleaned a door knob in months, certainly havent vacuumed the halls in months  or washed the outside windows in a year  Have lived here for 2 years, great location and Matt, the manager, who tries to make a silk purse out of a sows ear, is the only reason I am still here. I have moved into two apartment here and they were both filthy when I moved in, trash room is always disgusting and stairs filthy.  Do not move here until management commits to making this a "luxury" apartment. It is sooo not.
We really enjoyed eating here. It was packed and loud, so not too intimate, but the food was creative and tasty with vegetarian options.
Love the team at DCH Lexus @ Santa Barbara. I love the attention to detail that I get along with the quick and responsive service. Their texting options make it so easy! Efrain and Isiah are great!

Absolutely excellent! This a a very charming and beautifully decorated restaurant. I went for brunch around 11am on a Saturday. There was hardly anyone in there, around 12pm the restaurant was packed. There is a very chic brunch vibe. Our waitress was awesome! The food was fantastic. I can't wait to go back. I ordered the strawberry rhubarb Bellini (sweet especially at the last drops), mushroom soup (amazing), shrimp salad (there was a leafy green that was a little bitter but tasty). My friend had one of the omelettes and we shared the dessert. dessert was very good the mousse cake and creme brûlée absolutely amazing. Can't wait to go back!

i used my groupons for this place and have one left to go-- I actually thought of cancelling  but figure groupon would not refund my money because they always give hard time to refund. I booked one labor day figuring a Saturday night and the slots would be looser. No they were tighter than the previous trip I made. First trip I won $13  from the free play they gave, second I won $55  plus additional $30 and labor day i on $17 from their free play. I think this place is disgusting for calling itself a casino. I is pure garbage. I did not even get points for the $300 I spent and the $150 free play I used.  yes I asked personnel in the players club area and the reply was oh we don't have any money. Either do I to ever give to VF Casino. You didn't attract me but reminded me to stay away after my last Groupon. The bed was horrible three times Is stayed there. It was lumpy and twisted and I tossed and turned all night.    You have to use entire voucher for food at one time. This management must be incredibly lame as I cannot figure how they cannot split this into two $20 vouchers - one for dinner and one for breakfast. This casino is awful and I see in Living Social there is a new ad for $99 but no free play but with the food This is not worth it- go to Atlantic City. you will lose your money and not sleep due to horrible junky twisted beds.

A great little place to share some great wine and lovely bites.  Great service, cool atmosphere.  

Highly recommend doing the small paltes/small taste things and to me there are more interesting things going on there.  But the larger things looked interesting going by.  Interesting wines by the glass, so it suited our mood of trying out a few familiar and then some unfamiliar things.  This is the sort of neighborhood place doing interesting things, in a cool setting with great wine.  The sort of place you want to live around the corner from so you can walk over after a crazy day at work, have some good wine and a bite to east in a great surrounding.

Whoa Nelly!

So somebody tells me that New Orleans has a restaurant that sells the "Best Fried Chicken" . Not only that,  Food Network also said this is THE spot to eat Fried Chicken! Game Over! Sorry restaurant August, all the fancy winin' and dinin' can wait til next time!

So we only had a few hours left before we had to go the airport, and my crew decided as our final restaurant would head to Willie Mays. I was so stoked to try this place that I forgot to call Augst to cancel our lunch reservation.  It's alright, we passed by it later and there was still plenty of seating in the restaurant. 

So i know you all are waiting...was it the best Fried Chicken I ever had?

The answer is....yes...to an extent. I am no fried chicken connosour, but I have to say it was finger lickin delicious. Although I felt the skin was a bit too salty for my palatte, I know personally that I like things on the blander side so this may not be their fault. Nonetheless, the skin was crispy and delicious while everything inside remained juicy and tender. 

The sides were also a home-run as well.  I had the greens and rice  all smothered in gravy; the gravy was tasty but definitely not salty to ruin the sides.  Overall this place is awsome. The service is friendly and efficient, and the food is frikkin delicious. If  you're ever in  New Orleans, definitely take the time to take a quick cab ride and enjoy some delicous Fried Chicken at Willie May's

Genine....Togo failure...paleo non friendly.

I seemed to be bothering Genine with any request that I had or even that I was even on the phone with her. And when I asked for traditional condiments for my togo monster burger she said "Ya know that is going to cost extra!" Come on really?! Go for the upsell and say "for just an additional 99 cents I can add some extra guacamole in there for you!" And hook line sinker and fishing pole i would have bit because I lOOOOVE Guac! But you had to ruin it and be rude...it's a shame...I never hang up on people but your poor service got the best of me and I went to applebees where they were happy to customize my burger. 

Red Robin-We love you! You have a team of very skilled servers but there are a fw that ruin your reputation! You haven't lost our business because your food is good and you have some extremely valuable servers. Maybe just some additional phone training? I certainly don't want to feel like I am inconveniencing you by giving my money...but unfortunately that is how Genine made me feel in this particular instance. Don't worry we get it you have your good days and your bad. Your good definitely outweigh your bad! We'll see you soon!

MILK TEAS!!!!!! And Herbal Jelly Goodness!!! 

I am extremely excited for the opening of Kung Fu Tea in NOLA!!! Last night my family and I went to the first day of opening! We arrived at around 9pm and there was quite a line of people waiting to order as well as waiting for their drinks. I've had Kung Fu tea at various locations across the country so I knew exactly what I want.  

Milk Green Tea with Herbal Jelly
Milk Winter Melon Green Tea with Herbal Jelly 
Mango Slush

Those are my MUST ORDER! 5 drinks for 2 adults and one 21 month old! LOL

Although wait time was a little long, I perfectly understand as this is their first day running the business and working out their kinks. 

I will visit pretty much on a daily bases! Staff seems great and I see the potential there for a great milk tea joint! Pretty Legit!
The smoked salsa is worth a visit on its own. This was a first time for us. The sampler platter was perfect way to get an introduction.
The food at this place is good, but between the language barrier, terrible service and extremely long wait, the stress is just NOT worth it.

On my continued quest to eat hella cheesesteaks before I peace of Philly forever, I tried Jim's Steaks because there's hella hype around this place.  I will mention, again, that I base this rating only on steak, provolone and bread.  No bells and whistles, no sauce, no onions.  Just the essential elements of a cheesesteak.

I went during lunchtime, so the service was quick and friendly.  5 stars for service.  But this rating ain't for service, so let's talk steak.

The cheese was placed on the bread, and the meat (pulverized status) was placed on top of the cheese.

As is the case with most times I've gone to get cheesesteaks, I was starving and scarfed half in the car and half at home.  (Ps. This rating should be a 3.5, but yelp doesn't roll that way.)

And I have to say that Jim's steaks were just kind of meh.  The meat was tasty but not mouthwatering (and kinda dry.  I know ... it's because there wasn't any stuff on it), the bread was average, and I feel like the cheese would be better distributed if mixed all amongst the pulverized meat instead of just underneath it.  At $8.21, however, the price was crazy for the size.  You get like 20-30% more steak elsewhere for the same price or cheaper.  However, there wasn't any gristle in the meat, which for me is a bonus (and the reason for the extra .5 stars).

Honestly, I'm still thinking Tony Luke's is by far the front runner, but I have to remind myself of Geno's and still haven't tried Pat's (and I'm sure there are a million other places to get steaks that hella other people claim are the best place for  steak.  I'm not a local, cut me a break.)

Also the following is speculation, BUT I think a HUGE reason why this place gets such a high rating is because people with major drunchies stumble in here after a night of drinking and think it's the best thing they've ever put in their mouths.  This is a drunchy-free rating, so take that as you will.

Background:  Went here after a long day of work and a major thirst for a tall cold beer. and some simple bar food.  I ordered the Mexicano burger (jalepenos, avocado) which hit the spot.  

What I like:  The food is good and the dining area next to the bar is cool.  There are a lot of options of beer on tap behind the bar and several booths with taps attached to the table tops.  This is a pretty nice feature, as you can pour your own beer, assuming the beer is flowing nicely (in my case it was not).  

What I don't like:  Though the atmosphere is supposed to resemble a sports bar, you don't really get that feeling.  There are a ton of TVs and a game might be on, but the sound is not, which to me takes away from the experience.  The location is not optimal, being several blocks away from Canal St. and the French Quarters but its doable.

Recommendation:  This is a good place for beer and bar food.  The burgers are good and they serve waffle fries.  For those waffle-fry aficionados, this should be your next stop.  If you're looking for a place to watch the big game, might want to look elsewhere.

As always, the beautiful waterfalls make for a nice relaxing al fresco dining experience. Had very nice blackened salmon, nice bottle of wine. Too bad servers don't understand that if you make sure water glasses are full, bread basket refilled and checking in will not only ensure a better tip, but more food will be ordered!  Go for the view, don't expect service.

From what I remember this place serves Seattle's Best coffee, so it's nothing unique but it's good and convenient. Tiny space so I imagine it's cramped if/when it gets crowded, but if you're looking for a quick iced coffee on the way to/from the beach, its a decent place to stop.

Shit service tonight I'm not sure why. Just went with friends to have some drinks and take it easy, waitress was a complete bitch.  We barely bothered her with any small Talk, we were all very respectful. In the service industry I'm sure people have bad days, but fuck, we spend our hard earned money so the least we expect is 'non bitchy' service, and we couldn't even get that tonight. We were ready to Leave and then waited over 20 min for server to come back, so we approached the bar, and the bartender gave us a cold mean look. WHY? Then the server came with the bill and asked why we approached the bar for the bill, so we told her we waited over 20 min and she never came to us, but still walked past us. She also gave a dirty look and told me next time just to wait for her to come to  the table. I felt she wanted to start an argument. Fuck that, we wanted to leave. Management needs to be more careful who they Hire. Utterly utterly DISAPPOINTED. ZERO stars tonight.

I have been going to this salon for the last 6 months. This place was my favorite. They do a perfect job, best gel manicure, I would say. However, I noticed that when the owner is not around, some  staff people couldn't not care less. Today I had an appointment at 2.15 pm for a pedicure, appointment was confirmed by the salon through the app as well as over the phone. When I got there I was told I have to wait 45 mins due to some mixed up in the schedule. When I said I wished I was notified about the change in my appointment, the lady at the front desk told me she did not have time for that.  What?? You didn't have time to call your customer? I understand things happen and schedules get mixed up, what I don't understand is such a disrespect to your customer's time. The lady at the front desk could not care less.I will have to switch to a different salon unfortunately.
Good near the Marriott. Easy to pick up a few items. Also serve hot food items.  Kind of reminds me of a small Whole Foods.  But good selection from what I quickly saw.

Dee's comments are untrue.  I think the way she's chosen to handle this situation is quite unprofessional.  I won't even dignify her untruths with specific responses. I'll simply say that I was with my children, and as their chief mentor and teacher I choose to conduct myself respectfully in their presence at all times.  I stand by my review 100%.

I reached out several times with no success. Finally got a hold of someone and started the price quote process. I sent pictures as they requested and never heard back. Possibly out of business or just not interested in my "small" job.

Good heathy option for the night owl eater. Eat a pita always came in clutch when I was studying late night for exams or finals. They deliver within a fairly large area from campus, and compared with any other late night food option that's open till 3, eat a pita is the best place to eat.

We popped in here for a quick drink.  We were able to sit outside and the waitress was friendly.  They have a unique selection of European beers including Belgian available in bottles.  They also have a decent wine list.  While we didn't have a chance to eat here, it's worth a stop I think and I imagine we will be back.  The outside area is dog friendly.

Little Korea had fantastic service! The new location is really nice inside. It was not too loud in the restaurant as well. The food was great, however, the food is too spicy for me. My friend ordered the kimchi soup that was unbearably spicy for me after the first bite. The bibimbap was cooked perfectly, except I did not mix in the spicy sauce- thus it lacked flavor. If I liked hot food, this place would be 5 stars!

I've only been here once and I ordered something really boring- a burger. I remember this place being pricey, but other reviews are saying it's fairly inexpensive, maybe they've changed their menu,but that's what I remember sticking out in my mind. Sitting on the deck is fun, watching the world of St.Petersburg walk by on the streets (it really has grown around there in the past year!). The deck is nice, with big fans with weird wooden fan blades that give a rustic feel. 

As others say, the place has a weird vibe to it. It always seems like "well to do" people are dining there or standing around waiting for a table.

My husband and I went here hoping to find gluten free options on the menu (which sadly they don't have), but they were very accommodating. I had brought my own GF soy sauce and it was a quiet night in the middle of the week, so they were willing to make some modifications for us.

Thanks to Quin for our great meal!

Appears to be a pretty efficient airport. TSA only had one loud semi power tripping agent. 

They moved people through relatively quickly. 

Parking was easy to find. Driving in was easy to navigate. 

Well fly in here vs. Tampa.

Before Saki came, I was referred to another technician. The estimate seemed over priced, so I told the guy I'll think about it. Then I came across Saki after doing an extensive search, including Yelp. He came 10 minutes before the scheduled time the day after I called. As soon as he arrived, he discovered that the first guy cut up the wires on the control panel and the thermostat.  Not only that the first guy's diagnose was completely irrelevant to the malfunction of my AC, but also demanded for the service fee of $80 which was never mentioned or agreed before his visit. Saki was thorough with detecting the problem and reasonable  with the cost. My time spent on searching for a reliable, prompt, and knowledgeable technician definitely paid off and I know who to call from now on!

I ordered the french dip- While I like my roast beef to be very thin and no fat the french dip here was thin but not my version of thin.. it was very fatty. So much fat that I only ate 1/2 of my sandwich. I have the other half to my husband who took one bite and was like WTF all I got was a mouth full of fat. My husband had a southwestern chicken burger the seemed to like it. 
I think we will go back and try breakfast.. I saw that they had sweet cream pancakes and well that sounded better than what I ordered.

This place is the best. My wife loves the Khao Poon (King Soup)- it's her favorite soup in the city. I'm a little more boring and always go with the Pad Thai or House Fried Rice, and they are always top notch. We've also had their duck, angel shrimp, fish cakes, and spring rolls which are all phenomenal. Everything is always fresh and very well put together.
They make a great cheese burger! My mom and I split and we both agreed it was cooked perfectly and hot and juicy. The only downfall is we went on karaoke night and it was WAY too loud.

Worst Pizza & Unapologetic, Bad Service.

I ordered the "Ode to Ukraine" and the pizza was luke warm, soggy and gross. The favour combination was extremely unbalanced and overpowering. ( I am Ukrainian. I have a lot of experience on how the flavour combinations should taste and this one was clearly off.)
