If so, they will quickly go over the ordering process. Most items are a la carte. You order at the counter and they bring your food and beverage out to you. Portion sizes are relatively modest. If you are big eaters like we are, ordering 3 items to share between 2 people is plenty.

The menu changes frequently so we'll just say the food was fresh and delicious. Service was friendly and prices were reasonable. We will definitely be back.

Easily the best quick-serve gyros outside an actual mid-east restaurant.   

 "Authentic"?  No.   Delicious? Very yes.
I met there years ago...got a blueberry smoothie...really good.  I hope to try their coffee someday.

The actual service itself went well - the individual assigned to my pedi was pleasant and did a great job, and seemed to take extra time to make sure she was doing a good job. 

BUT - this place ultimately falls flat due to 1) the 25 minute wait before I could be seen (despite being told repeatedly that it would be "just one more minute" until they could get to me), 2) lack of sterilized tools, 3) HORRID selection of polish, and 4) general uncleanliness.

With an appointment you are almost guaranteed to be in and out in less than 10 minutes. The place is amazing, looks really nice like a brand new airport. As soon as I checked in my number was called already and literally had to wait zero seconds. The old place was terrible and I remember waiting hours. Fantastic safety protocols for Covid. 
The new place has optimized wait times to an absolute minimum but only if you make an appointment.  If you check at 7-8am online on their website you can often find appointments for that same day that were cancelled. With an appointment, the service you will experience is 5 stars or more.

Easily one of the best breweries in Tucson. The quality of the beers here is always outstanding and the customer service is great. Everyone behind the bar is really knowledgeable and there are always fun events happening every week. Their beers are all brewed in the traditional styles. You'll find a great Pilsner, German-inspired brews like Berliner Weisses, a Scotch Ale and various styles of IPAs, among many others. 

This place is no frills. They won't make a blueberry pie beer or put fried chicken or other weird stuff in what they brew. You're going to find something here you like if you're a beer drinker and even their lightest beers have a ton more flavor than any macrobrew you see in commercials. 

The owners are really nice, cool people and they run a family business in every sense of the term. Todd, the one who ad the idea to open this place, is also the head brewer and you can tell how passionate he is about what he does. This brewery was a labor of love and it shows.

My wife contacted them to sell a Peg Prego $900 stroller system we had, was told they can only offer 120-150 for it, makes sense as they need to make their profit, she agreed...took the time to go there to bring it in , the young lady (extremely cold and unprofessional) tells her (after we overheard her telling her colleague "wow, these are very expensive ") turns to my wife and tells her she will give her $43...... we were shocked.... I told her I'll donate it to a family in need and get more as a write off..... we weren't even greeted farewell..... Pawn shops make this place look good .... waste of my gas money from arrowcreek
Must try! You won't be disappointed.  From appetizers to desserts your tastebuds will be in Heaven.

The circle center mall Taco Bell is trash!! I work at a different Taco Bell in the state, and not only did they prepare my food incorrectly, they did it with no haste or consideration. There were about 6-7 workers within the small kitchen; I understand they aren't give as much space as a full size Taco Bell. But they were chit chatting, playing with food in the preparation line, and the kitchen appeared to be filthy. The young man at the counter even gave me the wrong change back, to which I didn't correct him because I was just at a loss for words. The slushee machine was down and they still handed me a half blended mess of a drink, and they didn't grill an item that's meant to be grilled to function correctly.

Great view of the NOLA skyline,  quick trip maybe 20 minutes.  Downside is you must pay 2 dollars each way. You actually have to get off then back on. Oh and must have exact change,they do not give change at all PERIOD. You are bound to see atleast one person find this out the hard way, hopefully they don't act like a 2 year old like they guy we saw.

I'm only reviewing for the music & cocktail I had. Classic jazz club feel. If you love jazz, you'll probably love this place. Great talent with a fun vibe from the guys onstage. We had a great time & wil come back next time in NOLA.

If I lived in New Orleans, I would come here for breakfast every day. My family and I stopped in here on Friday morning because of all of the high ratings on Yelp and I am so glad that we stopped by!! Everything here was fantastic, especially the service. Our server, Alberto was beyond wonderful! He checked in throughout the meal to make sure that we were taken care of! My mom and I ordered the mimosa which was delicious because a large portion of the drink was champagne (just the way I like it!). Then I ordered the pancake trio which had blueberry danish, cinnamon swirl, and bacon praline and these pancakes were HUGE!!! I couldn't even finish half of it! These were definitely the best pancakes that I have ever eaten. They were so full of flavor. Even writing about them right now makes me hungry!  
Overall, I had a wonderful experience. Food was impeccable and service was wonderful and attentive. Next time I am back in New Orleans, I will be coming back here for brunch!

MIKAYLA Capelo is my hair hero!! I have very dark hair and previously to going to her, my hair would instantly turn orange when going to other salons. I was always so scared to go to anyone until I was referred to Mikayla. She colors my brunette hair perfectly and always makes sure I'm happy with the result! I promise you, you will get the bang for your buck!
This place is fast and they did a great job! It aint luxurious but it gets the job done!
Hard to find honest, fast, and reasonable people to work on your car.  My friends and I have all been 100% happy with this place.  Highly recommended.

The best house tour I have been on. Wonderful staff and very knowledgeable!  I loved every minute of it!!  Fantastic piece of history in downtown St. Louis. A must see!! A great gift shop on lower level. Can't believe I've never been here before. Christmas tour coming soon.

I like the food, but tired of their nickel and diming charges. I used to go there every week but stopped.  The menu states guacamole is $.99 no problem but doesn't say anything about sour cream or sides of salad dressing.  I always get charged $.99 for sour cream and $.50 for salad dressing when I order a side of salad instead of the rice and beans. Once I didn't want the pico de Gallo on my taco because it makes it soggy so I asked for it on the side.  Guess what? They charge me me $1.00 bc I wanted it on the side.  I order for two, so every visit results in $2-$4 in extra charges for side sauces. Sick of it. And the people there are so unfriendly. Would it kill u to smile? Oh and I see employees handle food without gloves all the time. In fact, one employee went straight from checking out one customer at the cash register to then helping the next person.. touching their food with her bare hands.

Pretty solid little local, hole in the wall watering hole. Came in for a couple drinks and some food and I was not disappointed. Their green tea shots were perfectly measured, the wings were hot and fresh and the fries were crispy and delicious. 

The bartenders did a good job of handling the crowd and being attentive without hovering. I love to play pool so the pool table is definitely an added bonus. I will be back ASAP for some of their drink and food specials as well as to beat my girlfriend at pool
OK, it's loud and crowded, but they've got the best sweet potato fries we've ever had. They aren't limp like most others.  I think they fry them in Viagra.

Linda is the best nail tech you will EVER find. No question. I have traveled all over the country for my job, and I never found anyone that does the things that she can do. She's courteous, funny, and her prices are so affordable! Stop going to that nail salon that you aren't happy with, and go see Linda!
This is my favorite steakhouse ever! I get the same dish everytime lol my favorite drink is the strawberry margarita. It's like 2 drinks in 1! I only eat steak from Longhorns!
We just had another lunch at Havana Dreamers Cafe. What a great little find. Excellent food and service. Michael and the others are efficient and friendly. We'll definitely be back.
Prett good food, consistent and fresh! Not NYC Thai food but def good for this area. I enjoy the pad Thai, it needs some extra sauce but it's good.

Decided to have a night cap and grabbed a seat at the bar. Boyfriend had the beer flight,  I had the biggest little city gimlet. He liked the emigrant the best. The depot smells like new wood and the lighting is romantic, Thomas Edison romantic. My gimlet was refreshing and the bartender spanked the basil with such pizzazz. Took a peak behind the bar and was impressed by all the quality and care the bartenders took in the products used in their drinks. They even use high end heavy whipping cream. (I saw it myself) 
         I like this place and will return to try more drinks. The bartenders are super nice and take a lot of pride in their drinks. Classy.
Excellent, my only issue is with people who does not eat gelato during winter months! We need more of us so they they stay open all year around. Hot or cold I am always up for good gelato!

Lamb steak was amazing... Juicy, tender, very well seasoned... Flavorful. The first bite was a symphony of flavor and I am not even a huge fan of lamb!!!.
Pot roast was ai'ght. Sweet potato puree a little runny. It needed a little seasoning. In general good atmosphere, good food, good local beer. I'd give it 3 1/2 stars.

We were seated right next to the front door so everyone (and their screaming kids) waiting for their table were standing right next to us  our server was slower than molasses in January. I got the salmon quinoa plate and hubby got the ribeye. Food was decent.

Since we don't feel comfortable about eating at restaurants yet, we decided to get some take-away.  We have always loved their buffets.  In the past, we have felt that we were able to get our money's worth at their sort of pricey buffet.

We ordered the Mixed Veggie Plate, the Chicken Shish Kabob and the Lamb Shank. The Mixed Veggie Plate had many items that we loved off the buffet like:  hummus, baba ghanoush, stuffed grape leaves, 2 fried falaels and a dab of tabouli salad.  Every item was tasty.  The Chicken Shish Kabob was a bit disappointing.  When we've eaten the kabob chicken on the buffet it was always moist and tender...this wasn't.  I don't think that I'd order this item again for take-away.  The star of the meal was the Lamb Shank.  OMG, it was an ample tender portion wonderfully spiced.  We also order some Maust' khiar sauce that's essentially tatziki sauce. With all that we ordered, we only got 2 full pita breads (8 quarters).

Overall, the lamb shank was awesome and the Mixed Veggie Plate made for a nice appetizer.  However, the price point for this meal was pretty high for what we got.
I was extremely impressed with the the professionalism of the Nigro's team.  Their solid communication skills and knowledge of insurance nuances made my life much easier!

The service here was excellent! I loved how much care and effort is put in to hair styling here. I personally would recommend Patty and Linda. Everyone there was so kind and I couldn't have asked for a better cut!

A friend wanted to go here for a low key birthday dinner and it was perfect! What a perfect place for a different twist on fries. We got several different varieties, but of course the burger fries were my favorite. We also got a flight of the sauces and they were delightful. My favorite was the herb aioli. We tried most of the dessert pies and those were also good. My favorite was their take on the pecan pie. The homemade whipped cream was delicious! Pair all this cheap drinks inside Hi Ho Lounge and you've got a perfect lowkey birthday celebration!

This TJ's location was my first experience of TJ's in Santa Barbara County. I find that the store is always clean and is constantly being stocked with merchandise. I love the fact that you can grab any employee and ask them a question and they are usually skilled in all products. I also enjoy the coffee and samples they always have going on and they seem to have a very great fruit and flower section everytime I visit. One star off because the parking lot here is  NIGHTMARE.

review update: as of the end of may the customer service did apologize. They provided a $50 gift certificate as a result. However, our underlying problem was never fixed, so I feel comfortable giving an overall rating of 2 stars.
Excellent food. But I feel like price was kinda high. $4 for mango lassi is high for me I don't believe even in nyc I didn't have that much for a lassi btw the food was good

I went to Twenty Manning for dinner to catch up with my former boss, not because there was anything that had particularly appealed to me from its menu or the Yelp reviews, but because my boss and I had both wanted to cross it off our Philly dining scene bucket list. And the sentiment on the other side of the experience is equally indifferent. It was a fine dinner, but I wasn't overly impressed.

Because I was hoping for something lighter, I ordered the Chop Chop Salad as an entree. Before anyone points their finger and says that's where I went wrong, I want to just assert that the server told me of all their salads, the chopped salad is best suited to be an entree. Besides, I added salmon to it. 

The salad itself was wonderful. Great blend of flavors and textures from the corn, cucumbers, and gala apples. The herb-citrus toss was also wonderfully light but flavorful. It was the salmon that disappointed. It was dry, and I always take off a star for dry salmon. It became one of those rare situations when I actually thought the salad would've been better without the protein.

For dessert, I got the famous half-baked Toll House cookie. It was undeniably delicious, but nothing completely mind-blowing or original. The only real wow factor, I suppose, was the portion size. I will not lie to you and say that I did not eat the whole thing in that sitting. I was feeling particularly victorious and wholesome after that delicious salad and dry salmon.

In any case, Twenty Manning Grill wasn't a let-down, but it also wasn't a restaurant that I'd be gushing over to my friends. I agree with other reviewers that if you're just sauntering over because the line at Audrey Claire's is too long, stay faithful and get your wandering eye in check. You will be glad you did.

Sooooo I've been here twice.  The first time there I was sold, but this time.....THIS TIME blew me AWAY!

Every single thing was top-notch.  We had a lunch reservation at 12:00 and they were kind enough to push it back to 1:30, because we were having a busy morning and weren't sure if we would make it there in time. 

The ambiance is beautiful- from the swamp themed wall decor to the bird theme in the main dining room.  

The service is impeccable.  These servers were well-trained and clearly have a passion for the food here.

We each got the quarter martinis for lunch and the 2 course lunch menu.  The martinis are solid- three is the limit and that was the perfect amount. 

The turtle soup was PHENOMENAL.  I came real close to licking the bowl, but I refrained, as I thought that might appear desperate and/or inappropriate.....

I had the tamales and my travel companion had the monte cristo.   

Both exceeded our expectations beyond measure.  The monte cristo was more than just a sandwich- it was something you had to eat with a fork and every fork-full was sheer and utter bliss.  The cornmeal that made the tamales was delectable.  Every last bit of it was so good.  I couldn't quite finish, so they wrapped it up in foil and shaped it like a swan. 

(Sidenote: I ended up scooping it into my mouth as we were walking around the garden district- I couldn't wait any longer to eat those leftovers!)

We did save room for dessert:  the bread pudding souffle and the praline sundae.  I am not even sure how we had room, but it was well worth it.  

Afterwards we wandered around Lafayette Cemetery (directly across the street) in the pouring rain. 

Whatever you do, GO to Commander's Palace!

Going back for a delicious lunch.  Same
Quality of service and the food I ordered Adana Lamb kebab which is a ground lamb infused with lots of herbs and spices and is very juicy and tasty.    I like their French fries here too. The Turkish rice is yummy and the baklava dessert is so good.

This place is very cool. The idea of "pour your own beer" is awesome. I could come here every night so I can have a couple sips of beer and be on my way. It led me to trying a bunch of different beers that I normally wouldn't try to do because I wouldn't want to try a normal sized pint.  The prices are by the ounce and are pretty decently priced. The manager was very nice and asked us what we liked me didn't like. They are really open to suggestions. 

Plus.. they had Abita on draft and the Nola girl in me fell in love with an Indy bar with Abita

Berlins Doener delivers on their promise:  bringing Germany's most popular street food to St. Pete.  It is excellent because it is simplistic in the way they create their menu.  They are not one of those restaurants that try too hard to deviate away from an original recipe to be different.  True German food is based on just a few ingredients and that's what BD does.  

I visited mainly to have a doner kebab wrap and I was not disappointed.  The wrap's bread was perfectly toasted just slightly to give it a crisp taste but was not burnt.  The quality of the lamb/beef was acceptable, and the red cabbage and feta cheese were fresh to bring it all together.  I used their hot and spicy sauce, it complimented the wrap just fine.  I tried their tzatziki sauce as well and I was very impressed by it.  It wasn't bland and had very bold taste.  

As a side, my wife and I shared their pretzel.  It's gigantic!  Definitely a perfect side to share between 2-4 people.  I loved their cheese and mustard dips that went along with it.  DB also has real German  1/2 and 1 liter beers on tap, be sure to take advantage!

Went there for early happy hour. The prices are good for drinks. The appetizers are tasty but very minuscule. The service was very bad from the beginning when there were only a few people and became progressively worse. Only one server for 8 tables. She started the evening off in a bad mood and continued it through the evening. Probably because the poor thing knew how the evening would progress. The restaurant cannot handle the influx of people that hoard at happy hour resulting in poor service. Sorry, but I cannot give a good review when the restaurant takes advantage of their employees that way.

2 stars because our cocktail was decent. Not a friendly bar for people of color....maybe just the white male LGBTQ community(the only other customer demographic when we walked in). Unfriendly service from the moment we walked into the door. Sad to receive this kind of service in my own community. :/
Don't know why they remain in business. The store is not clean looking. Delivery never made it to the house.

Yes! Loved that this place was tucked in NOLA Brewery. Being a visitor, I was intrigued by the "BBQ  Jambalaya". I had to order it just to give it a try. And am I glad I did! This may have been the best jambalaya I had while visiting! It's not sweet or saucy at all. It's actually more like traditional jambalaya with pulled pork as the meat. I topped it off with some of their homemade hot sauce - it was amazing! We also tried the hot chicken wings which were also very good. I highly recommend giving this place a try!
The best little byob around. Fantastic pizza, very tasty paninis, in fact everything on the menu is really good. Easy on the wallet prices too. Typical strip mall ambience, very friendly place

Quite possibly the worst mexican food I've ever had. Ordered to go, was told it would be about 15 minutes, so I arrived at about 20 minutes and paid. I had to wait another 25 minutes to receive the food. I live about 3 minutes away, and  opened it right when I got home. Everything was cold and the nachos were soggy, so I'm guessing that extra 25 minutes was to make sure it was barely edible.

I ordered enchiladas supremas with no sour cream, so of course it came with a huge glop of sour cream. The enchiladas had very little flavor and were tiny. I ordered a number 6 entree for my dinner guest and it looked worse than most fast food joints, and she couldn't even finish it. I ordered nachos as a side and they were cold/soggy and the cheese was not real but something fake like velveeta. 

I hope this review helps people from making the same mistake as me and wasting money on this place that has no business serving food to anyone.

We went last night for our jack and Jill package! It took our little stubborn one sometime before we got a clear shot but the ultrasound tech was so great with allowing the baby to have some time she had me get up and repositioned until we got our results :) would definitely recommend. The space was a great size and the office was homey feeling.

My gf threw up the pork chops she had not one hour later. Unfortunately the chicken pot pie and great beer selection isn't enough to hold this place down. Also rednecks everywhere, and they over serve them, people bringing beers into bathroom and trying to start fights.

Unfortunately the food quality is pretty good here but the ability to properly take orders is not good. Even though we make sure that the person taking the order repeat it back to us over the phone they are still unable to complete the order properly and I would like to add by the time we got our order the food was cold

The food is good, but the service makes you  not go back anymore. I think managers and owners are not aware about their mean waitresses. The staff treats customers very bad. I will go back more often, but service is terrible. Owners open your eyes!

We are enjoying the pulled pork sandwich with slaw and their special sauce which is sweet and tasty. The baked beans have a smoky BBQ flavor. Fries are hand cut. It's near the Country Music Hall of Fame and parking across the street is $5.00.  It has a good atmosphere and the wait staff is attentive.

The roofs leak. Garbage is laying all over the place. There is asbestos removal in some buildings. Rusty nails throughout the property. They keep starting and stopping the remodeling and exterior construction for the last two years and they aren't even close to being done. Most of the wood underneath is completely rotten from years of neglect. Dead trees all over the place and most all of the grass is dead too. There is a reason every review on this place is bad!

So I live in Beverly. This is my to go place for Pizza. If you like thick crust please try this place. It is so delicious. Tonnes of toppings, beautifully cooked...and delicious. My kid finds the pizza too greasy so she likes ordering their clubhouse or BLT sandwich. If I am not in the mood for pizza, their baked pastas are amazing and have a sinful amount of cheese on them. Take out is good. Not much to look at on the inside. I would love it if the owners  invested more in revamping the place. Really Beverly needs a good place to meet for a cold beer and some great pub food. The food is excellent but the décor isn't the place where you would meet friends to watch a game or have a good time. So go ahead and enjoy the food. I would suggest though take it out and eat it at the comfort of your own home.
This place is amazing! They put together 14 fabulous gift baskets for me and even helped load the car! Everyone was so impressed with the selection and can't wait to dig in!

I don't really want to like it here, but I still do.
It is an incredibly weird mix of people -- suburban visitors, babies dressed in gingham ties, occasional hipsters, people who write "COCK" on jenga blocks, 50 year old professorial types out w the professorial bros -- I just can't figure it out and I think it's better the less I think about it.
I am not really into the Stephen Starr restaurant industrial complex and try to avoid his reach, but I went here a few times last year for Nerd Nite and (ugh why!) I like it a lot.
I like that you can play Jenga at your table, I like the beer prices during happy hour, I like the giant pretzels and the weird condiments they come with, I like sitting outside in the summer, I like that it fits a lot of people, I like the gravel in the biergarten, I like the system they have for ordering food, I like the beer selection.
I will continue to reluctantly really like Frankford Hall.

Poor customer service I did not like chicken quesadillas and manager I quote stated it's just chicken and cheese like everyone in world would like it well it's nasty and he hung up on me I didn't even want refund just to exchange order rude af
Front page has fun karaoke on Thursday nights.  It is a sports bar, so it can get a little bro-y, but there's plenty of room to have your space.

So disappointed! Hadn't been to Charley's in years and remember it being awesome. Went with my sister. Wine waiter recommended, salad, and bread were good. Filet was overcooked (both of ours and the 2 guys next to us as well). I was the only one to send it back...they wanted to, but were too hungry. My sis got the lobster tail (as did one of the guys next to us) and both were tough. They were out of sauteed mushrooms and creamed spinach.
For the price we paid, I'd have gone to any number of better quality restaurants in town twice or three times over :(

I've been hearing great things about Lucky Buddha and finally got around to eating there last night. It was okay, but disappointing as I was expecting much better. The service was strange. We were seated by a young woman who said she'd bring menus and then never showed up again. The guy who waited on us told us up front he wasn't a waiter but had been roped in to waiting tables for the evening. He tried, but had some issues. Everything about the place seemed very haphazard.

They were out of all of the draft beer on the menu and many of the bottled/canned beers.

The food was not as good as I'd expected. We had Thai Spring Rolls, which were okay, but far too much lettuce in them and not enough other ingredients. I'd heard that the Porkapocalypse Ban Mi was terrific. When it arrived at our table it was, again, just okay. Mostly bread. Good bread, but still... Very little pork in the sandwich and the horseradish was perhaps waved over it, but not spread on it. 

I'm hoping that Lucky Buddha was just having an off night and that if I stop in again I'll have my opinion changed.

Sooooo many great gourmet, specialty food store to stop in to. I was drooling all afternoon looking at all the meats and cheeses at the counters. you can tell a lot of love goes into all of these stores and great quality food come out.  There is also an AMAZING cooking store located on the road. I cant remember the name but it looks little from the outside but once you walk in.. BAM! it has everything you could possibly need and more. This street is a must visit if you love food and near Philly. You'll want to keep going back. Trust me.

The food is great however the service is consistently poor. The last time i went they refused to take a 25% off coupon from the 2016 entertainment book which is valid simply because they don't want to take it anymore. It was specifically for their restaurant too! It was actually absurd. Then a friend of mine asked for different soup and the waitress gets frustrated, throws the silverware on the table, and says "i already made this one". When a customer tells you they don't like something you take it back. That is basic customer service. Then for the remainder of our visit the staff were rude and giving us nasty looks. They are really lucky they have good food because otherwise they would be out of business. I know my friend and i will never be going back there again. If you do decide to go there order takeout.

Jimi loves him some fun fruity drinks.  My Hinge date suggested I get the "Sweet Tart" because I'm so sweet.  I said thanks doll and smacked her on the behind like a gentleman.  Tried to ride a Bird scooter home with the drink in hand.  Was hard to brake.  Thank god I was sober.

5 stars

Worst McDonald's In Missouri. Soggy fries, they are rude and they always get my order wrong. A girl named Rachel was being so mean to these two young girls for no reason tonight and made it super awkward poor girl looked like she was gonna cry... just thought someone should know.... your workers should not be treated like that by another employee.

Excellent Greek food in the midst of a wonderful shopping town.  
If you can make it before 4pm, they have a lunch special that includes your choice of sandwich, of which I recommend the gyros since they pack them full of meat.  They also have excellent Greek salads, and a couple soup options that are included in this special as well as dessert.

I was walking nearby and stopped by this place, which was a good choice. I liked the burger because it was full of mushroom flavor. I also enjoyed their unique and savory oven-baked fries, but I would not recommend it to those who want "crispy" fries. For me, it was great.

I usually give everyone a chance even after reading reviews. In this case I did just that. I read the reviews here on yelp and still called in. I just wanted to inquire about some of the services they offered for my new pup. When calling in I just asked the name of the person I was speaking to (since she didn't give it willingly) and she was very rude as the comments state. Do not waste your time here or even calling.

I just started going to this bage shop as it is close to my work. The bagels are great, the employes are polite and cheerful, and they always complete your order quickly. The bagels and other ingredients always taste fresh. I believe they are a small family owned business and not another corporate, big business franchise which is great! As Americans we need to stop shopping at Walmarts and Home Depots and start supporting our local small businesses which is what our great nation was built upon.

I was in the mood for some stone crab claws as the season just opened. I called and the friendly guy who answered said " we got plenty claws come on down we will fix you up" well they sure did. Since I was staying in a hotel they made sure I hade everything to enjoy this meal. Their seafood is fresh !! Enjoyed with tremendously. Highly recommend this place.

I want this place to be amazing.  They are just mediocre.  Their seafood is not fresh  meaning it was either frozen or from a can.  Their eggs are rubbery and over cooked.  I wish someone would take their chef aside and tell him to raise the bar.  Midtown has become the hub for fresh ingredients.  It's easy to park now that Maytan Music has closed.  The house is great and the seating is comfortable.

The atmosphere for a appetizer and drinks is a true hang out spot. Its a huge cafe that has two entrances and really get a bang for your buck. The Hurricane's are always on point and good laughs with friends. The menu is not big at all. I had the fried catfish which had an alright taste to go with a Hurricane. This is a must when on vacation here.

My husband, some friends and I stayed here for a night while in town for an event. It was not an enjoyable experience, and I wish we could go back in time and not waste money on our dirty room. Both rooms we booked were super dated and dirty. I felt uneasy the entire time I was there and was barely able to sleep wrapped up in my own blanket. The carpets were disgusting and the shower was so nasty that I refused to use it while we were here. The photos and reviews on the website are totally misleading. Don't waste your time or money here.

I feel so honored to be one of the first to review such an amazing place! I went on the opening day just before closing. Saw lots of excited faces ready for the same experience I was expecting ! ( this made me feel a little better about eating desserts after 9 at night lol) I guess Rita's is a southern thing? I heard it was really good so I decided to try and it lived up to its expectations. The owner (he was ringing everyone up) grew up with a Rita's and loved it so he decided to bring one to Fisher's. His mom and dad was there for the opening helping  and they were really sweet people. (Awwwww right ?)  We actually got to talk to them for quite a bit. 

Now the sweet part... (pun intended) 

I had the Gelati : it's a layer of custard then a layer of Italian ice then custard on top . (It's very pretty) I had vanilla custard and dragon fruit Italian ice. Before trying this I thought Custard and ice cream tasted very similar . But I was sooo wrong. The custard has a very light fluffy feel . It's very smooth and not as strong and sweet as ice cream to me. I now prefer custard over ice cream .  It's so much better. Like where has it been all my life. Now, the Italian ice. It was yummy. I also tried cherry and sour apple jolly rancher. I thought they were going to be super sweet but they weren't. The Dragon fruit was also sugar free and I couldn't tell . Still tasted really good. 

If you've never had Italian ice or custard or its your first time I would recommend the Gelati. You get to taste both :). 

The pricing was pretty moderate or what'd you expect from any ice cream place. Not a lot space so I'd keep that in mind for bigger groups of people. 

The servers were very nice. He watched me decide and go back and forth between flavors  with the biggest smile and was super patient. 

I will definitely be back.

I've been here a few times and always had a great meal. Steaks are cooked to perfection. I llke medium and they have gotten it right every time. Today I had the 11" sirloin on special for Wednesdays and it was excellent. Seemed to be a garlic and onion seasoning and that's really good. I've also had the BBQ pork sandwich and loved it. Give this place a try, be prepared for a wait after 6pm.
Good location and clean room but the wifi comes and goes and it takes running the bathtub and waiting about 10 minutes to get hot water in the shower.

In the interest of full disclosure, I'll mention that I knew Dr. Gilbert before I went to see him as a chiropractor - he was my mom's chiropractor and a friend of the family. That said, when I got in a car accident in December 2011, I was quite skeptical of going to a chiropractor at all and went to see Ari not knowing what to expect. I'm happy to report that he is a professional, knowledgeable doctor who really cares about relieving pain. Our appointments are quick and effective and he really listens when I report new or returning pain. He is also schooled in alternative medicines and nutrition, though I haven't used any of those services. I recommend him 100%!

Without fear, I'm about to give my opinion on a St. Louis institution.  Humps functions as a college bar and has a good patio, but beyond that, its reputation is pumped up to epic proportions by drunken college memories and stories rather than quality food, service, drinks or atmosphere.  It's smoky and, during certain nights of the week, super-crowded.  The bouncers routinely act with a ruthlessness normally reserved for an occupying army.  The food is standard bar fare, nothing special.

That Humps is still around and thriving is, more than anything, an endorsement of the ancient maxim "location, location, location."  Its extreme proximity to SLU's campus solidify's Humps' status as an archetypal college bar and all the pitfalls contained therein.
Small little Cuban cafe with great Cuban sandwiches. Cafe con leche with Cuban toast in the am   Always a newspaper laying around too.

The food was outstanding!!  I had the steak and rotisserie chicken with rice and beans and plantains.  Just really, really good food.  The service was excellent, portions large, and tasted delicious! I will be back!!

So I have a mixed feelings about this place.

Lets start with logistics - good luck getting a seat on time (even with reservations - we waited about an hour) because this spot has become insanely popular (especially during the winter). They also seem to run out of things rather quickly (i'm assuming popularity has something to do it - then again popularity might be a sign of how they are doing things right).

There seems to be an utter shortage of staff and I felt really bad for those that were there, just completely unable to keep up.

Now the food is to die for and probably the best I will ever have in Nashville without losing my bank account. Everything from the bread to the salmon to the goat cheese spread is a heavenly experience. 

The portions may not be French, but they are on the smaller side of things for an American food standards. I will also say that the staff was super friendly to do what they could to take care of us when things died down and give us alternative menu options and comp us for the wait - which I really appreciate.

History right in front of you!

Christ Church was on my list of things to see in Philly, and I'm sure glad I stopped by. Entry is free and they have a little gift shop in the front as you walk in. The church itself is beautiful and the pew boxes are a great place to take a load off and relax, especially if you have been walking all over Philadelphia like I had been. I was surprised, yet delighted, that there was a tour guide in the church! I wasn't expecting this but the man was a wealth of knowledge, and he pointed out and explained many aspects of the church that I would have missed had I just wandered around on my own.

As far as chain restaurants go, this is one of my favorites. The lighting and decor are warm and authentic, and the food has never disappointed. I haven't tried a dish I haven't liked, though the orange chicken is my favorite. There are usually spots open at the bar, too, if you want to watch a game of some sort. It gets crowded during weekends, so make a reservation if you're going Friday or Saturday between 5 and 7.

To start off, the service was prompt and thorough.  Three types of water were offered. The water and the drinks were ordered. The drinks, bread and olive oil arrived. The game was afoot.  

Ordering was kinda hard. So many decisions to choose from. We settled on a three course meal with biscotti dessert. The food was impeccable. I had the best sword fish I've ever tasted. The pasta with pork black truffle sauce was on par with the pasta I sampled in Tuscany. The deconstructed biscotti was very cool. Fabulous. 

Hit up the very cool Passyunk neigherhood for one of the best Italian experiences I've had.
The tacos were really greasy and there were flys everywhere besides that good service .

I'm very conflicted with Harp & Crown, 4 or 5 stars. It really deserves 4.5. 

I came here twice, and my first visit I was not as impressed, so 3.5 or 4 stars. However, my most recent visit was much better, and makes me much happier! Both visits, the service was fantastic, and the atmosphere is amazing. Just loud. The difference between my visits was my choices of food, and drinks, for the prices. 

5-stars: 
- Scallops. This dish blew me away both visits. Some of the best scallops I've ever eaten. WOW chef, bravo, and that sauce on top, amazing! Its more expensive than the other dishes, I think around $19, but its so delicious that its worth every dollar. 
- Butternut Squash Toast - amazing! Decent size, they cut into 3-4 slices.
- Fig Toast - also amazing, but the squash toast was my favorite, which is rare because I'm a huge fig lover.
- Hamachi - WOW, this was impressive, with grapefruit and the sauce was so good.
- Lamb meatballs, everyone's favorite. These were better on my 2nd visit.
- Truffle pizza. I love pizza with egg on it!
- Fried cauliflower was amazing. Perfect lightly breaded, was so soft and fluffy, and the dipping sauce is amazing.

4-stars:
- Spaghetti - Yes! This was surprisingly delicious, a white clam sauce with garlic. Even had some hot red pepper flakes for a kick. Yumm.
- Charred Broccoli
- Brussels sprouts
- Chocolate Cake was massive, and nice and rich. Can't compare it to other desserts though. 

3.5 stars:
- Ricotta Gnocchi. Sounds delicious, but both times was slightly disappointed. It was perfect texture, but needed some more rich flavor in the sauce. If you want pasta, order the spaghetti. 
- Cheese plate. The cheeses were good, but I've had better, and there wasn't a lot of garnishes. Maybe add some honey, fig jam, nuts, mustard, apple slices? We only got grapes.  

DRINKS: 
Ruby slippers and Crown Jewel were very good, but tiny. For the high prices, I find the Charred Stone to be my favorite bang for your buck. Its in a larger glass (with ice).

Its easy to run up a massive tab here. Be careful. Most of the portions are small, so you order several things which adds up quick. The Pizza and Pastas are the best portion sizes for the money.
Great little deli/market. The staff is so friendly and it's always incredibly clean and organized, unlike many other bodegas. The deli sandwiches are excellent and very fresh.

Bee Naturals is tucked away from the main Maplewood business strip so it's easy to miss when you're shopping downtown but it's a must visit when you're looking for gifts for yourself or others. They have a great selection of bath and body products as well as a small spa offering massages and facials. The products are affordable and good quality. I usually come in for their baby and dog products as they are unique to other natural product stores in Maplewood. I've also been in for a massage and facial in the past which were both relaxing and enjoyable. Will definitely keep frequenting as a customer in the future.

I've tried all of the "bougie" coffee places here in town so you don't have to: this one is the best by far.

You can tell right away that the baristas here know what they're doing. The milk is steamed perfectly (if you're a latte lover like myself), the syrup appears to be homemade and not overly sweet, and the espresso itself is really good. I'm sure it helps that the roastery is around the corner, so the beans are probably super fresh. The selection of pastries is nice and they always have something new and unique. I got a caramel espresso bar the other day that was really good.

They have great specials. The salads are second to none. But the service here is one of the worst ever. I've had to walk out because the waitress seats us and never comes back after 15-20 minutes. It's happened 3-4 times so now I'm done even trying. It's not like once they had a bad day. Maybe I will get take out. They delivery and will make orders right if they forget something but delivery is on the slow side even at non prime times.
I was quite surprised at the fact they serve the food so quickly. Unfortunately though its prepared in advance and was not tasty. Very small servings

Tacos Cancun has the best tacos in town.

So there are basically four (very different) Mexican options in the Lambertville / New Hope area...

*Tacos Cancun - Great authentic Mexican style tacos.  These are the smaller , traditional sized tacos with minimal toppings and super flavorful meat... the carne enchilada (spicy pork) is awesome.
*El Taco Loco - Pretty good tacos.  Somewhere between totally Americanized and authentic Mexican. Tasty and slightly larger than the ones at Tacos Cancun, but just not as delicious.  Still a solid taco though... especially the fish tacos.  And my wife says their enchiladas rock due to the amazing homemade red enchilada sauce.
*Tortuga's Cocina - Totally Americanized, giant burritos and overstuffed tacos.  While not at all authentic, there are times when you just crave that giant taco platter with lettuce, tomato, and the side refried beans & rice... usually when hungover or something.  You get a lot of food for the price and it's attached to Mitchell's Tavern so you can get drinks as well.
*Blue Tortilla - AVOID.  Not even worth talking about.  Bad on so many levels.

There are also some tacos on the menu at Triumph Brewery as another option... and I think all of their bar food is pretty solid believe it or not.  They do care about what they put on the plate, which is nice for a brewery.  It's borderline gastropub type food.  Slightly refined versions of things that are usually heavy and messy.  The nachos are a good example.  Theirs are done well.

I tried this place several times always "giving it another shot". Evertime it was the same thing. The only thing worse than their pretentious clientle is the rude staff. Everytime they acted like they were doing me a favor by giving me mediocre coffee after a ten minute wait. I dunno. Maybe my jeans weren't tight enough.

I've been twice, and this is the best brisket I've had outside of Texas (the only place I've had epic brisket). The ribs were pretty good, but I think I'll pass on them in the future since they have a little too much gristle for me (I prefer TN style, being a Tennessean). Locals love their meat covered baked potatoes, but I can't vouch for those. Just buy a pound or two of brisket with some sauce and then go home and pig out with your favorite sides (I always find sides at BBQ places to be underwhelming, so I didn't try Hank's). In other words, I'm just giving them 5 stars for the brisket. Damn, I am starting to salivate.

Absolutely love the place. Staff makes some killer craft cocktails. Kristen was amazing and suggested a few different ones for us. I want to eat everything on the new food menu. They really stay close to the NOLA vibe. The chef even made a special vegan dish for us! For sure recommending.

Best Sushi in West Chester and it doesnt hurt your wallet. Ive been here numerous times for lunch / dinner. The resturaunt was reccomended to me by a friend, now I reccommend it to everyone. Atmosphere is suttle, nothing loud or outragous. We went here ounce for a friends birthday, great warm saki and great fun time with good service on a party of 10. Definitly get the Pink Lady, my favorite roll from here.
Amazing breakfast! Everything is very flavorful! They have tons of options to fit anyone's preferences! Definitely stopping in next time I'm in town!

Zero stars wasn't an Option. This dirty dingy Ghetto Walmart. Store shelves are always empty. No staff diversity anymore. Just a bunch of hoodrats working here young and old. They now have security. I see why.
Their system is always down. The customer service registers are held up by clear tape. Managers complain about the staff and customers out loud. So damn unprofessional. I'm done with this location. I spend so much money at this store and I don't know why. I brought my husband a dremel tool and went to return it. Didn't have my receipt. Ok no problem they looked it up in their credit card system. Only to turn around and blatantly accuse me of already returning the item. What I look like doing that. I'm not desperate for money I make enough. but the audacity. The old black man at the return register with the 1962 ponytail Victor Vincent whatever that clown name is rudely slide the item back and said it's your item now we're not taking it back while his manager Tamika stood there and listened. This Walmart needs to be shut down like the Ghetto East Norristown location. It's coming soon. I can feel it. Inconveniently I will drive to Street road or maybe even Hilltown to go to Walmart anything but here or Cheltenham Ave. I don't care what time it is at night. Pass this location by don't waste your time unless you like being disappointed in every way..

If you want heavenly half shell treats, run straight to Acme Oyster House for the chargrilled oysters. Locals and tourists alike are well informed on this establishment, so get there early or late for a weekday lunch to avoid the crowds. 

I was fortunate enough to experience Acme twice last week, once with a local, and a second time when my husband joined me. On my first visit, I enjoyed the Peacemaker po'boy, which was packed to the gills with perfectly fried oysters and shrimp and slathered with a zesty Tabasco-spiked mayo. The next visit I sampled the aforementioned chargrilled oysters, which were grilled with a hint of spicy butter and Parmesan cheese. Once the oysters vacated the shell, the oyster juices made for an excellent flavorful dipping sauce for the bread. In addition, we also ordered a side of jambalaya and hushpuppies. 

The "bad" food was pretty darn tasty (hushpuppies 3 and jambalaya 4), but the Peacemaker and chargrilled oysters were a easy 5. The service was helpful and personable, and also a 5. 

I recommend sitting at the bar, where you can be dazzled by the expert oyster shucking and the incredible oyster-inhaling record board. House record is 42 1/2 dozen. That's 510 oysters - in a sitting! 

I can't argue with the prices for this place either, which were exceedingly reasonable, unless of course, you're one of these folks aiming for the 15 dozen (oysters) club.

I had crave catering cater my baby shower. The experience was nothing short of incredible. Everything down the the table clothes were provided, the food was some of the most delicious I have ever had and the chef was loved by all!!!! I highly recommend crave catering for any important event!

I came to New Orleans with 3 things in mind that I had to do, in no specific order:

1. eat beignets
(check! Cafe Beignet)

2. eat jumbalaya - the way I think it should be eaten, the original way with rabbit and sausage
(check! Coop's place)

3. eat cajun/creole food and French food done New Orleans style
(check! Coop's place for cajun/creole & Lilette for French food done New Orleans style)

So we were walking around the French quarters in the unforgiving 100+ degree sweltering NOLA heat as we saw Cafe Beignets and my eyes immediately lit up. I looked left, crossed the road, started walking really fast and poof, I was inside with my friends following me. It's quite long and narrow with cute metal victorian chairs that cannot fit your bum if you weigh 200+.  It barely fit my 169lb bum...

The decor on the wall is quite interesting...it's sorta tropical and paradisey with victorian chairs and wobbly wrought iron tables with tile on them. Funky.

Anyway, we ordered:

+ sweet tea (4.25 yelps)
----apparently, you're supposed to do sweet tea with beignets and that's what we did. It was quite good - sweet, iced, and was a well brewed tea

+ iced coffee (3.75 yelps)
----the iced coffee was a strong black coffee, no cream and no sugar. Was good and complemented the beignets well

+ one order of beignets (3 are served in the order) (4.37 yelps)
----fried doughy sweet powdery messy goodness. Reminds me of eating zeppoles or doughnuts done traditionally in a paper bag (i.e. the week before @ Pike Place market in Seattle)

Thoroughly satisfied and the best beignets I've ever had. I can't give it 5 yelps as I need to become a beignet expert and then realize it's in the top 2-3 beignet places ever in my experience. Then, and only then, it may get 5 yelps.

go eat here and get fat
Clean restaurant, clean bathrooms, great fresh food and friendly servers. Love this place!

As a fan of the original Function Coffee Labs in Bella Vista, I had try out this new location when it opened. The name was taken from the coffee roasting and catering business, and has a new bakery, so the pastries are baked in house at this new location. The latte I had was just as good as at the original location, and the ham and cheese croissant was tasty (I believe many their pastries are made with sourdough, so might be a little different from what you might expect, or be used to). To top it off, the service is also to notch at this new location. Definitely stop by, of you're near Rittenhouse Square.

Another unpleasant oil change experience. Again, no one answers the phone when you call to make an appointment. They then call back the next day which can be hit or miss if you don't have a cell phone. 

Then you go to the appointment with someone in another car to drive you home/work and it's almost impossible for them  to find a place to park and wait. Go in to give the keys and they are short staffed so you wait until someone is available, even behind walk-ins w/o appointments.

When the oil change is completed they don't call you to inform you, you have to call them.

To add insult to injury, when we picked up the car they gave us a form that showed what they'd checked and they wrote that the tire pressure was off so they filled the tires to 40 psi. The door jamb say 33 front, 32 rear.

I've had new cars serviced in Reno at Toyota, Mazda and Ford, as bad as Ford was, and I'd never buy another Ford from them, Lithia Subaru has been the worst.

I did not like their "The Hour Long Joke" performance, it wasn't funny and it felt pretty forced on top of the music severely hurting my ears. I'm not really too sure what to take away from the performance, maybe it was improv or something but the way they delivered their scripts and dialogue was not great. After sitting until the end and giving the show a chance, it dawned on me, "Was having the audience endure an almost two hour long intentionally unfunny show part of the so-called one hour long joke ?"

I'm surprised to see the two reviews here.  A review from St Pete Florida and California?  This is not a neighborhood dry cleaner for either of these people.

I live about a mile from this cleaner.  Until recently this was an excellent cleaner.  This year the entire staff changed ( and presumably ownership changed too).  Immediately I noticed a difference in the customer service.  The new staff is impersonal, unengaging and occasionally rude.  My shirts are sloppy after laundering and buttons are often missing.  I had a shirt that was one week old returned with two missing buttons.  To top it off, they increased prices and reduced a pre payment discount that has been offered for years.

I am so disappointed in Varsity's decline that I have decided to try a new cleaner.
Great atmosphere, super friendly staff, and just a fun place to to be.  Oh yeah, their Cajun chicken pizza is insanely good

This salon used to be very friendly and good.  There were nice stylists that did a nice job.  Something has changed and it seems a requirement now that the stylists have attitudes.  Asked one to take my son's hair shorter.  Instead of asking how much shorter, she took a 1/2 inch.  It now sticks up all over his head.  Why not just take a 1/4 inch?  I know.  It's because she was defensive about having to redo it!  Poor customer service!  She needs to work alone in a file room away from the public!
Super fast, friendly service. The lot is well lit and they make it super easy to transfer your bags and get you on the shuttle.

Bonefish is a classic favorite that manages to keep things fresh. I haven't visited in a few years, and I was pleasantly surprised to find some old favorites on the menu (hello, bang bang shrimp), as well as some new delights. The Saucy Shrimp turned out to be a pleasant surprise, and the salmon pasta looked light and refreshing.

One unexpected delight is the Bonefish cocktail menu. From sweet treats to smoky sips, you really can't go wrong. The wait staff was phenomenal and the service was pleasant without being overbearing. One note - the AC did not appear to be working properly, so that could be an issue if it goes unattended much longer, but overall I would definitely return once the climate is regulated within.
Very good food.  Service excellent.  Enjoyed our fancy tacos and the guacamole is fabulous. Quite a bit of variety.

This rating was higher because I just went there today with my friends and the food was much better than the first time we went there. The salad, the calamari and the bread was good as usual. Service was excellent.
Rachelle at Bardenay (airport edition) is awesome! Super sweet and knowledgeable. Great new bar for the airport!!

I like this place a lot.   Great View of the water...   $3 build your own bloody mary on the weekends, $3 mimosa's.
Breakfast menu is very small, but a decent selection.    service has been terrible both times.   We literally sat there 30 minutes before we got a drink-- although the waitress forgot about us after taking our drink order  (even after asking what we wanted to drink, setting our table and grabbing the sugar, yet she claimed she had never been to our table , (drugs are bad kids...)
but other than the poor service, the breakfast has been great both times.  our skillets were drenched in grease but the taste and calories were worth it.

Heading to the Reno area to visit friends for the weekend, but we needed somewhere to eat Friday night (7-30-10).  So, I did some research (yelping) and came across ZoZo's which I noticed had a solid 4 star rating with 30+ reviews.  I told the wife about the place since she's the picky one and even though she wanted to go to Johnny's Ristorante to eat, I convinced her to take a chance and give my fellow yelper's the benefit of the doubt.  The gamble paid off.  We found a new place to dine in Reno.  

ZoZo's sits in a strip mall at the corners of Moana Ln & Lakeside Dr.  Basically, it's in a "if you blink, you'll miss it" spot, so keep your eyes open.  Parking is ample and abundant and well lit at night.  The area surrounding the restaurant isn't so great, so I suggest driving and not walking around the area alone.  Upon entering ZoZo's, you'll find it reminiscent of the old 70's style pizza joints.  It's dark, but cozy.  It's dimly lit by candles and has the red pleater seats that squeak when you sit down.  In other words, a fun and nostalgic place (at least for me).  I made reservations for 7:00 pm and we arrived a few moments early.  As we walked in, we were immediately greeted by the owner Judy who seated us right away.  Our waiter (Pepe) came over within a few moments to take our drink orders and he explained the specials on the menu.  We selected a Chianti wine and we went with Pepe 's recommendations for our appetizer, dinners and desert.  

Prior to any food hitting our table, a loaf of fresh garlic bread was given to us to munch on.  The goodness of the bread has been beaten up already, so I'll skip the details and move on.  

Our Appetizer:  Quail cooked to perfection placed upon a bed of artichokes, onions and spinach.

Our Salad:  Was a basic green salad with croutons, cherry tomato's and a house "creamy italian" dressing. 

Our Dinners:  The wife selected the New York Steak topped with  Gorgonzola cheese accompanied by Asparagus and Mashed Potato's.  I went with the Cioppino on a bed of Linguine pasta.

Our Desert:  Only Tiramisu would do.

As some of you already know, I rate the totality of the restaurant when I dine out.  Nothings left out or missed.  Everything from the bathrooms cleanliness to the wait staffs attention to detail, it's all fair game.  So as far as ZoZo's overall rating goes, this place is a solid 4 star with a 5 star potential.  I enjoyed watching the owner Judy take the time to conversant with all the patrons in the establishment as they dined (which is rare nowadays) and I really enjoyed our waiter Pepe's kind and friendly attitude.  Pepe is a true gentleman as defined by Webster himself.  The food was "out of sight" and the ambiance of  the establishment can be described in one simple word; "nostalgic."  

Now for the cons of my review:  1.  ZoZo's is NOT open for lunch on the weekend.  2.  The mens restroom was a bit unkept.  3.  I had my heart set on an espresso after dinner, but their machine wasn't working.

Overall, ZoZo's is still a solid 4 stars restaurant.

I am from new Orleans and have had many good meals in this town.  Herbsaint is average to below average with both food and service.  I would recommend spending your money elsewhere as there are many more options that are way more satisfying.

This company starts out great however, after the first cleaning changed my cleaning team due to an emergency... which I understood.  After that, the team changed two more times.  Finally told they found my permanent team which was fine for a couple months until cleaning crew cut corners.  Requested to be reassigned another team which was perfect then another change!  Office first stated the change was due to my request that I didn't like the new team.  NOT THE CASE!!  Then they back tract saying it was because the team I liked merged with another team (which cut corners).  Asked when did the merge happen... one week ago yet I received a call The day before my service to tell me no service will be provided that day.  When asked, why I was not contacted prior to The day before my service, I was told they just finalized the team a few days ago...Too many discrepancies! Looking for a more organized and reliable company to work with who wants my business!

Cool atmosphere and great band.  We were very disappointed with the "punches for the table", definitely not worth it.  They had the largest ice cubes possible in there and came out to 4.5 drinks, stick to the beer and sidecars.

Food was average, had the turkey pastrami - would have rather had Arby's.

Pot pie was pretty good, so if your going to get something get that.

I would suggest sticking to drinks and truffle fries and head over to Eddie Vs for dinner.

The food was very good.  I had the lo mein combo and my wife had sushi.  The most impressive part, though, was the waiter.  That guy was going 100 MPH...never stopped.  Soda never went dry!

Great place!!!

There is the potential for private karaoke to be an enjoyable experience, but the karaoke system is so complicated that it uses up all your time to figure out what's going on. There is no easy way to scroll through and browse song options -- you have to know what you want and then you can search for it. There is a TON of music, but limited U.S. artists, so it was hard for us to scroll through such a huge volume and find songs that we knew. I think a simple binder with the song list that's on their website could go a long way -- we eventually pulled up the song lists on our phones, browsed songs that way, then searched them on the in-room device to add to the queue.

We didn't figure out how to adjust music to mic volume ratio, and one mic was on a half second delay. The waitress said she'd help us figure that out, but didn't end up sorting it out. Service was otherwise fine, food was fine. Drinks are expensive. The building is beautiful and the rooms are nicely appointed. I wouldn't go again because of limited selection and difficulty in finding songs.

Ordered to go from here, some of the best Mexican food I have had since moving to the area. We ordered the Nachos, shredded beef quesadilla, and a steak and chicken burrito. The salsa was spicy and flavorful. Everything had its own unique flavor and the homemade chips were crunchy and crisp. Definitely will be going here again!

3.5? thats maybe a fairer assessment. I wasn't blown away what was offered but its still  good sandwich. The bread is decent but its nothing special or super soft. I wish the meat was a little more moist, but it still does a good job. the peppers can creep up on spiciness after a while, but thats fine. It actually does really well as leftovers surprisingly.

Me and my boyfriend went here hoping to have some quality BBQ. Our food was delicious and came out quickly but the service was horrible. We were served the wrong food and then told that is what we ordered (which is was not). I also waited at least 20 minutes for a glass of wine, which then I was fed up and took my credit card out to pay the bill. The bartender then QUICKLY came over snatched the credit card from me. I'd only he was that quick at serving a drink. We each only had one drink the entire time we were there. Might I add the place was dead, so the bartender was not busy. I wouldn't return. You're better off getting take out from there.

First time, won't be the last! Punctual and friendly. Was having areas of specific pain and my massage therapist listened to what I had to say and tailored my full body massage into a very detailed massage working my problem areas. Left feeling relaxed and very happy overall! Great experience

Service was ok, IPA I ordered from tap was empty, ordered my food and was told the wheat bread had ran out. Utensils weren't given, we had to ask. Chicken fingers came out with the middles still raw and fries seemed like they sat in water, sent them back. I finally recieved my turkey sandwich (not sure how you screw that up) and I could barely hold it, the bread was so soggy it all fell apart and the turkey looked and tasted like spam. Get rid of the bimbo on the menu and the sticky substance on it..it's not hooters. I would give -1000 if I could.
This place is a real hidden gem, the food and service are equally great every time.  Try the mussels and spicy red sauce, delicious.
I've eaten at some ligit mexican places before but this is the BEST i've ever had. Wow.
Delicious hamburger washed down with a crispy Diet Coke in an upscale bistro atmosphere. Service was quick and accurate; my server took the time to chat with me about Boise, much appreciated.

We'll be back!  Friendly staff, charming atmosphere and close to everything. We were given an updated room that was newly renovated, with no carpet. It had wood-look flooring. The room was clean (except for a bit of dirt in corners of bathroom floor) and there were no signs of bugs of any type. If you're looking for luxury, this isn't the place for you, but if you want to experience the history and charm of the French quarter, this is it!  In the past, I've stayed at the Wyndham and Hotel Monteleone but I liked this hotel better. The smell of jasmine in the back courtyard is heavenly.

Wife ordered green curry with tofu and got chicken instead. She ate it but if we had been with a vegetarian it would not have been acceptable. While a lot of food at $45 for lunch for two a bit pricey. The hot tea was tasty. But the meal overall wasnt very flavorful.

Perfect in so many ways.  This was the last dinner we ate while visiting for Mardi Gras and it was the proverbial icing on the cake.  The seafood was fresh and delicious.  Our waitress, Elizabeth, was wonderful.  The open view kitchen and great wine list were just bonuses.

The delivery guy would not give me my food because I didn't have a tip. I ordered my food on grubhub so it was already paid for. He through the food to the ground and started hitting me. Then he tried to stab me with a pen. I told him I was calling the cops he started screaming" f**k you muthaf**ka!!" Then when I went in my house  he kicked my door in. I want to press charges on him but the restaurant wont give me his name. I don't recommend this place at all.
Delicious pizza and a nice beer selection. The outside seating is spread out generously, so it's prefect for social distancing! My family and I will definitely be back.
I had the catfish dinner and it was amazing. The potato salad & baked beans as my two sides were delicious as well.  Great service!  I'll be back.

Had a little trouble finding the place as we were in NOLA for the first time and this was our first stop after dropping off our luggage. Misty was the best server we've had in years.  While it wasn't too busy when we got there as things picked up she never slowed down.  Char-broiled oysters, crawfish bread, and gator bites were all delicious!

I recently stayed here on a Saturday night and was very pleased with the quality of service as well as the look and upkeep of the room and hotel. Despite being located in an old building in Indianapolis, the accoutrements are all modern with nods to the city dotted throughout. We were upgraded to a corner executive suite on the top floor, which would have had a great view if not surrounded by a swath of unsightly rooftops below. If you can get past that, there's a nice view of Lucas Oil Stadium. The room had a huge television mounted on the wall and a king size bed, which felt a little short, length-wise. The hotel is centrally located in Indianapolis and within walking distance to the mall, Lucas Oil, Bankers Life, and a number of restaurants and bars. I'd stay here again.

Is it authentic, traditional Vietnamese? No. But it's delicious! Mopho has been a staple for us for a while... it has really good, really interesting food for an excellent price point. It's more of a South Louisiana twist on Vietnamese. They even have a kids menu (that doesn't just feature chicken nuggets). The best veggie pho broth I've ever had. Weekly & daily specials are good too!

After watching the food network special on pats vs geno's, I decided to take the pepsi challenge on my recent trip to philly.  I knew going into it that it most likely wouldn't be much of a challenge but I went in with an open mind.

After a few bites into each (actually one bite into each) it was obvious that pats wins hands down.  Geno's just doesn't have the right taste and they dont chop their meat.  Sorry Geno's but your mass of annoying (and hideous) neon lights, unsanitary conditions, and greazzzzy employees (yes greasy so bad you have to spell it with 5 z's) will forever keep me away from your restaurant.

Such a staple in my life even though the owner has no clue who I am. He walks around and says hi to everyone except for me and the people I bring in, none the less ,I love stopping in for a pungah to quench my appetite.

Whaaat?! Why is this not something I can have access to in the Bay Area? This is like getting some bomb.com fair food or Disneyland food but for half the price. $6-$7 dollars for a molten pizza crust cone of cheese and toppings? YES. PLEASE. Go try this- right now. If you like pizza like any sane person this will give you a whole new experience. They stuff your bread cone full of cheese, sauce, and meat and/veggies, put it in a spinning oven that looks pretty neat, and out comes a piping hot cone of deliciousness. If you like hot pockets get some class and have a pizza cone instead. One thousand percent better. Awesome idea executed well. 


I'm a fan! I will be back. Thank you coned. Thank you.

If Hillary is visiting  the Secret Service won't let ya' in.  When hubby Bill was runnin' for Prez before Bushie, the Clintons enjoyed the excellent shakes. Bill & Hill stayed down the street at the midtown Loews Vanderbilt Plaza Hotel during Bill's campaign when swinging(not literally?) through Music City.  Maybe during the third Clinton campaign Elliston Place Soda Shop will again be graced by Clinton.
I wondered why they had two dozen brown eggs for five dollars when I got home I found out. Over six eggs broken between the two cartons.

A gem on St Roch Street. They should do more advertising.  I have been here several times and always enjoy the food.  There are several small kitchens set up serving dillicious food

The prices of everything are very reasonable.   They offer a variety of diiferent types of food.  

The sweet plantains were an awesome appetizer from the Haitian shop.   The crab cake plate with has potatoes and sweet corn priceat$11 was amazing from another shop.   The spicy ginger tea, did the job

Unfortunately I can't remember the names but they were great. Oh from the photo is the name of the Haitian Restaurant.   Spicy Ginger tea too

I plan to go back for Breakfeast because they had some different types of food

It's been a few years since I've stayed the night at Silver Legacy. On our last visit, we were greeted with a glass of champagne while we waited in the long hotel check in line. That was a really nice touch.

The rooms were standard.  I would love to see what their pool looks like during the summer.  I really enjoy visiting Silver Legacy to walk through the casinos and hang out with my friends.  Their Sunday brunch was noteworthy!

This is my second time reviewing this location after a very poor experience the first time I visited. Management reached out to me, which was appreciated. This time I visited with a couple co-workers. Service was okay. The hostess could use a few tips on their attitude. I visit the Speedway location often and find it to be a much more pleasant experience than here.

We purchased our AC system last year from TCA. The service was excellent. Today, their technician, Susie came over for the yearly check up. I was pleased to see a woman in this field. She was very thorough, professional and competent. It's a pleasure to do business with this company.

Felicia in Seminole

Their sales team sucks. Went to purchase two firearms. Both times was told that the display was the only available firearm for sale. I requested a discount on both, and both times a new firearm was magically discovered in their inventory. Lol. On the other hand the people behind the counter are super helpful and friendly.

More food for your buck than a good truck. Hoagies, paninis, "specials" like a salmon burger, poor pizza selection (but hey, there's pizza!), fresh and abundant salad bar. 

They also have revolving monthly specials (i.e. dollar off foot long hoagies!).

My friends and I came here to celebrate pride and they wouldn't let my friend in because they claimed her ID was fake when it wasn't!! This was her first time celebrating pride since coming out and she was very excited but was denied. They refused to scan her ID and when we asked to speak to a manager they said they were the manager and couldn't do anything about it. This was very upsetting and ruined the night. Woodys needs to have a better system in place when it comes to things like this. Totally not okay!!

Pancheros is very much like Chipotle, minus the long lines!  The one thing they do that really stands out is that they press your tortilla from fresh dough as you order, which I think really makes it taste quite good.  Portions are decent and the prices are fair, although if you add a number of extras that can escalate quickly.  The service has been consistently good and I would pick up one of their "frequent diner" cards to get stamps towards a free burrito.

So glad we were able to have lunch here while visiting Franklin.  Read other reviews & found menu items that sounded good to us were some of the same others liked - the shrimp hush puppy appetizers, the shrimp, oyster & catfish bucket & the bbq shrimp & whiskey grits.  Loved it all!  Coupled with friendly service, we felt like 'hanging out' 'til dinner time & trying some other entrees (but didn't)!
One of the few places you can get chauource.  It's not the same as the real deal from France since it's pasteurized but still very good.

Delicious. Service was prompt, food was fresh, extremely satisfying even for omnivores, and especially gratifying for my vegetarian boyfriend. Menu had lots of tantalizing options, definitely worth checking out!!!
Absolutely the best NY Style pizza in Florida! Have eaten a lot of pizza and this is by far the best crust, sauce, cheese. Highly recommended!

I have been to so many different nail salons in my life and this is the best one. Its top notch for a general nail salon it pretty much has everything, a slightly boutique vibe, does gorgeous acrylic, long relaxing spa like pedicure, and its clean with a very friendly and helpful staff. It is really hard to find a nail salon that hits all the main points of great service. I have found that some places may do a great pedicure but not a good full set. Or they do a great full set but dont do a good job on pedicures or natural nails. Or the place is dirty and your stressed while you there. NAY NAY this places literly does everything including just having a cute clean spa to the T. The downside is that as they are growing in popularity they are more difficult to get into and there prices have gone up a tinge. It is worth scheduling a appointment and paying 5 more dollars I promise you.
One tip: They are always busy so you must have a appointment. 
one more: sometimes they can be kinda shit about answering their phones give them time, leave a message or call back a bit later. Again worth the trouble.

After reading the good reviews, I decided I would try this place out. I already have places I like for pho in Philadelphia, so I was curious how this place compares. The verdict? Not good at all.

The biggest problem with pho was the broth. It was too salty. I almost never think anything is too salty, and this broth was salty to me. The broth also lacked complexity. The saltiness was flat (compared to other places), as if they just added salt to the broth and thought that it was good enough.

The meat. The brisket, flank, fatty brisket was not nearly as good as other places (especially Nam Phuong). The meat broke apart to all over the place and it seemed messy.

Finally, they got the order wrong on two accounts. I ordered regular and they brought large. And I ordered #44; they brought me #45. I wasn't going to argue over a bowl of soup that costs like $7 to remake the damn thing. But it would've been nice if they got the order right.

I think they are lucky to get even 2 stars. Their portions are HUGE though. If you order a large bowl of pho, you're good to go, even if you're a hungry 18-year-old (I think). If you want a *good*bowl of pho, go across street to Nam Phuong or Pho Ha on 6th.

What a refreshing place! An expensive supermarket turned into aisle after aisle of adventures. I love how the refrigeration units were turned into bookcases! Minimal seating, but I had no problem finding a place to sit and read for a bit.
Strange restaurant.  Plastic silverware, salt and pepper packets, food was just okay and the service was mediocre.  Won't be back.

I've visited 55 South now a few times, so I think it's time for a review.  I've actually only been for drinks and oysters; I've perused the rest of the menu and it looks pretty good though!

As for the oysters: right on.  They were very fresh and I'd come back and eat them here any day.  My only criticism is that they seemed like they'd been shucked for a while (not freshly shucked to order), so liquor had run out of some of them and they were a tad on the dry side.  Didn't affect the flavor but I like to have all the juice!

The drinks have always been great here including the martinis.  I tend to be a wine gal so stick with those mostly, and they have a pretty good happy hour until 6:30 I believe ($5 glasses).

I'll certainly be back here in the future when I get a hankering for oysters, or maybe someday I'll actually try the rest of the food!

Let's get this out of the way:  The "service" was awful.  
Now, on to the food:  After having been to a couple of fish boils, I was pretty keen on checking out Rhone's Friday fish pot.  What was supposed to be a Thanksgiving-grade plate of flavorful abundance turned out to be what I think is my most disappointing restaurant experience.
