Shocker:  I go to local restaurants ALL THE TIME (at least as much as I can afford to) and I haven't had such a long wait ANYWHERE in St. Pete. I was willing to give you guys another shot since I liked the food but when a friend and fellow Yelper told me about your response to me, it really turned me off to ever giving you another dollar.  The fact that you're unwilling to admit your mistake, apologize, and improve is really a shame.  To go further and argue with customers who gave you their $$ borders on the insane. 

Quality restaurants produce consistent food and service, something you're failing at. I can see by a number of your other reviews that other people have had a similar experience 

**Yelpers please see the reviews from the following folks: Devil M, Ej P. Jon C, Andrea I. Sandra A, Judith H.**

All the Best!

The Rack has been a place I've envied for being able to almost separate it's douchey late night crowd, from it's AYCE regulars in a space that is far too small to house an eager billiards, crowd the frat kids and seasoned sushi veterans, but sometimes it's caught slippin....(Hyde Parkers are starved form any real pool to be had) A vast difference from it's Brandon crowd where they have a respectable space, but then the bar area still manages to smell like puke. I love you Rack, but sometimes I wanna kill ya.

Thieves. First of all, I never got a fair price on my membership. They advertise $55 per month and or whatever reason I was charged $60 per month. I called and emailed several times about this and was offered no clear explanation other than "that was the price when I signed up" even tho $55 is on the website and brochure. 
I froze my membership (put it on hold) and was not told when automatic charges would resume. I called today to extend the freeze after I saw a new $60 charge to my bank. Again, I was not offered an explanation other than I should have "inferred" the deadline to freeze. The manager does not care about making the customer happy or treating people fairly. Don't be fooled by the friendly appearance of a rock climbing community. This is a predatory gym who sneakily charges people. I am so glad I finally cancelled my membership.
Had the Espanol burger. It was OK. Just OK. Nothing special. Was a little slippery and messy. Side order of tots,.... Mehta. Nice ambiance.

Chorizo tacos on corn tortillas. OMFG. That is all.

Oh wait, their mojitos are good as well! 

Minus one star for all the mosquito bites I got while sitting outside, but that's in no way, shape, or form the restaurant's fault. Just a minor glitch in my entire experience.

The Steamboat NATCHEZ, owned by The New Orleans Steamboat Company, is the last authentic Steamboat on the Mighty Mississippi River. I enjoyed the authentic experience of a grand paddle wheeler on a leisurely, two-hour cruise on the Mississippi. During my cruise I also enjoyed a margarita cocktail and all the sites along the river. There are four decks, but, the top deck had the best views of course. Unfortunately, when we reached our halfway point to turn around a storm moved in and our return was with windy rainy. There was little interior room inside the boat to stay dry. By the time we returned to dock the rain had stopped so I was able to walk back to my Hilton Riverside Hotel. Check out my pics.

This is where I mainly get all my produce.  Great prices and fresh veggies.  This is also a nice place to get grains and other staples such as rice, beans, quinoa since you can get this bulk and just get what you need or however much you need.  The deli has a nice selection of meats.

Love the concept. Food 7, presentation was 10, experience was a 10, wine was a 50. I rated this high, because I love the idea of non-franchised restaurants. To me I rather have something coming from the imagination of a gifted chef than the minds of a bunch of corporate slobs.

I recently discovered that this store is under new management...and has a new location since my last review.  The new store is still chock-full of merchandise, but it is better organized and you can actually make your way through the store now.  The sales person was helpful (and honest when she didn't know the answer to my question).  

Still a great place for vintage and unique gifts AND the with better organization and better sales team/owners, oh yeah, I'm definitely a fan.
Our server Winston was great! Enjoyed my crab cake sandwich as well. Will return. Price was reasonable.

Awesome spot. Wings were bomb. 

Although I ordered a summer shandy and it was not a summer shandy. Still drank it though. lol 

Good food, good service, good atmosphere

After a few frightening experiences regarding how thin some of the waxers at European wax center have made my eyebrows I finally found Nayeli. She is really great and always listens to how I want my brows to be full. Today I showed up for my appointment with Nayeli and they told me she was running 30 minutes behind schedule. I could not wait because I had class, so I reluctantly decided to use another waxer. I told the waxer I liked my current shape and wanted to keep them full so to just clean them up. When I saw them I was extremely disappointed. They are now so thin, probably the thinnest they have ever been, and exactly the opposite of what i wanted. Not only are they way too thin one eyebrow is completely uneven it looks like there is a chunk missing.

The young lady working here this afternoon must have been having a bad day, and we all have them, but when it includes being rude it goes being just a bad day.  
If I were the owner of this store I wouldn't be happy, and would focus my attention on coaching her in providing great customer service.  Sad to say that it was so bad I cancelled my order.

This is hands down my new favorite sushi spot by a mile! So good. So fresh. And the service was fantastic. The owner actually served us at the bar and was super personable and chatty. I'm already planning my next visit. 

Couldn't be happier to have found a new local spot for amazing sushi!!!

They have the most amazing burgers. He got the Ted's Bacon cheeseburger and I got the bison meatloaf.
While I am not a fan of green peppers in anything because it overwhelms my palette the sweet sauce topping the meatloaf masked the green pepper a bit and made the meal worth eating. 
The Ted's cheeseburger, which I snuck a bite, was fabulous and I know what I am ordering next time.
The fries are made on site and along with the burger have now become our #1 place to come for a burger dropping that 5 dudes place to 2 place.
Also o do not eat chili, I just don't.  But this chili was named Karen so I had to ask for a sample ... let us just say I ordered  a bowl to go and leave it at that.
Worst service I've ever had. Would not recommend to anyone. Good music live bad was amazing. Poor staff

A few stars taken off here for some things that may not seem important to most, however, here it goes.  I ordered the fried chicken taco and the tin roof taco.  I felt like the quantity of meat in the taco was lacking. I understand they are street tacos, but they were slim on the filling. Also, the temperature of the tacos were cool, as if the the meat was not kept warm enough. The roasted corn was a hit, as a side, however, and I enjoyed placing it as a topper to my taco to warm them up.

I had dinner at Tinto with a good friend from grad school whom I hadn't seen in 7 years. We got there early for our 7 pm reservation in anticipation of sitting in the bar but they gave us the choice of the bar or taking our table early and we opted for our table. We were seated in kind of a strange place, downstairs near the bathroom and the back door. The hostess thought my friend and I were a couple and told us it would be quieter down there and you know, whatever else she said just to make my friend and I have to joke awkwardly about having an intimate meal. I certainly would have preferred the main floor with more natural lighting. There were patrons and employees buzzing past us quite a bit, but I was engaged in conversation, so it didn't bother me much. Another couple was seated near us at some point and that was slightly awkward as I think they were a relatively new (older) couple and every time there was a pause in their conversation I felt like the woman was staring at us.

My friend ordered a mixed drink and we also ordered a bottle of the 2009 Bodegas Taron Rioja Alta Tempranillo (which was good). We ordered the following dishes, a couple at a time: Arugula, Short Rib (a bocadilla [sandwich]), Prawns, Gatxuxa (a paella with rabbit, shrimp, and chorizo), and the green beans. Everything was excellent except for the green beans which I just didn't care for. Perhaps we were full by that point, but we only ate about half of them. Everything else was consistently good, with unique and excellent flavors. However--and this is a big thing for me--everything was just a little too salty. Look, this complaint of mine comes up again and again. I like good flavor, I like salt, but many upscale restaurants just really overdo it with the salt and it's a shame because what could be 5-star food becomes 4-star (or 4.5). As I'm writing this, other reviews for Tinto are appearing on the RH side of my screen and someone else is remarking about the saltiness.

We passed on dessert, but stayed and talked for probably an hour after finishing our meal, finishing our wine. We were not rushed out and our server, who was pleasant, continued to serve us water. All in all it was an excellent meal, but I think it's because I had excellent company more than the ambiance and the food. I'd give the ambiance a 2.5 (for where we were seated), the food 3.5 stars, averaging to a 3. I was going to give them 4, but then I realized that bias was due to my company and not the restaurant. Dinner for the two of us was $150-$160.

Very friendly family run service. We stopped in for lunch and ordered pupusa combos, horchata and guanabana drinks. I this was my first experience eating pupusas and they were very helpful in telling us how to eat them with the tomato based sauce and the crunchy salad. It was delicious. The drinks were very good but extremely sweet.

A superior restaurant in the heart of Santa Barbara. Some what old school but in a good way. Steak, seafood, and salads are of excellent quality and prepared just right. The service staff know their business. Attentive but not intrusive. Hard to go wrong here.
Crowded. Noisy. Packed in like sardines. Service was very good. I got a cheeseburger. The chef was a little heavy handed with the salt shaker. I wouldn't return.

I used to go here before new ownership took over, wasn't happy with my cut/beard shape up last visit. It took entirely too long and when I got home I found a few big spots missed by the straight razor shave and my jawline was "shaped" like I was slackjawed. A few spots on my the top of my head were also very unbalanced and shaped poorly. Considering going elsewhere next time.

Edit: This isn't a fake review, I didn't reply because changing the review wouldn't be truthful for those looking for a place for a haircut. Duke was the one who cut my hair. I appreciate your offer to remediate and I'm sure most would take you up on it.

I picked this hotel due to the reputation of the Hilton chain and it was a good location close to everything we needed.  The hotel itself was very nice, clean, nicely renovated.  Rooms were advertised as what they were, and again, very clean.  Staff were mostly nice with the exception of one front desk agent where I regrettably didn't catch her name.  We sensed a bit of hostility and attitude from her and I'm really not sure why.  Yes, there was a phone incident which was a pure accident and I'm sure caused them some unnecessary extra work.  I apologized profusely and was very embarrassed, but it was in no way intentional.  However she was quite unfriendly to us so I had to avoid her and was relieved she wasn't at the desk when we checked out.

I will stay here again though! And mmmmmm love the cookie.  They even give it to you warm (you get it when you check in)!
Great Mexican food. The chips were fresh and hot. Service was quick and our waitress was extremely friendly. I would eat their carnitas everyday. Yum.

It might smell too healthy when you first walk into this establishment, but don't let that fool you because the food is pretty good!  I've been on quite the kale kick lately so I ordered their half order of kale salad.  I was quite shocked when I received my order because it was huge (for a $4 half order) and full of fresh veggies; so much quality/value for so little money.  The dressing was good but I felt it had a little too much lemon in it, but still good nonetheless.  If this place were in Chicago I would eat here daily for lunch.

Horrible horrible service.  Super slow.  When we received our food it was disgusting.  Saturated in greasy butter.  I understand that you use that to toast but it was soggy.  The Reuben meat was dry and just chunks.  I'm not even sure what it was.  Everyone in the restaurant got their food and left before we were served.  Waitress had no idea what to ask on the menu and didn't care.  I'm not sure if it has recently sold  or what the case is but this is a true review.

Nothing Italian about Gigi's.    it is all about tourist prices and mediocrity.    I have lived here since 82 and am situated between two Gigi's.    Every few years, I give it another try.   Each time, disappointment.   Nothing I have tastes homemade or with any great flavor.    Just had a meatball sub.    Bread - boring.   Meatballs-no flavor.  Sauce - bland.   Just no reason to eat here.  The prices are extreme for casual Italian.   Better bet would be CD ROMA's or Carino's.    For pizza, worth the short drive to Little Italy at 38th Ave No and 49th St.    If not for tourism, this place would have closed long ago.

This will be forever remembered as the restaurant that got me into pho.   The shrimp and chicken pho are delicious.  My significant other loves their combination fried rice and swears that they know to leave out the onions whenever he comes (he has never asked for this but probably pushed the onions to the side the first time).  The service is incredibly quick and I honestly think this owner is awesome and is not trying to be rude (as noted by several other yelp reviewers).  Finally, the prices are great.  I highly recommend Noodle City!
Great service and excellent food. $1 tacos on Tuesdays and Happy hour all day Thursday! Great spot to chill! Highly recommend.

This small joint was pretty good. I'm not a huge cheesesteak person but I did like it - especially because the bread was good!

It did take a while for our to go order but it was kind of crowded. And in fact - having a good crowd at 3 pm says something.

I wanted to give this place a higher review. However, yesterday was my first time coming here and it was around 1-2pm on a Sunday (not busy at all). They had already run out of Passionfruit so I couldn't order several of the items that peaked my interest on the menu. So that was a disappointment. 

I ended up ordering the royal milk tea with boba - it was so good! In comparison to Green Island milk teas and boba , I prefer Bobacup!! Chewy, sweet, soft boba - yum!

The place was clean and had a fun atmosphere. Very few tables. The menu was extensive. They had Japanese crepes which I'll give a try next time I visit.

I got my drink very quickly. Service was fast and friendly. Even though they ran out of Passionfruit, the associate apologized.

On my next visit, I hope more of their other flavors are in stock/ available.

Nice people if you can get over being charged $26 for a basic men's haircut (my hair was short/straight when I had mine cut). I prefer fair prices over a great decor. One recommendation I would have for them is if you're going to charge $26, at least have a coat rack for customers (especially in the winter).  :/

We ordered a "settle for less ugly" burger, grilled chicken sandwich and large order of waffle fries. The Fries were yummy and very crispy. The Chicken sandwich was large and well cooked (not dried out) chicken and the burger was very tasty, still juicy at medium well. 

There was a very nice atmosphere, we were right next to the Big Ugly eaters and Adam took care of all of our needs and questions. My only complaint was the time it took to get our food, but at least you know everything was cooked fresh!

What a absolute joke! Where's the minus stars?!? DO NOT GET A LOAN FROM THEM! They will pull out more than what your payment is, then state that to fix this you have to go online & fill out a form so they have your signature....by the way, if you are Military.....don't even try!! NOT Military friendly at all! For 3 months, 3 times, they have pulled out a payment PLUS 1/2 of a payment! Never ever have I seen this before!

I am not a photographer but my friend his and we went there and my friend had went 9 months ago and the store owner still remembered him. The guy just has LOT of contact. he his a professional and a very nice guy.  HE even gave my friend a free film for his HAseblad. That's the other cool thing there: if you need service for a oldschool 1960 camera or a newer model, He's the man!

Should have guessed by the translucent paper bag that this was a bad idea. The burger was dripping with grease. The fries, dripping with grease. Best part of eating at Burgers Priest was the hot girl behind the counter, other than that no reason to go there.

Fabian the beach chair attendant was amazing. He was always checking up on us and always making sure everything was ok. Not only was the staff at this hotel great but everything about this hotel was amazing. So far being our 2nd day here is Fabulous
Got a very nice email from them apologizing for the experience. Adding a star for the kind follow up note.

Jason and Hope are truly dedicated about what they do. They have a true passion for food. They shop at the farmers market every week for the best local and fresh ingredients they can find. Their meals are truly inventive and delicious.

I wish I had something like this in my area...and I live in NYC! 
No honestly NYC has everything you could every dream of,  but we don't have a Spa this LARGE. I loved the size and how everything has it's own area.. and so much to offer!  Even a Med Spa with a on team Doctor.

I love going to one place and getting everything I need in one shot, instead of jumping from place to place. Mani-Ped here, Hair there, massage here... That takes forever!  So to be able to book all your services in one day, and then have lunch delivered to you is the only way to go.

In the basement they have a Spa, which is dimly lit and has a very relaxing feeling. A nice waiting area as well, I also believe the Medi Spa is located in the basement as well... 
Upstairs is more of the hustle and bustle, the hair salon, makeup area, clothing boutique, manicures... 
I enjoyed my visit. And I already scheduled my next trip for a FULL day of beauty! I can't wait. I had a salon in my old area (Cherry Hill) called Rizzieri, it's similar but I like the uniqueness of this Spa. It's a nice treat for when I come to visit the New Hope area.

(Will updated my thoughts after I get my massage and hair cut/color!)

Great first impressions!

The floor is well laid out with plenty of room in the front and back dining areas.  The space is tastefully decorated with Asian influences.

The takeout menu fits on one page, front and back, so it is not too complicated, even for a first time customer.  Appetizers run from spring rolls to fried egg rolls, dumplings and sugarcane wrapped ground shrimp.  We were there for the Pho, and had Pho Ga (chicken in steaming chicken broth with a heap of rice noodles).  The garnish of sprouts, basil leaves, jalapeno slices and lime, was fresh and added great textural flavors.  The Pho comes in two sizes, kids and regular.  The regular bowl is large enough for your pet goldfish (to swim in comfortably). Next time we intend to branch out into the sandwiches and grilled entrees, as they looked real good on the next table. 

I have loved Vietnamese coffee since visiting Ho Chi Minh City, and it was exactly the same with condensed milk and personal size french press coffee drip at the table. 
The fresh fruit smoothies looked tasty, too. Next time.

Bottom line - Maybe not quite the experience of a Pho cafe in Da Nang, or our bigger cities, but still authentic, flavorful and worth the trip. 
Highly recommended.

2.20.13 - I have been back a few times and tried the Tea (personal teapot and wonderful teas), Sandwiches (BBQ Pork on authentic French Demi Baguette very tasty), and Mango Smoothie (creamy, fruity and so good going down).
The food here is excellent. The staff are friendly and attentive. The atmosphere is a bit gimmicky but I don't hate it. I might seek it out if I'm back in the area.

First things first: If you haven't had a "Borgia," go get one now. What's a Borgia? Well, in this incarnation, it's a mocha with some orange juice. A bit wary? Don't be. It's delicious. Chocolate and orange were meant to go together.

Next: The food. I got the Mediterranean plate. It was a bit smaller than I would have expected for $12, but it tasted great. The hummus, tzatziki, pita, and veggies were all very fresh and very flavorful. The falafel was...okay. I'm not sure if it's just a unique style of falafel, or what, but it's certainly not the type I was expecting. I'm used to crispy falafel with a moist, soft interior. These were kind of grainy all the way through. They were spiced perfectly, and they were still pretty good, but they weren't exactly what I was expecting.

Finally: the service. When I went there, there was one guy (the owner, I believe) manning the whole place for lunch. He's a really friendly, inviting guy, and so good at his job that the service I got here is better than I get at most restaurants with a full staff. 

I will definitely be going here again, but mostly for the coffee, and to try the desserts.

Excellent! I had the bbq pork omelet.  Their biscuits are great! 

Well worth the wait, there's plenty to do on their property while you're waiting.
My very first Mardi Gras Krewe. What a fun time!! The floats were amazing. The beads were amazing. The feeling was amazing. Thank you for making my first time a special one.

Due to cancer, the owner of the Peg Leg Porker had to get a prosthetic leg, giving the restaurant its name which I thought was an interesting tidbit.  They also have won best BBQ in Nashville for the last three years. These were two things I learned while waiting to order (I had to wait 29 minutes to order on a Friday night).

Food: The dry rubbed ribs are incredible.  The seasoning they use would make literally anything be seasoned perfectly but the ribs are a must get here.   Based on other Yelpers, I got the green beans which were good and I am happy I got to eat some veggies although they weren't that great. I mean, I am not sure how to make green beans that great, they are pretty regular.  I also got the slaw and people were right, it was not too heavy but rather the kind that was a little sweet.  I would say definitely get that side.  I also got to try the Mac and Cheese and the Fries, both were below average and not sides I would get.

Overall: Best ribs and slaw in Nashville (Compared to Edleys and Martins) but the rest of it was pretty average.

"Does the trick" tex-mex food.  I didn't know this particular chain existed outside of Austin, but if you don't have many other local choices to go to, I would recommend eating here.  Granted, it has about a years worth of sodium and fat in any of their plates, but just go for the heart attack because it tastes good.  Try the chica-chica boom-boom plate.  It is quite good along with their house-made salsas.

We rolled up pretty late (around 9pm) and we're seated immediately on the water. We were tended to quickly but unfortunately informed they were out of pasta (a main course favorite) and fajita shells (the special for the night) - they were open until 11 so not sure what they were thinking. We "settled" with the calamari appetizer and steak/shrimp meal. It did not disappoint. Max, server, was on top of it and even sent an item back to the chef before it hit the table. Overall, great experience.
Wow! The portions are very impressive. Just a little too much for what I would consider normal which is why it's a 4 star instead of 5. Yummy food though, you definitely get what you pay for.

Just finished the dead sexy tour with Miss Loretta as our guide. She was wonderful. Made the tour that much better with her fun attitude. Was very knowledgeable. I learned a lot today. I recommend this company also because they do smaller group tours. Only had 10-12 people. Saw many tours with well over 20 people.

First time here and I am most impressed! Lots of color choices which is great! Staff is super friendly. This will be a go to when my normal guys are booked! Pricing is in line with other places in town. They also have two butterfly chairs for the littles!
Great lift to the airport! Clean vehicle, amazing driver, on time and got me into the airport without getting wet! 5 Stars!!
Bright friendly atmosphere. Traditional favorites with a slight twist and some very untraditional offerings that will become your new favorites. We've made it a weekly stop!

Had a reservation with my family on Christmas Eve. There were 9 of us and they sat us at a pretty small table which was a little difficult but ended up working out fine. The service was excellent. Really impressed by that. They had a great selection of beers and wines and the food was really good. I had the shrimp pasta and it was ok, but everyone else's food I tried was pretty amazing.

Excellent food!  Some of the best catfish I have had. Crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside. Sides were great. The cornbread dressing was the best I have ever tasted. The carrot soufflé was good-tasted like sweet potatoes.  Hubby got raw oysters, and they were huge and delicious. Sister got fried chicken, sweet potato tots and mac-n- cheese.  Everything was so good! We will be back!

By far my favorite downtown spot to party when I feel like having fun and doing the"club" thing.  The age of the people who go cover ALL ages so everyone is welcomed. The employees all are very nice. The drink selection covers pretty much everything. It's really not a place to sit down and have a fancy meal as they mostly have bar type food. The DJ's and bands are also good. Again, if you feel like partying and dancing , this isthe place to go to in all of Tampa.

Just okay. I got the 2-meat combo (pulled pork and chopped beef) with mac n cheese and potato salad. The presentation was great, nice smoke ring, a good thick bark, basically everything good smokey bbq should be.........except the taste. The smoke taste was almost non-existent, the beef was dry and blah, and the pork was very fatty and again no smoke. 

The sides, again, looked the part but weren't to my liking. The potato salad had strong flavors of mustard and pickle which I don't really care for in my potato salad. The Mac n cheese. You can't mess this up right?......try again. Sometimes less is more and this was no different. I don't know what they put in it, but I think I would've enjoyed Kraft Mac n cheese right out of the box more than this. 

So, to summarize, it wasn't on my "horrible" list but it certainly won't be a place I'd willingly return to any time soon. And oh yeah, almost forgot. No sweet tea!!! How do you have good southern bbq without sweet tea!!

Yes, I know the past reviews are horrible, but I gotta admit they renovated the place quite nicely! 

I found this place while booking our trip to NOLA. Not going to lie I was a little hesitant since the reviews weren't so hot. However, they did mention on their website they were under new management and renovating. Not going to lie they also had the best deal I could find and the deal included two swamp tours.

We stayed here last month for four nights. The lobby of the hotel is really nice and a cool vibe going on. There seemed to be more staff than people in the hotel. I think it was cause they officially reopened just a few days prior.  I do like that the ice machines in the hallways also have chilled water and your hotel room has a tall glass carafe to fill up. 

The rooms are amazeballs! I think we were the first people to stay in our room too, so that is always a bonus! The room is a little smaller than the chain hotels, but the space is used very efficiently. One thing I learned in NOLA is that many places really don't like using or blasting the A/C. The boyfriend and I were happy and relieved that the A/C in our room worked.  Trust me after being outside in NOLA summer weather, you will want a cold room! Another nice thing to note is  the shower has body wash, shampoo, and conditioner containers with pumps screwed into the wall. None of those annoying plastic mini bottles. 

The hotel and our room surpassed our expectations. So why the 4 stars and not 5? The paperwork said our stay included a continental breakfast and one staff member said it's available from 9a-11a. When we checked downstairs during our stay we didn't see the breakfast except for one day.  Not sure if they were still working out the kinks, but would've been nice to have a free breakfast.

First time going to this place and I am quite impressed. Doesn't look like much from the outside but inside it's quite cozy. We went around 11 on a Saturday and didn't have to wait but we were the last open table. I had a hard time choosing because there were so many good things on the menu. I decided to go with the Bayshore benedict and my husband got the Italian omelette. We decided we wanted to try the pancakes so we got an order to share of the classic. Let's get the bad out of the way...The pancakes were not good. They looked and tasted like microwavable pancakes. That was a waste of money. Never again. Maybe children will enjoy them. On to the good. My breakfast was delicious. It looked as good as it tasted. The eggs and cheese and tomatoes were perfectly layered and the potatoes were crispy. My husband was so jealous. The Italian omelette he got he said was really good too. They were both a lot of food so I would say to not feed your eyes before your stomach. I think the prices are great for what you get. Everything was fresh and the service was very friendly, even though we had a groupon. I would love to come back here.

I am 2 months post-surgery and doing well.  My PTH is labs are normal.  And, I am a fan.  Like others, my experience was positive and NPC delivered what they promised: surgery was quick, ALL the staff I interacted with were helpful and positive, and they followed up.  My local doctors -- an endocrinologist and a surgeon -- both agreed that the total time under anesthesia would be significantly less and that is a good thing. I truly felt better the day after surgery than the day before and spent the day out and about the greater Tampa-Sarasota area.

I give them only 4 stars because of arrogance, some of which is obvious from the web site.  Their Sestambi scan also didn't reveal any adenomas and my surgeon scoffed at the 4-D scan I had that showed 2.  Surprise, surprise, they found 2 adenomas.  I also think the $1750 charting fee is ridiculous and they make you pay the co-pay beforehand.  But, they have a monopoly, it is well-earned, so they can get away with it.  And, when it turned out that they had overestimated my copay, they refunded the difference promptly.

So, if you can swing it, go to Tampa and have the peace of mind that comes from knowing that the surgeons do this all day, every day.

I traded in a car on a purchase of a Honda Fit in June 2008.  Several months later I received a report from the Sheriffs about this car being parked on the street (near the dealership). I told them I wasn't the owner, the car had been turned into Santa Barbara Honda.  At the same time I told SB Honda of the issue.  They said they would take care of it since they had possession of the car.  Almost three years later I have received a notice from a collection agency for towing of the traded in car-towing that occurred 1 year after the trade in.  Santa Barbara Honda did not take care of the registration of this car, and although they own up to the fact that they had possession of the car at the time of the towing they refuse to take care of this matter.  They have not called the towing company or the collection agency even though they have copies of the release of liability as well as the sales receipt that shows the trade-in car with Vin number.  Don't trust them to complete the paperwork or assume responsibility for their mistakes

Chris N.

We had the best experience with Ronit! Our newly adopted dog snapped multiple times at our friends and family and we were worried about her aggression. She was also anxious often, worried when people were walking behind her on walks, and bugging our cat. Ronit was able to show us how to bring calmness to our dog and also taught us how to communicate with our dog appropriately (which we weren't doing). It was awesome! I loved her whole approach from the moment she walked in our door. Thank you so much, Ronit.

We came in for a quick bite to eat, but weren't greeted at our table for probably 15 minutes. The waitress was friendly, but the place was understaffed. When we finally got our order in, it took over 30 minutes for a salad, a sandwich, and a cup of soup. Will not be coming here again.

The man who arrived at our house to do the work was very professional and did a great job. My complaint is not with him but with the pricing. When I scheduled the appointment I was told by David that it would be $35 for each bedroom (there are two) and $45 for the "great room". When the man arrived he mentioned a $25 trip fee which had not been mentioned when I scheduled the appointment. After he measured the rooms he gave us an amount that was almost $150 more than what I was told over the phone. He called the Secretary and explained the situation and was able to get the price back down. I would highly recommend that the people in charge of scheduling be more honest with their pricing and mention the trip fee ahead of time also. Do not make your employees deal with the situation you created.

Disclaimer: I did not receive any treatment at this facility and was only there for a one hour free consultation. 

Also run away from Utopia Wellness. 

Let me just say I am very interested in holistic therapies to help heal my cancer and have a background in holistic nutrition as well. When I heard of Utopia Wellness myself and my family were very excited. I watched the testimonials and researched the facility. I then booked a consultation through Mark at the front desk. I also read the many negative reviews that centered on Dr.Garcia's character and on his malpractice that some former clients claim. We went anyways to form our own opinions. I am a skeptic at heart and would not be writing this review if I didn't truly believe that this place is bad news.

Almost 2 minutes into the consultation I was completely unimpressed by Dr.Garcia's "direct" and "tough love" approach. He recited his protocols as if he had for the 100th time, which I'm sure he has, but when you travel a distance to get information on a potentially lifesaving treatment it would be nice to be looked in the eye while listening to someone talk about it. 

When I asked questions he shrugged at me. I had to lead the conversation when I felt like if I'm about to spend $35,000+ you could maybe take some interest in my and my family. He basically read word for word from his website. In the end he blamed my teeth & an issue with a female to why I have breast cancer on the left side.

Dr. Garcia is very rude, defensive, and unimpressive. He does not create an air of healing which is what I would expect. He took no time to share any part of the facility at all with us and just dumped us into Mark the receptionist's lap. Mark is amazing by the way. Thank you to Mark for showing true care and concern. 

While I believe the therapies Dr.Garcia is offering will help someone with cancer, it would be much better received if you welcomed your potential new patients. 
 

Also once you step into the office area from the waiting room it has a pretty terrible smell. Yikes. There was also 2 instances where children were walking back and forth from the office doors unattended. Weird.

Not only is the food amazing at Wild ginger, but the effort that they put into the presentation of each plate is unbelievable. The portion sizes are huge. One sushi roll is equivalent to two sushi rolls at any other restaurant. Would highly recommend.
Really great ramen and great service. Could have done without the Taylor Swift marathon of video's on the main TV but thee food was great and the rest of the atmosphere was nice.
Always a good time and atmosphere. Staff us always friendly. Its easy to get to and recommend going to their oktoberfest

My opportunities to eat out someplace new have been limited lately so maybe that increases my expectations, but it isn't really the food as such that earned a poor rating this time.  The "Super Salad" was actually quite tasty as salads go, but it was the size of a $6 side salad rather than a $12 entree, and then I was charged $1 over menu price as well.  I doubt it would have satisfied a small child.  Food cost must be the envy of the industry.  They might at least provide bread or something to add a little weight to the "meal".

I went to Cody's Cafe with a co worker for brunch. It had a really nice diner feel to it. I miss places like these because they are being replaced with Denny's and IHOPs. I usually don't like ordering breakfast items, so instead I ordered the Turkey Santa Fe sandwich with a side salad and fries.

The sandwich was grilled and the cheese was melted. It was nice because the jalapeno added the right amount of flavor to an ordinary turkey and cheese melt. The jack cheese complimented the jalapeno as well and who could forget the sourdough. Seriously, sourdough is like the king of sandwich bread. It has such a distinct taste that far different from whole wheat or white bread. I did not have high expectations of this place, but I was satisfied and the portions were great. I loved the french fries because they were golden brown and crispy. A side of ketchup helps any side of fries, which didn't hurt. I had a great meal and our lemonades were kept full during our meals. This place is very underrated. I will definitely be back. It's nice to find these gems in Goleta. Thanks Cody's Cafe!

-Tej
This is one of my favorite places in town. The whipped feta is to die for. Every dish I've had here is fantastic, and I couldn't recommend it more.

I knew that I was in for a treat when our server showed up in a boy scout uniform. At first I was a bit confused, but that quickly subsided when I realized that the creativity of her outfit simply complimented the uniqueness of the food I was about to eat; the idea that nothing in theory goes together, yet somehow it does so perfectly. 

Take for example my "pancake" covered with sautéed veggies, meat, and a spicy sauce. Here I was with the misconception that Mrs. Butterworth was the only thing worthy enough to adorn my fluffy stacks of flour, and sugar, and goodness. Boy was I wrong. 

Come early, fight for a table, drain the bottomless coffee, devour the food, sip a cocktail, stay a little longer than you probably should, tip your server more than you often would, repeat next weekend. Hope to see you there.

The desserts are so good I can't tell a lie afterwards! The bacon maple cupcake and salted Carmel whoopie pie are amazing. If you ever want to make a great impression just show up with her pastries in hand. Forget flowers and wine... This is the best choice for life time bliss!
Excellent food, excellent service, fair prices.  Cannot wait to go again. Would prefer to give them 4 1/2 stars but it is not an option.

Wow, so I read the reviews of this place.  I seriously cannot imagine why people have issues with this place, I never have.  In fact, all of my experiences at this store have been the best possible.  If you compare their prices to other furniture stores that we have access to in the area, you will see that you certainly get what you pay for.  One of the things I like most about them is that they always seem to have things in the store that others just don't have which makes them even more special to me.  I can't imagine not going in there and seeing Christie.  She has always helped us and has been excellent to work with.  She was very helpful when we went in to find lamps.  I had looked all over Indianapolis and surrounding areas and found exactly what I was looking for here.  They are never pushy and do not follow you around.  The place is huge but fairly easy to navigate.  They have so many excellent things in the store.  The Christmas room is CRAZY!!  Seems like they may have scaled back this year a bit but it is still very nice.  if you are looking for upper scale Christmas décor, they are a great place to go.  I highly recommend this store because of the service and selection.  I prefer local businesses that take pride in their community as well as their customers.  I will always speak highly of my experiences here and will be back soon because it's almost time to replace my bedroom furniture!
I got dip for the first time, and within 3 days every single nail fell off. Refused a refund or a gift card, will not be returning.

I can honestly say I would never go back here. My breakfast was way overpriced and AWFUL!!! I ordered nutella and banana crepes. The crepes were cold and doughy. They were wet, it was just an awful experience. Our server spilled 1/2 of my glass of juice and left it on the bill and did not bring another glass. We were sitting at the counter so it is not like she forgot, she just did not care that she spilled my drink. 

My mom ordered berry french toast. It was significantly better than mine however it was still way overpriced for three small pieces of french toast. It just just not an enjoyable experience. We paid for breakfast for what we can pay for dinner out somewhere. 

Not an experience I would repeat.

The beds are super comfortable and the breakfast has a lot of really good options, both healthy and indulgent. We really enjoyed the pool area as well.

The bathrooms in the rooms are not so much bath'rooms' as a toilet in a closet and a sink in the bedroom, but it works. Also, the fitness room is smaller than any other room and has absolutely zero ventilation.

A pretty nice hotel in a bit of a strange part of Tucson. On the bright side, it's next to Target so if you forget  your bathing suit or workout clothes, you can pick some up on the cheap!

The Metropolitan has been under new management and has made new improvements to the living quarters such as upgrading the countertops, backsplash, and sink which is a nice change of pace. The apartment location is also quite desirable in Belle Meade and is super close to Vanderbilt, Belmont, hospitals, and the freeway. Overall, living in the community was quite comfortable, quiet, and enjoyable. 

It is worth noting that their business operations has been a bit shaky as inconsistencies with their contracts and their business practices become more apparent. Perhaps it's because records were not appropriately transferred as they transitioned new management. For example, several reviews have mentioned that the Metropolitan has been either overcharging or charging for extra itemized billing. I have had a similar experience with their management and have tried to resolve these issues with them for over billing (especially during move-out). 

However, their insistence and inflexibility to hear your concerns are quite deafening. It felt like my value as a resident meant nothing to them. Landlord and tenant disagreements are never fun, but I wanted my fellow Yelpers to know of the poor service I've received during my time at these apartments so that you can make a better informed decision before committing to them as your next place of residence.

excellent cocktails and decent beer. we also had some crack fries and wings both were very good!
the elote is basically just roasted corn and a bit of cheese, doesnt even attempt to imitate an authentic Elote, wouldnt recommend that. must order food with drink bc of Covid rules, the outdoor sitting area is cute and has heaters/umbrellas for the elements. will definitely return!

The absolute BEST sandwiches in Tampa! They have a large selection of side salads and many different sandwiches that you can choose from. The Cuban is enough for 2 people to share and is one of my favorite sandwiches there.

It was a very rushed Saturday morning, and I simply forgot to schedule my Shitzu/Poodle an appointment for her haircut and bath. It was desperately needed, specially since I had company coming over that night. Called about every groomer in the area and Spot Spot's was the only place to graciously take her in. This was amazing since it was the first time they were gonna have her in.

When I dropped her off she was very anxious, but the staff calmed her down and seemed to have loved her. I know when Bella is treated well because she will want to stay, and that is precisely what she did. Bella loved it there, and they made her look beautiful! Everyone that night asked me who was Bella's groomer.

I would have scored higher but our takeaway order didn't come with utensils or napkins...carryout without utensils!!! Fortunately I always travel with extra so we were able to eat!  The food was ready when they said it would be and was hot too...parillada was plenty for two but I enjoyed the spinach enchiladas...good sized amounts of food in each order...

We've been to several Thai places, but Siam Elephant is our favorite!!!  We always hit this place on our travels,  may i suggest the Pumpkin curry, i get medium spice, my daughter gets hot.  from the first bite to the last, it is satisfying... look forward to our next visit... (last ate there on 3/15/2015)

Can guarantee you won't come across anything like it anywhere else. Under new ownership by a long-time employee, the Spacebar is only getting better. Stop on in for a quick beverage or stick around for an evening with friends...plenty of beverages to choose from and a cool atmosphere.

Ehhh this place is a hit or miss.. sometimes things are fresh yet other times not so much. For the price it should always be fresh! As this place is not the cheapest. Do NOT order a salad unless you want to pay for a small plate of mixed greens with 2 little toppings and dressing unless they happen to run out which has happened. The pies are okay.rve been here on multiple occasions and ive left disapointed far more times than pleased..

this is my favorite restaurant in the whole world. the staff is always SO friendly and fast with their service. the food is meant to be shared with your table, which is such a fun concept! the wagyu is always incredible, basically perfect. i always get the crazy rice and the miso soup too! its not too expensive either.

I am the type of diner that when I go to a restaurant I judge quality of food as well as atmosphere equally. If you dine similar to the way I do I would HIGHLY suggest getting takeout from ATL wings. Lets began by saying I am very glad I went to try this place out. The prices are great for Tucson and the wings are delicious! I love the fact that they serve kool-aid (definitely brought me back to my childhood nostalgia) and the sides that I tried were also delicious. The side of fries were fresh and more than enough for two and the biscuits with honey, well; I had to stop myself from ordering multiple orders. Food was served promptly and piping hot, very very good quality! Had I known what I was in for as far as atmosphere I would have definitely gotten my order to go or sadly probably had avoided this place all together. As a diner I love to be surrounded by good conversation really about any topic. However, as a place of business besides your quality of food, your employees should also strive to make customers feel welcome. Upon sitting down to eat with my husband and newborn son I suddenly felt like I was observing the filming of a poorly written reality show. I frankly wanted to focus more on my lunch and my family than hearing the two girls behind the counter loudly talk about who texted who, smoking weed and personal relationships. I don't need to know how many shots you took last weekend, who you want to have sex with next or how your Mom got deported. I don't mean to sound harsh but I think this type of conversation is better saved for home or a happy hour. Overall I would say the food left me wanting more the conversation however made me wish more people enjoyed taking vows of silence.

Hit or miss depending on what you order. My husband got Merlin's BBQ pork and the garlic parmesan smashers. Pork was good, smashers outstanding. I got the roasted veggie salad and added curried chicken salad on top. The salad itself is very bland, couldn't taste the vinaigrette. It either needs a more flavorful vinaigrette or some goat cheese or feta to add some flavor. Curried chicken salad on top helped some. Curried charred cauliflower salad was good, but I'd love more raisins in it. Update: the owner reached out after my review , responsive management gets a star bump
One of the best pulled pork sandwiches I have ever had.  If this place was closer to me I would be a very fat man not just a sort of fat man.

Extremely friendly staff (there was only one woman working the day I went), great deals, and of course a free sample just for walking in! Their current deal that I couldn't pass up on is 75 truffles for $20! The original price is $25.

My wife and I went to Tried & True for a pre-game ceat night (diet-wise). We sat in the bar with the doors open. Decor is refreshing and clean. We ordered buffalo hot wings, parm-garlic wings, buffalo chicken dip and brussel sprouts. Wings were good (not Ale Emporium or Sahm's good) but solid. Buffalo chicken dip was standard and only luke warm. Sprouts were very good. Beer selection was very good. Our server Jocelyn...amazing. I hope the management keeps the menu and environment fresh.

DO NOT GO HERE! They are rude, unprofessional and down right nasty people. I had a woman by the name of Kelly helping me, her customer service skills suck. she was short with me. If I was asking too many questions she got annoyed. She had a bad attitude. I don't know how they are still open with how unprofessional they are. It was the worst experience at a jeweler I ever had. Not only for myself but while there, another couple came in walking around looking at the jewelry and caught a brief moment to ask her a question and her reply to them was so short, just her tone was mean. I remember the lady looking at her husband in disbelief and they just walked right out the store. If you ask to talk to the manager she's just as unprofessional her name is Lisa. And they do not want to accommodate you for anything. A coworker of mine husband purchased a ring from here and their diamonds look like crap after a few weeks of wearing them as well. Stay away from this place

Don't bring a Starbucks in this store god forbid. Never going back. Rude staff about having Starbucks as I'm about to purchase a book at the counter. I obviously put the book back on the shelf and left. Barnes and nobles it is. I didn't even know there was a cafe in there. Was looking for a book for my vacation.

The service was great however this place needs 3 $$$! I decided to get a meal and garlic naan and it was almost $20. The food was tasty and they offered a great amount veggies. May only go if I get a discount.

Went to this place the first time when I was in California. I was thrilled to find out they have one in PA considering the drive from NJ isn't long & we had plans to head there for a few days. Everything in there is delicious....u just have to pick the one that has everything u like in it. It reminds me of a similar dessert called halo-halo in the Philippines. Def look fwd to visiting again when i'm around the area.

Meh. Yes it is crisp & clean and beautiful looking but the service left much to be desired. I ordered a roulade, quiche Lorraine, and a lemon bar to go saying I was going to eat in the car. My fault for figuring they would heat the quiche for me. (Are they served cold if you dine in? Seriously,  are they??). Also ordered a chai latte which came out as basically steamed milk. I asked the girl to add some chai to it since it had NO CHAI FLAVOR and she added a very small bit. I saw and told her I use Pacific Trail at home and could she just pour some in but alas, bo more so basically I probably got a shot worth of chai for $3.50. Bummer. (Just FYI - Pacific Chai is not a syrup so needs to be mixed 1:1 with your milk) Ended up giving it to my daughter who also rejected it saying it had no chai taste. Oh well. The quiche was good but would have been much better warm. The roulade was not what she described but the chocolate ganache (?) On top was yummy. Lemon bar ok. I wont be going back. Will try other area bakery/cafes. Was excited for the 5 star rating though since they are rare. Dang it.

Bread pudding is amazing. Great way to be introduced to New Orleans. Staff is fun, and the fried chicken is top notch. We felt like we were being taken care of by family which was perfect as we were visiting over thanksgiving.
Those biscuits tho!!!!'   Yaaaaaas. The best ever in life. The biscuit was perfectly cooked, honey on top and the middle was nice and soft.  All I have to say is PLEASE get the biscuits

Made reservations for a Monday night for a birthday party, 10 top. They gladly accepted them. We showed up on time and were greeted as soon as we came in the door and seated. The place was quite small and a little cramped, but surprisingly busy for a Monday night. They were cranking out a decent amount of food for such a small place. We ordered appetizers, salads, and entrees. All arrived in good time and every plate was beyond our expectation. The prices were average and actually quite good for being on the beach. I would highly recommend this place to any of my friends or family. Just make sure you show up early as they are a little short on parking. You can park behind the building that is next door though, but there are only a few spots over there.
By far the best pizza you can find in Mt. Juliet. Don't waste your time going anywhere else!
Extremely overpriced considering the multiple other liquor stores in the nearby area.

Had an appt. they showed 45 min early when no one was home and so far (3:15 min later) no one has responded to the 3 voicemails.

Eventually they came and did the cleaning, but we had to pay extra even though we had a Groupon...

At first I thought this location would be just as good as the Illinois one. But total opposite. I am going to point out a few tingz that I disliked. 1. The service is horrible - No one comes and ask where you'd like to be seated. You jus move freely. 2. The wings are basic. The wings have no special bonus to them. Just regular hot wings. Soggy as well. 3. The food is very greasy and to add on that I found a hair in my food. I am very disappointed and would not recommend to anyone. I'd rather cook seafood myself.

I love Aveda products to begin with.  I had not shopped at this store, however, for about one year.  I visited the shop on Sunday, December 28th and glad I did.  Not only was it a pleasure to enjoy the familiar scents, but the service was professional yet personal and helpful.  Thanks to Molly for helping me choose skincare and makeup products that I've been enjoying for days.

Wish I could give this location zero stars. I went to get passport photos and they did them incorrectly costing me $200 in passport fees and I missed my trip because the passport could not be done in time. Don't understand why they offer this service if they cannot do it correctly. Horrible experience.
I had a full set of acrylics put on. Kathy did a fantastic job, just what I wanted.  I would definitely come back to her.
Despite their efforts, the smokey smell set off my allergies.  Loud crazy rock music from the seventies made it difficult to relax.  There was little action.

Nice and quiet on a Monday morning. I cannot speak of the safety of the neighborhood, as I did not go around looking. It is sandwiched between a wooded area and some type of factory. I was the only person as you can imagine on a Monday morning. Great view of the city.

This is one of the party spots in SB for my friends and I. We have had many good times in this place, some that I can never ever ever speak of, but then there are days getting drunk in the pool area, missing the 4th of July fireworks because I was passed out in the grass while my buddy was fleeing the police becaue he hit one in the parking lot while driving drunk and I woke up to an angry general manager and a rent-a-cop who were kicking me off the property, then there were hookers and I chased a pimp who stole my clothes across the parking lot screaming in front of dozens of guests and all this while my buddies wife was the catering manager who had to watch all of these wonderful displays of public dissobedience take place. But I have nothing bad to say about this place. It is absolutely the place and the suites are large and impressive and most of the guests are not like us!
Nice place with good food. I sat in the bar and ate their but they also had a very nice white table dining room available. The server was attentive and I will definitely be returning!

Terrible customer service i went to make a reservation and he told me no then when I questioned him about it he told me i was being rude and he didnt care what i had to say then hung up on me and when i called me he told me not to call again and hung up on me after I requested to speak to a manager

What a quaint place! Even if not a beer drinker, they have ciders and wine on tap. Samples are provided before having to purchase. Basic munchies are available as well. Was there on a week day and there was plenty of bar space and family style tables. If you like unicorns, this is a must see! Will be returning during my next visit to Dunedin.

The place started great.  Great salsa with the right amount of cilantro. But the guacamole was guacamole dip (read: sour cream added because the taste of real avocados is too "exotic" for our white-bread clientele). Despite this, I enjoyed it a little but I would have appreciated some real guac, you know, made primarily with avocados!  I loved that alcohol prices were on the menu.   
  
The food was pretty bad.  Normal Mexican food for Indy but pretty horrible as far as food goes.  My enchiladas (a "specialty") were swimming in super-rich queso, so much so that I had to eat the chicken out of the middle to avoid the sauce.  My wife's steak (also a "specially") was bland and fatty. 

Seriously there are other places that give you the same "blah" food without having to deal with the crazy crowds.

Extremely poor management. Man was cursing and called women several profane name while management did nothing. When management was asked about this they said he was a regular. Management was more interested in making excuses for him instead of correcting the matter. Will not go back ever. Would not recommend to anyone.

Great experience at Arirangs!  Staff is awesome!  Stephanie is one of the best.  On top of her game and very attentive to the tables needs. Liz behind the bar is awesome.  Brian and ed as managers are the best!  Very helpful and we can't forget barb!! She is the best!!

I wanted to wait until I've had both lunch and dinner at Ulele before writing a review. 
Both get 5 stars. I wish I could give 10 stars. Consistently, Ulele has been a gastronomic treat. The deconstructed seafood pot pie is amazing. The crab Mac and cheese is so creamy and heavenly that it's worth the calories, and then some. The okra fries and blistered peppers are both delicious puffs of fabulousness. 
Their own brewed beers are really good, with a variety of kinds to please anyone. The wines are also good and are stored in a gorgeous room under the stairs. 
The portobello sandwich at lunch is fantastic. The giant open doors facing the Hillsborough offered a gorgeous view, and when the sun started the blind everyone, they lowered a screen and it provided relief from the sun but you could still see out. 
The service has been pretty consistent, slow at times, attentive at others.  It takes a while for a new restaurant to get its groove, and it seems Ulele is well on its way. 
Ulele is fast becoming my favorite go to restaurant in Tampa.

Still thinking about that vegan chili piled high on quinoa. For some reason, I thought that wouldn't be enough for a meal so I ordered the olive oil cake as a "side dish" - - err dessert. Truth be told, I could barely finish the chili it was so filling (and flavorful!). 

I popped up my laptop, took advantage of the wifi while eating and enjoyed the natural light that floods in from every angle at this Monon Trailside business. I can only imagine how happening it will be in the summer with hungry runners and bikes rolling past. Beyond the chili, the menu features rotating salad options, fresh juices and plentiful baked good options. 

It's not just the chili that had me scheming for my return visit. The cause behind Public Greens is what it's all about for me. All profits from Public Greens help feed the at-risk kiddos of IPS with an educational after-school program. The program teaches food preparation, nutrition and feeds the students. Money well spent, right?

Very nice people working at the restaurant, and hard working, but unfortunately, I didn't get the hype. There was a long wait time for the meal and it was expensive for the meal that was received. None of the taco meat (beef/chicken) had any flavor (ni siquiera sabor sal). The food was unsatisfying.

Showed up around 4:30 on a Saturday when not only the NFL draft was going, but the local hockey team (go Bolts!) was playing in the playoffs for the cup. Anyway, found the last parking space and went inside. Greeted by 3 very bored and unhappy looking teens at the front, one of whom asked me how many. I replied "two" and one of them walked off after we THOUGHT we heard her mumble "follow me". Apparently we misheard, because she walked over to the very opposite side of the floor and sat down to do some prep work. Confused at this point, we seated ourselves at a clean table in the middle of the floor where we were sure not to be missed. After a couple of minutes, a busboy saw us and looked over at the bored teen crew at the front door and gave a "WTF" arm raise and shrug. I assumed at that point someone would be over, but it took a server walking by about 5 minutes later to state "be with you folks in a sec". He (the server) is the only reason for 4 stars. The wings were good, of course, and the atmosphere was decent considering it was a Saturday and playoffs. All in all, not a bad visit, but it could have very easily been less than it was. 

Tips--the wings are, like, Fucillo HUUUUUUGE!!! So be prepared to either leave stuffed or take some home if you order more than 6. 
Their bleu cheese dressing is very good at taking the bite out of any hot wings you get, so keep that in mind in case you overstep trying to be all macho and stuff. 
The sweet tea is decent, but not "southern sweet", so if you're a transplant, you'll be fine. They have all-day $5 "homerun" margaritas, so there's that.
If you go before dark, you're likely to encounter some families (with young ones), so plan accordingly. 


***UPDATE***

So the wife and I came by after a trip to the coast and Ybor city since I always give a place two tries. 

Saturday night, not too busy, got seated quickly (next to the bar, but didn't mind). Congenial server came by and took our drink order, so far so good. Fast forward to the food. 

I got a dozen boneless in honey bbq (I'm easy to please), the wife got the chicken tenders platter, Mo' in law got the steak and rice bowl.

Boneless wings were okay, but a little dry (even smothered in sauce), the steak and rice bowl was missing the guac (and seemingly the steak, unless it only comes with 7 little pieces), the guac itself was 'meh'. The sweet tea was the same as before, and the lemonade still didn't get up and dance like 3.99 lemonade should. 

All in all, this is our last visit. I can think of many more places I can spend $20+ per person and be more satisfied.

Calling this the "best sushi in STL" is a bit of a stretch but they do put out a good product.  I would recommend sticking to the more popular varieties to ensure freshness but that is a gut reaction, not based on a bad experience.

Lunch special with an eel & avocado roll was what I ordered.  They were kind enough to substitute a piece of white tuna for the shrimp.  Other pieces were salmon, snapper and tuna.  The sushi was prepared well but possibly not at the peak of freshness.  Not far enough away from it to warrant a bad review or a send-back.

Salad was fresh with a typical sesame dressing.  Miso soup was on par with other places but nothing exceptional.  

Service was prompt and attentive.  Decent place for a sushi lunch if that's what you're craving and you find yourself in South County.

Great Chicago-style food. I got the Chicago dog and house chips. YUM. The only thing I was a little bummed about was having to order the chips a la carte. For the prices they should have a side included with the meal. They've got some drink deals throughout the week that I'd like to try at some point. A nice place in Zionsville Village if you want a hotdog or burger. The Cubs decor is a nice touch!

Came here on a Sunday night with my fiancée and we loved it! Ordered a chicken quesadilla (which was delicious for "bar food") had beers, we bowled a few games too. The staff was awesome and the atmosphere in the place was beyond awesome. We can't wait to come back on our wedding night to hang out, drink, and bowl with all our friends!

Maybe it's because I had an awesome evening with my friend at Pastaria, but this place made such an impression on me that before my meal was even over, I was texting my other friends that they needed to try this place. My friend and I shared the risotto balls (fried balls of risotto and cheesy goodness), and each got a plate of pasta for dinner. Here's what really impressed me, the  dishes were interesting without being complicated. I think a lot of times in the quest to be inventive, chefs loose sight of the idea that less is more, and that classic flavor combinations are classic for a reason. Luckily, the people over at Pastaria have not fallen prey to this trap. Also, I have to give a shout-out to their gelato, particularly their GOAT CHEESE GELATO WITH RASPBERRY SWIRL. I had no idea what I was in for when I ordered it, but it's basically cheesecake in gelato form. I have no earthly idea how they do it, but it's mind blowingly awesome, and better yet, you can buy a pint of it and take it home with you. What's not to love?

I went to IHOP this morning.  It took 15 minutes for a waitress to take our orders and another 5 minutes for our drinks to arrive: it took 20 minutes for us to get our drinks. It was not like they were busy since there were only four tables. We never got refills. My glass set empty for 30 minutes and I had to eat my breakfast without a drink.

Our food was okay.

When it came to pay, it took us asking three times for us to finally get our bill so we could pay in leave.  

I usually tip 15% or $5, which ever is higher.  Our bill was something $19.32. For good service, I would have left a five dollar tip (five dollar was bigger than 15%). But because the waitress did such a terrible job, I gave the waitress a $20 bill and told her to keep the change (a $0.68 tip).

What a wonderful occasion we had on Christmas Eve which was also my husbands birthday.

The owners  and staff were absolutely great.
Every special request was taken care of with such friendly attitudes.

The food was 100% 5 star.  All 17 of our group were raving about their dinners.

We plan on returning within the next week or two.

Thanks to everyone.

Stopped in on a girls day out. Beer, board games, comfortable atmosphere and convenient food truck for noms. Great place to spend a Sunday kicking round town. Try the Bearwalker or Rainy Day Blues beers if you like hardy brews. Not too crowded, friendly servers. All around good place to hang.

11/10/2019: Today I ordered a bowl of Hu Tieu Sate. I think Dong Phuong is the only restaurant in NoLa that made this noodle soup. It contained grilled beef, brisket, and the fat white noodle. Since it was named sate, it's a little more on the spicy side. And if it's not spicy enough to your liking, you can always ask for more sate on the side. 
On a side note, the noodle will be sticking in a clump, so watch out for the splash. If you don't like the fat noodle, you can ask them to switch it to the banh pho (pho noodle) or the mi (yellow egg noodle).

This is one of my good go-to places for ramen if I'm around the Meridian area. Definitely a solid option for lunch and when it's pretty cold outside. My favorite is their spicy miso ramen with extra pork topping. Don't forget to grab some boba to add to your meal. Overall, service is efficient and friendly staff.

Stopped at sparkman wharf after having an appointment in Tampa. Looked at all the options and decided to try the bbq. I got the chicken and my wife had the pulled pork. We both ended up with the baked beans and mac and cheese for sides. That leads to my first issue. I wanted the slaw but they were out. Several people after us ordered it as well. I would like to have tried it. However, both the chicken and pork were both good. The Mac and cheese was as well and we even ended up taking some home as there was too much to eat. The baked beans were okay but seemed a little dried out. Luckily they were still somewhat tasty. One great value here is that they have cigar city jai alai for only 5 bucks. I will definitely try this again. Hopefully they'll have the coleslaw that time.

First thing I have to say is I am mad at myself for not remembering my toe drivers name . Stupid me
He was a great savior to my afternoon going to crap fast . The driver was courteous, prompt & very helpful . This gentleman went above and beyond what you would expect . I will be finding out the drivers name to make sure he gets his proper appreciation from all . Thank you

Went here recently to try their steamed mini bun, beef dumpling, char xiu tofu, Japanese cheese cake and matcha crepe cake.  First off the steamed mini bun which I ordered in pork and beef.  They were good, fresh and hot, however lacking a little maybe in soup.  The beef dumpling was good.  The char xiu tofu, I wished the tofu was a little bit more crisper, but overall it was good.  We ate the matcha crepe cake, which had great flavor.  I do wish the layers were a little thinner.  The Japanese cheesecake was quite delicious that gave hints of fluffiness and airiness. 

Overall good, but can be a little bit better.

After two visits of ordering ahead for pickup I am dropping a star for sweetgreen as both times my order was incorrect when I got back to the office.  Fortunately for them the lines are still always long, so I can't really wait until I get there to order and see that my requests are being granted - so sweetgreen will be taking a backseat to my lunch rotation. I do really enjoy their combinations and dressing choices so this bums me out a bit but onion breath and cucumbers repeating on me all afternoon are unfortunate dealbreakers.

Talk about the worst delivery service ever. When I tracked my package it was marked as "delivered on front door". My apartment building is locked so you have to buzz the apartment to be let in. I've been teleworking so I'm home all day, there was never a buzz and since it wasn't left outside my apartment door I'm guessing it was left outside... if it was even delivered at all... I never saw a package outside the building. The tracking site has a contact form to fill out, one of the reasons was "Tracking shows delivered, no package". I filled the form and their reply... "Our delivery records indicate this package was delivered, but we understand you have claimed the package as not received. If the package has not yet been received, please contact your seller for further assistance." You are literally telling me what I contacted you about. Absolutely useless! Your delivery driver either didn't deliver it or left it outside where anyone driving/walking by could take it. Thanks! The retailer shouldn't have to replace something for YOUR company's negligence. Thank goodness my replacement package was NOT delivered by your company, cause I probably would never have gotten it then.

Love this place. Eaten here for over a decade. Best beans in town. Patricia is wonderful. Breakfast burritos (bacon, chorizo, machata, etc) are really hard to beat. Super Nachos are super gigantic. The wife loves the enchiladas. Fast and fresh.

Very different experience and pretty neat. You could definitely make a whole day out of it if you want to see everything and take time for pictures. They have large life-like statues, and smaller life-size still life ones as well, along with some very different sculptures. The grounds are absolutely beautiful too: there are different paths and different nooks and crannies that need to be explored. Make sure you bring water with you if it's a hot day and ladies, leave the high heels at home (there are a lot of uneven surfaces, but if you insist in heels, then make it wedges).  Entrance fee is $15 which seems a little high, but I don't mind doing that every once in a while, especially for something unique.  I did see a few kids there so it appeared to be kid-friendly, but there is nothing specifically geared towards them. One part that was deceiving was the Meadow. On the walk there, it seemed like it was going to be just one little field so we just turned around: do yourself a favor and keep going, there is a ton of cool sculptures in the Meadow. We went back later to check things out eventually. If you get hungry, they have a little cafe in the main building where the gift shop is and you can purchase snacks, sandwiches, salads, coffee and much more. There is also the Rats Restaurant on premiss that offers sit-down dinning: you can walk there if you're already in the grounds, or you can drive there separately.  Prices are a little high but the setting is absolutely beautiful. We didn't eat at either place so I cannot comment on food quality or service. All in all, it was a fun day running around and seeing different things. It wasn't too crowded there when we went (Friday 3:30-7pm), but it seems like there would be enough room for everybody to spread out even if there were a lot of people there.

Chawffles (LOL) was awesomesauce!  Probably the best fried chicken I've had in a good long while.  We ordered the Pickle chips and Tot-chos to start and then I ordered the Ironwood (2 waffles and 3 dark meat) as my entree.  OMJesus, I got two huge thighs and a drum stick with a scoop of fluffy butter heaped on two tender waffles.

Appetizers:  The Pickle chips were great but not amazing.  The pickle flavor was good but the dipping sauce did not stand up to the pickles over powering flavor.  They were also a bit soggy.  The Tot-chos stole the show.  They were huge and covered in cheese and jalapenos and other stuff and cheese and jalapenos and cheese --did I mention jalapenos.  It was soo big it fed us all with a few to spare....and then the spares were gone.  The tots were not as good as Grill tots but, well, Grill tots rule.

Chicken:  The crust was crispy and savory, lovingly surrounding the juicy thigh like a security blanket.  On the first bite, the chicken is more than willing to cover you in it's love juice (aka greasy fat-fat), it will squirt on to you if you bite into the right part.  The drumstick was just as tasty and moist but not as juicy.  Please whatever you do, do NOT forget to douse your meat with Louisiana style hot sauce.  It is a must!!

Waffles:  The waffles were so light, so ready to absorb the melted butter and syrup!  So pliable to my forks demands, I just had to give it what it wanted.  BUTTER AND SYRUP THEN MORE BUTTER AND MORE SYRUP!!  My fellow diner is not a fan of the waffles because she is used to the big ole' belgium waffles that are tasty all their own; which isn't bad but it's not southern style!  I was trying to explain to her that southern style cooking is about decadence and variety!  She just didn't get it...

Overall, I am already planning my trip back to try the chicken breast, because honestly the best test of fried chicken skills is how moist the chicken breast is!
Incredible food, Excellent wine list, Great service, and wonderful vegetarian options.

Went in recently after a hot day and was pleasantly impressed with the fun and refreshing decor.
Faux greenery is lined on the ceiling making a fun and refreshing take from our typical southwestern theme places. 
Of course, the nice cool AC is also a big plus!

Hostess greeted us immediately and stated it would be a 5 min wait while she got us a clean table, it was nice to see they were still implementing a COVID - social distance rule.  So, safe establishment.
We had a moment to run to the bathroom to wash our hands and was impressed with the cleanliness, not super fond of the sink - seems like there is allot of splatter, but give them effort for trying.

Table seems to be the old Korean BBQ tables they just vamped up the top part, so the bottom makes it a bit uncomfortable to sit since you have little to no leg room. However, since I'm pretty short that didn't bother me too much.
Service was friendly and prompt. Refreshments including water was refilled diligently.

We decided to partake in a "pickle theme Bloody Mary" and it was pickly delicious!!!
I decided on the Chicken & Waffle ( nice brunch staple ) with the bubbly waffle. Yup, you heard me. Bubbly!!
Makes for a fun new texture in the common waffle game, however they do offer Belgian Waffle for those that like the good classic comfort!
The chicken was a bit spicy which I absolutely dig!! And was nicely sliced, so easy to dine and enjoy.

The waffle itself was okay, not amazing, but good enough.
My husband enjoyed his breakfast sandwich and was too busy inhaling it to have much of a conversation -so, needless to say he quite enjoyed it!

The few cons that make this review a 4 star...
-Food is a bit salty. Like, everything is salty.... entree, drink, and sides. Makes you constantly chugging down some water while you eat. I would recommend to try and order something fruity and fresh to help balance everything out, but that was my main complaint. It's not that the meal was inedible, just more salty than average.
-Price was above average . 2 adults came out to roughly, $40 for 2 entrees & 1 alcoholic beverage.
I understand that seems to be the ongoing trend, recently in Tucson, but that's why most business usually fails... once the hype is gone, people tend to avoid the steeper price gauge.
