I understand that may not be their fault but they should have told us before we payed. The only was bonus was the presentation of the flower ice cream was unique.

Hands down the best pizza I've ever had.  The meaty pizza did not disappoint. What did disappoint and the reason for the 3 stars was for the deceptive description on their so called "pitcher of margaritas " for $30.00!!!! The picture on their website clearly shows a pitcher of margaritas and says it serves 2-3 people. What I received was a CUP of margarita with no ice. Which as it was explained to me is equal to a pitcher with ice. 
If your going to advertise a picture of a pitcher and describe it as a pitcher then that's what you should give the customer. Not a cup and sell it for 30.00!! Just so no one thinks I'm exaggerating here is a picture of the "pitcher" I got next to a bottle for perspective.  This is deceptive and wrong. 
Everything else, food and customer service was spot on.  My recommendation is don't order your drinks online. Go in have a great pizza and hopefully an actual pitcher of margaritas

Correction: it doesn't show a pitcher on line but only states a pitcher. My bad on that. This cup did not serve 3 people.

This place was great. Pretty clean, and they have Several different saunas. Pretty accommodating for the guests as they provide towels, bath ropes and slippers. The food was also amazing! Had the borscht, chicken and beef kabobs! The only reason for the 4 star review is because the masseuse refused to do the platza for us. We called a head of time and asked questions about this and were really looking forward to it. When we inquired about why this couldn't be done we were told "because he's tired." So that was a bit disappointing. Other than that we were pretty satisfied!

We had a brunch for my wife's 60th at the Spring Mill Cafe about a month ago.  We've always liked their quiet country setting, and we were vacillating between renting the barn for 12+ or being in the dining room, mostly because our guest list fluctuated between 10-14.  We eventually had 10 confirmed, so we went for the dining room.  Day of, we had 2 more people join us, which made for a cozy squeeze in the side room where they had us set up.  The servers were very accommodating, and things went off without a hitch. 

Every course was great, starting with the butternut squash soup, which had a dollop of sweet lump crab meat in the center. Our diners had a mix of breakfast meals and lunch meals, but there was unanimous kudos all around, especially the omelets, which were light, fluffy and tender with just the right amount of filling.  

Ezra had a chocolate cake baked for us, which my wife swears was one of the best she's ever had.  I can't disagree with her, it was moist without being too wet, dense without being heavy, icing was creamy without being oily or greasy.  Wonderful flavors came through without any negatives to distract, if that makes any sense. 

Service was great, very friendly, never rushed.  Dining room was quiet, conducive to adult conversation.  All in all, one of our go-to places.

I needed a suit and some dress shirts cleaned and pressed with a quick turnaround and the service was excellent and very affordable.  This was my first visit to Colonial and Steve remembered my name as soon as I came to pick up my clothes.  I have tried a few other cleaners in the area and this place is the best - hands down.  I would recommend taking your clothes here and will definitely be a return customer.
Rosario and her assistant finished cleaning the bathrooms, bedroom, family room, and kitchen in good time. Great job ladies! Thank you!

First off their French fries are bodasciously deliscious! Tons of warm soft and crunchy flavor. Not sure what they put on them but I want more!
Had the Southern Burger with fried green tomatoes and sweet butter pickles!
Good fat food!

took me this long to get back, oh the grizz how you satiate my needs.  newspaper menus are great even though i have that menu memorized and order the same given time of day and the staff really friendly

for dinner options that pecan crusted trout is delicious although my waitress that evening called it the salmon, i chuckled with my infantile mind than doubled checked the receipt just in case

coffee delicious as diner coffee should be, peerless from oakland i believe? an underrated fave for sure and the bear claw? i've downed that thing in an atlantis tower room once with zero shame
Hidden gem! They have amazing breakfast sandwiches, good coffee. Small, cozy, friendly environment.

I went yesterday for dinner with my fiancé & it was amazing, although it was little busy, we got seated very quickly... our server Ralph was funny & very attentive to our needs again it was a little busy but he handled it well also we ordered macaroni & cheese & the first time it was very very dry & had lack of seasoning but when we spoke to Ralph about he didn't get upset or annoyed he simply just fixed the issue.... my fiancé loves outback & we can't wait to return again !!!! Thanks Ralph for making our date night even more special!!

What a wonderful restaurant!! I usually go here for lunch for their all you can eat special. You definitely won't leave hungry. Their pork dumplings are amazing and the beef teriyaki is cooked perfectly every time. The seaweed salad and kani salad are also very good. They offer a large variety of food that could please anyone. The ice cream afterwards is great too. I love this place and I highly recommend it.

When we first moved here we were told that My Dad's was the best sweet corn we would ever taste and they were absolutely correct! This corn is fabulous! I don't know what their secret is, but there is something about it that makes me want to gobble the entire sack in one sitting! You won't be disappointed!

My check in process was more than amazing. He was polite, smiled and went above and beyond. Upon my check out my boyfriend and I decided to hang out at the pool because our flight left late that day. By the poolside I needed to use the bathroom and I saw two ladies walk out of the these glass doors. I assumed that's where the bathrooms were so I headed in that direction. This girl from the bar (natalie/natalia) hauled towards me and stuck her long arm out in front of me to stop me from entering and yelled at me telling me I couldn't go in there.
     I was confused as to why she was being this rude and yelled at me in front of all these people considering she works in hospitality, but proceeded to ask her where the bathrooms were. All she said was "the bathrooms are there & there". With no direction. I asked her again and she pointed towards the lobby. 
       Personally, I'm well aware that every hotel pool has pool bathrooms and I'm not going to walk through the lobby with a bathing suit on. So I found the pool bathrooms on my own & while I was away Natalie took it upon herself to go and ask my boyfriend if we were even guests at this hotel who belonged there. He answered yes and then she asked him what room number we were in.
    I have worked for hotels before, specifically Marriott and I know exactly what Natalie is doing. She was rude from the beginning and then judgmental and racist. No other white person at the pool was being asked if they had a room at the hotel or if they belonged there. 
    I talked to my boyfriend about the situation because he saw Natalie yell at me by the bar & he told me how this girl waited for me to leave his side just to ask him whether or not we were guests at this hotel. He said "in this society, especially when it comes to white people, I'm used to this kind of behavior".
     Well I'm here to use MY white privilege to tell you that I'm not used to this nasty behavior and I will not tolerate it whatsoever.
     This uncultured little girl is rude, judgmental and racist and shouldn't be working for Marriott. I'm not sure if this is the first or one of many reviews about this person but I don't see myself staying at any Marriott until they get rid of people who are racist. Its been 3 days since this situation and I really tried to refrain from writing a review at all, but it just bothers me so badly, how people like natalie exist. 
    I sent an email to the management of the Sheraton property and he emailed back that the pool was open to the public as well. Now, I'm even more confused as to why she question if we belonged there or not. I emailed back asking him why we were treated such a way and I have not received an answer. Poor/racist staff and poor management. No, thank you. I travel once or twice a month. I'll happily take my business elsewhere.

I went there for dinner by myself. The hostess(?) sat me in aseparate section by myself. No server showed  up for 15 min. I finally went to the desk to ask. The response was was "Oh sorry I forgot about you"!!!
A server appeared at my table and "explained" that this section is usually closed so no server came !!!!
I got served. Food was as good as expected at a diner. Of course the server took a long time to bring my check.
I complained again at the front cashier and was given a half -hearted apology, Maybe I'm paranoid but it was clear that they did not want to bother with a single customer and did everything they could to get me to leave except for throwing me out. This is no way to treat any customer and I can promise thus establishment that I will never come back and will do my best to bad mouth them.

Try one of the chef's special creations, you'll be glad you did! I can't remember the name or remotely how to spell what I had, but it was an eggplant type of dish with bechemel sauce. I've got to go here at least once more whilst traveling around Tarpon Springs!

The unfortunate part is I have been coming to St Pete Beach for over 40 years
And yesterday was first time to Ricks. Needless to say I am back today. Great cheap drinks, great service, Terri Rocks!!
Rick acknowledged our second day with some free coolie cups.... Ok now to the food
I had the burger with provolone and grilled onions with tots and my girlfriend had the blackened grouper sandwich and fries
Both were amazing and best we have had on the beach.  We will for sure make this a regular spot for years to come
Great prices, portions service and atmosphere... This was lunch. May be back for dinner.

Paul 
I asked for sugaring,  but I believe I was waxed.  The experience was much too painful to be sugar, and also it was much warmer than sugar is supposed to be. I hope the next time that I get what I asked for. I was charged for sugaring,  but the experience was definitely one of waxing.

This past weekend was my first trip to New Orleans.  I took the French Quarter ghost tour.  There was a nice, small group of 6 of us.  Walking around and seeing those massive tours of 30 people, you wonder how they hear or learn anything!  Judy is vastly knowledgable on New Orleans and can answer any question you have.  Being from New York, I can tell you that Judy keeps it real and there is no fluff!  I highly recommend a tour through her, she made such a lasting impression on all of us and I cannot wait to get back to New Orleans!
Fast service as always. One of the cleanest Waffle House's I have been in... including the restroom. Lala was our server, very friendly and efficient

Yum!
Healthy. Tasty!
GF and Vegan options abound! 
Desserts were tempting but passed.
Enjoyed their complimentary cucumber water with lunch: Veggie burger on lettuce with a kale salad. Quick service in a clean and pleasant environment. Open one in Franklin, please?

Living In IV this place is overrated in my opinion. It's basically a chipotle. With all the drug and alcohol consumption in IV this is a really popular spot. I think at midnight this place is more popular than during lunch.  It's definitely worth checking out and if your going to UCSB your probably going to spend a lot of time there anyway. 

Also you can ask for a "salad" and they give you more quantity of food without the burrito I think it's great for those carb conscious students =D.

This apartment complex has a decent maintenance team, OK grounds, pet friendly (although the require a 20 dollar pet rent monthly and a 250 dollar non refundable deposit), and it's "gated". 
The unfortunate side is that they have increased the rent but is not justified on a property that is this old, the buildings have mold and all the apartment does about it is  wipe it with a Clorox wipe (this does not fix the problem), the gate is a joke considering it is always broken or run down with a car ... Ohhh and tailgating is very easy because the gate arm is constantly broken, there are plenty of roaches to go around, and be forewarned they require a 60 day notice to move out and if you do not give one they will charge you a month to month fee plus a hundred dollars in order to leave you with a parting gift :-). It is worth just paying the same amount and living some where like Brentwood considering they will charge the same for a nicer larger apartment. .... Also the one bedroom apartments do not come with washer dryer connections.
No wait to be seated. Was able to order quickly. I was able to get my meal in a timely manner. Waiter/waitress' all seem to enjoy working there.

I've been looking for a good, low-key taco place in St. Louis for a while now. Make sure to get the hot sauce from the fridge (or medium or mild, I just prefer hot) - it really adds to it. Breakfast tacos are delicious as well if you're into that. It's become a go-to for me for virtually any meal of the day.

Quick service, very nice and friendly people working there. Hole in the wall - but that's where the best food is. It's pretty cheap too.

I came here for brunch on a Saturday. We used the app and were seated at a reasonable time. Then the awfulness started. We waited almost 20 mins for our order to be taken, then another 40 to receive our over cooked food. We both had eggs Benedict which were basically hard boiled, the bread was rock hard and stale, my drink never came out and we still hadn't seen our waiter since we put in our order (food was brought by runners). I had also told our server when we ordered I would like to put in a to go order when the food came out. I told the runners this as well. Another 45 minute wait. Finally my friend spotted our elusive waiter folding silverware (we had not seen him for about an hour) and went over to ask for our checks and that I needed to place the to go order. The to go order when brought home was on stale bread as well, over melted/burnt cheese and sloppily prepared. Million dollar bacon is on point though.
This morning I saw a barista add cold water to my drink because she failed to steam enough milk to fill the cup. Appalling. They aren't about the coffee here. They're about moving people through.

I have no clue what I ate, but for $6 you aren't going to get a better deal.

Ok, I do sort of know... lamb, some sort of beef stew, and this fried beef thingy.  The rice was plentiful, the hot sauce was hot, and the food was super tasty.  Very much a mom and pop restaurant, where the folks behind the counter were very helpful in explaining the different options.

Really this is the perfect hole in the wall.  Don't go here for fine dining, go here for delicious food in copious quantities, at a ridiculously good price.

Had such a wonderful time in this quaint studio.the lady's working we're both professional and approachable. They greeted every customer with a smile and treat you like they have known you forever. There was a child's birthday party going on the afternoon I was there, so it was a little loud, but not crazy loud. Even with the party, they were able to give each guest one on one help. 
They have a large selection of items to paint, colors to choose from and design idea nooks stencils and more. You do not have to be crafty to create a beautiful piece of work here. I am on vacation here or would go back weekly. The turn around for your pottery is one week. They also offer canvas paintings in their paint/ party room. We did not get to much detain on the painting part, but they have lots of painting options on the wall.great place for children and adults both  I believe  they offer a buy one get one on the studio fee one day a week ( might be on Tuesday) if you are in the area check them out you will not be dissapointed.

So far, this place has PROVEN to be uncared for and in disrepair. As a daughter of a contractor who worked in the industry for 45 years before cancer stole him, I got to learn a lot about how to look at homes. My husband is just as astute. 

1. Careful for the bait and switch! We were shown two apartments, an "older model" and a "remodeled one" and the one we got was none of the above. It looks nothing like either of the apartments we looked at. The apartments we looked at had a slight rise on the front porch and my daughter got me in and out in my wheelchair without any problems. I motivated myself around in my wheelchair and even went in and out of all the bathrooms in the house without any problems. The only problem was they were one and two bedrooms and we need three bedrooms. That's the only reason we even looked for a different place to live. 

Then we get to the new place today, the three bedroom apartment that we've been waiting over a month to even view because they said they would call me to look at it when it was available and they never did even though I called them 4 to 5 times asking to see the apartment, they always found a reason for me not to be able to look at what we were putting money down on. We didn't get to see it until after they took our money.

2. No baseboards. Anywhere. We have an 8 month old baby in our home and there are NO BASEBOARDS. Seriously an eyesore but a danger as well. Our girl could get her whole hand under the wall! (If I can get my fingers under there, she can get her whole hand under there). All she has to do is lose a toy in there (and it's even that way in her bedroom)... ALL of the rooms. We won't be signing a second lease at this place. not when she'll be nearly 2 years old at that time. It's dangerous! 

3. Other dangers... to top it off, with the place this aged you would think that they would be concerned about her pulling out insulation or getting cut on the sharp glass on the corner of the laundry closet. (See photos) When they did the walk-through with us today, they only wrote down what they wanted to see and they wouldn't even let me put what I saw because I don't want to get blamed for other peoples problems. Especially the people who maintain the property. Obviously they have a problem. I'm not getting blamed for the two cigarette burns in the linoleum. Was it written down on the sheet? No. They could've done this walk-through before we even got there and had everything fixed and put together because they KNEW we were coming today and now we can't move in until...? Do we move in?

3. I'm handicapped and even though my wheelchair fit through every door in both of the apartments that we were shown when we first looked at the property, it does not fit through  ANY of the bathroom doors of the one that we actually were put in. They can't even make an offer on how to make it right! I spoke to "Destiny" when she was showing us around and I said that I needed something that was handicapped accessible using my wheelchair. This apartment is not even close to ADA compliant. Yes, they said we could put up handrails but at what price? Who pays that? Who pays for somebody to build a ramp to the front door so that I can get into the apartment without having to have somebody lift me into the building in my wheelchair? The step is too high for me to get up it by myself because my anti-tippers don't even let me lean back far enough to get me into the apartment. Speaking of ADA compliant IN the restrooms? No handrails is the least of my worries if I can't get my wheelchair through the door of either one of the bathrooms in the home. Who pays THE bill for cutting the doors a few inches bigger? You think that just because I'm handicapped, we can take the doors off and put up curtains because the rest of my family doesn't deserve privacy in the restroom? Nice. 

Yes, we were very excited about this apartment and have been long waiting since the early to mid part of August to be at the point of moving... until today when we realized that the people who run it are cold. They don't even care if an eight month old baby gets hurt living in their apartment because they are too cheap to put in baseboards.

Technically we haven't moved in yet because all we have is keys. We have nowhere else to go. So what do we do?

What they did to us is WRONG. 

The last and the lady said before we left to go look at the apartment was, "welcome to your new home" and the minute I saw it I was absolutely heartbroken.

Wow! The flavors are spot on to the descriptions. The staff were friendly and informative. While it's roughly 20 minutes away from our house the family agreed it's worth the trip and the wait in line. We will definitely be back!

Delayed checkin, lost luggage, food is overpriced, hidden fees are overpriced, nothing is open if an early bird, room was cleaned once in a week. Guy checked in had semen on bed cover. Great location but it is the typical hotel/time share to make a buck and go for quantity. Now many of the staff is very nice and helpful, but for an established management group, they dropped the ball.  Can't justify the money for the quality of stay.  Too much around that has the same thing and better amenities.

Great BYO, but a bit expensive to go here regularly.  Correct me if I'm wrong, but the style is Asian street food which I assume a $22 duck pad thai dish wouldn't normally be part of.  I used to get the Panang special ($22) which is fantastic, but I feel like the portion has gotten a lot smaller over the years.  I recently switched to seafood crazy noodles ($19) which is also spectacular.  

If it was a little more reasonably priced, my wife would drag me here once a week, but we only go on special occasions.
My husband and I come here routinely. The menu is ok. Their waitlist process is very frustrating and rude to customers. We are taking our business to Rize and Wild Eggs.

The food and our waitress was excellent.  Unfortunately, I do not provide five stars because of the hostess:

Is she an owner? Relative? Miserable salt and pepper haired lady?
Me and my guest were late for our OUTSIDE reservation for 6:30pm. I called at 6:26pm and left a message, at the restaurant, as no one was available. We arrived late and were greeted with, "Can I help you?" Her question was written all over her face- we are in the weeds, too busy to handle business and you are an inconvenience. I concentrated on the outside ambience instead of her rude welcome.  
Moments later she comes back and says, "You were late we have no tables outside." Okay, I said to myself, no big deal. As she proceeded to take us to our table (her attitude appeared as if we were placing her through torture), she told me, "You never had a reservation for outside."  I had the confirmation email, from my OpenTable reservation, on my iPhone, but I was here for a nice dinner, not an argument with a miserable, old lady.
As we are being led to a table, next to the kitchen, my date tells me she likes a particular table (all of these tables were open). I nicely asked
if we could be seated at the table my date requested and the hostess said, "I can seat you there, but now I am going to have to switch all my tables around." For the record, there were four tables that led to the bathroom- she only sat one additional couple, in one of the three remaining tables, during the rest of the evening; wow that was a lot of work on her part.
In summary, don't lie to your guests who plunk $200.00 for dinner, drinks and tip. Don't make them feel as if you are doing them a favor. Appreciate all of your guests. I understand the restaurant business; it is quite difficult. But when you have a niche and reputation, in your town, every guest must and should be treated well. If you can't do this, don't be the "face" for the restaurant.  Although the food is delicious, I will not be back. If I am in the mood to be lied to and experience condescension, I will invite myself over, for dinner, at my ex mother-in-laws.

P.S. It's not just a coincidence- I read some of the poor reviews, after I wrote my review, and I am not the only one. I guess the owner and his staff are riding on their reputation. Disappointing attitude to have. I did not think I was the only one; other reviews share a similar story.
I actually don't mind going to the dentist now!  The folks at the front desk are great--Jose is very friendly and responsive.  The doctor are friendly and fast.  The office is bright and modern.

Excellent restaurant, la nourriture est totalement délicieuse et l'assiette  pourrait nourrir 2 personnes. 2 verres de vin de bonne qualité ce qui est rare au USA pour 6$. Je recommande fortement ce restaurant.

This is one of my favorite spots! I have loved every single item I've tried, and I want to work my way through the entire menu eventually. It's so nice to find fast reasonably priced vegan food. And the owners are great! I cannot say enough good things about this place

Overpriced and overly hyped up. This place is mediocre. Their food is good but not great. The price point is even worse. There salsa is decent but this place is just too expensive for what they have to offer.

My husband and I go to this location often and Brandon the manager is the ultimate stand up guy! Brandon sets the tone and always has a smile on his face. They are super fast when there is a long line and NEVER have any complaints with our ice cream!

Opens at 5:00 and we got there at 4:50.  Worker or chef was mixing dough and looked at us standing outside. At 5:00 the worker walked past us as he headed to the back room or maybe the bathroom.  At 5:05 he still never came out to unlock the door and invite us in. We left and will never go back. Very rude to potential new customers. I doubt whether he will make it in the restaurant business.     Del M.

I ate here for a close friend birthday dinner an I order a steak cooked medium well  and it was cooked to perfection I didn't need any steak sauce at all no added salt an pepper I mean the steak was juicy lol an very tender and Size was good as well besides that I also had asparagus well cooked still had a settle crunch an good seasoning so yes please try this out this place...

Some updates for this cafe: You will notice lots of construction when you drive by -- they are building an outdoor deck and will have many more tables! Fridays and Saturdays, they now stay open until 9 and are BYOB. (Although isn't anything without a liquor license BYOB really?  Help me understand.)  "Beer and wine only" is specified -- do people come in armed with bottles of single malt? :-)

I am delighted that raw can attract enough Berks (and Montgomery) Countians to be this successful, because it took real guts to invest in raw vegan food here.

The cute little dog was actually outside on a leash when I visited this time, and he treated me like I was the best thing he had ever seen. I was smitten!  :-) He definitely loves the flow of people and thinks he is the ambassador.

Honey is gone from the smoothies, so I tried a new Creamsicle one (over the chocolate banana so Mr Banana Hater could share).  Wow, intensely great freshly-flavored smoothie, especially after experiencing some lackluster ones around the area lately.  

We shared the mock tuna swandwich, open face on the amazing dark onion flatbread. Raw is filling, and it was enough for us -- because we also had sunflower hummus to share with friends later, good enough to eat with a spoon, AND the Cosmic Kale Salad.  I must learn how to make the tamari-style dressing, and the staff will share recipes, which is very giving.  We also took vegetable chips home.  They were out of kale chips.

I did something I have always wanted to, brought my own packaging, to save them on their expensive recyclables and to reuse what I already have.  Mine is scavenged from Chinese takeout, where you can't really get away with this, but RCRC handled this with appreciation and without acting like I was nuts.  I know this is nerdy, but I had a variety of shapes and sizes, hoping there would be something they could work with.

Afterwards, we stopped by Kimberton Whole Foods for groceries and saw a guy walking around with a wheatgrass smoothie from RCRC, then heard him rave about it.  Don't be afraid of a dark green drink -- wheatgrass is like a nutrient blast that will really pick you up, much better than caffeine, not that I oppose that either.

Walked in and was waiting for a fun time all day. Looked forward to seeing puppies but couldn't even see any except from the outside window. As soon I walked in they rudely asked of my age and demanded I go back out to my car to retrieve my license. However, I am not 18 years old I am 17 years old and they would not let me in to see the friendly faces of the animals. Will not be back even when I am of age.

really enjoyed coming here! I always have seen it and it looks so cool to be at! I took my husband for lunch. He had a great time and loved the music and decor. The food was really good! Loved the garden burger. Great taste and holds together well. Cola slaw yummy too!

If you are looking for a one-of-a-kind experience and willing to spend a really shiny, pretty penny....this place is it! It's got magical experience  to say the least. I will start from the beginning...skip to the end if you want just a quick recap.

Getting into the venue:
It's on 3rd avenue which is hectic in itself so prepare yourself for traffic jams, but don't let it deter you. I heard they used to not have valet, but they do now which is across the street from where the restaurant is located. Not the most well displayed, but just look for the sign. Now there is not a sign that shows you where the restaurant is which keeps the speakeasy feel of it exciting. But for those of you that just need structure, the entrance is inside the Johnny Cash museum. Now this place is strictly cocktail attired (ladies a dress or cute pantsuit and men...put on a jacket and dress up tonight). So when you walk in, the greeter can recognize you and will wave you to the door that allows you access into the restaurant. The stairwell down looks like a castle going into a dungeon so to speak. It's light enough to see the stairs and makes you anticipate what you get to experience. After going through another door, you enter into a lobby of dark red velvet drapes and are greeted by lovely hostesses that will check your coat and direct you to your table (if you are eating dinner). DEFINITELY BOOK A RESERVATION!!!

Dinner:
This is where the pretty penny comes in. There are delicious entrees from meet lovers to vegetarian options. Our waitress, who had been there since the opening, was kind enough to give us the rundown of how everything works, from dinner to the small magic shows. We ordered the marinated scallops (9/10) and the beef tartare (10/10) for our appetizers. Both were fantastic and filling so I would get just one appetizer for two people. I ordered the rack of lamb which comes with a risotto and my boyfriend ordered the 75-day aged ribeye steak which is sold at market price topped with butter and a side of Brussels sprouts. Again both dishes were fantastic and quite filling as the portions were hearty and enough to fill you up. Dessert we had flourless chocolate cake (super chocolate-y so I hope you like chocolate) and their cheesecake (phenomenal). Small portions, but enough to take the taste off and leave you with a wholesome meal. Again, I can't stress enough that you are paying top dollar at this place so prepare. 

Magic shows: 
Our waitress was great to direct us with how the night is supposed to go. Dinner and then the main magic show after. They give you plenty of time to eat before the show so don't worry. The main show was amazing. They have a new act every week that allows you to come back often and see something different. We had the mentalist Joe Stenson and just incredible. After the show, you are directed to enjoy the bar services, and two areas designated for smaller magic tricks that still blow your mind. Everything is interactive and the magicians are funny, witty, and are excellent at their craft. There is also a magician that walks around to pop in on groups of people to perform tricks and then pops on out. Definitely a fun experience that keeps you guessing for more. 

Ambiance:
You have this speakeasy, castle-like dungeon experience. With classy chandeliers, interactive piano, and playing cards all around. The hallway to the bathrooms are trippy and a little spooky, but don't worry nothing will jump out at you. They also have a patio where you can smoke cigars (which you can purchase from them) with an epic waterfall. It is a small little oasis right in the middle of downtown, but yet away from the chaos. 

Recap:
Overall it was a great experience, the staff, the food, and the magic. The only reason I gave it 4/5 stars is because there was a not so great smell when I walked in that kept following me everywhere. I can't put my finger on it, but it wasn't pleasant. Also, I wish there were more stations for magic shows because it would get quite crowded around the stations. My advice? Get an early reservation (around 5:30ish), enjoy dinner and the main show, then go around to the smaller shows. If you don't want to spend the $$$$ on dinner, go for drinks :)

My friends and I headed here after our high school reunion nearby. The bartenders and wait staff were friendly and attentive. We ordered some appetizers- the Philly Cheesesteak Quesadillas, Loaded Kettle Chips and Loaded Nachos. They were all great and hit the spot as late night snacks. They had a list of festive holiday drinks which looked really good (although I think we just stuck to beer and wine). The TVs had the ND-FL game on so all the sports fans were happy too. I'd definitely come back for some drinks and appetizers on a weekend or even during the week.
Easily the best Chinese restaurant in Doylestown. Lo mein and beef in oyster sauce is good. Place is clean and fast service.
Waited 15+ minutes for my order to be completed and when I got it, it stunk so badly of cigarettes I could barely eat it.
Love the wings, the Sygoons, and the potato skins here! A little too crazy and loud for me sometimes, but their happy hour is worth it!

Came back for more... Came down to Tampa for the weekend with my wife and we made our way over to Clearwater Beach. We had to slide down to Haze and try their non-dairy and gluten free ice cream! It was great. Exactly what we expected. Ever since we came here almost every day on vacation last year we've been raving about this place. It's a must stop! Go out of your way! The ice cream is great and the owners are the best... I wish we didn't live 18 hours away. Till next time.

This is my new favorite brunch place! Everyone on staff was kind and helpful. It was especially neat to see the open kitchen and the process of the food preparation. The menu has a little something for everyone, and I look forward to trying the bananas foster crepes next time I'm in. I was impressed by the extensive drinks menu, and, of course, all the delectable treats in the dessert case. Don't worry if there's a little bit of a wait, there are several shops around the area to peruse or window shop.

Today was my third and probably last time here. The place is cute and centrally located. The service is fine, although I wouldn't call it stellar. The food is just bland and boring and extremely overpriced. Today I had a $14 "Chinese chicken salad" that was a plate of butter lettuce drizzled with oil and rice vinegar and topped with three small chicken strips. It was bland and underwhelming in every way. You can get a Chinese chicken salad at the deli around the corner (I'm NOT MENTIONING NAMES and not affiliated with them in any way) that will blow your mind. It is four times the size of this one, and spicy and tasty and loaded with carrots and snap peas and daikon sprouts and cilantro and crunchy noodles and now I am starving for it, and not just because the one at Jane was so disappointing. There are just too many good restaurants in this town to settle for mediocre in my opinion.

I placed an order for carry out and am extremely disappointed in not only the accuracy of my order but also the service when I picked up the order. The hostess was incredibly rude, and i waited for about 8 minutes just to get the extra bag of chips which I ordered when I called. The salsa was served in cups far too large to dip into, my fajitas were missing sour cream, and had a very small amount of the other toppings. I ordered a side of the guacamole and was given/ charged for a large guacamole. If the hostess had been more polite I more than likely would've noticed these mistakes, but she took my ticket & told me she would "take my money" and get my chips for me. At that point I was just ready to get out of the restaurant. For $50 I'm incredibly disappointed in the overall experience.

Once again I'm going to Write a review I have tried 4 times to deal with this hotel and even the corporate office of choice hotels and neither will cooperate with me.  I am so very disappointed in this hotel and choice hotels. I am still out 100 dollars for a room I cancelled and the hotel did not cancel my reservation, truly amazing. I will never stay at another choice hotel when I travel again, everyone beware of there tactics, make sure to always get a confirmation number when cancelling a reservation never take anyone's word that the reservation has been cancelled without receiving an email, don't trust anyone. I'm a victim of this although the hotel told me I would receive a cancellation email, and this never took place, and of course I did not check my email for a couple of days, and just assumed that the hotel did there job and sent it, but this did not happen.  Buyer beware!!  I can't stress that enough,,

Great I outside patio and great staff. I totally love the oxtail and red sangria. Love the small portions it encourages you to try other stuff on the menu. If you eat a lot, you'll spend a lot though, lol.

CLEAN CLEAN CLEAN CLEAN This can be hard to come by in Tucson.

I enjoyed the breakfast and loved the pancakes!  I usually don't care for pancakes but these wholegrain pancakes were awesome! 

This place is not if you are looking for a good old-fashioned Midwestern omelette.  I think they don't exist in Tucson. For new American breakfast items, Yum! This place is good.  I have only had breakfast here and cannot comment on lunch or dinner but I feel optimistic about trying it.
Enjoy
Rude customer service. Doors for the dining room were locked during business hours with no explanation or signs.

Arrived here on a rainy afternoon and it was relatively empty. Very friendly service and beautiful decor. The blue ceiling is artistic and peaceful. Ordered iced almond milk lattes and an avocado toast. Avocado toast was not only instagram worthy but actually tasted great too! I would of liked if the spinach was dressed a bit more. I'll definitely be back for more iced almond milk lattes!

Been here many times. This is a review of their Snickers French Toast and Fried Chicken Eggs Benedict. Service was on point as usual

- Snickers French Toast: very good, a little bit sweet, but that probably means it's just right for the average American. I could taste the snickers throughout the french toast. My only complain is that it was barely luke warm when it came out

- Fried Chicken Eggs Benedict: meow :/ 
   The egg wasn't poached perfectly as it normally should be. When I cut into the egg, I expect its gooeyness to flow all over my egg and chicken. It didn't. It was medium-well on the inside. Luckily, I used to be a well done egg eater, so I ate it anyway. The hollaindaise was good. The chicken, I don't remember it being advertised as such on the menu.. correct me if I'm wrong, but it wasn't your average fried chicken. It was more like a breaded, buffalo chicken breast. Flavored very well I must say, but not the fried chicken I was looking for. Waffle was good, potatoes were pretty good although it tasted like there was ginger in it, so that threw me off a bit. IMO, go to Hawthornes for the chicken and waffles!!

Ive been waiting for a gourmet burger joint on this side of town for years! Of course, living close to the location, I had no expectations other than an option better than McDonalds. However, I got much more than I bargained for! The prices initially startled my wallet and I, but once I sunk my teeth into a funk zone with no mushrooms, I knew my wallet was worth the sacrifice. Lucky for me, financial aid checks are on the way, so soon enough ill suppress the craving of Kat Cora's captivating culinary creations!

Smitty's is one of my two local crawfish go-tos during crawfish season. Reasonable prices, spot-on seasoning, and a nice atmosphere if you happen to be dining in. While I haven't had anything besides crawfish and fixin's, it's delicious, convenient, and a family favorite.
Best Chicken ever, their sauces and fries are great too.  My personal favorite is the southwest egg roll with the avocado sauce.

We celebrated my Mom's 90 th birthday and they were accommodating and helpful in the reservation process.
Food was fantastic and the waiter was quite helpful in helping navigate the menu.
Totally enjoyed the experience and will be back when in Clearwater

I came during the lunch hour and the line was almost out the door. I decided to wait, and I'm glad I did. Even though the line was long, my food came out in no time at all.  I ordered half of a chicken Caesar wrap, and tortilla soup. It's delicious.

The place is well staffed, everyone is hustling around, and I like that the ambience and menu cater to all ages and walks of life.

Climbing the last hill on a beautiful Nashville day, we found ourselves in a charming neighborhood that looks like it has stoically remained the same while everything around it has changed. Husk is located in a beautifully renovated house that is full of Southern glamour and eclectic details. 

We were seated by the floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the garden, where they clearly source many of their fresh herbs and, I imagine in summer months, their vegetables. The food was delicious, from the soft rolls and honey butter beginning to the very last bite of my husband's cheeseburger and my chicken.

This is a lovely restaurant from top to bottom.

They are doing a good job during Pandemic with only outdoor seating and self service. Menus are laid out on the bench so you don't have to touch them which is great. I had veggie burrito and pina colada and my friend had chicken bowl with some strawberry based drink. Food was great and I loved the spicy green sauce they gave. The review is 1 star shy of a 5 star review because the drink was great tasting but a little weak (alcohol content).

Use your student ID and save $2. Make sure to come about 30 mins before you actually plan on seeing the musuem. for example, come at 11 AM to be let in the musuem at 11:30. They allow waves of people to come in every 30 mins. 

The outdoor exhibit was much smaller than i thought, but there is so much to look at . there are about 3 different levels. make sure to head inside and check out some of those exhibitions, also the back is now open and there are some added pieces there. make a trip or 2 to the bathroom since thats part of the exhibit too = )

overall i liked and appreciated the hard work that was put into here, its a good way to check out something unique and kill about an hour of your day if youre in the city and looking for something to do!

So glad we got to visit 1933. Everything was simply amazing the covid protocols were spot on . We Made a reservation and was seated immediately . Our server was great and was very knowledgeable about their extensive menu . We decided on two medium rare steaks that were cooked to perfection very juicy not dry at all. For the sides my husband got a lobster tail and a got the lobster Mac and cheese that was very cheese and filled with large pieces of lobster with every bite and we split a French fry . Overall place was great a great compliment to St.Elmos for a fraction of the price overall a great experience. Could not tell the difference between St Elmos and 1933 we have visited both steakhouses.
My mom and I went this afternoon for pedicures, this place is great!  It's bright and clean and the staff of very friendly.  We will most definitely be back!

Best breakfast around. 
From friendly, fast service to the food, the view. 
Can't be beat. 

The breakfast buffet has everything I expect except grits but I can live without that.

Fresh cut up fruit, not from packages but real Whole Foods. Huge red Strawberries, long slices of pineapple, cantaloupe, etc. 
Hot oatmeal with every trimming imaginable.

Ask and Made to order station in the one end for waffles, pancakes, omelettes. (Caged free eggs) Condiments would make my hubby be in heaven as they have peanut butter, blueberry syrup with so many whole blueberries floating around, I ate it with my other fruit, didn't use it as syrup 

They have usual processed cereals and milk but my fav is the almond milk they offer. Vanilla and dark chocolate, yum! Plus Chobani yogurt. 
Mad I missed it yesterday as it is below eye level at the opposite end of the made to order chef. 
(Under all the gluten carbs where I usually glance and ignore. )

I would eat here even if I was not staying upstairs. 
Can't say enough about this place. Spacious, you don't fight others to get to the buffet, even play appropriate music in the background. (Music therapist approved, me) 

Breakfast is my least fav meal of the day but I think eating here makes it my favorite

Great food, cheap happy hour drinks, okay scenery (we got stuck on the side of the restaurant facing a wall maybe because we had a dog?). 

We ordered the peel and eat shrimp, fried scallops, mussels, and a fish platter. The serving sizes were great and everything tasted fresh and was hot when it hit the table. 

The boys beers were cold, my sister and I tried a happy hour margartia. Tasted premixed and very sweet, we ordered an extra shot to even it out and switched to wine after. 

We were sat on the side of the building when the patio was empty. It would've been a little better if we weren't right next to the door going in and if they maybe had higher tables so you could see the water and some music playing.

We had some time off before heading back home, so we went to the historical town St Charles near St Louis, MO. Then we found Lewis and Clark on Main Street.

I ordered the Mahi Mahi. It was grilled perfectly and served with a house salad and steamed veggies. Simply tasty.

This appeared to be a traditional family run restaurant in the heart of St. Charles. I saw a table tent about the bbq sauce made with the owner's mother recipe.

We could not be on the top floor because the 4-top tables were bolded on the floor. Otherwise, it would be a nice view.

I went to the ruby slipper during my trip to New Orleans I gave it three stars because it was mediocre service but good food. We had to wait a long time for her to get a menu and then to take our order the food was good I got the fried French toast bites which are really good.

This place is awesome. I got the Lamb Kebab which was juicy and cooked as good as any place that I have been. The Plate comes with salad, saffron rice and Arab stewed vegetables. I especially liked vegetables which I have never had before. After my main course I had some kanafa and black tea which is how any meal should end. My friend gave me a bite of his chicken shawarma which was well seasoned and I might get next time I'm here.

Awesome awesome awesome. We had trouble with our Nissan Quest and what we thought was the transmission.  We took it to the Nissan dealership where they told us 'We don't know what went wrong in the transmission but it's -real bad-'  They quoted us $5600 to replace the transmission and transmission computer.  We went to Yelp and found Ewing Bass and took my van there.

I think the most amazing part of the story is that Ewing Bass took the time to re-diagnose the problem.  Rather than just replacing the transmission as we had talked about (incidentally, they quoted me $1000 less than Nissan), they figured out it was something else that was causing the transmission to not work - some cam shaft or something...  Either way, they had read an article recently discussing the very problem my van was having and figured it out saving us a TON of money and heartache when changing the transmission wouldn't have fixed anything!

Additionally, they were honest.  I would have believed them if they said they had changed my transmission and charged me a boatload of money.  

Thank you thank you Ewing Bass!!!

I've been coming here for years and my favorites are now both gone 

PLEASE BRING BACK THE EDAMAME DUMPLINGS AND PANANG CURRY! This would for sure be a 5 star review if they still had those items! I'm from Seattle and made the trip here each time we came just for those!!

Good place to go with groups, or just as a couple.  The food was good, especially the noodle dishes and the appetizer tray (for a larger group).  Drink menu is good, and vegetarian options are many.   This is our neighborhood Vietnamese restaurant, and I will go back many more times.

World class joint, with some of the most blue collar bartenders around. The Coach also known as the Sheriff runs a tight ship and has a heavy elbow. Drinks are always ice cold and the DJ on the weekend makes the ladies panties fall to the floor. The locals love to chop it up about the Philly sports teams BUT beware of the Crypt Keeper who slithers around the happy hour crowd talking nonsense, he will chew you ear off. Perfect places if you looking to play some competitive shuffleboard or darts. All in all, this place feels like home.. if you cant buy happiness you can sure as hell buy a beer HERE!

Let me start by saying I ate here in Summer 2013, and it was great.  Great service, great food, no issues.  Ate here on 1/22/14, and had the totally opposite experience.  Service was ridiculously slow.  None of the rolls I ordered were correct and the food was mediocre (and that's a gift!).  Normally I'd cut some slack if I go to a restaurant during busy times.  But this was a Wednesday night, and it wasn't busy.  AT ALL.  Looks like Ijji 2, and the newly opened Ijji 3 have become the priority.

Great Idea just employees dont execute. Serviceis very slow my friends treat me good but if i didnt know them idk how it would go because everytime i order food it takes 45 minutes to get it and waiters never check up on you for refills.

We came here on a whim while in town for the camel races. I checked Yelp and saw the good reviews, and we went in right as it opened. The place looks like an old hotel or something, and it's really cool to see how the owners used some of the exposed interior wall surfaces as part of the decor. We had a party of four, as my wife and I were accompanied by our 7 and 4 year old boys. 

As we waited, I saw full size coloring books (not kids' menus with pictures) and crayons on a table and thought the kids were covered. The hostess/waitress who sat us wasn't very friendly, which was a bit of a turn-off, but I didn't care. I was tired from getting up at 3 a.m. in Reno for the balloon races. Just seat me and give me some food, thanks. 

You would've thought the waitress would've offered coloring books and crayons for the kids, but she couldn't be bothered. Oh well. I went back and grabbed them myself. After that, everything went more smoothly. I had the eggs benedict, and it was GOOD. I tried my son's wheat pancakes, and that was pretty good. They didn't have a kids' menu, but at least after what seemed like 20 minutes of my wife and kids deciding what they'd have, the waitress offered that the pancakes could be made in a smaller size. Sold. 

If the service was better, this place would've received 5 stars from me. As anyone with kids will tell you, the way an establishment handles small children is the way the parents end of feeling about it. It would've taken NOTHING for the hostess/waitress to optimize the experience, but, as with any customer service failure...she chose not to treat others as she'd want to be treated. Too bad.
Jeet is the best !!! She is available only thursdays and friday's. i only recommend her ! I always love my shape

This is by far the best restaurant in Philadelphia! I've been multiple times trying something new each time and yet to have anything I didn't enjoy. Their spin on Italian food is amazing so much flavor going on and the cocktails are perfect complement to their food.
Great spot! The beer is delicious. Love that they always have food trucks! I did a yoga class here once too and that was really fun!
Very pleasant surprise! Wanted a quick lunch after stopping at Costco and enjoyed a great meal with my wife. The servers were very pleasant and attentive. The meal was delicious. Will return.

I will begin with the cons first because there aren't many. We are out of town-ers looking for some great seafood. After reading some recent reviews we decided on avoiding the typical tourist trap restaurant and instead venture off the path in search of quality. This led us to Guppys on the Beach. Now here are the cons. The wait was very long. I don't mean they tell you 45 minutes and usually it's 20. It was literally 1 hour and 15 minutes long. When we approached the host we were put off by his unwelcoming greet. Instead after a few awkward seconds of him ignoring us glaring  down at his seating chart and talking with staff about seating, we are acknowledged with a why are you here look and  a mediocre how many are in your party and did you make a reservation? He then proceeded to tell us that there will be a 1 hour and 5 min wait (first available). After a painful 50 minute wait I return to inquire about time. A few seconds of awkward pause again, no smile and glaring at the seating chart from the same gentlemen "20 more minutes." Okay I get it. He appeared to be more than just the host. I'm guessing the manager or owner. Also he looked to be very skillful in the art of seating people for dinner. To move such a big group is to be commendable. Remember we are out of town-ers and some bedside manner goes a long way making a difference between a 4 star rating and a 5 star. Hence my reason for a 4 star. Your host is the keeper of the keys. The first to make an impression. A "welcome folks" or a little smile goes a long way. Out of town-ers are important with spreading the word to others to patronize these establishments. That little bit of effort in making each guest feel important outweighs any 1 hour wait. Now for the pros. Our waiter was warm, welcoming and friendly. He answered any questions about the menu and even reassured my picky daughter that the tap water was very good. She is a bottled water girl however agreed with the waiter. He brought our food out promptly and checked on us throughout dinner (even with the busy crowd). The food was simply fantastic! Our order included mussels, fish chowder, scallops, Florida two tail lobster and surf and turf with lobster. Everything was delicious including the sides, salads and bread. Well seasoned and tasty. All and all it was worth the wait once your past the keeper of the keys.

Food is great. The cauliflower grits and devilish eggs were great. Fast fresh and heathy, i have a busy week he'd be didn't have time to prep my meals. This was a great alternative. I will be going back and I downloaded the ap

I wanted to have a nice Margherita pizza and figured this was the closest place around.  I searched the internet and couldn't find a menu with pricing.  Though I did happen to find some pictures of what they offered....It didn't matter because I knew what I wanted: a Margherita pizza and some sort of an appetizer.  I called and ordered my pizza and after asking how much the sante fe rolls were, which I understood to be 4.49, I ordered two of them.

The bill was $35 and I nearly crapped my pants.  I figured it was my first time ordering at this place so I let it slide. 

Got it home.  wife and daughters gathered around the table.  The pizza was mediocre at best, please understand I've had a lot of pizza in Italy over 40 years.  So, I know delicious pizza!!!  This pizza had about an 1-1/2" crust around its perimeter.  It was totally, unequivocally, wet and limp.  The sauce and mozzarella and basil leaves slide off the slice as it was lifted.  The sauce was not so great.  A lighter, fluffier sauce with more texture would have been tastier.  It was "meh" at best.  It cost $13.99, not such a bad price for a brick over pizza.  Then we opened the Santa Fe Rolls....they cost $9.49 btw, not $4.49 like I thought I heard.  (The background noise was blaring into the phone when I called the order in, so I guess I just messed up and didn't hear her good enough.  My fault, I could have asked.)  

I digress...   

I opened the box-o-Sante Fe Rolls and to my surprise there were three in the box.  The girl on the phone said there were two, (4 halves).  They were soggy and laying in grease on the bottom of the box.  They weren't cut on the bias (angled cut) which is easier for dipping.  They too were droopy and soggy AF.  Borderline nasty.  They gave a small container of ranch as the dipping sauce.

Overall, I was totally disappointed in this establishment.  They're supposed to be a Select Pizzeria in a Premiere Town, The Township of WASHINGTON (08080) but they were just soggy, under-cooked, non-biased cut, dud-of-a-place.  I probably won't ever go back.  Too bad.  

Oh about the ambience.  It is nice and trendy, kinda super freaking loud though.

Such a fun place to go! Took my niece for her birthday and she loved it. The servers are all very helpful and patient. The manager makes sure everyone is doing well and walks around regularly. Good place to go for a girls night out. Their happy hour is really awesome.

This establishment previously had only raw vegan options but has changed to vegan with hot options. Don't let the fact that it's a vegan restaurant fool you though. The flavors created in the kitchen compete whit almost all other restaurants in town. Prices are between $9.99 and $16.00 but worth every penny. The atmosphere was also remodeled since my last visit here, it's much more sleek and colorful. I really enjoyed the different decor. The service is also beyond comparison. I had to most friendly, kind and bubbly server and I'm sorry I can't remember her name she had only been there for two weeks, either way she was amazing. If she didn't know the answer to something she would quickly run over to a team member and get the answer for us. I had the Burger and OMG!! Yummy!. I am not vegan but my partner is and we often wat at vegan establishments since I'm the least pickiest eater in town. Even if your not a vegan give this place a try it's worth it. Oh I almost forgot the espresso vegan ice cream, my goodness was it delicious. Three of us shared it, but I think I ate the majority of it. Ooops!

Had a very nice dinner this evening. We were quickly seated, the hostess was pleasant, the menus easy to read and attractive. I ordered a small tequila and lime margarita to start, and it was delicious...best I've every had. My wife had a pina colada, and again, it was top rate.

Ice water was served without our having to ask for it, and the chips, salsa and bean dip were very good. I don't usually care for bean dip, but this one was seasoned well, and I liked it a lot. The salsa was exceptional. Minimal cilantro, which is how I prefer it, and a rich, tomato-y taste made the salso delicious. The chips were fresh-tasting as well.

We were quickly able to decide what to eat. Our waiter took our order soon after the drinks came, and both plates arrived quickly, and just as we'd ordered.

I thought my seafood enchiladas were perfect! Seasoned mild, with a good dollop of sour cream. It went exceeding well with the rice and beans, and the margarita!

My wife enjoyed her pollo a la crema, which is her standard fare and all Mexican restaurants. This one was top ranked, very creamy. She said it was unusual in that instead of Parmesan, this dish was made with jack cheddar, which made it creamier.

I enjoyed the music, too! Soft contemporary rock sung in Spanish, with several almost-traditional tunes that were nice, too. I'm not a fan of the polka-like musica norteno, so I appreciated the more up-beat musical ambiance.

Our table was clean, the booth seating comfortable.

What kept this review from rating five stars? The staff was pleasant, but not friendly or chatty. I like to be treated special at restaurants. I like the wait staff to seem warm and inviting, even curious about us. This evening I felt nothing special...just a customer to whom the staff was willing to be courteous.

There was no Wi-Fi. A small matter, but still important to me.

Nothing special about the beer selection. In an area with so many craft breweries, I think top-rate restaurants should serve local beers.

No cazuela was on the menu. Cazuela is probably my most favorite mexican-style dish.

From Wikipedia:

Cazuela (Spanish pronunciation: [kawela]) is the common name given to a variety of dishes, especially from South America. It receives its name from the cazuela (Spanish for cooking pot) in which is cooked. The ingredients and preparation vary from region to region, but it is usually a mid-thick flavoured stock obtained from cooking several kinds of meats and vegetables mixed. (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cazuela).

So, four stars is my rating, making this restaurant a favorite for us.

We'll be back!

Really enjoyed my lunch visit to Local Taco. Stoped by to grab a quick bite and it was pretty quiet. Had a nice server who was attentive and answered all our questions. I had three tacos - a fish, chicken and shrimp. Those are listed in my order of preference. The fish was bangin, love the jalapeños on top! Chicken was also good, excellent amount of chicken. The shrimp was ok but it was too saucy for me, I would probably order minus the boom boom sauce next time. I also appreciated the variety of hot sauce options on the table. I would definitely come back and try some more.

There are several good Thai places in Carollwood and Sweet Basil is one of these. I have always taken out and never dined inside though. My one and only complaint is I like it spicy and my girlfriend doesn't.... They miss labeled the boxes once and gf got spicy.... I should have doubled check before setting the table..... No complaints on the food though and thats what"s important.....

Their Lo Mein and Chow Mein are very good.   They are reasonably priced and have good lunch specials.   The staff there is very friendly.     My biggest issue is that their version of General Tso's chicken (which is my all time favorite Chinese takeout dish) is not very good.   All of their chicken dishes that are fried use the same soft breading as their sweet and sour chicken.   I like General's Chicken, Orange chicken, etc. lightly breaded and very crispy.   I just do not order those dishes there anymore and stick w/ the Chicken lo mein, Mongolian beef and wonton soup.   Overall, glad to have a Chinese takeout option in the area

I went to this place mainly because I was a loyal follower of Jose Garces from my Amada experiences in the past. But it was a uniquely different and amazing experience in comparison to Amada (like comparing two children).  It was definitely more of a lounge with excellent drinks and tapas but the food is good enough to go for it alone (unusual). Jose can do no wrong.

I especially appreciated its proximity to Rittenhouse when I lived there. Go over to Capogiro afterwards for a night cap!

BEST BEIGNETS EVER! These beignets are more fluffy and cake like  as opposed to fried and chewy (ya I'm referring to Cafe du Monde-gross!) cafe Beignet is a charming little cafe, small iron tables. Delicious. Safe. Friendly.

This is our new favorite place for Mexican food. Bucks county has been lacking a place like this. We expanded our search a tad further out and found la Choza. Excellent variety on the menu (though - to be honest - I think they could cut a few things as I'm not sure they need to include pasta, lol. ). The chicken mole was to die for. We will definitely be back.

I love this bakery ! Ever since I was little and still to this day this is the only bakery I buy baked goods from. ! The cakes and ice cream and cookies everything is soooo good and made with love! Every time my birthday rolls around I always get a cake from here . And the location is great as well. The service is amazing, I just absolutely love this place!

Cafe Zen has been my favorite place to hit up when I need a sushi fix.  Yes, it is located in an unassuming strip mall in Gretna, but don't let that deter you.  We all know that sometimes the BEST restaurants are the ones without all of the outside bells and whistles, and if you have great offerings, there's nothing more that you need!

Last night's dinner was no exception to the experiences that I've had here.  My date and I split three rolls: the rainbow roll, fresh salmon with avocado, and the shrimp tempura.  Cafe Zen takes a lot of care in a beautiful presentation, which I find is lacking at many other Westbank sushi joints.  The fish was also very fresh and not fishy at all.

I also like coming here for lunch.  They have great specials, my favorite being the maki combination.  You choose two small rolls--I always opt for fresh salmon with avocado and the spicy tuna--along with a bowl of soup (the miso is great!) and a side salad.

Next time you're cruising down Belle Chasse Highway and feeling a yen for some sushi, be sure to give Cafe Zen a try!  I wouldn't steer you wrong!
Just ordered takeout from this place. The food is fantastic! Best Chinese food in the area and such a huge variety!

Amazing food! Very authentic Peruvian - this coming from a nyc resident x 15 years! Refreshing change to the doylestown restaurant circuit. Food can be spicy if u like (they ask you your spice preference). Staff is super friendly and accommodating. Didn't bring my kids this time (3 and 5) but they have a kids menu, so will next time. Highly recommend!

How difficult is it to NOT toast a bagel?  This is the second time I've asked for them to not be toasted and they came back toasted with the butter melted and soaking through the wrapper and bag, making a mess in my car. And when only one napkin is in the bag and it's under the bagels, it's pointless to even give me a napkin.   Twice, I've had to drive back and have them redo my order. It's bagels not rocket science.

Stopped in for weekday brunch and was not disappointed! The place was packed at 10am, which is always a good sign, and I see why. 

Ambiance: it's like sitting in a big, cozy but edgy farmhouse kitchen - urban rustic with that nifty blue chalkboard wall. We sat inside, which is noisy and echoey, so chatting was a little challenging but it also means that I can take my kids there on another day. I saw a few other munchkins there and clearly, they were enjoying themselves. 

Drinks: Fresh OJ for the spouse and The Cure for me. Double-yum on both, and the Cure was oh so pretty too.

Food: Pork belly sandwich: portion just right, and while I don't eat much starch, the bit that I nibbled was delish. I was more focused on the pork belly, cured in house. Hubby much enjoyed the tri-tip sliders and the bite that I took was phenomenal. He wanted lunch, I wanted breakfast, and we both were completely satisfied. The dessert-for-breakfast options looked fantastic and the selection is creative and not overwhelming (I like a decent selection, but not a fifteen-page menu, and P&P's is just right) - raspberry pecan pancakes!

Service: attentive, interested and interesting, and they all seemed to be having fun and are really into the food. Good job. Maybe a little too attentive - at least 3 people came over to check on us right after we got our plates.

Verdict: I'll be back. Soon. I don't give 5 stars on the first date, but if they smack it out of the park again, I'll be upgrading my review.
Took the sunset cruise. Saw several dolphins! The crew was very engaging and entertaining. My 11 year old daughter loved it! Lots of fun things to do for the kids. She loved the dance party.

I'm a little surprised I never reviewed Shake Shack before, since I've been here a few times and I'm absolutely in love with it. No other burger is as perfect looking and as mouthwatering as the Shack Stack. 

After coming home from a trip to LA and Vegas, dejected and miserable because I was unable to get In-N-Out, I sought out Shake Shack for solace. I'm not really sad I missed In-N-Out anymore, because no one can be sad while eating a Shake Shack burger.

The burgers here are delicious! I would love to get my hands on the meat ratio they use, because their patty is meaty, juicy, and just fatty enough. They are consistent in their use of perfect looking ingredients - center cut slices of bright red, perfectly ripe tomatoes, and beautiful, crisp green lettuce leaves - not that sad white/light green crap they have at McD's so often. And what else to sandwich all this perfection than in a lightly toasted Martin's potato bun? (I read one review that said Shake Shack doesn't toast their buns - but this is wrong. They toast the insides lightly! For sure!).

Definitely the best thing about Shake Shack is their consistency. I feel that I have had the same, identical, delicious burger the first time I came here (a year or two ago) as I did when I came here last (last week). The Shack Stack burger (with the crispy, cheese filled portobello mushroom) is to die for! Just wait a little before digging in, because the cheese is seriously very hot, and you don't want a burnt tongue when you have something truly awesome to taste.

I am not a fan of crinkle cut french fries, but Shake Shack fries don't do any harm. Not bad, but nothing to write home about. It is the standard accompaniment and I will always order them alongside my burger.

For dessert, the Liberty Shell concrete is perfect! I love cannoli's, so I was ecstatic to try it out in ice-cream form. I wish they would add a bit more of the cannoli shells (Termini bro's!), but you don't really have to fix what isn't broken, I guess.

The service here - although not a wait staff - is actually pretty awesome. They offer to take away your trash/tray once you're done eating, and the cashiers are always friendly. Maybe sometimes too enthusiastic at times - one time they chanted my name loudly as they called my order and proudly announced that I was their like 136th customer that day. I was confused yet amused.

I would rate this place 5 stars if the price were a tad bit more agreeable, but still, Shake Shack is one of my favorite burgers ever.

On your salad you must try the Cramy Carsar dressing!

OK, that might be a little mean. My wife and I were out and about on a Saturday and I have read several good thinks about this place on a Smyrna Facebook page. I really think "diner" would have been a more accurate name for here than café. I would like to comment on the food we had, but all we tried was the water - great news - it was wet! 

I had heard the sides were good, so let's go. My wife is abstaining from meat for a while - more vegetarian than vegan - and thinking they might have a good selection we go in. One of the reviews has a picture of the menu - it's worth a read especially looking for misspelling due to the language difference. I am not sure where the owner is from - so I'm not being phobic because of that. It was just entertaining to peruse the menu - great way to kill time. Actually Cramy Carsar we figured out was creamy Caesar. They served marinina sauce with their Fries Mazzarella Stickes. They would probably include some Parmsan cheese if you asked.

OK, enough of that - as I said we did not try the food. She wanted a veggie plate and the only way to get that was to buy, in this case, 4 of their $2.99 side items. Since most of you are probably are not good at math - that's almost $11.96 - well precisely $11.96 so you can put your phone up - you want need a calcinater...(see what I did there?) We chose to leave, very politely I might add, and go to Cracker Barrel where 4 veggies cost eight bucks and you get bread.

I PM'd the owner on Facebook and offered to proof and correct the menu. As it were he was rushed to get the place open and cranked these out - obviously without spellcheck. There are new ones on the way - glad someone got a pic. I give them an A-OK because I think they deserve a chance based on the good things I have read. I will give them another shot and let you know.

One side note - they are apparently VERY understaffed. If you know or someone looking for a job in the area, they could use the help. I think the family is doing it all. A friend went there on Sunday because of what he had heard as well and they turned them away because they could not handle a party of 14.

Menu has a lot of promise, but unfortunately doesn't come through. I got the Swegs Combo: a house salad and half a mushroom and spinach panini. Salad was fresh and a decent portion, but the dressing was really acidic, but sweet. Wasn't a fan. Panini was a disappointment too, unfortunately.  Bread was dry and amount of mushroom and spinach was laughable (a tablespoon) compared to the 6 inch wide bread. Also tried the turkey chili, and that was bland as well. Inside is very clean, and has a nice variety of healthy seeming bottled drinks. Theres not a single soft drink in sight (a great thing!), only water and tea on tap. I really wanted to like this place, but I don't see myself returning unfortunately.

Very cute dessert place in ctown!

5/5 ambiance. So cute here with woodentables and little plants on each table.

5/5 service. The staff takes your order if you do dine-in, and they are very friendly and attentive. 

5/5 food. All the desserts look so cute and they are not too overpriced!

Since moving to Indianapolis Goose the Market has been maybe my favorite find.  The selection of fresh and local products is fantastic and the service is amazing.

The featured attraction for me are the sandwiches (you can not go wrong with the Batali), I have in the past very literally planned my weekend around getting one, and the news that they are opening on Sundays really opens up my calendar.
Highly recommend!  My new BBQ place!  I couldn't suggest to change anything.  From prices,  staff,  food.  All was very good.

Went here with my husband and son.  I wasn't impressed the last time I came here but decided to give it another try.  Nope - still not impressed.  I am completely baffled by their kids menu.  It is a BBQ restaurant but the only choices on the kids menu are chicken strips (frozen from a bag), corn dog (frozen from a bag), or a grilled cheese.  No kids burger or kids bbq sandwich.  That is bizarre to me.  Sorry kid - no bbq for you unless you want a huge adult meal.  

I ordered the brisket (ok) and sausage (greasy and no flavor).  I sent the sausage back and got more brisket.  We were there early on a Friday evening and it was not very crowded yet our server was disinterested and took forever refilling drinks.  There are many other barbecue restaurants in town that do it better (Mickey Roo's in Franklin for one).

After our race, my friend and I needed some food and we stopped in at Hard Rock.  Not normally a place I'd choose when visiting a city, but hey.  It was there and we were hungry.  The wait wasn't too bad, considering everyone who ran the Rock 'n Roll that day seemed to be eating there (and at every other restaurant in the area).  It took our waiter a fairly long time to even bring us water, but all I wanted was a seat.  I wasn't too picky.  As for the food, it was fine.  The onion rings I craved were not so hot, so that was a bit of a disappointment.  Good bbq, good twisted mac 'n cheese.  This is a fun "touristy" place to go if you're in the area, but I wouldn't go out of the way.

Dr Bolser and staff go above and beyond in listening to the family and treating the patient. The care here is extraordinary, as are Dr Bolser's medical skills. And the fees are very fair. Most remarkably, one week after major surgery, our dog Lucy was thrilled to go back to the clinic and to snuggle with Dr Bolser and staff. Thank you, thank you, thank you!

Decent coffee shop with friendly staff.  Tried the iced latte and was good.  I liked that they don't add any sugar/sweeteners.  Inside decor is nice with several tables to read/work. Its at a great location within minutes from love park.  Would come back again

I have lived in tampa for 10 years and this was the first time I visited Charley's because I have heard mixed reviews.

I have to say i left as cool as the center of the rare steak I was presented.

I ordered the Kobe ribeye and my wife ordered the Kobe filet with a lobster tail and both of our steaks were cooked incorrectly.  

I ordered my ribeye medium rare and it came to me extremely rare, so I sent it back and they simply put my already cut steak back on the grill which diminished the flavor of the $90 steak I ordered.  

My wife ordered the petit filet medium and it came out medium well to well done.  Also- her lobster tail was over cooked and they forgot to send out the dipping butter.

We shared the cauliflower which was actually the star of the show.

In all, we spent nearly $400 for a date night between drinks and dinner and for that price, either Eddie Vs, Ocean Prime, Capital Grille or Flemmings are much better options in the international mall area.

Good hangout spot with friends over bubble tea!  It is slightly more pricey for the typical kinds of drinks, but they have a good variety to choice from.  They also have macaroons and other desserts,  along with snacks now,  if you're hungry while doing work or craving sweets

Line is most likely going to be out the door. That's okay. Wait your turn and you will be rewarded with one of the best cheesesteaks in cheesesteak city. They use lots of high quality meet, fresh ingredients, and the bread is nice and soft. These sandwiches are an excellent use of calories and I can't wait to get another one of them.

Casual atmosphere, BYOB while they are waiting for a license.  We had an exdellent meal, noodles and dumplings.  The dumplings were excellent, the ramen decent, and the lamb with glass noodles superb.  Atmosphere was a bit noisy, but that is very consistent with the customer base--young, hip, and cool.
They will give you hard time in cancelling your membership, I waited until my membership expiry date and still wants you to pay the cancellation fee. Not happy with their policy .

This could be my new favourite restaurant in the area. Over the years I have seen restaurants come & go from this location so was skeptical. We were pleasantly surprised when we entered the restaurant - a beautiful wooden bar & an area for fine dining.
