After we were seated & had drinks, Chef Andonia came to our table & warmly welcomed each of us to her restaurant. She explained the nightly specials, asked about allergies & explained that she would be happy to accommodate any of our dinner requests. The six of us were delighted with our dinners & yummy desserts. I look forward to the next time.

Visiting from NYC, came for brunch here based on several friends having heard the place had a good reputation.  The food was very good, the bloody mary bar novel, and the music relaxing, but overall we felt the meal to be overpriced and not worth the 2 hour wait.  We also felt the staff to be a bit pretentious and atmosphere stuffy.

1. Incorrect measurement of Sq Footage
2. Arrived without any samples of colors
3. They basically only offer the flaked options. 
4. When i addressed them about hte Sq footage misqoute (significantly higher than other floor companies and our own assessment).  We assumed they did not remove the dog shower and the tiled area that were being left untouched.  However the office person stood firm on their quote.  
5. They also promised it by week's end and it took a few weeks for the qoute.
6. The person who arrived told us to look online for more color and example images but it turns out their website is not updated so it was a waste of our time.
Time Waste all around.  See my next review for who we chose to hire.  And wait for the amazing before and after photos.  

We do hope this feedback helps SB Surfacing improve.  I suggest:
A. Bring samples. B. Update website + instagram with images. C. Offer to re-measure when such a discrepancy D. Keep your word even give or take a day or two, not weeks.

I LOVE taking my family here! My daughter is always excited and mesmerized by the fire when they do the onion volcano thing! And the food is fantastic! Amazing portions and very filling! I always get the steak and lobster with the yum yum sauce and would highly recommend! Sometimes there can be a little bit of a wait but it's not too bad. The employees are friendly and the Chefs are VERY funny and helpful! The restaurant is also very clean! Will definitely be back

Went for dinner. The service and ambiance were excellent. The poke. was my favorite, but the halibut. and albondigas. were also great. The bourbon. was good, just what you'd expect, and the mezcal. was interesting.

I really don't know why this place isn't listed on Eater.

Very small venue loaded with Storyville history. It's near the Marriott and Hilton so you don't have to go to Bourbon Street or Frenchmen Street to hear great music. We were there on a Thursday night. No cover but there is a one drink minimum per set and they pass the hat for band tips. We saw something Seville and the Cadillacs. They were fabulous. Great jazz and blues foursome. Lead singer also played sax, flute and trumpet. Drinks are cheap--around $7 so it's an easy place to hang for awhile. The place is super small-maybe 10 or 15 tables. Apparently there is burlesque in the back but it's only two tables a pole. There's a sign on the door with a Help Wanted Burlesque dancer. So we were out of luck last night. Guess it ain't the 1930s with burlesque dancers populating NOLA. Check it out and maybe put in your resume.
Gyro platter is fantastic and the portions are huge. Acropolis is extremely consistent and has a fun dinner atmosphere.

The best place in town to get a Gyro is in the Soulard neighborhood at a tiny hole in the wall joint, fittingly named Soulard Gyro and Deli. This family owned place serves up a pretty mean Gyro. The meat is juicy and perfectly seasoned, the tzatziki sauce is creamy cucumbery deliciousness. What's not to love? It's better that any Gyro vendor we've ever eaten at in Chicago, and that is saying loads...don't tell anyone I said that!

  If you feel like trying something new, skip the traditional Gyro wrapped in a pita and try the Doner Kebab. It's not really different from a typical gyro except that is is served on the BEST, ginormous bakery style bun. The bread totally takes an already tasty Gyro and kicks it up a notch. A must try if you ask me! I've yet to find out which local bakery cooks it up for them, but I intend to find out. I could eat the bread by itself, it's that dang good :)

  If you order the gyro salad like I did on my last visit, be prepared for a salad worthy of feeding 2-3 people. The meat and veggie toppings are generous and it's served with warm, lightly fried pita slices on the side.  It's by no means healthy, but who cares? It's so delicious, you'll forget all about that pesky diet and not feel one bit guilty about indulging in the kebaby goodness. 

  If lamb isn't your thing, fret not! They also serve turkey and ham sandwiches as well as a vegetarian "Gyro" and a veggie sandwich. They also have a few meat-free salads, cheese bread and homemade Greek desserts.

  Service is always fast and pleasant. The shop is small, but we usually have no problem getting a table. Prices are exceptional and totally worth the amount of food you get. I have yet been able to finish a Gyro or sandwich from this place in one sitting.

  We've tried gyros at several other places around STL and Soulard Gyro and Deli is by far the best. I dare another Gyro joint to claim they are better. I double dog dare ya!

Eating STL, A Chicago Perspective
http://eatingstl.blogspot.com/

1 star b/c fewer isn't an option.  Terrible.  Loews is not a "resort" & barely a hotel.  Planned to have a spa vacation with a friend.  We are both native Arizonans and were coming back for a little R&R.   It was early October, still warm, therefore the "slow" season.  We got a good deal on the room, but the rest was downhill.

Arrived, the valet was overly chatty. Told us we could either park ourselves or valet depending on where our room was and our preference.  Didn't mention that it was $9/day either way.

Porter wouldn't stop talking as he brought our bags up.  He wouldn't leave either.  So we finally shoved $10 in his hand & showed him the door.  A larger tip than deserved, but we just wanted him to leave.

That night we spoke to 3 different people about the Ventana hike (on the resort property).  Each of them told us something different:  "12 miles round trip,"  "6 miles round-trip and you should plan for several hours,"  "I think it's about 4 miles, but here's a pamphlet on it, all the details are in it."  The pamphlet was just as confusing as the descriptions from the hotel employees.  So, we figured we would just start out on the trail and go as far as we could until we felt like turning around and coming back.

Dinner the first night was ok, but expensive.  

I had my lap top, tried to figure out how to connect to the internet.  The message that comes up is "applicable charges may apply..."   Really?  Seriously?  Well, ok, if you insist on nickel-and-diming me, then what the hell is the fee?  It was vague enough that I just turned off the computer.  Didn't want to risk being charged $20/day for internet access when I could do the routine stuff on my iPhone.

Reading the hotel guide in the room trying to figure out which spa treatments to do, then realized there was a daily fee to use the hotel gym.  Seriously?

Next morning, had breakfast.  It was fine, portions were big, but nothing spectacular.  Went to the spa to make reservations for the afternoon... lady at the counter was a horrible person.  The fake salesperson.  She listened to my friend and I discuss the treatment options, she told us which massages were the most popular, which ones treatments were no longer offered, etc.  We were entertaining the idea of purchasing a package, $250 for 3 treatments.  She said, "well, you'll have to do all the treatments in one day, we can't split them up..."  Seriously, the resort is empty, is it such a big deal to split up the treatments?  We were only there for 2 days.  Fine, we each picked a massage, we scheduled our time.

Went for the hike.  Dry season, not the best AZ hike, good exercise, but not very pretty.  Came back to the "resort" through the back, walked by a t.v. monitor that was advertising things for the resort, on the monitor in a flash we see something that says, "Spa Happy Hour..."  Waited for the loop to go around.  Apparently there are spa deals to be had.

Went to the front desk to inquire.  That person had no idea what the Spa Happy Hour was.  Bellhop, had no idea.  Went to the Concierge who had no idea.  Finally she called the spa... multiple treatments offered during the slow season for 1/2 price.  The bitchy lady at the spa never told us there were specials.  May have changed our minds on what we scheduled for that afternoon.  We were pissed.  We rescheduled our treatments for the Spa Special Massage.  

1.  Why don't the people at this resort all know their facts?
2.  Why wouldn't you tell people about spa specials, isn't the point of having a special  to have more people sign up for things?  Afterall, it's the slow season.
3. Why would a "resort" nickel-and-dime the customer.  It's unbelievably irritating to be charged $5 for this $10 for that, just add it into the price of the room.  Seriously, the Holiday Inn offers free wi-fi, so WTF?

Dinner that night was fine, not great and not worth the money.  I live in NYC now, so when I pay $60 for dinner, I want it to be really good....

Next day, went to have brunch.  My friend ordered the fish tacos, asked the server if the tortillas were corn or flour because she has a gluten allergy.  He said, "pretty sure they are corn."  Our food arrives, he sets the tacos down in front of her and says, "oh I was wrong, they are flour tortillas, is that ok."  I finally said, no it's not okay.  She has an allergy.  his response, "it's no big deal we can make them with corn it will just take a couple minutes..."

So many things wrong with this interaction:
1.  Why wouldn't the server come back out and ask beforehand if flour was okay.  Why would he bring the food out and then ask?
2.  If it's so damn easy to make them with corn, then make the f***ing tacos with corn tortillas
3.  The correct tacos were brought back by a manager.  We never saw the server again... (chickens**t, he was probably afraid we would rip him a new one).  Manager offered us a free dessert.  How lame.

WORST EXPERIENCE EVER.

Such friendly service!  Very good food!  Best double cheese bacon burger in the area!! Outdoor dining across street from marina w great live entertainment!! Fun to sit outside, eat, n sing along if u wish!!   Large separate game room w pool tables n arcade games!  Separate bar/dining area appears to b for private party. Reasonable prices!! Definitely b back!  Eric is a hoot!!
The coffee here was great! Cute little coffee shop and the area around is nice and walkable.
Fantastic vegan food in Santa Barbara! There are many wonderful options for great food and it's all vegan! You don't have to be vegan to enjoy it all either. Try the rajas tacos...amazing!

Super helpful & friendly staff (grey haired guy Mike was especially helpful - took a lot of time to explain pros and cons of a bunch of different products). Pretty good selection, not the cheapest but great quality.

I liked the meal I had at this location. It was fast as it is supposed to be. It is a really cool concept, healthy and fast food. 

I had a Quesadilla with roasted peppers. It was really good and fresh. I had a fountain drink which consists of natural soda with cane syrup. These were also very good. 
I ordered a fruit cup and the fruit was all very fresh and tasty. 

Of the other people in my group the food all looked to be fresh and bright. I had some of the sweet potato fries and they could be a little more crunchy.

A couple of notes for this location, first the staff were friendly and insured even when we sat down that we had excellent service. They took an additional order. Went and got something I should have grabbed.

The only downside I found was the overall cleanliness of the tables. We had a group of 7 people. All the tables were dirty in the establishment. They had loose food particles and stains. For a healthy fast food restaurant, they need a system of cleaning the tables. We were there an hour and a half maybe two hours and no one ever came and cleaned tables after customer use.

Disgusting would be an upgrade from the crap they served me. I should've known better. I was tired, craving a burger. I pulled in and saw there were no cars in the parking lot, or in the drive through lane. That should've been my first clue. When nasty ass Taco Bell has a full parking lot and a line at the drive through, it's my fault for ignoring the obvious and surrendering to my fatigue. 

The triple was three layers of old, dried out ground beef? Shoe? Horse? Horse shoe? The bacon was chewy as hell and the bun was old and stale. It will be awhile before I can eat another burger. I think I have fast food PTSD.
I know almost nothing about guns, but wanted something for home defense.  Big thanks to Mark and Mike for all of their patience!

I was super excited to visit Morimoto because I'm a huge fan of Chef Morimoto on Iron Chef!  Of course I was expecting good food, but I was blown away by how much I enjoyed my meal.  We started off with some cocktails.  Karai is a bit spicy with cilantro and jalapeno.  Kiku is a blend of pear and chrysanthemum tea. Both drinks were great!  The hubs ordered the eight course omakase and I got the duck duck duck. 

duck duck duck is not for the faint at heart.  You really gotta love duck to order this dish.  The hubs isn't much of a fan, so he wasn't really impressed.  I LOVED it!  The roasted duck breast was cooked to perfection.  The skin was crispy and had a nice amount of fat.  The meat was tender and flavorful.  The duck confit fried rice was kinda oily and too salty.  I still gobbled it up though.  Duck egg had the best runny yolk.  Mixed well with confit!  

It was my first time having omakase.  Even though the portions look small, we were both stuffed by the end of the meal.  We took home a good amount of the duck duck duck.  The whitefish carpaccio with yuzu sauce, miso marinated black cod, diver scallop with truffle, and austrailian raised wagyu on sizzling platter were definitely the highlights of the meal.  We really took our time savoring each entree.  I could taste the quality and flavors of the ingredients.  

Our waiter took his time in explaining each course and was warm and inviting.  We enjoyed our first visit and would recommend Morimoto for a special occasion or just a very nice gift to yourself!  It's not a meal that we could afford often, but it was very much worth the splurge.

A lovely experience here tonight. The service was friendly without being overattentive, the food and wine were great, the space was clean, and the atmosphere was really nice. Between us, we tried the beet salad and smoked chicken and butter night squash ravioli, as well as the lump crab raviolo (a special). Everything was delicious! All around, a really nice dining experience.

Excellent!

The chicken braised in white wine crepe, and the rib eye au poivre (special) were very very very good!

Too bad I was too full for dessert.

This place is Cute! inside.

I'm pretty sure now that there are no good buffets in the Metairie area, especially not of the asian variety. Ok, so let's start with the good: large selection, service was expected for a buffet restaurant-drinks were kept full and partially finished plates were taken away, nothing memorable but not horrible, good sushi selection.  The bad- food was lukewarm, heavy, dry, sauce drenched, salty, the sushi is what saved it from 1 star.  The price is standard for a snowcrab-seafood buffet at about 13 a head.  I'll stick with the 'HOT' take-out place down the street.

This place is really fantastic. Excellent selection and fantastic prices. Kind, helpful staff (Jane is Especially AWESOME!). Convenient location just a short drive from charming downtown Carpinteria. Check it out!

The bowling alley had 4 groups bowling on a Wednesday afternoon in between snow storms. The employees were friendly and the facility was clean and well maintained. The 3 of us had a great time. 

Shoe rentals are $3.50 and each game was $3.50 or $4 depending on age. Hourly lane pricing was $17.

Was in the area and saw all the glowing reviews so we decided to stop by on a recent Sunday afternoon. We had tacos with three different kinds of meat and burritos with carnitas and barbacoa. The Barbacoa was fatty but good, the carnitas and chicken were average. With so many Mexican places in the area I can't believe that this is the only one that gets 5 stars.  Also they serve everything in styrofoam. You order a burrito you get a styrofoam clamshell to-go box. They bring you water in styrofoam cups, they bring you salsa in a styrofoam bowl. Styrofoam never degrades it would be great if they stop using it.
Too overpriced for what you get. The tacos are just ok.. nachos are delicious though

Ordering dinner 20 minutes before they close to be delivered. Being called 3 minutes before they close to be told they are cancelling the order. Not cool. Reputable businesses actually fulfill their orders when they are made during business hours.

This is my favorite place for some quick tacos! The tacos are huge. I usually order two and it's more than enough. The cabbage on top is a nice touch. I also like that they come on double corn tortillas versus flour!

Dooriban's food has the same authenticity as if I were still stationed at Osan Air Base! One of my favorite things was going off base and having the local restaurants cook up same amazing bulgogi. It's nice to know that Dooriban absolutely nails their flavors so much that it reminds me of my time in Korea! Thank you Dooriban, your food is perfect!

The only reason they are not receiving a five star is they are a bit pricey. My only critique...expensive based on entrees

Finding a reliable, compassionate, knowledgeable vet can be a daunting task at times. I stumbled upon both Dr. Stoffts about 8 years ago at a clinic near me. I was extremely pleased with their care of my pets so much, that when they moved 2x over the years, I followed them. They're now in their own practice at Sabino Vet Care, and hopefully, the moving is over!
They have always provided excellent care of my dogs and cat. They're extremely knowledgeable and don't try to push unnecessary tests or medications on you, in fact, they take a bit more of a conservative approach on most things. They have a wonderful staff who are quick to answer any questions you have, or have one of the doctors call you back fast.
To sum it up, I couldn't be more pleased! Zak, Zoe and Boomer second my vote.

This a wonderful cafe with delicious croissants, crapes, sandwiches usually great coffee. I have been there several times and tried all three kinds of croissants. They are fresh and delicious. The quiche is excellent but very small, it comes with a side of spinach and a nice dressing. I would have preferred a lower price point than $12. The crapes are delicious and well price.

The employees are very friendly and welcoming and efficient. They always greet the customers with a smile and warm greeting. They deserve 5 stars. Thank you for your hard work.

But the reason for 4 rather than 5 stars, besides the expensive quiche, is that the bathroom didn't have a toilet paper holder. The toilet paper was placed on the toilet's tank and made it difficult to use.

Was helped by Mr. Benjamin Saint Ford, and could not have been happier with the service he rendered. I was in and out in a half hour, and had my every question answered in a direct, professional, and friendly manner. I've been to the other three ATT locations in the area, and I will never go to another one again. By far, the store at 2056 Sproul is the best AT&T store in the region. Accept no other.

(3.5) Met a group of friends here for weekend brunch and I was pleasantly surprised. I've been here other times for happy hour or a late night bite (both of which didn't leave an impression), but brunch definitely changed my view. Something else that was unexpected? Parking... or the lack thereof. Which led me to believe there just might be something to their weekend brunch.

We started with a couple orders of the Baked Artichoke and Crab dip. It was quite tasty. For my main, I got the Spicy Caribbean Hash (mostly because it seemed to be the most unique thing on the menu). It was a delicious mixture of Andouille sausage sautéed with onions, peppers, and fried potatoes that was topped with Monterey Jack cheese, perfectly cooked eggs [over medium] and a Pickapeppa hollandaise. All the flavors were well balanced and had the perfect amount of heat. I'm not exactly sure what made it "Caribbean", but it doesn't really matter when it tastes excellent.

Overall, the service was just a touch on the slow side but had no real issues and the food was great. Though I don't have a strong desire to eat here during the week for lunch or dinner, I will not hesitate if some friends want to meet here for brunch again.
Shelby Plante is an excellent chiropractor.  I would recommend her if you are looking for someone thorough and gentle.  I love the location!

Wow... now I really know what people mean when they say how terrible Americanized Chinese food is! Seriously, some of the best food I've ever had! I went with a group of friends and ordered way too much food, but yet we ate every last bit. The service is friendly and the food comes out quick so eat fast!. They have an expansive menu so you're hard pressed to find something you won't like. I highly, highly, HIGHLY recommend the lamb with cumin. (I am still dreaming about this dish almost two months later). The chongqing chicken and shredded pork with long hot pepper were also very good. If you're a more adventurous eater, I'd recommend starting with the beef tendon in hot oil. Go with the dan dan noodles if you're not. I'm a chilihead so the heat didn't bother me too much, order it extra spicy and enjoy the burn!
I ate here with some friends who live next door. It was good with a great view. If you are in the area drop by and get a bite to eat and enjoy the view.

This Starbucks is my favorite of the 84647 that I have been to because of their staff. They have the friendliest staff and always perfect my order. Today, I spilled my drink EVERYWHERE and not only did they clean it up but they made a new drink without charging me. I have never encountered a more welcoming, happy, and fantastic staff than I have at this location. Thank you Hockessin Starbucks!!!!!
We couldn't have asked for better service - everyone was so attentive! The food was good and service was prompt. I will definitely go again.

Ordered food and then the waiter came out with all of the food expect for one. He then told us that they didn't have the broth for the other soup noodle that we ordered for my grandmother. My grandma has a religious background that cannot each beef broth and was sick so she didn't have appetite for anything else. All she wanted was some noodle soup. 

1 star because: it's fine that the waiter did not know before hand that there wasn't any chicken soup. However it is not okay to bring all the rest of the food for every one else and ask us to make adjustments. I didn't know whether he expected us to eat it while asking my grandmother to wait. Brought this to the managements attention and he scoffed it off blaming it on my grandmother saying she can't eat anything else.

I have been coming to Eyeglass World for years to buy glasses and I have always found the customer service to be excellent.  Staff are patient with me while I try different frames and they don't pressure you to buy something that is out of your price range. In previous years I had gone to the Park Mall and always felt that the people working there really didn't care for their jobs.  The experience here however is noticeably different as staff greet customers upon coming in and are always helpful. While there are times that it is busy and wait times longer than one has patience for, it is to be expected depending on the time of day you come in. Having been to several different eyeglass stores in Tucson over the years, long wait times are not uncommon so you can expect the store to be busy on a weekend or even after 5 pm during the week.  Earlier this month, I came in to reorder contact lenses and just as expected, was greeted on arrival and I was able to reorder my contacts in no time. I will continue to shop here as I have for years because I know what I can expect when I shop here.
A $7.50 salad without a drink? And one small chicken strip? My 5 star rating just went to 2 stars. Won't be going back there anytime soon.

Seafood store located in the Parkway Shopping Center.  Ordered a bushel of extra large steamed crabs that were perfectly seasoned, perfectly sized and very juicy.  Some seafood joints like to place the largest crabs on top of the bushel heap, and as you work your way through the pile, try to sneak in smaller ones.  Not Gadaleto's.  Every crab ordered met or exceeded expectations.  I will be back at least one more time and get another bushel.
I love the pick-up and drop off service!! The gentleman at the Arnold office are so nice and work hard to make sure everything is to my satisfaction.

While the MD's and most of the staff are competent or even great caregivers, the system is a mess!  Good luck phoning:  you'll be forced into an endless wait of various recordings telling you that you should hang up and call 911, how important your call is, and how much they care.  Bullshit!  If you care, you'd fix your system to make it more patient friendly.  They even opened an Executive Wellness Center so folks could pay more to get better service.  I wanted to find out how much it would cost but could not get through.  I finally got to a place to leave a message but nobody returned my call.  Is this our future with Obamacare?  God help us!

This is my third time here, the first time I was blown away by the excellent customer service.  The last two times was average at best.  Today I got a gel manicure, it looks like it was done by a beginner.  The polish doesn't go all the way back to the cuticle,  it looks grown out, like they were done a week ago.  Hand massage was almost non existent. Rubbed some lotion on and did some weird snapping thing to each of my fingers.  Never offered a beverage the last two times I was there, although a staff member was eating at the end of the nail bar.  But they do in fact have a sign hanging at the checkout counter almost demanding a 20% tip or you could be refused future service.  Last time going to this salon for me.

The Baltic birch panels this place sells are my favorite painting surface.  The sales staff is helpful and knowledgeable, but not obtrusive.  They carry high quality art supplies, but it is also fun to peruse the goofy rubber animals and assorted novelty toys.  I always send my students to Artist & Craftsman over other art supply stores.

The Graniterra experience from stone selection to installation was professional and customer focused! Christian patiently worked with my layout until I was happy and the measuring and installation team did a first class  job. I felt like everyone really cared about my project. I highly recommend Graniterra!

Awesome pot roast omelet with xtra sharp cheddar!!!!
Will come back. Nice staff.
Everything looked good on menu. Lots to try

After 4 long distance moves in as many years U was facing a local move from NJ to Philadelphia. I found Old City Movers on Yelp and based on the positive reviews contacted them via email. Their response was rapid and after a brief description of our needs, their quote was very fair. I was concerned that their policy was not to require any deposit to reserve our date/time, wondering how they could send a truck and moving team as well as pay for a city "no parking permit" without even asking for a credit card!  Nevertheless our subsequent text conversations somehow reassured me. Indeed the Old City truck and a team of two polite, efficient, and very courteous men arrived exactly at the time specified. My move could not have been any smoother or trouble-free!

Rick is the man.  I was slow to act on my wife's birthday.  Rick knew of a necklace she had been coveting for a while and was able to secure it and help me with a last minute save.  

Thanks Rick!

His Place is one of the best soul food restaurants I've ever eaten at. The first challenge is picking from all of their food options, I've had their smoked meatloaf, the catfish, the fried chicken, and it all was amazing. The second most difficult thing will be finishing all the food that you ordered because it all looks and sounds so good.

While the chicken limo was fun and hilarious, our driver was not. Instead of rolling up the divider, he decided to join in on our conversations and interjected his opinions. Instead of rolling up the divider, the driver insisted that our music was too loud and hurt his ears.... he literally could have just rolled up the divider but he really wanted to be involved in our convos. We are friendly but the lack of privacy made the night awkward...

Wow so amazing. I had the donut ice sandwich thing and . They said the donut would be warm but it wasn't. No worries though 8 second in my microwave and BOOM warm DELICIOUS donut with even better ice. I got 2 different flavors cause I couldn't decide. Definitely check it out

Queen's was ok.  Nancy the Waitress was very good.  The food was ok.  The place was not at all busy but it seemed to take forever for the food to arrive.  The long wait and rather boring atmosphere seemed to lend time to other things such as the powerful gusts of frigid air blowing out of the AC ceiling units.  This added to much discomfort of the post sun sunburn chills.  The leftover pizza seemed to taste much better the next day when heated up.  All in all a good place but nothing very special.

I rarely leave bad reviews but both my toes and my dip nails were awful.  I have really short nails so I get that it's more difficult to do them... but at least you can make them the same shape.. I have round and square and sideways filed nails.  At first Van also put 4 coats of dip on them.. they were so fat that they looked ridiculous.. then he filed them down for me but never shaped them... when manicurists get used to putting on tips.. nails are uniform. Another manicurist did my toes and the job was not much better.. none of my toes are filed even.. they look like crap!
Overpriced and not that good. Much better options all over in this area.  We just ordered a large cheese for pickup.  It was $16 and didn't really have much cheese.

Domino's you have really disappointed me this time.  You guys are falling way behind the competition. I ordered an extra large pizza and what came was barely a medium size pie.  If that's not bad enough the pizza was not that great.  From a 1-10 I would grade it a 4.  Not complaining about this store in particular but I am not happy with dominos products these days.

Indoor/outdoor bar setup.  A few tables and ample bar space made for a relaxing early evening drink.  As the night progressed the music changed and the crowd picked up.  Plenty to look at and distract you from your woes.  Drink, drink, and be happy

Still like going here for breakfast although we've switched up our breakfast. I order wheat toast, tomatoes and sausage patties which is just enough for a light tasty start of the day. My guy orders eggs softly scrambled, crispy homefries, bacon and wheat toast.  The Bloody Mary and coffee are always good. We like getting there 8-ish and sitting at the bar. Always good to see Nizza, bartender, and the other early regulars. Everyone is friendly.

The place has been updated in a beachy vibe. The menu is new but is still reasonably priced. The menu is accessed on line with your phone.

There is inside seating, bar seating and tables available outside. The parking lot has been resurfaced so you go in one side and out the other. Better that way.

Just passing through from LA to Solvang and saw the good reviews on yelp so decided to stop for an açaí / smoothie bowl. Definitely one of the best I've had, down to the last bite. Ordered the Green Bowl.
Parking is an absolute mess.  Tried to go here twice now with no success.  More than 12-13 spots would help.

This Fred Meyer is pretty reliable. It's a quick stop for the basics. Nothing too obscure but also not low quality items that you might find elsewhere. The truly organic options are limited, so plan your stops around that. The check out lines are generally quick moving and professional.

I am feeling just lucy goosey after my little shopping spree today....I enjoy this place so much.....if I only had more room and money I would have left with even more.  Today I got myself two very unique iron wall sconces---a nice sized mirror to use with a vanity for now---a lovely little three tiered wicker rack with some metal accents (think pier one) a I got goosed shirt as a present and two pair of local artisian earrings for gifts all for right around 100 plus tax....I love that!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

They had some nice sofas for good prices today and also some nice tuscan wine decor that just came in---

They always help me to my car with my treasures also and are very friendly.....

I would be in so much trouble if this were in my neighborhood....

ONLINE BOOKING!!! Before you go, don't forget to reserve your spot. The guys here were very helpful. At the beginning we kinda had a rough patch, but then at the end it was great. 

On the other hand, Anthony made my family and I have an amazing day. He truly has his heart, and great customer services out in the waters. He made us feel like we were at home. He was filled with joy and happiness; great vibes. 

Make sure to do the banana boat and jet ski, really fun and adrenaline. Super fun! Thank you guys :)

I had a wonderful experience at Peruzzi Nissan...all thanks to Dave Jones! Dave was extremely patient and attentive. He made himself available to answer all of my questions, worked diligently to get me the best rates on a car and even took the time to show me the many different features of my new Rouge.  He single handily made my car buying experience enjoyable and efficient! If you want the best, non pushy, car buying experience, I highly recommend you to see Dave Jones at Nissan Peruzzi!! 
Thank you Dave for everything! I truly appreciate you and will ABSOLUTELY be purchasing my future vehicles from you!

My "Long" awaited visit to Longwood Gardens is finally complete! Over the years, family and friends keep telling me - "Stevie, you have to get to Longwood Gardens with the family and kids, everyone will love it!" I can now corroborate that statement, as I just recently visited the Gardens on an absolutely frigid December evening. I haven't yet had the blessed privilege to visit this garden oasis in the warm weather, but you can sure bet that I'll be back in the Fall or Spring to explore the 1,000+ acres of natural beauty! I personally wanted to experience the extensive Christmas lights, ostentatious decorations, warm chocolate drinks (even with some rum for the grown-ups!), holiday tunes, and many other variables that Longwood adds to make this the perfect happy, heady, hearty, high quality, high caliber, heavenward, hermetic holiday horticultural experience!

This is where I get my hair cut.  This is what I like about George's:

1. It's close to my home. 
2. No appointment is required.  
3. The price is right - $16.  

Paradoxically, the less hair I have, the more often I need to have it cut (and I have a lot less than when I started going here about 10 years ago).  

So that makes proximity, spontaneity, and economy are of paramount importance to me.  George's meets or exceeds these needs.

Great place for brunch. Excellent service, very fast and great classic breakfast. Big mimosas and super friendly staff make this place especially amazing. So glad we stumbled upon the Seahorse for brunch today!

I was going to do 3 stars because I didn't really enjoy my food and the food felt very heavy after, but I realized I didn't like it because I'm more plant based and don't care for the fake meat. If you're bringing a meat eater or you're vegan and miss the taste or texture of meat, you'll probably enjoy this. -1 star because of the tight seating and stuffyness, I felt like I couldn't breath at times

We've come here twice so far, and the staff has been attentive, the ambiance has been warm and friendly, and the food has been great. We most heartily recommend the Thief roll, which is raw ahi tuna, wakame, soy & wasabi crema, with a strange but delicious crust.
Good wine, good food, good neighborhood restaurant.
The menu items are great and the specials set it apart from anywhere else. Great BBQ, but the southern hot chicken is still the go to

One of the best brunches I've had lately,  and I'm an aggressive bruncher. I definitely left Buckminster's fuller.

We basically had the place to ourselves at 11:30am on a Saturday and service was great. John, our server took good care of us and the bartender checked in to make sure my friend's Yellow Mary (a play on a Bloody, with yellow tomatoes) was ok when she was drinking it slowly. They serve Rival Bros coffee and have a few interesting looking brunch cocktails.

The vibe (and clientele and staff for that matter) is hipster enough that the food is really good (but a bit pricey) but not too much to make you feel uncomfortable. There are a few tables in the front,  booth and tables in the back and a long bar with stools in the middle.

BRUNCH ITEMS YOU MUST TRY:
-Congee: a rice porridge with a soft boiled egg and seriously awesome flavors. I love congee but haven't seen it outside of Chinatown and my family reunions,  and was very impressed they pulled it off.
-Bologna sandwich: the cranberry mostarda perfectly smothers the baloney,  cheese and house made bread, and once that yolk splits into that you're going to want (need) to lick your plate.
-White Bean Mole with Eggs and Sour Cream: kind of a play on shakshoukka and extremely delicious.  Another plate licker.
-Biscuit- we got two, to facilitate sauce sopping. No regrets.

Don't rely on the online menu,  it varies slightly from the actual menu, which can be alarming if you're the type of control freak that needs to have a good sense of what she's going to order before she walks into a place. 

Will definitely have to come back for dinner/drinks! Highly recommend for brunch.

Cute general store with local items. I was loving my lunch there, until I saw a rat running across the ceiling piping. When I told the girl behind the kitchen counter, she shrugged it off. Definitely makes me question for prep quality. I liked my food a lot, but hesitant to go back because of this experience.

A friend was getting surgery here so we decided to go pay them a visit. Parking and directions weren't bad at all but going inside the hospital was a nightmare. We saw people coming out of the visitor entrance by the visitor parking lot but we weren't able to go in, not sure why? So we went around to the emergency entrance where they told us to check in. The communication and directions were horrendous. The emergency check in was the wrong place we needed to be and we had to wait with sick people for 15 minutes before they told us at the counter. They re-directed us to the other side of the building for visitors and we had to walk all the way over there. It would have definitely be helpful if they had signs to direct you where you needed to go. I've had nothing but bad experiences with St. Joseph hospitals so I'm not surprised but it is such an inconvenience.
The food was delicious, the atmosphere was wonderful and if you have the pleasure of sitting at Jo's table you will enjoy it even more! Hats off to Chuy's at Cool Springs!

Always a big fan of this place. The ramen is excellent and severed the traditional way of piping hot. You also can't take it to go so be sure to come hungry! The crispy brussels were the highlight of the meal! They were so perfectly seasoned and cooked. The service could have been better.

Super nice place for a tasting! Great views and it wasn't crowded at all when we were there. The person pouring was great - would recommend and pour wines from both reserve and regular tasting menu. After the tasting we each enjoyed a glass of wine looking over the water and beach. Great time

Lynne is AMAZING! She helped me and my fiancé find our first home here in Reno, NV. She was great at being intuitive into what we liked and disliked about homes that we saw, payed extra attention to details about what we were looking for and really searched the market to find us the perfect homes to look at. She was great at communicating whenever we had questions and I couldn't have felt more comfortable asking her anything about the home buying process. Her outgoing and positive attitude made looking at home stress free and a really enjoyable experience for us. If you are looking for someone who really cares about the Reno/Sparks community and wants to help you find the perfect home for your needs i wouldn't go to anyone else besides Lynne.

I had made an online reservation for a vehicle without additional insurance. The young man taking care of me asked me about purchasing additional insurance, which I declined. However, this s.o.b. tacked on the ticket an additional $100. When I questioned it, he stated it was security. That was just bs. Upon my return, instead of being just $100 it turned to $200. The manager refused to deal with it and just ignored what I had stated. When I talked to another employee who deals with the vehicles outside, he told me this employee has had complaints for tacking on additional charges and asked me to call the 1-800 number, which I did and had the charges reversed.

Just walked out. Service was terrible. Twenty minutes after being seated we had to ask our hostess to get our waiter. After ordering, we never saw our waiter again. After 50 minutes without seeing our waiter, food, or refills, we left. No excuse. The place was not busy in the least.

Bamboo is our favorite comfort food place! I love their egg foo young (chicken), sweet and sour chicken, egg rolls, fried rice and my hubby loves their beef and broccoli dish with an appetizer (or dinner ruiner if your at our house ) of fried shrimp. It's all delicious, so if you like Chinese food, it's the place you should go.

YUM!!!! Always get the Lox, but went outside my comfort zone  and got the chicken artichoke and was delighted. Good food, good service, clean and laid back. My only feedback is that the more veteran employees could be nicer to the newbies. Kinda awkward waiting for my food listening to someone berate another employee. No matter how veteran you are or what your job title is, don't embarrass other co-workers in front of bystanders. Other then that

Fabulous food here. Planned to come during our vacation and it didn't disappoint. The biscuits are light and fluffy - absolutely delicious. I asked if I could order from the kids menu because I wanted smaller amounts of food to avoid a food coma. No problem there. Coffee is yummy and the vibe is just fun. Came on a weekday so there was no wait.

Nice salon but the service is not the best! Before Kim left, my nails would last a good 2-3 weeks. 

I'm one week in today with chipped nails and the price is two much not to expect better.

Consistently incompetent. It is horrible that they have little or no competition because they act like they have a corner on the market. On the pursuit of a nursing license in the US from a foreign country, they have exceedingly disappointed in every way possible. However, I will say the "customer service" contacts are consistent. Consistently you will wait a long-time in the queue, consistently be treated like an inferior person, and even screw up your application. Our latest problem is where they actually mistyped the university name they received the transcripts from and then stated we made a mistake on our application and we need to submit the change in writing. The correct university name is clearly listed on their own letterhead from the initial application and there is no way we could have actually requested the transcripts using THEIR form without it being correct. They are an embarrassment to society.

I'm a huge fan of Ruby River Steakhouse, never In 4 years I have left this place dissatisfied.
Ruby is a great example of a steakhouse where you don't have to pay an absurd amount of money for your meal. Prices are reasonable and portions are generous. I usually walk out with a food comma. 

RESTAURANT:
This amazing restaurant is located on Virginia Street, across from the Peppermill Hotel. The decoration and the inside suggest a cowboy/rodeo style. It's a little more casual than other steakhouses but the quality of the food can easily compete with the most expensive steakhouses in town. Lots of rodeo pictures on the walls, cowboy boots and buckets with peanuts are part of the decoration. 
Good size restaurant, with option of seating at the bar, table, booth and private room (upon request). 

FOOD: 
The food at Ruby River is just amazing!! Everything here is delicious! You can always judge a place by the fresh baked bread they bring, Ruby's SOURDOUGH is just incredible. They have a big selection of appetizers but my fave are the "coconut shrimps."
Here are some of my favorite choices for entrees: 
-Bacon Wrapped Filet mignon! I like it medium rare, juicy and flavorful. Sooo tender! 
-Prime Rib, cooked to perfection. 
-12 oz. Ribeye, marbled steak with incredible flavor. 
-Steak Oscar, great option if you want to try something different. The topping with crab is delicious! 
-Parmesan Halibut, when I'm not in the mood for steak, I'm in the mood for seafood. This halibut it's super filling and tastes great! 

The entrees come with two sides, so I normally get a salad, house salad with blue cheese! Omg! I crave this salad. They put eggs, lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, onions and croutons in the salad! The plate is chilled so the salad feels super fresh! 

For my second side, I normally get a jacketed baked potato, which is served with sour cream, green onion, butter and bacon! Yummm!
Other times I feel more like a yam, mmmm they give you cinnamon butter to put on it! Delish!! 
They also have healthier sides, like broccoli, asparagus, and sauté mushrooms. 

It is impossible (al least for me) to come here and not have a "RUBY-RITA," similar to a margarita but stronger and with some sweet juice, cheers! 

SERVICE: 
I can't write a review about Ruby's without applauding the excellent service here! The front staff, bartenders, waiters, cooks and manager. They all work together to give you the best experience!

I've had JOSH, several times and he is always on point. He does such a great job managing the big crows that suddenly arrive here. He is fast and always check on us. 

You know a business is doing the things right when the manager always takes time to visit every table and make sure that everything is good. I love that! It makes me feel they care about customers. 

5 Stars Restaurant on Salmita's List :-) 
5/5 On Food
5/5 Service 
5/5 Ambiance

I'm originally from Atlanta, GA and have eaten at Longhorn Steakhouses for years.  I was very excited when I found out that one was opening in Tucson even though it is 45 minutes from where I live.

So today I decided to try it out.  I went by myself for a late lunch (around 1:30).  Walked in a was immediately greeted but had to wait a few minutes because I didn't want to sit at the bar.  My server, Amanda, came over and asked for my drink order and I ordered water with extra lemon.  She brought it back shortly but with only one lemon slice and quickly disappeared before I could say anything.  A little later she came back for my food order and when I gave that to her I again asked for extra lemons. 

Then I went to the restroom and when I came back by table had been cleared - no water or silverware and wiped down.  Someone who worked there was near by and I told her that my table had been cleared.  She apologized and told me that my water was "right here".  Right here was a large, round table full of dirty glasses and silverware.  I just looked at her and she said "I'll go get you a new water".  While she was gone to get the water a hostess came up and asked me "did someone seat you here?".  I explained what happened and she said she just wanted to be sure since I didn't have a menu. 

When Amanda brought my salad to me I had to remind her (3rd time) that I was still waiting for my extra lemons.  Finally got them. 

While I was waiting for my food 3 people were seated in the booth next to me.  They had to wait for a server and when one finally came over to them they had questions.  The customers wanted to know about a sauce (not sure which one), the waiter starts to tell them what was in a sandwich.  When the customer said he wanted to know what was in the sauce and not the sandwich the waiter gave him a look of disgust and said "I'm telling you all I know",  looked at them again and then said "I'll be back to take your order" and walked off.  Amanda went to them sometime later and said that she would be their server because he became busy.  One of the other diners stated that she thought they might have scared him off and that he was snarly with them.  Amanda looked at them and said "you're not going to run me off, are you?"  I didn't think the either server was very nice to those diners.

Back to me, once my food arrived the fries were limp, very brown and lukewarm.  Flo's filet came out fine.  I ate my food and I think Amanda only checked back with me once.  Someone else (manager maybe, she didn't identify herself) came to clear the table and asked if I wanted a box for the fires that weren't good.  I told her no and that they weren't very good.  She apologized and asked if I'd like another side.  Hello - I'm through with my meal, offer me a desert or something but not another side.  Received the check shortly afterwards, paid and left.  BTW, the table with the dirty glasses and silverware that was next to me was dirty the whole time I was there.  There were two couples waiting to be seated even though there were empty tables.  I may give this Longhorn another try but more likely than not I'll go to Lil' Abners.

The servers are quick and friendly. I haven't gotten any food that I wasn't happy with and the price is comparable to other similar restaurants in the area. My only complaint is the cocktails felt a little over priced. I will definitely be back here, but maybe during happy hour!

These guys are awesome! Always very helpful, fair priced and when needed service when truck was broke down they were right there -brought the parts and took care of everything. I have had this store service my brakes, tires, batteries And would never go anywhere else.
Great meats and great service at competitive prices.  About $10/lb below Whole Foods and the boise coop.

Super helpful people working here - I brought a purse that I had purchased from this store less than a year ago to see if they could do anything about a broken zipper. I expected them to say I was out of luck but instead, they offered to send it to their leather repair service provider. The woman helping me also called another store to see if they had leather repair service, as I'm moving away from Philadelphia soon. When that store didn't, she offered to take the purse to see what they could do and to ship it back to me either way. They went above and beyond my expectations!

We were up the Street looking at a long wait time for a breakfast place and a gentleman asked us what we were looking for and if we needed help. He said he worked at the Marsh House in the Nashville Thompson Hotel and recommended we try it. His name is Thomas Booker and he was so right! Very hospitable of him to help and believe in his employer. Biscuits and gravy, quiche, service, atmosphere were all amazing!

Parkshore Grill is my go to spot for entertaining clients in St Pete.  I always know what I am going to get in terms of food quality, service, and the little details are not missed.

For lunch time they have a great "picnic" menu that includes a salad, entree and dessert and is very reasonably priced.  They have good options for all the food items.

While I agree with some other posts that their prices are on the high side it is keeping the place at a certain level which is why I find it appealing for entertaining my clients.

They have a great martini list - I like the the Parkshore with blue cheese stuffed olives . . . it says very dry, but I get it pretty dirty.  They also have a nice wine list.

At dinner they always have some yummy specials and a tasting menu with two apps and an entree.  The menu is mostly beef and fish.  They have some "composed" dishes which includes sides, but most are ala carte with sides that serve 3-4 as add-on's.  I can't pick a favorite side because I LOVE them more than the entree's themselves.  Is my favorite the scalloped potatoes with blue cheese and caramelized onion or is it the onion rings or the mac & cheese or the mushrooms, maybe it is the asparagus . . . they all win in my book.

Last night Laura was our waitress and she has been there since before they opened.  She is knowledgeable and was on top of everything.  Ken is also wonderful, but he mostly works the lunch shift.

When I make my reservations I always let the person know that I will be entertaining clients, ask for a good table and experienced server.  I usually sit inside, but they have outdoor seating too which provides good people watching.  (TV at the bar only)

I was so excited that the Rack was coming to Center City- now I can get nice designer clothes at a discount! YES! 
I wouldn't get your hopes up when you come here. Your experience will be way more enjoyable if you come in with the mindset that you aren't planning on finding anything; when you do, it'll be like Christmas morning.

The store is gigantic, you would think that you could find something on one of the three floors. It needs to be organized a little better. Clothes and shoes were strewn everywhere. I felt like a tornado had just ripped through the store.
This is a great place to go if you are looking for a gift for someone.

Been here a few times and again tonight. The wait was long, as expected on a Friday night. The service was fast and very friendly. I love the Jack Daniels menu and the sauce is phenomenal! My wife likes the salads and sammiches. They do have a smoking section which doesn't really bother me even though I'm a non smoker I grew up with friends and family who do. Other than that great food and excellent staff!

Best crawfish ever.  I didn't even care that it wasn't steaming hot, I would have killed a few more lbs if I could.  Can't say the same for the bbq shrimp boat... that was a crazy salty/greasy mess... but the crawfish... my heart...  perfectly cooked and seasoned.  Really good spices.
Don't expect the deals if your sitting with family, away from the bar. Food is alright and priced about the same for the area.

This place is a great place tk eat if you do not mind spending a decent amount of cash. A regular hotdog with fries costs about $4 and some change but if you want any topping like chilli it costs $3 extra. The hotdog was delicious and the bun wwas good too! Fries were a  little cold and soggy unfortunately. I had ordered the mac and cheese which was 6.99 and i had received a cup of basically buttered noodles. It had no flavor and was not topped with the garlic topping :(

Wow. After reading other reviews here, I am now a bit concerned about my past experiences with this place. They seem to care very much, and they certainly give you the red carpet treatment. I would have to qualify that, though after reading other comments. It may be that we were able to pay the exorbitant costs. I have health insurance, so I pay little for tests and visits, but do know how much they cost. That said, I originally took my dog in for treatment because he would not eat. I was then told his teeth were showing major plaque and gum disease. I did see those teeth, and can affirm that it was pretty bad. It ended up costing me about $3000 for his treatment.

We had another dog, and she started having seizures, and was panting a lot and drinking a lot. Our regular vet did not catch anything. We took her in, and they did a huge number of tests on her, and came out with congestive heart failure AND heart worms, of which either alone would be exorbitant, but together would be horrible for her as well as our finances. We decided to go home and think about it, after getting the text results via email, and decided to not go thru any treatment. 

Now, this past week, we took our 13 year old because all of a sudden, she was panting heavily and her gums turned blue.  Off we go, to what I thought was 'the Mayo Clinic' for pets. Anyway, they gave her a bunch of tests and so forth, put her on oxygen and a number of drugs, and 2 days later, they tell us there really isn't anything can be done. In all instances they are very quiet and respectful, and so forth, but that whole event was almost $5000. 

With TWO dogs getting congestive heart failure, and not a lot of hope, I am beginning to wonder if this is maybe the MO for their business model. I don't think I'll go back.

Love Korean food and wanted to try this place for a while. A tip, grab some beer before going in, its BYOB. 
Food was good for quick service Korean and I would go again since I haven't been able to find spicy pork to my liking in CC yet.
The downfall for me was the staff. The young lady at the counter seemed as if she couldn't be bothered to take and order and when you started with your order seemed impatient. Almost to the point of looking at you like you are wasting her time.  I work in food service and wasting someone time is not anything I strive for. I also thoroughly enjoy Korean food and know what dishes I want before I even approach the counter.

They take credit cards but their is a $10 minimum. 
Maybe if I called in an order I can avoid the surly counter person who clearly doesn't want anyone there?
I can't believe I just had a bowl of salty pho here. I even added a full cup of hot water in it, it's still salty. Service was okay.

I went there today after being in pain for two weeks first of all the staff very kind and professional they make feel comfortable: Dr Paskill very nice as well I would recommend anyone to visit the Woodbury heights office and I would go there again without hesitation thank you all for making me feel normal again the pain of any tooth makes you feel different have a happy holidays

My wife and I have been thinking about getting our windows replaced. So when we were stopped in BJ's I actually listened to the guy to get an estimate. 
Of course, they try to pre-qualify you on the spot, but pretend that it's not a high pressure sale. Then the guy shows up at your house.

This kid comes in and starts his pitch. I mean, he's pulling all the stops, rebuttals, fear selling, props... I tell the guy that I am a "Sales Manager" and train sales people. Also, that he's doing well for a new sales person and he can work some of his pitch on me... 4 freaking hours later. 
I told him, if he were to sell to one of my clients for this long, he would've been stabbed in the face long ago. 

So finally, he gives me a price for $37k for 21 windows, a door and a bowfront.

I told him, I'm not ready and I don't 1 stop.

He said his price is for today only. I said, when I'm ready, not only will you do better on your price, you'll give up the farm to get my business. People need to learn to play hardball. 

I loved how he told me that all the other vendors would offer me sub-par products. I told them that I'll make sure that I get another vendor that buys the same exact windows he buys. 

Noob sales people are my favorite lunch.

Again, I have to say that it's odd when I see very negative reviews mixed in with good reviews. Either the staff has changed, or they took note of the negative reviews and changed their behavior...which is a good thing, because that's what reviews are there for, and that keeps people on their toes. My experience was excellent. I set up an appointment online, drove on over, was greeted by polite, friendly staff...and the nurse who drew my blood was very friendly, keeping me distracted from being stabbed by big needles, which I hate. I even remember the conversation because I was fucking starving after fasting for over 12 hours for a routine bloodwork thing, and she asked me where I was gonna eat lunch. I said  I wanted chicken masala. That led to a conversation about her experience at Taste of India, and based on her raves about that place, I'm gonna hit it up and try it soon.  I was out of there quickly and efficiently, and if I need bloodwork again, you can bet I'm gonna come here.

Very interesting hotel absolutely loved the decor and unique room service options and very pet friendly but we were missing items after housekeeping paid a visit and nothing was done about it when we mentioned it to the front desk; kind of sad

We met friends there for dinner last Friday evening.  It was not a good experience.  Our waiter was not very good and the food was really so so.  We ordered a shrimp tempura appetizer and it sure did not look like any shrimp tempura I have ever eaten.  We attempted to eat one of the small, four shrimp and they were super salty.  We sent the shrimp back and opted for a spring roll.  That was tiny too and just OK.  The main courses were nothing to comment on.  They were just passable.  I asked the waiter for some of the little spice jars with various peppers and sauces and he brought several that were just about empty.  I had to flag him down and ask for jars with actual content.  He came back with hardly anything.  The food and service did not come anywhere close to the price.  There are too many other excellent Thai options with better food, service and prices.

They have a nice coffee shop atmosphere.  Lot of choices for breakfast or lunch at reasonable prices.

Service was prompt and courteous.  

Tried the nutella and banana crepe, nothing fancy or special about it but my daughter love it.

Found out this place used to be called Penn's table.

I've walked by Lolita probably a good 30 times in the past, and each time it's packed so they must be doing something good. Friends suggested we try it out, and we were not disappointed!

We went for the Dining out for Life Menu (3 courses). 


DRINKS:
They make pitchers of margaritas for 10 bucks, and you bring your own tequila. This is actually a great idea, but make sure if you're meeting a party you only bring one bottle. We ended up with three.. ;) You can BYO Wine/Booze too, but we stuck with Margaritas and Wine. 

(If you're from out of town or not familiar with the city, there is a Wine and Spirits shop on Chestnut between 12th and 13th where you can pick up your refreshments).


FOOD:
Since it was the prefixed menu, we didn't have a lot of choice, but all o our options looked great!

Appetizer: Mexican Chopped Salad- AMAZING. I couldn't keep my fork down! The combination of the roasted beats, jicama, chickpeas, and goats-milk cheese with the mixed greens tossed in a herb-lime dressing was terrific.

Entree: Yucatan-style Chicken Breast- DELICIOUS. Served stacked, the fried plantains and black beans were on the bottom, topped by the chicken breast, which was adorned by a dollop of home-made guacamole and topped with a crispy plantain. I enjoyed the apple-cider bbq sauce, but combined with the fried plantains, I could see how some wouldn't like the sweet flavors. The bbq did have a savory finish to it though. The chicken breast was surprisingly substantial and juicy (unlike the thin dried pucks you sometimes get). 

Dessert: Pecan Cheesecake- HEAVENLY. Seriously, the portion was just right after the amount of food and alcohol that was consumed. One would think it would be overly rich and sweet (cheesecake/pecans), but it had a really good balance of both, with out making you want to feel like you're going into a coma afterward. 


DECOR/INTERIOR:
The restaurant is a tad bit small, but that's to be expected for it's location. Seating parties of 6+ is a bit difficult as they have to combine tables. I wouldn't even attempt to seat a party of more than 8 people. 

The acoustics in the restaurant are terrible. It has high ceilings, brick walls, and an open kitchen with nothing to absorb the noise. If you have the option to sit outside, I recommend it. The occasional loud vehicle/bus is much better than having to scream across a table to have a conversation. Unfortunately this is why the restaurant did not receive a 5* review for me. 


FINAL THOUGHTS:
Great food, great drinks, and I like the quaint atmosphere. Try to sit outside (weather permitting), as the acoustics are horrific inside, and the space feels cramped when a lot of large parties are being sat all at the same time.

The BEST elotè (grilled corn) I have ever had. Along with great tasting arepas and the specials -- easily a favorite! Atmosphere is chill and the staff is very friendly, laid back and helpful. I would eat here every day if I could.

This is the place you're looking for. You know a place is good when you dont wanna leave. Heck, i sat down for a few minutes waiting on the line to die down and was sure id have no problem staying if they asked me for dinner. There are some very nice people working here who are friendly and provide great customer service. These are good people, the property is cute and they have just as good a selection as anywhere else for the same or cheaper prices so why not support a local place that has a good thing going?? I came here not long ago after going to five other places local to me. Unfortunately that was at the end of the day so i felt like i had to wade through miles of crap just to get to the gold at the end of the rainbow...(yes the rainbow does actually end here). Its my new happy place and now it can be yours too. I have now saved you from wasting you're entire day driving around looking at beat up plants or not finding what you want (the nice young lady that runs this place even seemed interested in finding something i was interested in that she didnt have at least she expressed interest which is more than i can say for most other places) . Between this and another local place, i finally have my plants covered (no pun) and know what greenhouses i can count on.
I am in no way affiliated with Courts Yard & Greenhouse in any way. Just a guy who knows good people, good plants and a good thing when i see it.

We love this place. The food is always delicious, and the staff are very friendly and helpful. Ever since our first visit several months ago, we visit just about once per week- sometimes more! The beef pho is my personal favorite, but the Hiu Tiu (not sure if that's spelled correctly, but it's their vegetable and tofu soup) is a close second. Their mint lemonade is super yummy, as is their Taro boba tea and Thai tea. I used to have to drive 45 minutes to get good pho, so I'm happy this is here! The only thing I'd change would be to have more ambient music and dimmer lights in the evening.

DO not rent from this car rental. If I could give 0 stars I would. A 4 day rental of a midsize sedan(Nissan Altima) which started out being 19.00 day, turned into a $350.00 rental. I'm so furious. I'm waiting for a response from a manager who they claimed was not available  to return a call. Very poor customer service, misleading marketing, crappy car, charged me 38$ for a full tank of gas on return. And Robert, the return Intaker could have been more convincing that he didn't give a f$$$!
Go somewhere else!
No where on their website does it say they don't take credit cards. I wish I had checked here first. What century do we live in that they don't take credit cards?

When I lived back in Sacramento, the BWW in Citrus Heights was THE PLACE for wings, beer, and game night. I had a ton of friends that worked there, and even more that frequented the restaurant on a weekly- nay, daily- basis. So, after moving out to Reno, a coworker of mine (also new-ish to the area) and I decided to drop by the new site in Sparks' Legends Outlet to see what all the hype was about.

I'm sorry to say that, based on my first (and last) visit to this chain, I believe the hype to be totally unfounded.

After being seated by our host, my coworker and I proceeded to browse our menus and pick something like looked at least slightly appetizing. The lack of bacon was already off-putting, but seeing our 5-minute browse turn into a 10-Facebook tryst, into a 15-minute awkward search for our waitress, into a 20-minute glaring match with our host... Well. Needless to say, we lost our appetite.

The manager came out and apologized profusely for the terrible service, then got our food and drinks out in record time. That was nice, even if nothing was discounted.

But here's the kicker: Our waitress- who until then had been seen in passing on her phone while walking into the bathroom- had the audacity to bring us our check with a bright green "Thank You!" and a smiley face scribbled across the bottom.

Seriously, Cassie? Get your ish together, girl. That was just embarrassing.

But not as embarrassing as being watched by the other patrons as you got chewed out by your manger in the middle of the dining room. That looked like it sucked.

Big fan! 

I brunched here this weekend and was very pleasantly surprised. Lemme dig into this:

Vibe: sophisticated cocktail lounge. Lots of dark wood, high ceilings, huge windows and fiddle leaf plants. Always love a good fiddle leaf because nature. Dark brown leather, tall wine racks ala beauty and the beast library - sans books for booze. 

Food: 
First of all I picked this place for $17 bottomless mimosas. Being the basic b**ch that I am, you know I love to get schmammered on a Sunday off the bubbles. We tackled three and I feel good about their ratio. 

The food was legit. We got the avocado toast (again I told you I am basic with food - but no I don't have a "Live. Laugh. Love" sign in my house) and it was SO GOOD. It was on a herb focaccia, with a spicy aioli and radishes and egg. 10/10 would eat again. 

Main meal... I know I will be judged by most. But Louie's accommodated my picky self. I got the veggie Benedict, sans egg but add bacon. If you are reading this then yes, I got a veggie item and added bacon. And then made matters worse by ordering without eggs but keeping the hollandaise which is just whipped egg yolks. Any restaurant that can manage that with a smile - I can totally appreciate. And lemme tell you - it was bomb! Veggies where spinach and a piece de Gallo. The muffin was wonderfully toasted. Oh and those hash potatoes with rosemary and Parmesan I am all about. 

Service - ask for my dude Connor. He was personable, fun and kept us well hydrated through three crafts of mimosas. 

Great addition to the midtown area!

OH and pro-parking tip - park on Music Square West and then walk there and save yourself $5 on parking
i luv you dominos always order from here and always pleased with customer service and product!

This has been the best Panera I have visited.
San Jose, Gilroy, nor Merced can compare.
The clerk was attentive and helpful. Surprisingly, they didn't mess up my order. However, they never asked me if I wanted to order anything to drink after ordering for my toddler and myself.  So just got stuck drinking water to avoid the lunch line.
They brought out the food to our table and helped me clean up after we were done, with no rush.
Bonus: they sliced the apple, making it easier for my 2 year old to eat. 
Definitely will go again!!

Solid three stars.  Got a very good pour-over, and then decided for the vacuum pot experience, right?  And then the debating of technique started up among the working and not-working-because-its-my-day-off peeps present.  I've had vacuum pot coffee in various places around the US that offer it, and this method was... unique?  Intelligentsia has a couple of videos on the subject guys.  Just sayin'.

Still, the fresh roast coffee and warmth of the place and earnestness of the staff make up for most shortcomings and I'll gladly return to buy beans and see what's coming up.

This used to be one of my favorite places to eat. However twice now when I have gone in and asked for items I have been told they could not accommodate my dietary needs. I have not asked for anything unreasonable, I have asked for either a child's portion or to have an item split in half in the kitchen & 1 part boxed "togo". I was denied not just today but in a previous visit as well; I was told I could get a to-go box and box up uneaten portions myself if I wanted. It wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't for the attitudes that accompanied their responses. After 5 years of frequenting this location I will probably not be returning.

Excellent customer service! Very sweet. Great prices! Store so clean and cute. Highly recommend. They were able to fix a MAJORLY botched job from Pottery Barn (our family Christmas stockings).  Really appreciate their professionalism!

The staff doesn't smile very much. The room is not a good floor plan for two as there is no way to use the sink area without waking everyone else.
There is nothing around the hotel so make sure you have a car if you want to get anywhere

805 catered my rehearsal dinner, and it was fantastic. 

The food itself was out of this world. Great tacos, great sides, great salsa. Quantity was great, with more than enough for everyone. 

Gio was also great at helping to organize the event. He set up his taco truck at the event space, and was up and running with minimal help from anyone else. I also had a number of guests from England, who were unfamiliar with tacos as a whole. Gio and his team were great at walking them through what was on offer.

Great food, great service, great time. I would definitely recommend Gio and 805 Street Bites for their tacos and for any event.

Great Restaurant! 

I want to say we have lived in Reno for 15 years and never have tried this restaurant and now we are kicking  ourselves.  The waiters and waitresses are great and really made my daughter's birthday dinner a hit! 
The food was great and the suggested menu items from the waitress were really good all of them! They gave my daughter a complimentary piece of coconut cream cake with coconut gelato that put the cake I made her to shame.  It was a large piece so we could all share and then came the hot towels.  Just a very nice touch!
Amazing pizza, great drinks. A little small space-wise. Reservations are a great idea.

Very friendly staff

Desk clerk sent me code for $15 off uber

Sports bar. Good food. Had few drinks got outta there for price of one steak at ruth chris.

Room very clean, had view of river. 
18th floor has viewing deck of arch. Even though its march it was cold and snowing so didnt get to enjoy this feature much.

I understand that during quarantine they can only take emergency cases, but I gave them a call because I have been having BAD/PAINFUL jaw issues which ended in my front teeth getting chipped. The woman on the phone that works their front desk was trying to downplay the pain I was in and tried to sell me $100 video conference appointments... what is that going to do to help my pain? How are you going to know what's wrong over a video conference? She proceeded to rudely tell me that my instance is NOT an emergency even though I said I can't sleep and I can barely eat.....  never going here EVER.

This has got to be one of my all time favorite restaurants... had a fantastic birthday dinner here... and I was very, very grateful that no one did the "tell the waiter it is my birthday thing so I can be embarrassed with something on fire in front of me for dessert!!"

Great food, our dinners were flawless, of course... for me, the rabbit tenderloin appetizer sticks out.  It was cool to try something different which was so tender with a great creole mustard sauce.  The fried green tomatoes were fantastic too... I had the soft shell crab with crawfish on pasta - fantastic and visually appealing.  The crab was delicious!

Also, had my first Sazerac here and loved it!

This place is our new favorite sports bar. Came here on a college football Saturday and while completely packed, service was surprisingly fast. And by surprisingly I mean about 10 seconds after they put your order in the iPad, someone is there with your drink/food.. it's almost weird. Speaking of food, for bar food this is surprisingly creative and tasty. 4 Greek inspired dishes on the menu? Ok- I'll buy in. Bloody Mary's come spicy, which is always worth a star in my book. Overall we were super impressed and will be making this our staple football spot.

I want to totally love everything about this place. The idea is so amazing and clever. The decor is awesome and hip, like "The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly" meets "Pulpfiction". The staff are cute hipsters that are super friendly and helpful. The food is the only part that is holding this place back. And even then, not really. It is so close to being there, but missing something. 
When we arrived, we were promptly seated and given water. We ordered the Bruscetta as an appetizer, and waited for our food while watching a western on the small TV they have in the middle of the restaurant. Meanwhile, the people behind us were sending their food back. It was the wrong thing AND it was cold. We got our Bruscetta and it was DELICIOUS. Perfect. Then, of a party of about 8 next to us sent back 5 entrees because they were cold! Then we started to worry.
We got our food (Spaghetti and meatballs and lasagna) and, surprise, it was cold. SO disappointing. The meatballs were obvi hand made, which made them delicious, but the cold just made it not good. The lasagna was burnt and cold. How does THAT happen. But it was good food. 
I will be coming back again, because i really want to LOVE this place, but I will give them about 6 months to learn how to heat their food properly.

Fantastic service. They were on time, polite, did a great job, kept asking us to look at their work to make sure we were satisfied. When I asked them to do something, they did it even better than I wanted. They even educated me about all the different variety of palm trees. I would highly recommend them to any homeowner.

Hella's is soo good! We cut up a couple baklavas from the bakery at our table before lunch because we knew we would be too full to try one after. We shared a Combo Lunch and added an extra gyro and an octopus plate. AND you must order saganaki! Had great service. Lots of outside venders will try to steer you to other places to go, but don't listen. Go to Hella's

I recently visited my sister in Conshohocken for the Labor Day holiday weekend.  I was dying to have duck soup as it has been more than 10 years since I have enjoyed any (moved from Philadelphia to rural Tennessee) and I enjoyed the duck Asian noodle soup immensely from Dragon & Phoenix that I actually ordered it another two times (total of 3 times during my visit).
