Recently departed is what I considered my favorite appetizer, more commonly known as jalapeno poppers.  These poppers, however, had a very light batter and an unconventional filling, which I found amazing.  Perhaps they will bring them back!  Do you hear me, Tommy?!  Bring them back! LOL  It is worth adding that the last time I dined, I was told that the poppers were removed from the menu but about 10 minutes later, the chef brought them out to me.  So, I suggest to anyone who comes in to Tomasito's, ask for the poppers.  Maybe they have an unlisted menu.  Pretty slick!

For my entrée, I ordered the Habanero chicken.  I only had to wait about 10 minutes and my food arrived, hot and fresh!  It's a lot of food but it seems to be just enough!  The chicken was perfectly cooked; tender and juicy.  There is a creamy habanero sauce drizzled atop the chicken that, while spicy, literally drives you to eat more and more.  It was topped with a side of Spanish rice and beans and a dish of guacamole.  All in all, the meal was terrific. 

Now, for drinks, they do have a selection of house-made margaritas, which I have had before and was not too thrilled about.  The flavor just wasn't there.  I'm not sure what caused it but if I had to wager a guess, I would say it was probably due to a cheap tequila.  In any case, they have several different kinds and they may have improved upon the recipe since the time I've written this.  My advice is to ask the bartender what the daily special is.  I was there this past Friday (6.10.11) and the special was a Kamikaze margarita, a concoction made with vodka and fresh ingredients.  It was quite good but my favorite was what I believe is called a 'Spicy Lady'.  The bartender explained to me that a few weeks prior, some ladies had asked him to make a drink that was spicy.  So, he created this gem, which is a margarita made with Don Julio and a muddled jalapeno pepper.  It's a real jalapeno pepper, folks, not just the juice.  It was both sweet and spicy and I def recommend it to anyone who wants a treat from the bar.  I'm glad to see Tomasito's bartenders extending themselves out to create something unique.  Many bartenders in nicer restaurants these days are becoming mixologists, where making a drink is a art form.  I like to think of it as creative alchemy.  

I've been dining in Tomasito's for about 6 weeks now and the food has always been great and consistent.  I only knocked off a star because they are still struggling to put together a final menu and you're likely to find items missing from time to time (oh, I hope it wasn't one of your favorites!).  The staff is cordial and attentive (Monica, the chef, frequently comes out to greet people), the restaurant is clean, the ambience is solid and the prices are reasonable.  This restaurant does not promote itself well so tell your friends to check it out.  It's a great place to grab a bite before venturing into the Quarter.

Talk about CUSH, but worth every penny. Walking distance to the French Quarter, authentic evening tradition of PB&Js and the best hot chocolate, and an amazing rooftop pool with a view to die for. Plus the bed might have been the most comfortable thing my body has ever touched.

This is my go to place! I've been here several times, but most recently after my dog vomited ALL OVER my car. I honestly thought there was no way my car could be completely cleaned and rid of the smell. But, the guys at Prestige cleaned my car to shiny new in no time! Very happy with the service here and would recommend to anyone looking for a quick car wash or even a full detail like me!

Food was just ok at best! Service was horrible. They put us in a room with a big party and the waitress worried more about them then she did us. She walked by us four times before she took our drink order. After taking our drink order she came out two more times (w/o our drinks to wait on the other table. 15 minutes later we finally received our drinks. We got our food and my sides were cold but didn't want to send it back cause I didn't know how long it would have taken to get it back. So I just ate it. We waited and waited for refills and then when it was time to pay she had disappeared. She finally brought our checks and dropped them off. After 20 mins I finally asked a different waitress to run them for us and she couldn't find our waitress either. She finally found her and it took 10 mins to run my card. So needless to say service was horrible and food quality was below par in my opinion! We were the only table in the place!
Got the duck breast entrée- really good, but I wish I got the BBQ sampler to try all the other stuff. Sides were pretty mediocre tho
First time trying this place. I had the Memphis sandwich, it probably the best thing I've ever eaten. The coleslaw with the pulled pork was soo good!! I also love the regular BBQ sauce. Amazing!!

The place was clean however, front desk staff wore masks but housekeepers didn't. Couldn't eat in dining area and staff wouldn't let us bring chairs from dining area to our room for a family of 7 to be able to sit and eat dinner together. Breakfast was a joke, a bag of sugar zero protein. Got cereal without any milk. Coffee was horrible and they didn't have creamor one day. Housekeeper was given room numbers to clean before we checked out, I went outside and came back to bed being stripped. Apparently phone plugged in and TV on wasn't enough of a indication that we hadn't checked out yet. Worst customer service hotel I've stayed in.

Everyone I encountered at Pyramid Family Dental was extremely friendly, professional, and helpful.  They were able to sneak me in last minute before the year expired and I was able to use all my benefits.  Ask for Amy Blair when you go, she gave me the best cleaning I have ever had!!

The other negative issue this year is that there used to be a rule that was enforced regarding people wearing street clothes into the pool.  That rule seems to have gone by the wayside. We have seen people with socks and regular shirts in the pool.  If you want to wear a shirt, you should purchase a swim shirt. It is just gross to allow street clothes in the pool.  

Another year and they have the expensive sound system either too low to hear or completely off.  I really enjoyed it when you could hear the music.

Fuji apple chicken salad for lunch: disappointing. Less than one cups of salad greens dried apples and way too much onion. I had two slivers of chicken in my salad. I love Panera, yet this location needs to improve.

I don't know if this place got worse or my standards for pho got higher.  I remember this place having the best pho in town, however after visiting for the first time in years, I won't be back.

Parking is a pain. Since the restaurant isn't in a great corner of downtown, you have to take a sketchy walk.

The place felt dingy.  We ended up grabbing a table that was in the middle of 4 dirty tables.  The crew working there was a bit slow to clean up, so we had an ambience of abandoned bowls.

It's the first time that I've had a spring roll that was leathery.  Flavor was alright, but the wrappers were REALLY dried out.  (we visited at about 5pm, so I can't imagine how long they sat in open air)

The pho was good, but not great.  The mint leaves that were brought out felt a bit slimy, which didn't give me a whole lot of comfort.  (I just read that another yelp reviewer has witnessed toppings being recycled.  UGH)

Overall the service was oblivious.  I'm okay without a lot of service in a pho joint, but I'd like to not be given a confused look when I ask for a table.  I would also not like to stand at the register for 5 minutes before someone decides to take my money.

Unfortunately  this place is on the decline.  A little effort would go a long way in breathing life into this place. The pho scene in Reno has gotten a lot stronger in recent years, and I'd recommend that you avoid Pho 777.

I really, really can't believe I have to give it one star, but I do.  I've ordered takeout from here many times and the food is always good. I decided to have my birthday celebration there with some friends. The staff kind of ruined it.

First, I called a few days in advance to make the reservation. We weren't sure how many people were coming, so we rounded up to be safe. I asked for a reservation for 14. The woman on the phone was very short with me, she said "Yeah - but you gotta sit outside."  I was caught off guard and asked her what she meant. She said since we had over ten people, their policy was to seat parties over ten on the patio. She assured me that there were heaters, and it was covered and very nice. 

We arrived right on time, there ended up being ten of us. We stood at the hostess station for a good five minutes while servers and hostesses ignored us. Finally I caught someone's attention who told us to "go ahead and sit down outside."  No servers came by to check on us. One girl from our party went inside to order a drink from the bar, where a bartender spilled warm Sake all over her. She was not offered anything in the way of an apology.

After about thirty minutes of sitting and waiting outside, we still had no server. Finally we flagged someone down, who sent our server out. Her excuse was that "she was waiting for everyone else to get here," and it was "really rude of them to be so late." I explained that we were not waiting on anyone else, but that I had overestimated in making the reservations. Again, she did not apologize for making us wait. 

The service was extremely slow. I don't know if they kept forgetting about us because we were outside, or perhaps they had a lot of to go orders that night as the restaurant did not appear busy. Also, no matter how many times we asked, the "heaters" that the woman on the phone had told me about were not turned on. It was about fifty degrees out, which is far too cold to be outside with no heat. 

The food was good, no complaints there. But the night was pretty miserable - everyone was freezing and tired of waiting.

I recently kenneled my bloodhound here for 7 days. He is 5 and a half and I have never had him in a kennel before. I had heard horror stories from people that kenneled their dogs and terrible things had happened.  I recently moved from the beach in RI to Philadelphia. My hound was not adjusting to city life (noise, people, parks, going to the bathroom on the sidewalk, etc.) at all! He was afraid to leave the house and overwhelmed by dog parks. My life consisted of constantly worrying about him and shuttling him back and forth to my parents house in NJ so that he could run around and go to the bathroom comfortably in their yard. I am new to the area and my neighbor used to to care of him when I would travel. Seeing as that was no longer an option, I had to kennel him.  I was so nervous honestly contemplated not going away. He is a pretty timid guy and has a tough time adjusting to anything new.
From the moment we entered the building my fears began to disappear. A friendly staff member greeted us and immediately noticed what a shy hound he was. She calmly approached him and rubbed his ears (his favorite thing) so he started to relax. After filling out the paperwork and supplying his shot records, they took him back to the kennel area with his blanket and toys and bed that I had brought from home. They said I could call and check up on him as much as I wanted. 
I left and cried most of the way on the drive to the shore. 
I called later that evening and they said that he had eaten some of his food and was easily using the indoor/outdoor kennel well, going to the bathroom outside.
I called the next day and they said that he wasn't really interested in breakfast...I was positive my dog would starve himself to death. They assured me that he was adjusting. I called later that evening and they said that he didn't really want his dinner, so they added a little wet food and treats to his dry food and microwaved it. He ate it! Yay! 
The staff continued to go above and beyond in terms of compassion and care for him throughout the remainder of the week. They truly cared about his comfort level and were amazing. 
When I picked him up, I found that I not only have my healthy, sweet hound back, but a more well-adjusted, happy dog. He is now looking like a brave city-dog who is no longer afraid of other dogs and loves to walk around and explore his new neighborhood. 
A big thank you to the staff at allen's! You are awesome!!!

F**k this place with a capital "F". That includes the douchebag of an owner and management.   If you are looking for a liquor store which promotes shady business practices, this is your kind of place!!!

Great support from the crowds, great help from the volunteers, and a great course that makes me think I'm faster than I actually am.

I was roped into doing it this year (I hate running for any longer than 30 minutes or so) but when the time comes next year I might be inclined to get roped in again.

My only knock - that 9 mile marker must have been off. I'd swear I ran another 2 miles after that point! Or maybe it just felt like that.
I'm not a huge fan of deserts but pasties were amazing at this place. Fresh and tasty, worth the calories.

Me and the Fam been meaning to come here 
Service is great , atmosphere is amazing . Food is just as great

I have only been here once and was not impressed. The receptionist had better things to do than greet the only person in the place...ME. My massage therapist was to rough even after I asked for less pressure three times. I was also told that they want a $20.00 reactivation fee for a $55.00 dollar gift certificate that was expired by 6 months. I shredded the certificate and will never be back. To much competition to return to "UGGHH massage"

Not bad for a quick lunch. I'm admittedly spoiled by the gyro platter at Nick's Deli, which I give 5 stars, but this is a nice little place. The platter was reasonably priced and came with quite a bit of food. I prefer thicker cut meat, but the potatoes  on the side were a nice touch. The salad was also tasty. Worth checking out if you want a quick, healthy option for lunch.

My work ordered the curbside pick up through the online portal that the BJ's website offers. The only plus about this review is that the online ordering system is awesome because you do not have to call. We made the order at 11:30, and was scheduled to pick it up at 12:35, we did not get our food until 1:00. Unfortunately, when we arrived no one came out for at least 20 minutes, we then went inside to where you pick up pre-ordered food and waited about 10 minutes for someone to help us. The woman at the counter was very rude, and took an extremely long time to do any productive activity. She had told us that they were waiting on a few more of our meals to be done. Once we got our food, nothing was right. We had ordered a sandwich with fries, no fries, a mini pizza with a side salad, no salad and the pizza was cold, another mini pizza that was cold, ribs with green beans and salad, there was no green beans and the ribs had no sauce nor was it warm and the meat was terrible, two burgers that were both cold/dry and we also did not receive fries with one of the burgers. This food is also not cheap, its pretty expensive. There was a packing sticker on the outside of each box with the food inside that stated the time 12:10, and that was when the food was packaged. Overall, it was a horrible experience and completely unsatisfying. We will not be taking our business there anymore.

I started coming to Smile Tucson when it was owned by Dr. Garcia and I was so sad when she retired. But Dr Ricks truly is a gem. A little goes a long way and I appreciate his concern for the patient and their family. He's easy to talk to, kind, and knowledgeable. I wasn't waiting long for him after my cleaning but he popped in with a gift card and an apology for the wait which was so unexpected! And I love my hygienist Irina! She's a wonderful RDH and always a lot of fun to chat with.

The seeming absence of organizational processing & intuitive flow here pales in comparison to the impersonal, droid-like staff.  This is my third time being "cheerfully greeted" by the service advisors at Lokey Nissan.  One pulls one's vehicle into the protected arrival center, is immediately removed from one's car, then wanders aimlessly into the processing queue.

There are NINE(9) employees seated along the counter, not all of which are busy (engaged with customers), but nobody looks at you, acknowledges your presence, or offers any
 assistance or direction.  You're left standing unassisted for an awkward period of time, & then you're ask by the "service advisor" you chose to approach that you needed "to step aside" & allow the woman who just wandered in from the waiting area to be helped.  WTF

This is my second car I've bought at Lokey.  My first was a Volkswagen, & the service team in this division was very helpful, communicative, & cordial.  The only service-speak you'll get in the Nissan Bay is in trying to load you up with additional parts & labor when you come in for your "lifetime free service".  Don't count on anything beyond oil, filter, & inspection (chance at added revenue).

Pandemic be damned; wine is a must! 

We landed a reservation for 4 people on Friday night and we entered Versi Vino with giddiness. We couldn't wait! Tables were appropriately spaced out, chill music, and clean, clean, clean. 

We sampled nearly the entire wine menu during our visit. You get a real bang for your buck with the flights. Find something you like? Order a glass. Find something you love? Order a bottle! 

We ordered a slew of tidbits for the table - charcuterie board, crostini, warm olives (who knew olives are so delectable when warm?), shaved Brussels salad, cauliflower tacos al pastor, truffle fries, and meatballs. Everything complimented our wine beautifully. I love that they give you your own bottle of water for your table. Hydration = zero hangover. One glass of water for each glass of wine, folks! 

Affordable wine flights, excellent food, and helpful staff. And the bathroom was spotless. 

This place is located in a strip mall (as are most places in New Jersey!) and it's easy to miss. When you see the sign for Dunkin Donuts, get ready to pull off.

Versi Vino, welcome to our rotation!

Excellent food and beer. They have an extensive menu that goes beyond ordinary bar food. Very nice atmosphere and friendly service. I highly recommend a visit. I had the shrimp and sausage etouffee over rice which was delicious.

Purchased tires (Wrangler AT Adventure with Kevlar) in august. Service here was fast and convenient.  They did a great job on the alignment as well.  These are some of the best tires I've had for on and off road.

We actually did the Garden District tour and loved it-
Jesse (I think that name is right) was wonderful... and because the group was small (only my sister and myself) so we basically got a private tour-
I liked that the focus was on the history of the city and was not too much of a "celebrity house tour"
We ended things in the cemetery and learned a little more about the city-
It was really quite an adventure!

I have had Lorenzo's on my list of Indy restaurants to try for a long time. First experience was during Devour Downtown and was excited to try 4 courses! Food was good, my glass of water was always full and I really enjoyed the atmosphere. My only complaint was that when the server dropped off our checks, he shared that gratuity was not included. After many years of serving/bartending and being in the hospitality industry, I was a little offended and thought it was a little classless. Overall great experience and compliments to Chef Andy for for excellent meal!
Someone just got bumped out of my top 3 burgers in Nashville to make room for Hoss! So good. Cheese-stuffed burger and Cajun fries were great. Wish I had room to try the custard. Next time.
The Broodwhich is so amazing! Reasonable prices and great food. Buy local!

We've ordered delivery from this place a few times & this last time it was pretty bad. I got orange chicken & There was a huge amount of breading to meat ratio & it had zero taste, it was still doughy. The steamed white rice tasted old. My husband had general tso chicken & he said the same thing, that it tasted doughy & the meat itself tasted old. The egg rolls were good though, a little greasy but very tasty. Don't think we will be ordering from them again

This went from my preferred location to a location I will be avoiding from now on. I arrived and checked in with host, waited inside and witnessed 2 other groups arrive and get seated before me without reservations. Then once seated the table was filthy with hair and food residue. Once I brought this to the waitress's attention, she half ass cleaned one spot on the table and all the dirt remained. My glass of Apple Juice was dirty. When she finally got around to taking my order, she had a nonchalant I don't care attitude, then when I told her what I wanted she acted as if it wasn't an item they offered. (I order the exact same thing every time I go to ihop) then she again walked away for the 3rd time, came back and said "oh, you know what you want now?" I then repeated what I said the first time. She took her time and walked off and said she will put in. I then got up and left.

The place has it flaws and I have to make allowances because I was there Thanksgiving evening . They were a little cavalier about seating. We had a 7 o'clock reservation , arrived around 6:45 and at 7:30 , they still weren't going to seat us even though they were seating people who came in after us who also had 7 o'clock  reservations( we know we were talking to them). Finally my wife pushed it and we threatened to leave and we were seated . It looked  like there had been tables ready for awhile.Ok that I had to say. The food was plentiful and excellent. And service was polite and if anything too quick. It's expensive but quantity and quality are high.Make a point of asking for lamb .They have it and it's  good. The sirloin steak is also very good.Point of comparison: I've also been to Chima a similar restaurant. I think Fogos food is actually better but Chima seemed calmer and less rushed. Combine the two and you'd really have something.And look don't hesitate to go here. Just be ready and on your toes.

Dave's is a comfortable, traditionally appointed, old time barber shop, the kind that I knew as a kid.
He invested himself in my time in the chair and gave me a great cut and mustache/beard clean up.
This guy knows his craft.
Go there.

Went there on a whim as my wife and I walked by while visiting Philadelphia.  Since it's on the 2nd floor, we decided to try it based on the menu alone.

Wow!  What a lucky choice for us!  The food is terrific and the staff is attentive and friendly.  Try the ribeye steak and the Mac and cheese with truffle oil.  And my wife loved the crab risotto.  Seriously, folks, this place fully is deserving of 5 stars.  I don't easily give 5 stars, but Davio's fully deserves this rating!

We indulge on Rib Rack a few times a month . Wings for take-out, ribs eat-in.  I cannot eat wings or ribs ANYWHERE else without being disappointed, they're that good. Prices are great for the quality of the food!!

We're experiencing the most beautiful March ever on record in St. Louis, and I'm trying to commemorate the experience with great patio eating. La Vallesana to the rescue. After an amazing Saturday night out with my hubby and a friend from out-of-town, we needed some serious delicious eats for lunch, and La Vallesana was pretty great. I had the steak quesadillas, which were delicious. I was impressed because not only were the filled to the brim with yummy steak, but they didn't go overboard and use an obscene amount of cheese like I have experienced in my quesadilla days. The boys had the tortas, and they looked pretty awesome too. Wasn't crazy about the chips (they tasted a little stale), but I was pretty pumped about our giant Mexican cokes. Overall, great patio, great food, solid weekend lunch spot.

I am a big fan of Paramount. I have eaten there 3x this month of November. I have brought friends
and family there each time and we have left incredibly satisfied. 

The garlic sauce is delicious and rich and an all time fave. I love it on the yella fries. I love dipping everything in it. 

The kafta beef was something I have not tried before and now enjoy very much. Ground beef with herbs sausage on top of rice with the garlic sauce is my favourite. 

Alsoooo I am a tabouleh salad lover and Paramount has gluten free option for same. Usually tabouleh has cracked wheat and they were able to accommodate when I asked. Love the freshness of the parsley, onion and tomatoes mixed in lemon juice.  

Overall very healthy and everything is cooked fresh. 

The service is top notch. The servers remember me since have eaten there at least once a week
now. Which is nice. Warm, pleasant and welcoming. Also, fastttt service which is very impressive. 

The restaurant itself is a beautiful space. And the bathrooms are clean. It is also child friendly as there is play gym area. 

This is now my go to restaurant for delicious middle eastern food and I will definitely be recommending it to my family and friends.
Tiffany is the best!  She's an amazing stylist and so patient with those that are afraid to try a new stylist (like me!).

We heard a lot about this restaurant and wanted to see if it was as good as we heard. I had the the Prime Rib,loaded sweet potato, and claim chowder. The Prime Rib was good, but the chowder was maybe the best I've had. Really creamy and thick. Customer service was really good. I would recommend this place just to try.

One of my favorite restaurants in Philadelphia. Great food, fun atmosphere, attentive service. The pizzas and pastas are amazing and the appetizers are fun and tasty. Favorite place to go for almost any occasion! A bit pricey but well worth the extra few bucks.

What a disappointing end to an evening with friends. Our party of 10 was seated inside. After a nice dinner we decided to enjoy drinks outside by the water. The hostess told us to go ahead onto the patio where there were counters to stand by with a view of the water. Along came a manager who told us quite rudely to leave. We weren't loud or rowdy or disturbing anyone. When a couple in our group went to talk to the manager and stated they wouldn't come back, he said, "Good!" 
My husband and I have enjoyed Circles many times since we moved to Florida but unfortunately we will be crossing it off our list.

My all time favorite vape store! 
Zach was so helpful and friendly! 
Great vibe, open late. 
Highly recommend.

If I could give 0 stars I would. They set appointments in 3 hour increments so you have to take off work basically half a day to be home. They cancelled the first appointment on that date, they didn't show for the second appointment and on the third appointment today I just learned after waiting around all afternoon again and calling them that they will not be coming. This company is a joke. After missing two appointments you think they would have made me appointment with them a priority today. They could care less.

We have come to Bria Bistro in the past several years and always had a delicious meal in a cute Italian setting.  The restaurant has obviously changed hands and not for the better.  I made reservations for Valentines Day and nowhere did it state that they would have a special menu for this evening; not even when I received the yelp confirmation that explicitly said check out our menu on yelp and showed their normal menu.  This Italian restaurant had ONE pasta offering...Raviola, which turned out to be one giant round ravioli that was mediocre and hard on the edges...for $26!... that's  just wrong.  I ordered a Caesar salad which has always been so tasty with cold crisp romaine, just the right amount of dressing and shaved Parmesan on top.....this time is was disappointingly one entire skinny head of romaine that was moderately cold and not crisp at all.  They did allow me to add shrimp for an additional  $9 which was sauted with very little taste.  
Even the olive oil and spices they pour on a small plate to dip your bread in tasted rancid and bitter.  I think it is terrible to pay $75 for sub par food and leave a restaurant hungry; especially in Nashville where there are so many other options from which to choose.  The couple next to us never received their appetizer after waiting for 45 minutes and then their food arrived; they agreed with us that the entire food offerings were beyond subpar.  I am sorry that such a neighborhood gem that was once very good quality has disappeared.  We wil not be visiting this restaurant ever again in the future.
The employees here are adorable, when I gave the salon employee his tip he did a little dance. I discovered a bruise after removing the polish, but that could have easily been from something else.

I have had my nails done many times and they have never looked so awful. I think the girl that did my nails may have been on her first day to be honest. This was "fixing" them after I told them I rarely complain about things. The guy stepped in and "fixed them". I just moved to the area and work right around the corner so I figured I'd give it a shot for convenience. The guy proceeded to tell me the next time I go back to get them filled that they will look better. I told him politely "sir, I will not be coming back here" lol. This place was AWFUL! The people were nice, but the work was just plain bad

Of the three locations, this has the best stuff.  Its not as geared towards aging FL residents as the others.  Come here for some great shoe sales on Bandolinos! YES!!!  Also has a pretty decent home section to peruse through.  Not really discount prices, but if you can find it on sale - its not too shabby.  Unless you're 65+ dont' bother with the clothes.  Some of the kids/babies stuff isnt' too bad though.
Best pizza in town. Haven't tried pastas and other items since pizza, especially the Margherita, is so good.

This place is so hot. And cold.

And I mean that in a good way.  Incredibly friendly, helpful, happy-to-be-there staff.  And the mood when you walk in is just great.  Low-key, simple wall art, fun environment.  My only concern was the lack of seating, although, in all fairness, it was extremely hot and raining outside so the turnover rate could've been lower than usual.

If you are in the mood for any kind of snack or refreshment - from hot tea/coffee to cold tea/coffee to ice cream to popcicles - this is your place.  On that particularly HOT third of july, I went for a popsicle.  I got strawberries & cream, and it did not disappoint.  It was full of creamy, fresh flavor, and had chunks of delicious strawberries mixed throughout.  Yum!  Boyfriend got the rice popsicle, and while my strawberries & cream was delicious, I couldn't help but sneak bites of his popsicle!  When we asked the staff about this said "rice popsicle", the response was "Have you ever tried Horchata?"  No sir, but yes PLEASE!

I will definitely be back to try more of those delicious frozen concoctions!

Ok store. Walmart is still cheaper for pet supplies but I really only go here for flea medicine for my cat because they sell them in single dosages instead of forcing you to buy the 3-pack (90 day supply).

The employees are okay, but the good thing is they do have an animal clinic every other Saturday and since there aren't any vets close to my home, this works for me and it's affordable (IMO).

I must say I am very pleased with the services provided by Tiffany and Speedy. Called them out for bed bug inspection and they were awesome. I've used Burns before and I wasn't thrilled with the previous experiences but they got the job done. The main thing is to be clear about fees and services. Not always as advertised as there are stipulations and fine print to the services as with many other companies. However, Tiffany and Speedy defined the meaning of customer service and quality services and I am therefore proud to say that they will receive my business and referral because of Tiffany's services.
This place was amazing . The customer service was great ! There was a man named frank who brought us our food and he was so welcoming and sweet . The manager was awesome as well . I'll def be back !

Well, the service was better than usual. The lady at the counter actually didn't seem like a mindless zombie forced to sell bagels. I typically get something like that, so I was pretty happy at first. Then I played the waiting game. Waiting and waiting for 20 minutes.... Another unusual thing. However I'm pretty patient, and this was no where near as bad as the food. They don't do soup anymore which makes sense, they're cutting their costs and I can't blame them, but the avocado on my sandwich felt like I was chewing on rocks. It was no where near ready to be consumed. Way too hard to chew and ruined the sandwich. Couldn't even squish it with my hands. I would prefer they let me know they don't have any good avocado so I don't waste 20 dollars on a sandwich for my girlfriend and I. But what can you expect? This place is going completely downhill.

Have had a wheel replacement and full rebuild done on an old bike here. Hours are very convenient. Mechanic/owner is honest, extremely knowledgeable, timely and fairly priced. Banana chocolate espresso muffins are too good and coffee is handy too. Don't miss tacos next door if you have a little bigger appetite!

Friendly
Patio/parking lot
Hot cold, salads and chips
Pastrami & Swiss

5 people behind the counter at half one on a Friday with only 6 or so patrons. 4 orders in and I watched NO ONE making sandwiches. Worker Bs were chatting, wondering circles and standing around. After three minutes one guy answered the phone as a girl and guy disappeared around the corner leaving two girls walking back and forth behind the counter discussing how hungry they are.

My hot sandwich finally made it's way around from around the corner and I proceeded to the patio to enjoy. Mmm mmm good. The peppered pastrami was good, 4 stars. However the wait was too long with limited orders in. I hate to think the wait during a busy lunch rush. With so many sandwich shops in the area, I'll keep walking around rather than stopping here any time soon.

Nothing to complain about here, straight up good service and right on the Monon trail.  I like both the Kristofferson, an American oatmeal pale ale, and the Denim Komono, an IPA.  Not eating today, but last time I was here, the food was very good.

Got my eyebrows waxed from Kristin and she did a fantastic job. She definitely took her time and when I asked her touch up a little more at the end, she was more than happy to and took her time doing that as well! Great personality and super friendly. I recently moved to the area and needed to find a "go-to" salon for my eyebrows and I found it on the first try.
This is a great place to eat!  It's kind of like a hamburger joint, but they have phenomenal ice cream.  Cash only, so come prepared!!

Family owned and operated Greek Gyro shop, with fresh cooked food at reasonable prices. For the price you do get a fair amount of food which is served fast. The quality is good and the steak that was in my gyro was full of flavor. 

Atmosphere is very casual, with a large seating area with a TV. Nothing fancy, just plain and simple but who cares, you are here for the food. Overall this place offers some great good at unbeatable prices.

Went on a Saturday and walked right in around 5:00. When we left an hour later, there was an hour wait. One of those "we got here at just the right time" moments. 
 
Not much I can add to what others have written. Really really good BBQ. We had the burnt ends and corn bread appetizers and LOVED them. The infused butter served with the cornbread made it taste like carmel corn. Wow! The burnt ends were sooo smokey and tender, and had their root beer BBQ slathered on top. Drool. 

Our table had the pulled pork, smoked meatloaf, and the combo platter with ribs, pork and the tender delicious tri-tip. The tri-tip could be part of one of those fancy meat and cheese trays - it was that special. 

Their sauces are unique - our favorite was the smokey bourbon. That was good on everything - even the kids' French fries!

They serve fast, turn tables over quickly, yet are welcoming and helpful. We'll be back!

I would have given this place 5 stars but it's so damn noisy and crowded in there. 
My dad and I wanted to try this place for our once a month burger excursion. We walked in the front door and it reminded me of Fuddruckers. They had bags of potatoes lining the walkway up to the registers. It was noisy, very noisy. There was noise from the filled restaurant. The staff behind the counter yelling back and forth, commands and answers that were not discernable from the other noise going on. But, I digress. As we walked toward the belly of the restaurant, their menu was prominently displayed from the ceiling. A sparse menu. From hamburger to cheeseburger, mini ones, veggie burgers and a few sandwiches. 
I ordered the cheeseburger. My dad, the same. We ordered a medium fries. The girl behind the counter was kind enough to tell us that a medium would probably be too big, but we ordered it nonetheless. The clerk, who took our order had asked us if we've been here before. We answered no. She asked this after we ordered our drinks which I was pleasantly surprised to find out that the two fountain machines they had are computerized and that means, in English, they have over 100 different drinks!
I got vanilla Coke and tried a raspberry diet ginger ale. The ginger ale, she's not so hot. But the Coke was A1!

We were lucky to find a seat!!! Yes, it was that crowded at around 7ish. The food took just a bit longer than I would have expected it to take. But, when we get fries, we request them to be without salt. That, right there, saves over 1300mg of sodium! And, we got used to it without salt, fairly quickly. 
THE BURGERS ARRIVED!
I unwrapped mine and it looked pretty good. You see, when I went up there, I ordered specifically to my liking. I ordered Lettuce, tomatoes, grilled mushrooms, ketchup, onions, jalapeno peppers (raw) and hot sauce on the side (for dipping the fries). I was impressed. It came out just as I ordered it!

I took a bite. OMG! That is worth waiting an entire month for! 

The bottom line
-----------------------
Would I eat here again. Yes.
Would I go during rush hour/dinner time? No
But, they are open until 10:00 PM
So, a bit of planning and the next time we eat there, it should be a bit less crowded.
They do have outdoor seating, but my dad prefered the indoor luxury of noisy metal seats. They look like wood but they aint.

If there's something that could change. Maybe tone down the yelling behind the counter a bit. I have to give them credit, they have a full crew working there!

Wow! If you're feeling like having mind blowing, delicious, ridiculously great ice cream then make sure you visit The Revolution Ice Cream Co. Absolutely wonderful flavors! I'm officially addicted. Excellent service. All of the ladies working there are upbeat, positive and super friendly.  We tried the Nutter Fudger, Key Lime Pie, Banana Pudding, Chicken and Waffles, Curried sky and I forgot the name of the other one I think it was brownie something. However, we almost tried every flavor and I have to say that they are all amazing! It's worth a visit if you're in town. Yummmmm! Will definitely return soon.

We stopped for lunch one Sunday while browsing the downtown district of St Charles. I had a salad with grilled chicken and others had burgers. All very tasty! Small menu but a good variety. Would recommend and would stop back when it the area!

This is a smaller version of a Delta Club compared  to most that I've been to.  In fact it might be the smallest of a dozen or so that I've been to.  

With that said it still has a good selection of snacks and beverages to enjoy while waiting for your next flight.  They don't have a bartender but they do have a "help yourself" area where you can pour yourself a beer from the tap or wine or cocktail made on your own.   

Overall it was a nice stay but it was a bit cramped for me to say it was awesome.  

Enjoy!

Love pizza kind of just popped up in the 109st and jasper ave square where save on is. Love pizza is set up like burger priest, in that it's designed to be a nicer and better quality version of fast food dining. The restaurant partners with local companies so they carry grizzly paw beverages and Pinocchio ice cream (vanilla, chocolate and pistachio). Oh and they have beer and wine!

There was a variety of pre-set pizzas on their menu but they also give you the choice of making your own. They also give you the choice of whole wheat or normal (?) crust and the pizzas are all thin crust to decrease cooking time. We got the Holy Shiitake and the Meatatarian, both were really good, and split the pistachio ice cream for dessert. The ice cream was delicious to.

I can't wait to go back and try the other pizzas. Definitely be back.
Truly authentic. We love eating here and have tried almost everything on the menu!! Good service and the Tacos are to die for. Most other "authentic" restaurants in the area come up short!
Great place to see people karaoke. Or dance foolishly, or be one who participated on either side of the patios. Middle area is a standard bar fare.

Just had brunch there. The sausage was overcooked... like, could not pierce with a fork overcooked. The toast was cold with a thick layer of butter on it. I had a water with lemon to drink... had I known it would be my only drink there, I would have sipped. The waitress never came back to the table for any refills, ask how the food was, or ask if anything else was needed. I have lived in this area for almost 40 years... now I see why I have never gone there. Never again. Save your money and eat at home or somewhere else.

My favorite part of fall - RBW. 

In its fifth year, it has grown to 10 days. This year there is a noticeable structure change. Restaurants can offer $10, $20 and/or $30 RBW specials. And as past years, a different fabulous event.  Also new are slips that can be checked off for one of three local charities to receive a donation from RBW that Sysco funded. 

I began my kick off at Mellow Fellow, new to RBW and a spot I hadn't yet tried. (thanks to RBW for a new discovery.)Their kick off special was a bison sausage and a pint for $10. Their week long special is a stuffed burger and beer $10. 

Saturday afternoon Pignic celebrated its anniversary by hosting a Pigtoberfest.  Sausages, three sides and beer were available while listening to live polka music. 

Noble Pie offered a $10 meatballs and crispy polenta plate at both locations. 

Under the Rose hosted Blend Catering for a OktoberFeast- an Israeli family style dinner. $70 for SO much food and drink. I always enjoy Blend's participation in RBW. They are a Catering company so RBW is a special opportunity to eat their delicious food. 

Rapscallion opened its doors in 1977 and presented a one night special 5 course dinner based on it. So much old school food and a fun evening. Check out Rapscallion review for menu and pictures. 

I skipped the Tuesday night special event to dine close to home with a large group of friends at ZoZo's. Last year and this year they do RBW right. A 5 course Italian dinner for $30. Add to that a Yelp check in and receive a glass of chianti for free. So much food, wine and friends. That what ZoZo's is year around. 

Wednesday night was just wild, Yelp created a Far East event with nine Asian restaurants at the sky terrace on the Nevada art museum. What a night of fantastic Asian food and drink samples, as well as various performances. 

Moroccan food from Nicholle at Homage filled my Thursday night. Fabulous food and entertainment. Too bad the weather didn't get the same memo, it was just a bit chilly. But that didn't stop a sold out crowd from having a wonderful savory night in the spice desert. 

Friday for lunch Chris M and I braved the spitting rain and smoke to check out the yummy lamb sandwich special with fries and dessert bite at Creme for $10. Great bargain, totally full.  
The food truck wars was cancelled in the morning due to the unpredictable rain, winds and smoke of the day. 

Saturday- it's exciting and sad. It's the end of RBW, but it hosts the Chef Showdown!! An incredibly exciting free event where you can wander around Czyz's showroom and watch 8 local chefs battle it out with their unique cooking skills. This year with the help of Sysco there were small bites and beverages to be enjoyed during the event.  

I capped off my Saturday and week with a dinner and show. Brilliant combination of Tournant's Hannibal dinner paired with Good Luck Macbeth's hilarious production of Silence. 

Check out individual reviews of each business for a more detailed account of the events and meals. 

Thanks to Natasha Bourlin and Clint Jolly for starting and keeping this fabulous foodie festival going. Look forward to year six.
Most amazing and talented bartenders I've ever seen!! Excellent food. Order the steak but skip the scallops with it. Scallops too pricey for only 3. Killer drinks and food.
Honestly my favorite place in town for a date night or girls night. That avocado hummus is soooo good!

Came here with the girlfriends for after work drinks and happy hour snacks. 
It wasn't busy so we got a table right away! Our waitress was super attentive and nice. She made sure we got the happy our specials before time was up. We all had various glasses of wine which we all thought were tasty. I like sweeter wine so the pink Grigio was perfect. 
The happy hour margherita pizza is huge!! I was expecting it to be smaller cause it was a happy hour item but it was like a normal sized pizza! The meetballs were very yummy. 
Looking forward to coming back for a dinner or lunch!
Very nice, Clean, Social distance safe restaurant with many affordable options. Loved it, hands down the best burger I've had in a while.

We waited about an hour on a Friday night around 6pm. We knew we had to try the Chargrilled Oysters  here based on the many positive Yelp reviews!

For the 4 of us, we ordered 3 dozen raw oysters, 1 dozen Chargrilled Oysters, 1 Large Seafood Etouffee, and 4 Oyster Shooters. I have no idea why we thought the Oyster Shooter would be good, but when in NOLA, gotta try it. It was literally a raw oyster suspended in a shot glass with a little cocktail sauce. The 4 of us had a discussion about how we should eat it. Would we drink the shot first then eat the oyster? Would we eat the oyster fist then drink the shot? Or would we just swallow the entire shot glass and hope we survived? I ended up just swallow the entire shot glass, and it was a terrible idea. While swallowing the vodka, the oyster was stuck in my throat because I didn't want to chew the vodka-soaked oyster in my mouth LOL. Terrible decision for us to order the oyster shooters, but we brought it upon ourselves.

The Chargrilled Oysters were pretty good! Topped in herb butter and cheese, these oysters were perfectly chewy and savory. So indulgent! The raw oysters were alright, all of them were a decent size but they were pretty sandy. The Large Etouffee was so small! We had to double check with the waiter that what we got was a Large. I easily could've polished that off by myself + a few oysters.

While the food here is a 3/5, the service here definitely dragged it down a star. We were initially seated at the table right in front of the front door. Since it was a super cold night, we kindly asked the manager if we could move to a table that was more inside (we pointed to an empty table). We politely asked him, and he started raising his voice at us and being extremely rude to us. 

With so many great seafood restaurants in French Quarter, I will not be coming back to Acme.

One of the best craft beer stores in the US and you will see this throughout the Beer Advocate website. They have everything and anything they don't have Matt will get for you. 

Food is good but its about the beer. One thing you need to do is check out the draft menu and ask about prices. I know a few friends that ordered beers to be floored when it was $8 a draft or more.

So I'm the kind of person that gets freaked out and queasy by the kind of things that you see at the Ripley's Museum.  When I came to the Mutter, I almost thought that I needed one of those bags that you find on the back of an airplane seat.  With that aside, don't hesitate to come here if you are interested and mesmerized by medical oddities.

Great Dental Office with a true Caring Heart. I like to think I am like most people and do not like the dentist , but Dr Brett and his staff made my visit very comfortable. I truly recommend Dublin Woods as your family dentist in Upper Dublin and surrounding areas

Original review 3 stars

The wait time wasn't bad. And the cost was appropriate for the service. But I arrived for an oil change and when they handed me back my paperwork with the "checklist" it showed that everything else including my lights was checked and was fine. In fact one of my two headlights has been out for a couple days and I was planning to hit another location to get it replaced after the oil change was done.

But if they are pencil-whipping the lights check, what other checks are they recording but not actually doing?

When I brought it to the supervisor's attention he seemed unconcerned and said "oh I'm sure they checked everything important".

Pleased with the price and the wait time. Not pleased at all with the attention to detail and the lack of concern that the staff might be sending cars back onto the road with even bigger problems than a bulb being out.

------ Update a month later to 1 star, one of the VERY few 1 star reviews I've given anyone.

Two weeks after my visit for the oil change my car started running a little rough. But I assumed it was from all the smoke from our recent wildfires. I let things go until yesterday when I noticed the car was struggling to shift from 2nd to 3rd. Thinking I had a transmission problem I booked an appt with Arrow to have them look at it. 

Turns out the oil filter wasn't put back on properly after my oil change, it had leaked two quarts of oil all over the pan and the undercarriage of the car. And the loss of oil pressure was causing my Honda to struggle. 

The folks at Arrow cleaned up the mess that Xpress Lube created, correctly attached the filter, replaced the missing oil. And my car runs great again. I'll be leaving a 5-star review for Arrow shortly. But apparently my concerns about Xpress Lube returning cars to the road with bigger problems than a bulb being out was even more valid than I knew.

1-star, Express Lube. My future business is definitely going elsewhere.

It's fun! It's good! It's all you can eat! 

I love thali and they didn't disappoint. I got the vegan option, it was perfect!

oh my... I moved with in walking distance of this bakery and decided on Saturday morning to treat my husband to fresh baked doughnuts after years of Saturday Dunkin Donuts runs. 

First of all, I can smell this place from my house. It's bad. When I go for my run, I pass this place. It is so not condusive to my diet.... 

ANYWAY.... I went there that Saturday morning and OH MY... the doughnuts were DELICIOUS. I got 3 glazed, a jelly, a marble frosted and a chocolate frosted dipped in coconut. They were first of all... HUGE and second of all... so fresh and delicious that I had to stop myself from consuming them all..... 

The ones with the vanilla filling looked good, as well as the chocolate. They had a great selection of cakes, and cookies, and just everything you can imagine! I am, however, a doughnut girl.

Totally recommend, go there now!

I came here several months ago after seeing Monika's work on Instagram. I was excited to go blonder, and since she specializes in blonding, I was looking forward to establishing a new stylist as my previous stylist had changed salons and was no longer nearby. At the time, my hair was slightly below my chest and my hair is on the thicker side so it's not unusual for stylists to have to use more product which, of course, can increase the price as stylists need to pay for their supplies. While she did an absolutely AMAZING job, both with color and style, I found it ridiculous that she charged me $180 after spending 6 HOURS on my hair. Not an exaggeration. While I would never want to rush somebody that's doing my hair, I couldn't help but think that my previous stylist usually spent about two hours, maybe three, at most on my hair and ended up with the same result that Monika did. Furthermore, my hair color lasted less than two weeks before going back to a dirty blonde color. I actually purchased what she suggested (because if I have $180 hair + a tip I better be taking great care of it) and was disappointed that the blonde barley lasted, even with high end products that she recommended to me. No, I did not wash my hair every single day, nor did I take crappy care of my hair after this.

Overall, she was kind to me, but I think it's wrong to charge clients such expensive prices when a 6 hour color and cut could've been done in 3 or 4 hours at most and lasts about two weeks before fading away. As another reviewer mentioned, great stylists but ridiculous prices.

I just love this place, A family owned business passed down from father to daughter. Food is great, fresh and it's clean in there, a real plus for me. My favorite is the Black Bean burger with lettuce, tomato and onion. Then there's the Ila Mae salad topped with grilled salmon. delicious. All made fresh to order

i absolutely loved the trip we made here last autumn....i was one of two chaperones to a bunch of preschoolers, and i had a blast!! the children i was with were all crazy excited about pretty much everything we saw, from the way they make cider to the tractor/hay ride.

the "hay" ride did leave me scratchy for a few hours, but it was good fun anyway.

i think i need to go back this season, if only to wander around...

I think this place is amazing. I'm a vegetarian and, typically, at nicer restaurants vegetarian dishes are an afterthought at best and often there simply aren't any vegetarian options at all.

PRO's

Zahav makes you take your time, which could also be a con if you're not into a 2.5 hour seating. But I liked it. It allows you to really savor everything you're trying and focus on the food and company. Also the hummus is by far the best I've ever had. I usually don't really like hummus, but their hummus is so mild. Their salads are also great and, again, while many restaurants don't put much thought into their salads, Zahav clearly puts a lot of care into salads. They're fantastic. The desserts were also worth writing home about; they were very rich and creative. I also recommend the brussel sprouts (in the second course) and the eggplant (final course). The manager or owner (not sure which) also took the time to ask us what we liked and didn't like. He seemed legitimately interested in our experience, which we appreciated.

CON's

The cocktails don't seem to have the same level of creativity and care as the rest of the menu. They were fine, but I've had better. Also, some of the dishes we tried were just good, not amazing, like the artichokes and this cheese and dates dish. It's also a little loud in the restaurant...it was a little hard to hear my dinner date sometimes.

The food is delicious. I love the sweet and sour pork/chicken and the boneless BBQ beef short ribs. Their wonton soup and fried rice are good as well. Food from there is a soulful and ethereal experience.
Great food and reasonable prices, but expect to wait a bit since nearly everything is homemade.  Good burgers, Reuben, cole slaw.

Asia Wok has always been one of my families favorite Chinese food restaurants . I find the online order option is very convenient and user friendly which has been extra helpful for us at this time. The food is always good. The staff here are also very friendly and helpful!

A great haunted attraction. Halloween is my favorite holiday so every year i make sure to attend one haunted hayride. I love that they have week night hours because i wanted to avoid the weekend crowd. It was actually pretty busy for a Monday night so I can only imagine how crowded it is during the weekend. I was most impressed by the haunted trail and Bates Motel Haunted house. great props, amazing costumes, and effects. Sadly, the haunted hayride was a bit of a let down. The props were cool but there were not many actors. It also wasn't very scary. The whole night actually wasn't very scary. But it definitely was fun. It's more of a family friendly hayride/ attraction than actually scary. It may be scary if you're under the age of 12 or if you're easily scared.  But if you watch a lot of horror movies/ go to a lot of hayrides, you'll probably end up laughing and having more fun than you will be scared

Great neighborhood Italian place, we ordered two pasta dishes and some Garlic Knots. Honestly, have to say that I was more than pleasantly surprised. Penne Alla Boscaiola was fabulous and so was the Penne Bolognese. Both were done perfectly, great sauce; and pasta and bread both hit the table smoking hot. Looking forward to trying the pizza, will update when I do. Try this place!

What a hidden little stunner! I had absolutely no idea this was here and I have lived in Boise for almost 15 years! I can imagine that it is even more beautiful in full spring and summer. 

I needed a place to bring my kids to get some fresh air, but also to maintain some distance from our fellow humans. (we visited in March 2020) When I Yelped "Hiking",  this little reserve was one of the top hits. It is more of a leisurely walk, but it is just perfect if you have 30-45 minutes to kill. 

There are two parking lots. One along McMillian (with about 10 spots) and a bigger one along Maple Grove (with about 20 spots). There are restrooms located at the Maple Grove parking lot, plus a bench, some rocks to climb on and an informational sign. 

The paths are all packed and filled with fine gravel. The paths will meander you past the several "lakes", filled with a variety of birds and waterfowl and boarded by cattails and tall grasses. My kids loved pointing out all the birds, tossing pebbles into the water and getting a little bit dirty. 

The path is all interconnected, with a few short offshoots. Eventually, you will reach a fork and you can go up or down. Either way, you'll be able to loop around and take the other option. We saw quite a few bird watchers there when we went, which added to the fun of visiting a reserve. Highly recommend!

Amazing bangers and mash, my favorite here. The boys love the flat bread and huge pieces of carrot cake. Service was seriously fast even though his place was jam packed busy.  Our server was totally in the ball and had a great personality

The atmosphere is great! Feels like you're dining in a old log cabin...and you kinda are! Beautiful fixtures, great lighting. Went on a busy night and it was noisy but energetic and fun. Great location when it comes to events at Bankers Life. Had the Mozzarella...can't go wrong. And the steak...generous portion and the flavor was on point. The tequila cocktail has a good pour and is delicious. I'd recommend dining in the bar area. It's more intimate and cozy.

this place is tacky. the mascot is creepy and l0oks like an early 90s cgi cartoon. the food is average nothing special.  apparently it is a chain but i have never heard of it or seen it.  I gave it an extra star because if it is your first time you get a free cookie. other than that it is your average sandwich place

This spot was so perfect for weeknight sushi date! The staff was welcoming, the food came out quickly, and everything was delicious. I love the wood and light fixtures. This is definitely going to be a regular spot for me!

Tried it for the first time today, and it was just meh.  Everything was really sweet, even when I ordered things that were supposed to be spicy.  I didn't see mussels on the menu, but maybe I overlooked them...or it's just a dinner item?  It was okay, but doesn't hold up to Sushi Pier (One, not Two) or Hiroba's.

We stayed at this Radisson on June 10th-11th, 2012 and while we enjoyed our mountain view room suite we weren't too pleased with housekeeping and the cleanliness of the pool and hot tub.  Wi-Fi was very slow.

The on-site restaurant Ocean Breeze is a good place to chill and relax.

In regards to cleanliness we notified management and they apologized and are going to take care of us during our next stay at Radisson Tucson.

Thank You Radisson Tucson !

Oh my goodness, what SHOULDN'T you try here?  

Sizzling Rice Soup is a must- it's delicious and the table side preparation is a nice touch.  Calling ahead for a Peking Duck is a great choice for a special night out.  Best. Potstickers. Ever.- end of story.  The Yen Ching beef is my favorite, and I have to admit i now get that every time, but my slightly-less-set-in-his-ways S.O. always tries something new, and I've never been disappointed sampling from his plate.

This vet's office is considered reasonable in cost which might explain the crowded waiting room. The staff are condescending, disorganized and outright rude. If they make a mistake they don't take responsibility for it. If you are given incorrect directions they chide you for getting it wrong. Their phone line is always jammed. You rarely actually see the vet. We have had multiple pets all our lives and had wonderful vets wherever we lived. We never experienced anything like this office. Go here at your pet's risk.

True story: the main reason I begged my sister to go to New Orleans with me was to go on this kayak tour and see a bit of the real southern bayou. The tour was perfect!! Didn't feel touristy at all- very casual, laid back, educational and of course fun!! It was a rather small group of about 10 of us, we had the channels all to ourselves. I would HIGHLY recommend to anyone considering seeing the bayou first hand!!
Great quality food and excellent customer service !! Definitely would recommend!! Variety of options for everyone.

Nature's Table has been around for many years. They recently revamped a few things, and I'm glad they're here to stay despite many people closing doors around  them. I've always been a huge fan of their smoothies and shakes. The difference is subtle. The smoothies are made with liquid yogurt and the shakes are made with frozen yogurt resulting in a much creamier blend. Both are delicious and filling. 
For meals, their sandwiches are good but I love their southwestern salad topped with vegetarian chili.
Try them out so they'll stick around even longer!

I really want to like this place. It's so convenient for me, so I keep trying. Most recently we got a pizza since our go-to place was closed. The pizza was extra greasy and burnt on the bottom. We got this as take out on a night that was not very busy.

During other trips, they left us hanging by the register for ages (on a similarly dead night) and the food was cold by the time we got it home.

I'll keep trying once or twice a year to see if the food or service improves.

Nadine creates the most beautiful window displays in the French Quarter.  She updates the window regularly with the new goodies she has brought in.  So many little objets dart some whimsical and haute decore.  Hooray Nadine.

This is by far my favorite place to shop at when I'm looking for quality upscale rescued apparel! They have something for everyone. It's has everything from Funky, Retro and even Vintage. They have Levi jean jackets for like $10-15. You can't beat that! The store was well organized and the staff was super friendly. An awesome selection of graphic tees and boots. I even picked up a rare leather jacket for next to nothing. Anywhere else and it would have cost me 3 times what I paid here. This place is amazing and well worth the visit. I'm so glad they are on South Grand. We needed a place like this here. 5 Stars from me. Can't wait to go back.

First time in New Orlean this place was recommended by a friend we absolutely love it we've been coming here every day for the past 3 days for breakfast and today for dinner. The food is delicious and the people are so welcoming. A great big thank to to Jack who made sure our experience was a,memorable one. He is truly the best and makes the best chocolate cake. Thank you Jack for your friendly and genuine hospitality

This was a great lunch stop for Yodi and me!!! I had the big bleu!! Yummy! Yodi seemed to enjoy every bite of her pup burger. Tatiana gave us stellar and friendly service with burger cooked to perfection! I loved how dog friendly they are and the patio was warm and cozy on a cool day. We will definitely be back!!!

Service apartment has been always nice when I bring my vehicle there.
The last time I was there I have a problem
But Terry Robertson took care of it.
Thank you very much
 I appreciate your integrity

I was so looking forward to dining at Chifa, particularly since Jose's other restaurants are among my favorite in the city. But, I am sad to say, this was the absolute worst dining experience of my life. I am not exaggerating.

We needed a restaurant that could accommodate 10 people around a round table. We had several options, but went with Chifa. We called to confirm that we would be given a round table 3 times. And I was happy to see that when I arrived, there was indeed a round table available. We were told to wait 10 minutes before the table would be ready. Great! But then I saw them seating another party at our table, and 20 minutes later we were asked to go downstairs, to the lounge area, to wait some more. Finally, after 45 minutes, we came up to check on the status. At this point we were told that the round table will be a while and they can seat us at another table (one that was empty all along). We decided to try it - even though we specifically chose the restaurant for the round table - but the table at which they sat us was so huge that we literally couldn't hear one another from different sides of the table (and we are all in our 20s, with no hearing problems!). I then came up to the manager - Marc Grika - the one who was bouncing us around from the lobby to the lounge, and giving us estimates that he knew were incorrect. I inquired into what was happening and was treated with rudeness like I have never seen before. He was abrasive and unapologetic (even though at this point we had been waiting for over an hour for a table) and basically told me to go ****, in not so many words. 

I then spoke with another manager - Scott Clayton - who was initially much nicer, and assured me that we would be seated shortly. And we were - a brisk hour and 28 minutes after arriving at the restaurant. Fantastic.

We sat down and promptly ordered 22 dishes and some bread. The dishes started to slowly come out. Some were tasty, others were  average, or even below that, but the one thing they had in common was that they were all obnoxiously small. I say this having dined at (and loved) other tapas places like Tinto and Amada (which are also quite stingy on the portions - 7 tiny potato cubes on a plate for $12, for ex). Luckily, after asking 3 separate people and waiting for another hour, the bread came. 

When we finished our meal and received our grossly overpriced bill, I asked Scott Clayton to comp us the two pitchers of sangria that we consumed while waiting for the table for an hour and a half. At this point he became quite rude and patronizing, saying things like, "I'll think about it" while taking off with the bill. He then came back and said that they don't guarantee tables, hence they did nothing wrong, and will not do anything for us. At this point we asked that they take the gratuity off the bill, as we wanted to pay our server (who was great) in cash. To this, Scott threatened to call the police on us. I asked him to go ahead and do so. He rushed off again, only to come back 10 minutes later with the revised bill, explaining to us that we are punishing the waiter and not the restaurant (thanks, Dick, I've eaten out before). We tipped our waiter in cash and were happy to be done with the meal.

So to sum up our experience - it was frustrating, bewildering at times, expensive and unsatisfying. We were treated in a way that I have not seen before. I have had experiences in restaurants where things don't go perfectly, but the management usually handles these situations in a professional and courteous manner, in stark contrast to how Mr. Grika and Mr. Clayton treated us.

If you do decide to try this restaurant, I hope you will have a more positive dining experience. Just eat a little before you go.

The food was good but the service was terrible.  It took at least 20 minutes for our server to take our drink order.  Entrees came spread out 15 minutes apart.  This was our first time dining there and definitely our last.  We are understanding of staffing shortages but Osteria needs to limit their reservation.

Disappointing service, However the breakfast was so delicious and the atmosphere was fabulous! I ordered the Carrot Cake French Toast and OMG..it was the best French Toast ever! I was impressed. The atmosphere was perfect. There's outdoor seating with umbrellas to block the sun  and there's a beautiful serene waterfall.. My issues were with the service. The waiter was extremely unattentive. After we were seated, The waiter did not come by to greet us, or even give us menus. We sat there for a few minutes and  eventually asked the front desk for menus. Coffee  and water refills were almost nonexistent. We had to flag down another waiter and ask for refills since our waiter disappeared for a long while. This restaurant could easily have a five-star rating, however the service was so disappointing and frustrating. Overall we still had a good time.

I've been here 4-5 times over the last 6-7 years. Every time we come to NOLA we make at least one trip here. I was looking for my of my past reviews and found none. Let me correct this right here and now. 
"Mothers", without exception is he best restaurant in NOLA, perhaps the WORLD. 
Last night I had the BEST fried oysters I've ever had, (I'm from Cape Cod, Massachusetts, the home of seafood). For sides I had the cabbage and turnip greens. OUTSTANDING! I want the chef to bear my children. The Bloody Mary's are VERY spicy, but good. Bread pudding and pecan pie, also OUTSTANDING. 
I've had the fried chicken in the past (also some of the best I've ever had) but didn't want to wait 40 minutes (cooked to order), fortunately it paved the way for oysters. 
Do your self a favor, EAT HERE, (full disclosure), not my mom. For that matter, nobody I have ever met. 
I Love this place. I PROMISE, you will too.

This museum is amazing! If you have not been yet, you are missing out. The architecture both inside and out is show-stopping, and the gardens behind are interesting, funny, and fabulous. Yes, the fact that they charge $10 to park in their lot is beyond ridiculous, in addition to the higher-than-all-other-museums admission fee, and yet, you still must go. You have the options of taking a guided tour, or using a headset and listening to a pre-recorded tour of the museum, which is what we did.

We went specifically this time to see the M.C. Escher exhibit. It was an interesting and comprehensive collection, very well laid out according to dates and interests of the artist. They also had a fascinating looping movie playing about Escher, which featured explanations of his work, actual video from interviews with him, and videos of him making a print and cutting out his wood blocks.

Afterwards we wandered around the Dali portion of the museum, which is always incredible. As long as you don't use flash, you are actually allowed to take pictures of everything in here (which you can not do in Escher). Dali had so many things going on in his paintings that the pre-recorded guide was very helpful with explaining what you were actually seeing.

Make sure to leave yourself plenty of time to wander through the excellent museum store at the end of your visit.  They have a wide variety of t-shirts, books, jewelry, and assorted odds and ends, and most are very reasonably priced. There is also a Café in the building, but I have not ever utilized it.

This museum is a must-see in St. Petersburg - you will love it!

If you get a good technician, you get a good manicure and pedicure. Dont be too generous with your tips, though. I made the mistake of being generous with my tips when they did a good job, and after that the good technicians were no longer available, and I got stuck with the sub standard technicians who sold me their sob stories about how hard they worked and all the long hours they worked. All while doing a mediocre job on my nails. I wont be returning to this salon.

I've been to Grain and Berry Westchase many, many times and have yet to be disappointed. From the looks of it, many people feel the same. The place is always busy but the wait is never too long.

I love the bowls, I usually get them to go and its busting at the seams of the take out container. Filled with fresh fruit, crunchy granola and yummy smoothie base. They offer traditional açaí and my favorite- dragonfruit. They have around 20+ bowl options or an option to build your own. Each is reasonably priced at around $11-13.

They also offer avocado toast and fresh made juices. These options are equally as delicious, it just depends what you're in the mood for. Additionally, they offer Buddy Brew coffee. 

The staff is so nice and friendly. The dining area and restrooms are spotless. Overall, its just a fun, trendy place to grab a quick, filling bite to eat!

This company is not like it used to be.  When we moved to Boise about 20 years ago we used Atkinson Glass for a major window installation project.  They were great.  I remember Mr. Atkinson personally visiting our house to assure that the project was going well.  As the years went on we occasionally had them do some work for us and noticed that customer service started slacking off.  

A couple of months ago we asked them to come out and give us an estimate to buy and install a skylight. I gave them the specs on what we wanted including the type of skylight. The appointment date was but then we go a call the day before they were to be at our home and was told they didn't install skylights anymore. 

You think we would have learned from that but we didn't. About three weeks ago a rep came out  to give us an estimate on replacing quite a few windows in our home.  The representative said he would get back to us with an estimate.  Never heard from them again. Apparently not following up is their business model now. 

That's not the way Atkinson family would have wanted this business run.

Went there this past Sat around 12:00 for a birthday brunch.  They were really cheap with the very small Mimosas and the plates had super small portions, wish I took a picture, but my phone had lost it's charge.  The waiter also didn't seem to know his job very well, but he might've been new, and I know that can be overwhelming.  The saving grace was the yummy breadsticks, which reminded me of Olive Garden, only slightly better.  Haven't been there for lunch/dinner, but for brunch I would choose differently next time, though.

My family and I have been here for about 3 months. Overall thus is a good place to live. The front office staff is friendly (more the women than the men). Jenny, in the front office, is MAGNIFICENT and very responsive. She is trustworthy and a true pleasure to do business with. The apartment itself is well kept and the maintenance staff is wonderful at responding to any needs. There are a couple of big CONS about this place: 1st THERE IS NO PARKING. Do not let the front office staff convince you that there is ample parking for the tenants because this is FALSE. Each apartment comes with either a one or two car garage but outside of that there isn't any parking. my husband and I have a one car garage and when he comes home from work there aren't any spots available for him to park in. He drives the entire complex looking for spots and there isn't one. One of the members of the office staff told him to park outside of the gate (and assume all risks that come with that). When he parks along the curb, near the apartment, he receives an orange sticker telling him he will be towed. This is a HUGE inconvenience and very frustrating. We spend most of our time trying to find spots to park so that we will not be towed. When we moved here we thought we would gain the peace of mind we longed for after living in another complex. Once here we realized we gained the headache of "where to park". Having guests visit means constantly listening out for a tow truck because they do not have anywhere to park. Another CON is the amount of noise that some neighbors make. We have had a few mornings where we are awakened by children in the street playing. This isn't a huge problem (unless it's 7 am). There are also some neighbors who play music VERY loudly but if you mention it to them they tend to be accommodating. All in all, if you are OK with having only the garage to park in then this place would be perfect for you. As much  as we love the apartment itself, when our lease is up we will be searching for somewhere else to live. The constant headache of parking isn't worth it to us.

This grill is a nice low key local spot. It could be described as hole-in-the-wall, or a duck-off.  It really does have a "Cheers" feel.  The server/bar tender knew mostly everyone that came in by name.  The Grill has about 4 or 5 TVs around to watch sports. They also have a nice sized outdoor patio that I would have loved to eaten on, if it was at least about 40 degrees when i was there. They have a full bar and are operating at limited capacity. Currently there is no bar seating, but there are a couple of tables placed up against the bar. It was slow when I was there, late lunch, so I had no problem being seated.

They have the typical grill food such as fish, burgers, soups,  wraps, salads and sandwiches.  I got the Boathouse BLT with fries and it was amazing. I only had to wait around 5 minutes for my food. It was quicker than many fast food established I have been to.  They did not skimp on the bacon on my BLT. The sandwich was loaded. I was really stuffed after my meal. My server was awesome, one of the friendliest servers that I have had in a long while.

As for parking. They have a huge private lot in the small strip mall that it is in. You can park in either the front or back of the grill and enter/exit on either side as well. They are currently doing dine-in (limited), and take out
Excellent and Delicious!!!!! Everything on the menu was GREAT!  The wait for the food was long because of the lunch crowd but the food was worth it. I visit this place every time I visit New Orleans.
Amazing place!!! Caught 3 great shows on my last visit. Just a few doors down from Adolfo's.
