Our waitress Liz was warm and welcoming while serving up fresh shakers of the usual condiments: Parmesan, peppers, and ground oregano. Our 12" pizza was generously portioned for two while costing just under 12.00. Not bad for a genuine brick oven Sicilian pizza with truly fresh ingredients and the cheesiest of yummy thick cheeses.  
  We will be back very soon to check out the breakfast/lunch menu which looks to be extremely reasonably priced. (Tip- Breakfast served until 2 p.m. and pizza is served from 4 to 8 p.m.) All that said-- We'll be back soon because it was awesomely delicious!

Cafe Vicino was a great experience. The food was great, nothing mind blowing, but really yummy, and the service is fantastic.  Will definitely be going back!! It is a quaint little restaurant, so don't forget to book a reservation, and definitely don't plan on talking any secret undercover business because you are really close to everyone.

Would not recommend or go back. Overpriced and disappointing. I ordered the "cleanse" fresh pressed juice but got something completely different. The place was empty but it still took nearly 15 minutes. When I finally got my juice it was separated and I couldn't taste anything but cayenne pepper, which wasn't even listed as one of the ingredients.

I was SOOO excited when i seen there was a Felipe's in Mid-City. I think the prices are too high for what you get and i don't like how you have to pay for extra things like (caned) corn ($.50) or cheese ($1) i would think that things like that came standard. anyways i ended up getting a mini burrito for $7. Next time ill just make that drive to chipotle.

I'll be honest, I didn't know a thing about Johnny Cash except that I could recognize a song or two and that there was a movie chronicling his life played by Reese Witherspoon and Joaquin Phoenix. However, this is a must see experience. They told his life story beautifully, and I felt like I knew him by the time I left the museum. I wish I had more time and it was less crowded because there is so much to read, music to listen to and movie clips to watch. You could easily spend 1.5-2 hrs in the museum, just because there's so much stuff. It's also nice how they dedicated a small section of the museum to other musicians that Johnny Cash worked closely with like Elvis. Yes, the museum is small and it gets really crowded. To truly enjoy, try to go during off peak hours. Fan or not, there is no denying that if you visit the country capital of the world you must visit this place. There is something magical about seeing and being so close to the memorabilia that was once a huge part of the life of one of the one of the best selling musicians of all time. After leaving the museum, I can say I'm a fan. 

The Patsy Cline museum recently opened above on the second floor, but to be honest I didn't think it was worth spending almost another $40 on two additional tickets. I will save that for another day and time.

My first time at Soybean. Overall good. Mostly Thai but generally too sweet. They have a nice menu with mostly classic Thai and a few Japanese choices. We ordered beef sate and the sampler which included edamame, spring rolls, gyoza, shumai, and some sort of curry empanada type of thing.

The flavorful beef was grilled nicely but the peanut sauce was overly sweet. The edamame were salted to perfection. The curry turnover had a filing similar to Indian samosas. The shumai was dipped in batter and deep fried for full effect. The sampler came with a trio of sauces. The sweet chili sauce was more sweet than chili. The soy was laced with fresh ginger.

We got a Thai salad next. Again too sweet and I was disappointed that they used a green leaf lettuce instead if napa. I really wish the balance was better. I needed some sour and more heat. It's that combination of all the tastes that I love in Thai and other Southeast Asian cuisine but is missing here.

For our entrees, I tried the classic shrimp Pad Thai and Steve got Singapore Mai Fun. Not to bore you but the Pad Thai was too sweet. It needed tamarind. It also lacked the taste of the pan on the noodles. When you eat great Pad Thai you know it's pan fried. There's a point in frying when the noodles and broken bits of the other ingredients caramelize and approach the point of burning but are saved by the master chef. This version missed that.

I really enjoyed the Mai fun. It had a deep madras curry flavor and was not too sweet!

I will try Soybean again. The decor is nice and we got pleasant service. The menu has some nice things I'd like to try. I think the choices I made this time leaned to the sweet side anyway so I'm willing to give them the benefit of the doubt.

My husband and I stopped here for morning brunch and drinks. We couldn't have been happier with our choice. We had the Seasonal Beignets (peppermint for winter!) the Oyster Benedict, and the Breakfast Burger. All filling choices for the sweet and savory taste we were going for. 

Whatsmore, I had the best Amaretto Sour I've ever had thanks to General Manager Sean. Sean and his team were inviting from the moment we walked in. We enjoyed the vibe and service so much, we are going to make Ace Hotel our next destination hotel.  If Sean and team can make us feel so welcome in their restaurant, I look forward to what's in store for our experience as an official hotel guest.

Pros: The place was empty Saturday at noon and the Cinnabon guy was quite friendly.

Cons: Too much to list but what really stuck out was being approached by a little person caked in makeup selling cheap $5 holiday bags.  When I very politely turned her down, she scoffed with an "oh. My. Gawd, really?"  Lol.  I laughed in her face when I heard her.

Much better the second time around after I complained. The food as always is average, and it's nice to go when their not playing awful music; the drinks are very good; that's what I will say. I'll probably go back just to sit at the bar and have a few drinks if anything. 

DESSERTS!!!!! You need a proper dessert menu!

worst pizzahut ever.. guy named wayne know shit about menu and pizzas.. he was very rude.. he doesn't deserve to work in hospitality industry. I will never come again to this pizza hut and will tell friends to avoid it..
Great food. Today we ate outside but have eaten inside two weeks ago. We have found any item that will prepared and delivered to table by good waiters.
Best brunch spot in town! And I also love them for dinner too, but nothing beats Saturday's Bottomless Mimosas. I always have thee most friendly staff too!

I had mixed feelings about this place... my fellow yelpers have it as 3.5, my parents said it was ok, but others said it was great & it's obviously a NOLA tradition. However, to say I was underwhelmed is an understatement. 
So we went on a weeknight around 730/8, and there was no line, except for a couple groups trying to decide what to order. The security guard made it a very rushed experience from the start.. I felt like I had to decide immediately to keep the (nonexistent) line moving. I ended up going with the "original debris" and a side a fries. Ordering & checking out (counter service) was less than friendly, but efficient.
We found a table & a staff person brought silverware & took our receipts to get our food. 
The portions are huge!! I got a small, and my dining partner agreed we could have easily split it, and the fries were full too. However, that's where the positives end... the sandwich was soaked in au jus, and impossible to eat without a fork & knife. The sandwich came with slaw, mustard & pickles. I'm not a big mustard fan (& missed this in my hasty order), and the I think I make better flavored, shredded beef at home. The fries were slightly warm, but I was hungry so I kept eating both.
Despite the NO tradition, I would definitely not recommend this place.

This is definitely a 5-star location, a Zagar gem and a Michelin one star. What made it great: Taylor, Taylor, Taylor, the best table server in Nola. The food? Very French Nouveau, tasty, imaginative, appealing, and surprising.

We had the tasting menu with Barbera wine from Yolo, Zin from Sonoma, and Pinot from Monterey and San Luis Obispo. Puree of roasted beans and pork with graham cracker crisps, duck meat balls, daikon, white asparagus, pork jelly gumbo with pickled collard greens and mustard flowers and aioli. Red snapper and sassafras rice with bay leaf in a bisque. Followed by beef culotte, fried red potatoes, succotash, hush puppies in crawfish mousse -- or coulotte fried potato succotash crawfish mousse and hush puppies shafafa sauce, per Doug. Who knows how it will end? Our handsome native Neworlenean server said, when he surprised us with two desserts.

Taylor clinched the deal when he sent us a postcard from Nola thanking him for allowing him to make it a fine dining experience, which it was.

He's adorable, young, and ambitious. Kudos and best wishes to him in his future endeavors.

We had a reservation at 6pm on a Friday and ended up waiting for an hour, which was really frustrating. Once we sat down, service was really great, but I was underwhelmed with the food. To share, our table had the oysters rockefeller, souflee potato, shrimp remoulade, broccoli, and fried eggplant. I enjoyed the oyster rockefeller, but the other dishes were pretty bland to me. They weren't really seasoned and were the kind of things I could make at home. I got the crabmeat sardou for myself, and this was just a hollandaise gloop, which I had to scrape to the side of the plate. Overall, way too rich and once again not seasoned enough. Lastly, this place was just so overpriced for food I could just make at home. That plus the crazy wait makes this a place I wouldn't go to again.

Oh it hurts me to dislike this place but I really really really really disliked Harry and Izzy's.

Went for an academic luncheon and had the "party room" that was maxed into its upstairs. When we walked in, there were at least 5 hosts/hostesses standing there--no greeting, nothing. Finally we approached them and was seated.

We were serviced by 2 waitresses who were in no way filled with personality. They were clearly upset they got our group, they barely smiled and honestly seemed like they wanted nothing to do with us!

For the food, I'm not a huge fan of horseradish, so the shrimp cocktail was a let down. Not only the sauce was not appetizing to me, but the shrimps alone were only appealing by size, but taste was barely mediocre. Had a chicken sandwich, bland...I mean, $20 and 2 hours later, I think I was just done with the place.

Service definitely stole the stars, but food didn't bother gaining any of them back. Sad.

I washed a load of clothes and a load with a comforter and a few towels. Got both washed and dried for under $10. It didn't take too long either. In the mean time, I got a beer and surfed the net at the BBQ place that is attached to the laundromat :).

BEAUTIFUL, magical place. A MUST stop and see....and buy from. The owner has an amazing story of endurance. Buy the glass beads that survived the fire. This store has a lot to choose from and is totally well-priced.

a minute ago

I tried to call in a takeout order. The person who answered the phone seemed to have difficulty with the phone. After asking for my order her end of the conversation was peppered with "Hello?" "Hello?", interrupting my attempt to give her my order. She abruptly put me on hold. When she came back to the phone she read some of my order back to me, and asked for my phone number. I have an out of state number, an area code that was unfamiliar to her. She repeated back the local area code for confirmation. My attempt to provide the correct area code was met with her talking over me with her "Hello?" "Hello?" and hanging up on me. After a few minutes I called back and immediately received the "Hellos." No attempt was made to take my order. I hung up and ordered from another restaurant. Within 5 minutes I received two hang-up calls coming from Sunny's number. A third call asked if I had called with an order; they were ready to take it.....
I don't know what was going on at their end, but it did not instill confidence in me of their ability to prepare my order. There are too many other options out there to struggle to order food.

I had a Groupon for a large 2 topping pizza and a 2 liter for $13. Ordered 1/2 sausage and pepperoni and 1/2 Basil and tomato - 
the pizza was delicious and the guy at the counter was super friendly. They also allow you to choose a cheese mix that contains provel and mozzarella or mozzarella only.
They do have lots of specials which I'd recommend rather than the full price pizza. I was completely happy with the Groupon price but would have felt $23 for a 2 topping 16' pizza would have been steep. The only thing I was slightly disappointed with was the Basil topping as I was expecting real basil not Basil flakes from a jar.
Even so, the pizza was delicious and it didn't factor into the review; I'll definitely return.

So my boyfriend and I came here today. We've never tried poke and looking forward to it. Theres premade pokebowls and build your own which you get the choice of one protein, double protein, or three protein. My boyfriend and I choose double protein. It also came with a base which you can choose from (white rice, brown rice, noodles) and many topping choices. I can honestly say I really enjoyed this place, the food was amazing. By the way, this place is usually very busy around 12-1pm.

This place is turning into a dump. I don't write reviews for fast food places but I'm not letting this visit go unnoticed.

I went into the store tonight instead of the drive through. There wasn't anyone at the counter, no problem I wanted to check out the menu because I didn't really know what I want. While i'm looking at the menu, the kid working the drive through finishes filling up a cup of iced tea for the drive through customer. He looks at the iced tea and contorts his face, then turns to a coworker and says "this iced tea don't look right" to which she responds "yeah that don't look right" and his response "well he's gettin it anyway lol!" Oh great - this is the attitude in this place now, after spending a few minutes in this place this kid's attitude makes sense. 
 
After a few minutes a manager came out to take my order. I said "Hi, how are you doing?" The manager's response was to look at me like i'm wasting his time - he literally stared at me and made no sound, arrogance just dripping off of him. Well I didn't realize that I was dealing with the burger king himself and that a lowly commoner like myself should not have directly addressed the burger king in such a way!

See, I make an effort to be polite to fast food employees to offset some of the lousy customers that treat you guys like garbage. I'm not looking for a special response - you could have said hi/hey/whats up/i'm good - what can I get you. For you to stand there and look at me like I just walked into your home and interrupted your personal time is about as unacceptable as it gets - yes even for a fast food joint. 

At this point i'm done with that, I give my order, he punches it in. Unfortunately I had a question, which was the whole reason I came in. Even though I was dealing with the burger king himself, I decided to ask. I said "do you guys not serve grilled chicken sandwiches anymore?" His initial response was the same as his response to me greeting him. After the shock of a lowly commoner addressing him wore off he replied "does it make sense for me to drive 3 miles that way (points towards oxford valley mall) or four miles that way (points towards bensalem) to pick up a bag of chicken that only has 12 pieces of chicken in it?" I said "ok" but now i'd like to say your royal highness - please forgive me for not being aware of your personal problems. With me being a lowly commoner I was not aware of the dangerous trek that needed to be made to retrieve the holy grilled chicken. It was not my intention to imply that such a journey should be taken on by a man of your royal lineage.  If it be your will, I will assemble and lead a party consisting of a warrior, a horseman, an archer, and a mage to make the perilous journey to BOTH locations and retrieve the mysterious grilled chicken for you to use however you see fit. 

Next - the burger king helps the drive through kid by getting a chocolate milk shake that the kid just entered. The burgerking is standing with his face inches from the machine and bellows "WHIPPED CREAM???????" The drive through kid is still taking the order and the burger king proceeds to bellow "WHIPPED CREAM???????" repeatedly while the kid is trying to finish taking the order. After the kid is finished taking the order the burger king asks him "DOES HE WANT WHIPPED CREAM?!?!" Dumbfounded, the kid responds "i-i-uh i d-don't know" and the burger king proclaims "this is the kind of thing we should be asking every time because we could be getting it now rather than asking them at the window, see now you gotta waste time and ask"  My dear burger king, forgive me, but never in my life have I ever pulled up to the drive through window at any fast food place and had my food ready and waiting. As a customer, I appreciate any effort that the order taker makes to ensure I'm going to be happy with my meal - including taking literally 7 seconds to ask "would you like whipped cream on your shake?" The order taker would have had to walk to that area anyway. 

A short while later, my food is ready and the burger king graciously put my food on the counter and muttered "here you go" and scurried off to his royal chamber.

I get home, lets go over each item in my order:

Bacon King - Items included in my sandwich: two beef patties, 4 strips of bacon. Items missing from my sandwich: ketchup, mayonnaise. Both patties were undercooked. A little pink would be fine with me, these were pink throughout. Bacon King Judgement: OFF WITH IT'S HEAD

Double Quarter Pound King - Items included in this sandwich: two beef patties, a reasonable amount of onions, NINE PICKLES, 4 drops of ketchup, no less than THREE TABLESPOONS of mustard. The patties were cooked exactly the same as the patties on the bacon king, which is to say that they were hardly cooked. Nine pickles.........niiiiiine pickles, do I really need to explain what's wrong with that? Four drops of ketchup, well at least you tried (kind of). WHY SO MUCH MUSTARD??

I have been down in this part of the Quarter many times, usually for some music festival, and always while walking past this strip of bars I am overcome with envy.  You see, here in nola I have colleagues but not friends.  Yes, it is sad, I know.  My wife is not much of a drinker,and so rare is the night I get to immerse myself in a dive bar and get--how do the kids say it these days--wrecked.  And yet I still will walk past these places, see people getting loaded on cheap booze, and wonder what it would be like to be doing that, instead of just heading home to drink Miller High Life in front of the TV.

Well, on my 34th birthday I finally got to find out.  I choose Turtle Bay, although there a number of boozy holes you can choose in the area.  And I got to tell you, it was pretty awesome.  The bar was not very full, especially for a Saturday night, but there were a few sketchy characters, as well as at least one passed out frat boy.   The bartendress was gothy and served me a draft of Abita Andygator (FYI any good nola bar should have this on tap).  

The juke was blasting, of all things, Bad Brains.  When DK's "California Uber Alles" came on, this bar won me over.

First time trying Crumbl. We're not local but were in the area and heard good things so we decided to give it a try. Overall, I dig it. Cookies are delish. Parking is tight but ordering ahead makes it so convenient. The employees are not super friendly but they're also super busy so I totally get it. Pricey is in line with size and quantity. At first I was like my goodness $12 bucks for 4 cookies is a lot, but after seeing how big they are I feel the pricing is fair for the size and quality. Excited to try more flavors!

Ate there with friends last night and it was wonderful!  Our friends live close by the restaurant and it was our first time there. I was very comfortable with their Covid protocols as I walked inside. Our wait staff was very attentive. Their pasta seems to be homemade and delicious. I had the crab and shrimp ravioli. 5 huge ravioli that were wonderful. Dessert was delicious too. I had the chocolate moose cake. Yum. I highly recommend for a lovely evening and great food

Was so pleasantly surprised to see this new addition to Hillsborough Village, and it did not disappoint! The warm salads we had were excellent. All ingredients were super fresh and flavorful. The cookie was really satisfying. We will be back!
Wait was short, service was fast and food was awesome! Such a cool find:) we had the super crunchy and dragon roll so so good!
Quality work.  Wonderful, service-oriented people.  Perfect, downtown location.  You'll be very happy you chose this business.

My phone stopped working in roaming and after three hours of horrible phone techs i brought the phone into the store for help. They  openly mocked me saying my phone was old and 'what do you want? Did you expect TMobile to helicopter a tech in for you?' 

I was told my phone was considered old after the last payment was made and i should buy a new phone if i wanted roaming service. They also recommended Verison -which I am happy to take them up on their suggestion. Great job, Tyler. Goodbye Sprint.

As we were walking after I meal I stopped in here because the outside was so cute and didn't check it on Yelp first. I wished I did because there was another dessert place open we could have gone to.
Stephanie S. was spot on for this place.

Atmosphere/Decor: The place is small and it even smells a bit... dust?.. some random food?  I wish they would air it out. The outside is really pretty and inviting but it is a false front for what is inside. What a waste of a pretty package.
Service: The girl there was doing her homework and was nice enough.
 Goods: Basic candy, 8 flavors of ice cream, and coffee drinks to be made. I didn't see the display of cookies when I was there. The selection was grocery store candy fare and the scoop of butter pecan ice cream was ok. 
The only thing that made me stay was seeing the Earl Grey tea behind the corner.

The outside is going to invite you to come in but the inside will ask you to leave.  What a shame.

I was so excited when I heard Pressed got into the soft serve game, as my love for juices has started to plateau, but sad when they only released their new "freeze" option up in the Bay Area and in SB. Such teases they are!

Luckily for me I found myself in SB over the weekend and put Pressed on the itinerary. I tried each one of the 5 or so flavors. All of the juice ones were spot on with their liquid counterparts and would be a heartier alternative to the bottled version. I was a sucker for the chocolate and vanilla almond milk freezes, though. They are also non-dairy, which is ideal for those of us with lactose issues. I topped it with chocolate chips, granola, and Himalayan pink salt, which turned out to be $5.95 (small with up to three toppings). It exceeded my expectations. I really loved that I could eat the whole thing without feeling guilty and didn't regret my decision once I licked every last lick there was to lick.

Even more lucky for me, they just opened one at the Americana in Glendale, so I will be frequenting that bad boy often to get my freeze fix!
Best breakfast or lunch in town! Good service and great food! Price ain't bad either!

Legit. Best "street tacos" in Tampa. 
Very well made, traditionally seasoned meats go into these very tasty dishes. 
Well priced and a friendly staff. 
I will be back... Often.
A fun sports Sunday. The drinks, food and crowd were excellent!
I love this place! They're always nice, it's very clean and it gets the job done  I always go for the stand up bed and it's great.

For a few years now my family physician has kept me on Prilosec.   But when I saw Dr. Viglione he suggested I start with Zantac instead, telling me that not only it may help me just as well as Prilosec, but will be a lot safer.       It works!!         Thanks doc, you are the BOMB!!!

I was traveling with a friend from Korea and he had never gone to a diner, so we stopped in. We walked in and thought it looked as retro as expected. However, it is connected to a odd, noisy bar. We ordered from a extremely unhappy waitress, who seemed to want to sit on a corner stool and eat the entire time we were there. We ordered and I asked for a side of tarter sauce and she responded with a smug question and acted like I was crazy. Then, she never even brought the tarter, nor checked in on us. However, she was still sitting there eating when we left. 

Regarding the food, it was very good and exactly what one would expect from a diner. I would probably stop in again if ever in Philadelphia...as long as there wasn't a starving, sanctimonious, sad waitress waiting to ignore me.
Solidly good take out Chinese food. Very nice owner. Food is always great. Love the Mongolian beef dish here

Walked in without a reservation, just the two of us at 4:30 on a Saturday.  Looked around, NOBODY else in the restaurant.  We were told that there wasn't a table open until 10pm.   Really? I asked.   But there are lots of tables open.   I was told "those aren't for you".   I smiled and left.   If they don't want my money, I can spend it somewhere else.   FWIW - went to the parking lot, looked at OPENTABLE to make a reservation, and there were open slots all night.    Went back in, pointed this out, and was told they don't work with OPENTABLE.   funny that.

Don't know what I did wrong, but I will not visit any Melting Pot restaurants ever again.   I may be just one person and insignificant, but I felt like this could have been handled better.

Had a group reservation for indoor dining for 12 guests. No issues when we arrived 10 mins early. Staff was prompt to accommodate everyone's order, even though we were a big party and the place was extremely busy. I order the Red Snapper with Crab meat. Might be the best Red Snapper I ever had, highly recommend it. Everyone loved their dishes and when we left, there were about 15 people waiting to come in.  Great Job!!

Delicious food and very friendly staff. This place always makes our Friday night even better. Great business to support and the best margaritas in town! They also have great catering. Made our graduation party taco bar a big hit!

Definitely a 5 star. Everyone was so nice, including the parking attendant. Cocktails were perfect. Wife ordered the Pork is so buccaneers. I had the Costa Rica swordfish. Absolutely delicious, with nice salad and veggies. Prices are very reasonable.

I went to the Grand Lux Cafe to meet a friend for happy hour. I was really impressed with the feel of the place. It was comfortable, but it looked pretty classy, especially for being in the mall! My friend and I grabbed a seat in the bar area, which had plenty of open tables at about 5 pm on a weekday.

They had happy hour specials from 4-6 pm, I believe. There were four or five cocktails for under $6. I had a sweet margarita and a blueberry mojito. The margarita was good, but it was a little sweet for me. I wish they had a spicy drink on the happy hour cocktail list! The mojito was surprisingly flavorless, but my friend enjoyed hers. I did like that there were lots of small, whole blueberries in the drink. 

I ordered a salad with heirloom tomatoes that was pretty tasty. It was small, but affordable. My friend ordered a buffalo wonton appetizer. It was really large for a happy hour special. She couldn't eat it all, and she was pretty hungry.

I was really impressed with the waiters. They knew about all of the things on the menu and were able to make good recommendations. They were also just SUPER cheerful. I took out a card game after we finished eating, and they didn't mind us playing.

The soondooboo was pretty good, much better than the other korean restaurant in the area that has a 50% bump in price. They heap a healthy serving of protein depending on what you ordered, I had pork with mine. The pork itself was thick and I think seasoned. The broth wasn't too bad, the tofu was a bit odd compared to the other places I've had it, but I'm a bit of a soondooboo snob having eaten it in palisades park, NJ (the closest I've seen to an actual K-town or town of koreans on the east coast). They also have zucchini and mushrooms in it as well. You are given a bowl of rice, a small side of pickled yellow radishes chopped up, and a small side of kim chi. All in all, a pretty hearty meal for the $10 price tag. 

Unfortunately, they have a $15 minimum credit card charge and instead of canceling the order, I ordered more to hit the minimum. I ended up trying out the korean tacos. You get a choice of either pork or chicken, I went with the pork. It comes in a small flour tortilla, with seasoned red sweet/spicy rice, lettuce, cilantro, marinated pork, and some type of sour cream concoction. They also throw in a little container of their house sweet/spicy seasoning which was actually pretty good. While the tacos are $3.25 each, it's a minimum order of two, which isn't necessarily a bad thing.

I have stayed in a few Holiday Inn on my way down here. I have to say this is the nicest one of them all. Super clean, Super Friendly. Location is the best! I could not ask for anything better. Very beautiful!!!!
Thank you to all the stuff during this time of difficulty, I appreciate everything you all are doing.

What a nice addition to Mass Ave! I tried Moar Tea and Poke today for the first time, not knowing exactly what to expect. I was very surprised as I thoroughly enjoyed my lunch. 

Ordering is extremely easy as the menu is step by step and you literally fill it out yourself. I had the rice bowl but substituted zucchini noodles for the rice. It was divine! I will say the Chili sauce is quite hot and had me sweating by the end. 

I also had a honey Jasmine Green Tea, which was very refreshing.

One of the better sushi restaurants in Center City, it's a great place to go with friends or on a date. Everything here tastes pretty good and there are options for those who want staples like maki or nigiri, as well as more adventurous rolls incorporating eggplant or katsu chicken, etc. The fish tastes pretty fresh and the more complicated rolls have a good balance of flavor.

My gf and I got a plate to share: the green dragon, spider roll, katsu maki (crab stick, cucumber, avocado inside, white fish tempura and eel sauce on top) and spicy scallop (her favorite) were all solid. I really liked the "Rolling Fire" roll: shrimp tempura and cucumber inside, with a delicious creamy spicy scallop sauce on top. The ambiance is just dim but modern and very clean, and service was nice. As expected, it's not super cheap, but for good sushi and the great environment it's well worth the price. I look forward to coming back and trying other specialties.

Only in Philly for two nights, I was hoping for some authentic pizza. This was not it. Although the quick service was appreciated(and expected due to proximity), this was a thick doughy pie that did not live up to the expectations of the other yelp reviews. 

The price is low, and the flavors and options were interesting on the menu. The online ordering was a nice option also.

The red sauce pizza with only a sausage add on, was so thick and saucy the box was falling apart by the time we had eaten half the pie. 

Disappointing to say the least

The atmosphere is very relaxed and the food was very well portioned and tasty.  I truly didnt expect much, but I was relieved to see the quality of my BBQ Bacon Burger.  My lady and I are still waiting to enter into the main showroom floor, but I expect our comedian to be hilarious, since I do enjoy this comedian already.  There is a two item min requirement per person, so I would highly recommend arriving early enough to enjoy dinner/few drinks prior to, because what you purchase at the resturant, counts towards that policy.

Enjoy!

I don't get all the hype about this breakfast place. It is expensive considering it's breakfast and $3.29 for a cup of coffee or tea seems a bit steep. Writing on the wall, weird signs, etc., -maybe because it's a re-creation of what made the original so catchy and famous. Great?, no, but it's OK.

I try to find every coffee stop on my journeys when I travel! This place is definitely one of my top places to return to. The coffee leaves you feeling energetic and ready to tackle whatever the day has in store! The drinks are delicious and the staff makes you feel warm and welcomed! If your in Nashville definitely check this place out!

We just wanted to take a minute to say thank you for a great job! Moved into a new home that needs so many repairs, one of which was the fence. From the quick response to our request for a quote, to the awesome suggestions during the actual quote, scheduling and installing, the follow up call to ensure that we were satisfied with the completed job; all was handled so professionally and quickly. The fence was modified to accommodate some sloping in our lawn which had been allowing our little Shih Tzu to escape. The finished product transformed the curb appeal completely. We would not hesitate to use this company again with confidence. Great job!

Forgo the reviewers of Phily Diner with two stars or less, from their reviews they're either picky, bitter, or out of towners who stopped by once. Locals are lucky to have a diner that packs a wallop with bold flavors at all hours of the day.

Atmosphere - Phily (yes, one 'L') has been around for over 30 years. This diner, now combined with a Sports Bar, draws in quite the crowd mix. The lobby with its revolving door ushers you into either a warm dining area with fresh made goodies in the bakery cabinets, or the entry way to an outstanding Sports Bar. Those going early in the day or late at night, can find something for about every appetite. The sports bar prides itself with plasma TV's around the bar, and an outdoor deck for the summer months (including another upstairs). Inside the main diner, you'll find cozy booths and accommodating sections for all. 

Waitstaff - Diner part is staffed with waitresses from the seasoned pro school, or the college/high school crowd. All are friendly and knowledgeable of the expansive menu options and are always bringing fresh beverages and a smile to your table. In the sports bar, more of the younger side waitresses, again providing service with great care while dealing with the locals at the bar, chatting them up about the latest sports.

Food - Bar none, best diner food within 20 miles of Philadelphia. The Phily is open 24 hrs, so you can quench your hunger pangs with some great food. The menu, while long, provides limitless options for your party. Food is cheap in cost, but expensive in taste. From the homemade bakery good, to the ham and cheese omelette's, you'll definitely get a lot on your plate, and may need to take some home. There are always a plethora (how about that word for a review) of options for those willing to go outside of the regular diner comfort zone. One very nice touch is the free butter cookies you can take when you go in or leave, just that little something extra to make you want to come back.

Intangibles - I've seen a number of two and one star reviewers on this place, and I was honestly shocked. This diner is well worth the cost, and time to sit at. One thing I will mention is they are ALWAYS busy, so you may have to wait for a table. Sports Bar is another experience all together, but again, not as bad as some would make it out. If you go any diner in Jersey, you know that the crowd can be a mix of young and old, so if you're looking for a peaceful, quite place, this would not be the spot. If you are hungry at 3:00am and looking to meet up somewhere after a night out, there's not a better spot to finish at.

Overall - The Phily Diner is without a doubt, a local landmark and truly tasty diner in South Jersey. If you can get past the weak reviews and give this place a shot, I think you'll see why so many locals pack the place day and night throughout the year.
My wife, 2-year-old, son & I enjoyed our first visit here very much. The lunch line moved quickly and staff was very friendly. My wife's country steak wasn't hot but everything tasted great.

AMAZING. Went at sunset and it was perfect! What a nice retreat in Downtown St. Louis, with the Arch in view, and the people of the town all around. Great art and nature! Love that someone took these two blocks and did something great with it!

I could seriously sit at Citygarden and people watch for hours. My favorite part of the visit was watching all the kids run through the fountains and the little built in creek and the sculptures! So much life! Tons of great photo opportunities. (I've uploaded a ton of photos in this review.)

So much fun. I recommend anyone and everyone check it out!

My mom and maid of honor threw my bridal shower at Scaturro's last Saturday. It was FANTASTIC. I grew up in the Medford/Marlton area but have never eaten here, so I wasn't sure what to expect. It exceeded all my expectations:

Service: Fantastic. The waiters were attentive and friendly, but not overbearing. They were very efficient, and always came over to ask if I needed anything at all. They figured out I was the bride (although it wasn't too difficult...) and made sure I always had a drink in my hand. When there was a mix-up with an order, they corrected it and brought out a new entree for one of my guests almost immediately. I was really impressed with their professionalism and poise. 

Food: To be honest, I really didn't think I would notice the food at my bridal shower. I was wrong -- the food was excellent! I had the salmon with risotto, and honestly I'm not even that big a fan of salmon, I just really wanted the risotto. :) Everything was great -- the salmon was cooked perfectly, seasoned really well without getting the fish dry. The risotto was delicious and was a perfect compliment to the fish. Other people commented to me that the food was really good. 

Space: Scaturro's doesn't open to the public until 4pm, so we had the place to ourselves from 12pm-4pm. It was nice and quiet with just our party. They had a nice set-up so we didn't feel like we were in a large, empty restaurant. We were in an off-shoot of the main restaurant which was cozy but not cramped. The room had a lovely fireplace which was great for taking pictures, and they had several tables set up for cake and gifts. 

I can't speak to the organization and how they were to work with prior to the event, but my shower truly went off without a hitch. Scaturro's made the event perfect, and I'd highly recommend booking them for any event or just going there for dinner.

cute ambience that would be great for date night or even girl's night. i went for a small birthday dinner for a girlfriend, we ordered several plates & shared. sadly i don't remember many of the plates but the only thing that stood out in taste was the crab noodles, they were great. everything else didn't really catch my attention on taste besides the broccolini (spelling?) being salty. the cocktails were great & we ordered plenty of hot sake to enjoy our evening. the main reason why I am giving it 3 stars is because the menu is a little pricey (location is downtown nashville off 3rd) & nothing spectacular stood out for it being a new spot in nashville.
Definitely the best Mexican food I've had on the east coast.
The burgers, service and prices are amazing! We had no trouble parking. Definitely give them a try.

This is an AWESOME spot to see live music.  It's like having the band play in your living room.  Very intimate, great sound, and cool & quirky murals on all of the walls give it a cool atmosphere.  My only complaint is that, if you don't get dinner at Serrano first and land a "reserved" table in the front portion of the room, you often get stuck sitting on kinda uncomfortable barstools lining the side wall, and leaning to peer around the person in front of you.  It's not enough to make me hesitate before buying tickets for a show there, but it can be kind of a pain in the neck (and the back...literally).  Other than that one drawback, which is pretty minor in the grand scheme of things given the quality of the acts they get and the intimacy of the venue, this is one of my favorite places to see shows in Philly.  And if you get a chance to check out Grey Eye Glances, a local band that plays at the Tin Angel a couple times a year, do it.

#AsianOwned #WomanOwned #OpenToAll #GenderNeutralBathroom

Magazine Street now has literal cloud [puffs] of heaven! I definitely indulged a bit and ordered a few but by far my favorite were the creme brulee and bananas foster! Beard Papa's started off originally in Japan so it's pretty cool to see New Orleans have their first location.

I was pretty surprised how you choose your shell of choice (not including the dessert creations) and then you choose your creme filling. SAY WHAAAAAA. The strawberry filling was my favorite; however, they also have chocolate and green matcha fillings just to name a few.

Price wise they're more than reasonable and I love the little "fisherman" yellow tackle box. There's a few places to enjoy your little sweet puffs in-person btw.
4 pumps do not rhyme with 1 pump. Starbucks in Nevada is no different than the ones in California. They mess up your order all the time.

This is the worst Pizza Hut. Two hours after I ordered delivery I had to call to be told they were not sending drivers out. They were going to call me but they got busy. He barely offered an apology but said my pizza was ready and I could pick it up!! This is beyond ridiculous customer service. Stay away from this place.

Awesome service from Julie and hands down some of the best country fried steak I've had (recommended by Julie).


Could not finish my toast. LOL

It is a beautiful place with a live tree inside. The service is good. The food is good. I like the fact they have a fixings bar thy you can go to so you don't need to constantly ask for extras.i was allowed to fix my meat platter the way I liked, because of diet preferences.

Parking is only on the curb for 90 min max. The staff was very accomodating and quick with the service. All wore masks and gloves. They made sure the parties were spread out. The grill was changed several times without us even asking.  They didn't have much for sides though. The beef brisket and pork belly was delish. Would come back!
Started using front point 6 months ago because we were looking for home security while renting. We have been pleased thus far.

Went into the deli on 5/5/14 to check out their banquet room.  They had whole filet of beef advertised for $10.99 a lb.  I asked how long the sale was on and they said this is our regular price.  I went back on 5/10/14 to pick up the filet.  When I walked into the store the owner was screaming at an employee in front of customers.  They did not have what I wanted so I asked are they getting more in.  An employee gave me a smart answer and said not today.  I was then told that they would have more in on Thursday 5/15.  The price was still listed as $10.99.  I returned on Thursday 5/15, picked out my filet and was told it was $12.99 a lb. even though the sign was still up listing the price as $10.99.  The employee called the owner who would not honor the advertised price.  Another employee then called the owner (I found out later it was her son) and she finally agreed to honor their advertised price.  In speaking with my sister later she related that she went in earlier that same day for the fresh shrimp listed on their sign for $11.99 a lb. and they tried to charge her $17.99 at lb. Very poor way to do business, I will not return there ever.

We had a Church Youth group activity going together to Relleke Farms, about 30 of us went on October 19. The Farm was easy to access from the Freeway and they had parking flaggers,  which helped get us into their enormous Relleke Farm's parking with ease! There were many activities & attractions such as Face painting, Private group picnic area, Pumpkin catapulting,Wagon rides, Pony & Camel rides, Carnival rides, Food & merchant venders, Petting zoo, Live music by a local group called "Miss Jubilee", and not to forget to mention the acres of massive Pumpkins & Haunted Corn Maze!! We all had a great experience of what the Farm life is like and each of us came home with the best Pumpkin in the patch!! We'll Be Back again next Season for sure!!

I got a chance to try Oceana a few months ago while working an event downtown. We ordered to go from the lunch menu and got the fried catfish platter and red beans. I walked down the street and around the corner to pick up and while it wasn't that busy on a Wednesday afternoon I was still left waiting for a bit at the to-go/pickup area. Once I got back to the hotel we got right to the food and I enjoyed the catfish but was disappointed by the read beans. They definitely had a commercial feel but hey I get it. All in all the lunch was decent and I might go back to try a dessert one day.

Super clean pho place, not far from the freeway! The great Yelp reviews led us here and so glad that it did. This was a great place for lunch - started with the summer rolls, a rice paper wrapped egg roll with fresh mint, rice noodles and succulent shrimp. Also ordered the small pho, which was delicious - with plenty of accompaniments including cilantro, jalapeños and lime wedges. Green tea was the right thing to have with it all. Service was friendly and food was quick. Overall positive experience and would come back!

I read plenty of reviews on this place and was very excited for a dinner with my wife and her siblings, our annual tradition. The reviews were great, the experience.... Not so much. 


We secured a reservation for 8:30, arrived at 8:15 and were not seated until after 9:30!! The hostess was more than apologetic, but seriously, it's a BYO, turn your friggen tables over. 

Besides being antagonized by a patron who actually was holding up our table since their 6:30 reservation we enjoy some wine and the hostess' banter. Unfortunately it only got worse when we met our waiter. My wife actually pointed out how miserable he seemed, not that it was our fault he couldn't turn over his previous table. I watched him talk negatively about our tables and the others remaining in the dining room. Sadly, His only excitement came from letting us know all of the items they had run out of that evening - good thing I did not want crab or muscles or a few varieties of pasta. Way to be prepared Arugula. 

Once we ordered our meals it came out surprisingly quick and we were comped a few desserts. It's amazing how quickly food can come out when the staff wants us to leave, which was clearly felt by our party as the 630 res at our table sat for 3 hrs and we were done in half the time. 

My meal, the veal saltimbocca - the veal was good, the potatoes were bad and the brocolli was worse, pretty much inedible to two of us. 

I am happy others enjoyed their time at this restaurant as I will never return and happily let others know of the poor service and food quality at this lackluster establishment. Next time Id rather go to chilis.

Efficient, competent, and caring. I went to AFC for the first time this week, and I'll definitely go back for any walk-in clinic needs. I went to see if my finger was broken. There was little wait time, the intake process was streamlined, staff are incredibly friendly and professional, and the facility is immaculate. They took and read my film on-site but also sent it to a radiologist for a second opinion just to be sure, calling me a few hours later with the report confirming the doctor's initial diagnosis. They're patient and thorough. Bonus: I was offered and given the flu shot while waiting on the x-ray. A staff member called me two days later just to check how I was.
Worst experience of my life! Servers and hostess and kitchen guy were rude as hell! Not a single order came out correct! Was my first time there and I will never go back.
The Late night menu was perfect with chimchurri street tacos, wings, and drink specials.  The manager/ bartender was super friendly.  We will definitely  come back, the next  time we are in Boise.

Husband and I just had lunch here. Gyoza - good - nothing special, but yummy. Pork buns - yummy, light and airy. He had shoyu ramen, which was delicious, the noodles, al dente, huge bowl and the pork just melted in your mouth. I had the beef udon (which oddly enough is not on the online menu) and it may have been the best noodle bowl i've ever eaten. the caramelized onions were amazing and the broth was out of this world. the noodles were perfect. we can't WAIT to go back!

This was so disappointing. We dropped almost $400 for four people before the show, and not one of us had a good meal. The salmon and red snapper was dry. The vegetables and the rice tasted far too strongly of cilantro and were also dry. The bread we requested never arrived. I will say the soup, salad and charcuterie in the middle of the room were good. Service was friendly but spotty. I feel so ripped off by the high price. Never again will I eat here.

This company is HORRIBLE!! The person who answers the phone is incredibly rude! I had to call twice to schedule a taxi and both times the dispatcher was extremely disrespectful. I then cancelled the taxi deciding to go with a company that actually appreciates business. The rude dispatcher then calls at 10:30 at night yelling at me and accusing me of not cancelling the taxi. He then hung up on me.  USE UBER!! It's an excellent service with kind people.

Well, I don't think I have ever had bad service here. The wait staff are always so welcoming and friendly-a small town feel. I enjoy the food and the portions are huge. Fresh brewed tea for a plus. The gift shop is amazing. Really unique and cute things. Overall, everything from the food to the gift shop is priced really well. Only thing I'd like to see are a few healthier options, but otherwise it's a fun and yummy stop.

The hotel is nice but it could use a few extras. The fridge is way to small for anything. And there is no microwave. You need to put down towels before you shower. Otherwise the floor is soaked.  The rooms has only one lamp that doesn't light up much. Other than that it's a nice place. The staff are very friendly and helpful.

Heard so many good things about La Strada and they're all true! Fine dining authentic Italian dishes. Elegant atmosphere prefect for date night or dinner with friends. Pleasant, knowledgeable wait staff. Looking forward to dining again.

I wish I could give this place more stars. Their hostess was so rude and downright snotty the two times we went that it made the experience not worth it at all. Love the fact that they have tasty vegetarian options - Avocado Crispy Rice. Perhaps others will have more luck but I don't see myself going back again. Too many other local places.

I brought family in to taste the smoked meatloaf! I almost hate to even say this, but mine was cool towards the middle this time. My family could tell that the pork chops were made same day and incredibly thick for their preference. The greens were full of stems and tasted eerily similar to glory greens. I will be back to give it another shot. The staff is excellent and the banana pudding is to die for! I won't give up just yet.

It was just meh... after waiting in a long line my kids expected it to be phenomenal... it wasn't. They ordered an Oreo typhoon think blizzard or McFlurry and a mint chip milkshake. They thought McDonald's has better desserts.

We went for late lunch today and had a very good meal at a very good price.  Our waitress was very attentive, also. The light jazz and Sinatraesque music playing was a refreshing twist from most of Nashville's eateri

So I visited this craft sale for the first time ever this spring and was happy to come home with two dresses (one casual and one more work appropriate) and one necklace. I was pretty happy with the number of booths (especially the number of food booths) as well as the amount of clothing and accessories and art and and and! It was reasonably busy with women, children and men browsing. There is a lot of baby-centric items here but Yelp also ran a colouring area and there was also a face painter which makes the event a bit more kid-friendly. I also liked the fact that several booths featured some good discounts.

Admission is rather affordable at $6 per ticket at the door though several discounts are available online in advance (and a number of free tickets are given out each year). There is ample parking (though it is at the Expo Centre so it's a bit pricey) and it is easily accessible via transit (the Colliseum LRT station).

Worth a visit! You never mind paying that little bit extra especially when you walk out of a place having enjoyed it! I cannot remember the last time I had a draft beer that tasted like a bottle beer. Appetizers were great and entrees even better. Don't expect fast food pace of the staff but that's what I prefer to actually be able to relax and enjoy the moment.

Excellent Hattie B's Hot Chicken without dealing with downtown Nashville lines. 
Staff was also very friendly.

HEY! Cafe is GREAT. The coffee stirs something inside me that begs for more...it could just be my happy tummy. 

The Arnold Palmer is truly a treat. They also sell records here. At a glance, they had most everything that Louisiana metal dudes THOU have put out, as well as records from INTER ARMA, COUGH, and COFFINWORM. 

Like your coffee like you like your metal

This place was the worst.  First, it is a dump which is only OK if the food is good.  But, it wasn't.  There were three of us and it was a consensus dud.  The sesame chicken was awful...like biting into little hollow rocks with no chicken on the inside.  It also had a weird taste that I can't explain other than it wasn't like any sesame chicken I've ever had.  By far the worst Chinese we've had since moving to Nashville.

They recently changed their desk secretary. The previous one, Melinda, was extremely bubbly and fun; the new one, Peggy, is very serious and not very inviting.

Plus my appointments have begun to get screwed up. When I request a private room, I'm being scheduled for the porch room (which is freezing, they tried to put me out there once already).  Plus when I called today to make sure I wasn't scheduled for the porch room (I was), she also informed me that my appointment was 3:30 (the card she gave me on my last visit said 4:30, so I would have missed my appointment had I not called and switched)

The service is going downhill fast with Peggy rather than Melinda.

Dr. Trish is still great as usual! :)
Not quite sure why it's a "beer garden" but the seafood is very good.  Had the charred oysters and they are superb.  Good bartender and a nice place.

Made reservations and showed up for our time. Was told just because we have reservations for a certain time does not mean we will be seated then. (????????)  they've been in business for a few years and have done a few Mardi Gras. No reason at this point to be a scattered mess and backed up. While it certainly had ppl in the establishment it by no means was a two hour wait around the building. This will be my last time here and I'm in the media so I'll make sure everyone knows how we were treated. Zero excuses
Pleasant staff, good customer service. Great food!

Over the last three years, Crocker has given us fabulous service for a series of challenging problems. They correctly diagnosed a simple faulty thermostat, when another company said we had to replace a $4,000 unit. They quickly and efficiently replaced a chiller in a very awkward location. And this week, though booked for months for new installations, they sent a crack team that in just a few hours replaced an old, dead AC system because they knew we had 40 guests spending the weekend at our home for a hot, Fiesta celebration. Thank you, thank you, thank you!

Bluemercury carries a wide range of skin and hair care products that cover all skin/hair types and price points. Two of my favorite skin care brands; REN and Mario Badescu are carried here, which is great as they are not widely available in the Philadelphia area. 

The staff can be hit or miss. Some very nice, very helpful employees, and then some very rude and snotty employees. 

I've had a facial done in their spa, it was decent but not wow-worthy.

I love Napolese! If not for the food, then for the atmosphere.  The downtown location is a little loud for my tastes, but it looked like a great place to meet friends for an after-work drink and dinner.  With toppings like goose jowl bacon, leeks, and roasted cauliflower, their artisan pizzas are different than most other pizza places.  If you're not up for the fancy pizzas, they have some good "normal" pizza options like the Meridian Kessler, which comes with pepperoni, provolone, italian sausage and mushrooms.  For the low carb eaters, they carry a variety of salads, including a tasty Roasted Brussels Sprouts salad, as well as some favorites like the house Caesar.  They also have a nice little wine selection, but my friend was disappointed that they didn't offer a Chardonnay by the glass.  I've enjoyed the Brolio Chianti Classico on more than one occasion.  

Last night, I tried the Pie of the Day, which was a pizza with white sauce, roasted new potatoes, leeks, and goose jowl bacon.  It was absolutely delicious. The goose jowl bacon was fatty, but I really loved the flavor.  They start off the meal with some olives to chomp on, and my friend and I enjoyed them so much that our waiter brought us each a to-go container of olives before we left.  I'll also note that the service was incredibly fast and all of the staff was very friendly (but not overwhelmingly so) throughout the entire evening.  I'd recommend this place to anyone.  If you're looking for a quieter place, try the Broad Ripple location.  The wine bar in the back is a quieter setting, and a great place to meet a group friends for a night out.

Terribly slow service. 6 tables seated and it took 20 min to get a drink. Never asked for our dinner order. 
7 people dinner apps and drinks. They missed out on several hundred dollars tonight. Was excited to come here won't be back. Apps were good but not worth the time. 
Manager did acknowledge and tried to talk us into staying to no avail.
Great food. Super fast. Real good prices. Whether you want a snack or meal. Do make sure you have some of the lulo or passion fruit juice.

The karaoke dj is CONSISTENTLY rude to people of color. He has no sense of respect when it comes to people's time. Instead of being transparent he wastes people's time and isn't forth coming about what to expect. this is after three to four times of me coming into this bar. I'm so sick of how I'm treated here.

I love this branch.

I used to bank for years at the Hibernia/Capital One branch one block away. I got used to slow, casual service, and increasingly decreased hours.

I finally switched last year (major reason was Chase's iPhone app as well as the confusing posting rules/fees at Cap 1) and only wish I've done it years ago. 

These folks are professionals! It's nice to see tellers in a consistent uniform, after being served by tellers in sweat shirts and hoodies at Cap 1. I was introduced to the branch manager on my first visit, had no problems opening several accounts at once, and was treated very professionally each time here.

Being open till 5PM on weekdays and 1PM is a life-saver for me. The 4PM/noon cut off at Cap 1 was killing me. I had to literally sprint there many times before (no fun in the summer). 

They have many extra services (safety boxes), many of them free depending on your account. 

The tellers are quick. I would estimate most transaction are processed twice as fast then I'm used to at Cap 1.

Hot pot is good for 3 things, if you like soup or experience destination place such as fondue. And finally, nice atmosphere with great offerrings. Wait that is 4. I love soup, so I was all over that this visit. 

Service was very very very good. I am not sure why other yelpers felt it was not that good. There were ALOT of people there in large parties all whom seemed to be quite happy with being there on a Sunday late afternoon. 

Our server did not speak English wonderfully, but if you spoke slow, he understood and was really helpful. We had a few dishes aside from the Hot Pot just because and just in case. The kids were hungry, had to get them food faster than waiting on the Hot Pot to come and boil up and then heat the food. 

I swear this used to be my gym way back when there was actually a pool there too. It is like others said right near the Big Lots, Lowes and Walmart. Easy parking. Did not need a reservation, but waited a few minutes before they cleaned a family hot pot table. They ask you ahead of time if you are going to have it. I know what to do at a Hot Pot place, however, this place had me a little befuddled. They GIVE you the Hot Pot and you order which variety you prefer. Other places have different pricing, so really this place is a bit cheaper than others outside of TN. 

The Seafood does not come with vegetables. So although it is the same as the other combinations, if you want veges, you have to order them. The Seafood seemed fresh, but next time may not choose.  We had added the vegetables for 9 dollars extra, some Udon for 3 dollars extra, and then some pork for 4 dollars. 

The condiments make the Hot Pot. They are located in the back behind the pretty party Pagodas. The Hot Pot sauce tastes like a Pho base. They had low sodium soy sauce, because the regular sodium soy sauce is conveniently on the table. Chili Oil, Vinegar, Chili paste, green onions, cilantro, crushed garlic, vinegar, mustard and BBQ sauce, oops forgot Siracha sauce. 

When you make your own soup, you have to "doctor" it up to make it to your liking. If you don't like that sort of thinking, then this may not be your cup of tea or Hot Pot. As I love love love soup, I will be back, but not with teenagers who have a better social life than me and spending more than 1 hour at lunch is not easy for them. Very pretty venue and the servers and hostesses and managers were quite hospitable. 

No liquor yet but they have beer, however no sake. We had the Bone Broth and the Tomato broth. Agree with other yelpers, the Bone Broth had more flavor, the tomato not much at all.

So happy Nashville is adopting more and more interesting food choices to the fold.

We went on a warm night in December and had a great experience with Tricia. She was knowledgeable and answered all of the questions our group had (even ones not about Nashville). She even had some very spooky pictures to share of "ghosts" seen in the places we were touring! The tour had a good mix of walking with several chances to explore or sit for a moment and was truly mostly downhill with a few inclines. We had a great time!

A Maryland farms staple. I've been coming for almost a decade. Way back when I used to work in the area. Initially for Bubble tea, but then back for their delicious, healthy lunch options. They have a hearty selection of fruit tea, chiller, and milk tea. But Taro Chiller is my favorite hands down, just the right amount of sweet - thick, but just enough to still be able to use a fat straw. 

For the food - they don't have a huge selection - just a little variety of wraps, salads, sides, soup of the day, and plates. But their fiery ginger grilled chicken wrap is my favorite. Packed with plenty of meat - and just enough heat in the sauce. Today, I forgot to order sauce in the side, and it was just a bit too much in the wrap. But still pretty good. Got a side of fruits - strawberries, apples, and grapes. They also had a little selection of sweets on the counter. The cookie was tempting, but Resolutioner here...maybe next time.

Service is always great and fast. Everyone is nice and helpful!

Menu looked really good. We first ordered drinks. I ordered a dirty martini and my husband ordered a draft beer. My martini came out in a stemless glass that was about 12 ounces and was filled to the top. It was WAY too salty and with little vodka taste. So with a two/three ounce shot of vodka, I'm not sure what the rest was other than water and olive juice. 

We first ordered the Brussels and fried cauliflower. The Brussels came first and were delicious. Next, a food runner came up to our table with holding two dishes, he set one down and then changed it and put the other one down. It was definitely cauliflower, but looked raw or pickled. I said, is that the fried cauliflower? He said, yes, I think so. Then went on to deliver the other dish to another couple. So when our waitress came by we asked about the dish. She said it was not the dish we ordered and she quickly replaced it with the fried cauliflower. Our last dish was the fish tacos which were fried with a cornmeal-like coating and were average, but my husband really liked them. However, both of us were sick the next morning. Not happy at all.

I LOVE RALPHS.. 
My now Ex Husband "Lenny" used to bring me here all the time.. The food is scrumptious.. The mussels red or white are to die for.Food is always fresh and prepared to order. The Owners 'Jimmy and Eddie", super nice, very accomodating and made me feel like family... Ronnie too!!
I always left here in a food coma... Highly reccommend this wonderful Restuarant.. Gets very busy especially on weekends....Always a great dining experience!!

We took the 2-hour French Quarter Ghost & Legends Tour (offered at 6 pm & 8 pm nightly year round for $25).  We found that it was totally worth it to get a great overview of the French Quarter and learn a bit of (albeit embellished) history. We had an amazing tour guide, Ari. She studied theatre and you could tell by her ability to capture and audience that she really loved her job - and was great at it. 

We hit at least 5 sites, with a quick stop at Lafitte's Blacksmith Shop (pub) for a break (and beer if you wanted, it's NOLA, people!).  One of the best stories came when she stopped in front of a hotel and talked about ghost sightings.  Little did I know, it was was my hotel - Hotel Provincial - that I was staying in!  We had NO idea when we booked it! It was a super crazy coincidence!  

If you are in NOLA, it's worth it to do a ghost tour.  Next time I come back, I am going to do the Haunted Pub Crawl.  :)

It's more than a grocery store and there are people in plain sight and not hiding who can help.  Produce and meat fresh and the seafood is very good.  Sale items always in store.  First check in and review but have been a regular for decades.
Really really disappointed they changed their cheese for the loaded tots & fries. Been going here for years just for that and no warning or say so on the menu. now it's just plain nacho cheese

I come here for coffee occasionally... Specifically for their espresso, which is Illy (an Italian espresso that isn't very common in Tucson). It's $2.35 for a double espresso, which is very reasonable considering it comes on a cute little tray, with a glass of ice water on the side, and a delicious little chocolate candy to cleanse your palate of coffee flavor. Clever, since they sell a lot of candies here. Surprisingly I haven't been tempted by the candies (YET)! 

I love coming here for a quick caffe' al paso (coffee on the go)... Spending a few minutes in this cafe' it is apparent to me that it is locally owned. The owner (and I believe her daughter are both there- running it). They both have a great attitude, and this is the kind of business that I feel I am routing for- that they will survive. The daughter told me they've been in business for over 20 years, and she started working there when she was 14. Goes to show that if you take care of your customers, the business will take care of you! 

They also serve other drinks (including teas, chai, OJ, lemonade, regular sodas, and Italian sodas), pastries (homemade frosted scones that look AMAZING!) plus a wide variety of affordable sandwiches that average about $6. They also have soups, salads, and ice cream. I'm not usually in this area for lunch, but will make a special trip one day soon. To leave you with a sweet note, their signature drink is a double cafe' mocha with a scoop of mint chocolate ice cream, topped with whipped cream and swirled with chocolate syrup- finished with an EDIBLE iguana tail! Now that's a reason to come to 4th Avenue, if I've ever heard one!

This café is highly reminiscent of any old-fashioned café that can be found in a European city. Actually, Cafe Intermezzo reminded me of a tiny, less ornate version of New York Café in Budapest. I knew that my husband would appreciate that when I planned our visit--he loves old architecture and decor.

Our decision to sit out on the patio worked out well for us. The patio is covered and enclosed on three sides, helping to keep out the wind and sun. We could actually hear ourselves converse, even through the sound of traffic and city life. It was very pleasant outside and we thoroughly enjoyed our brunch date. 

My latte was delicious (be forewarned, though, that the drinks here are very expensive; prepare to indulge) but I couldn't tell what part made it good--it was difficult to judge the quality of the coffee through the caramel.

The charcuterie platter was just the right size to split between us alongside a main course: I had a caesar salad (unadventurous of me, yes--but I wanted the charcuterie and caramel latte to be the highlights of the meal) while my husband had spicy tortellini with salmon. He said the tortellini dish was excellent.

The service was great, too. Our server was very prompt and sweet. If ever we end up in Nashville again, we'll be going back to this place.

Great service.  Sushi was kinda underwhelming.  Daughter insisted on sushi so this is where went.  Not knowing better about Nashville...  Now we know better.  Japanese food is not a type they seem to get very well in the south...  If I were to have a do-over I might have tried the turkish place next door.  Ambiance was just OK.  Service was great.  I have had better sushi from my local grocery store (granted they do some really good stuff).

Second time I visit this place and the service was again terrible. The women who work there are just unfriendly and rude.
My daughter who needed glasses was so upset the way they are treated her didn't want to go back. So we find another place on Canal street where we were welcomed!

I think this place is not very authentic mexican food. The prices are higher than usual.  I got fish tacos and they were not very good. The service is good and they are very nice but I think it's not worth what you pay

Wow...I can't say that I've been blown away by a sandwich spot in my life until I ate at Parkway. While I'm sure there are probably a lot of sandwich shops that may be up to Parkway's caliber, for now I will say that Parkway has has THE BEST sandwich I had an opportunity to consume.

When I came here on a warm, January afternoon, the line was LONG. It was intimidating long. I was somewhat bummed by that but the abita amber ale I bought while I waited in line helped ease the wait. When I finally got to the front (which took about 20 min.), I couldn't really decide on what to get (especially since this was my first time having po'boys)  so I bought a 1 small roast beef w/ gravy and 1 golden fried shrimp. 

The aroma of each of the po'boys was MOUTHWATERING! I couldn't wait to sink my teeth in them. Now, I'm not much of a meat eater, but that roast beef with gravy might make a vegetarian convert to becoming carnivorous. The meat was so soft and the gravy was just a great compliment to the whole sandwich. The fried shrimp was made to perfection! The size of the shrimp was not too small and not too big, the breading was perfect and not too much of it and it was deliciously crispy! Top the po'boys with some Tabasco sauce and BAM! Deliciousness at it's greatest. :)

Prior to my arrival to Parkway, I really didn't think I was going to be this impressed by a sandwich. The wait was definitely worth it and I didn't wait too long after I ordered to devour these sandwiches. Dining out in their picnic style tables added a nice, touch to my experience here. If I had room in my belly, I'd definitely add those yummy Zapp's chips, some sweet potato fries and dessert...but those two sandwiches were already enough to put me into a food coma.

YES. YES. YES. how have I not known this place existed near me. I will definitely be a regular here because the vibes, food, drinks, view is amazing. once you walk in, you have the option to sit at the bar (fully stocked), or go upstairs and sit in tables/communal tables by the amazing view. the restaurant has floor to ceiling windows that really opens up the restaurant and makes it seem very spacious. and the view goes straight out onto the main street.

the menu here is seasonal. it also looks like there's a Korean influence to it, as there are Korean fried wings, japchae, and the truffle burger had a bulgogi taste to it. we all ordered our own flights (got the fall white, fall red, and Italian red. they are so well chosen for each flight and the fall ones are perfect for fall), the Italian Grilled cheese (because the dishes are meant to be shared and small tapas, it seems small but don't be fooled! it is VERY filling. the grilled cheese is perfectly blended and has a great buttery bite to it. recommend to share the 4 pieces amongst each other), and the truffle burger (BEST BURGER IN TOWN. the patty is always cooked to medium, and it is FAT. definitely don't skimp out on the meat and its not super chewy at all. it has a bulgogi flavor to it, and the truffle mayo doesn't seem to overpower the burger. can't really taste the truffle. and the crispy onions are a great crunch to the soft buttery bun. the bread is not hard at all, you don't even need to bite into it because it's that soft. HIGHLY RECOMMEND).

I will definitely come here again to try out the other dishes and new seasonal drinks/food that will be coming out. if you are not a wine person, the drink menu is 4x longer than the food menu so there are options for beer drinkers, cocktails, and scotch/whisky flights. you won't be left out!

service here is A+. the waiter, forgot his name, was SO awesome. he recommended a lot of dishes and drinks, and gave time to speak to us about the menu. not only him, but everyone was very attentive.  everyone at the restaurant was awesome, so thank you management for keeping the staff excited about the menu as well!

By far one the worst doctor visits I have ever encountered. I was told to plan on being there for an hour and a half, 30min would be for filling out new client paperwork. I was there for 3 hours and 15min & the paperwork took me less than 10min to fill out. This being said... The Optometrist Assistants were very kind and helpful and took the time to listen to my eye concerns. Where as the doctor (Leslie Weintraub) seemed very rushed and made me feel as though I was wasting her time.

Love this place! Go there all the time for happy hour. They serve Oreana wines for their house wine for $5!!! Usually i go to places and for "Happy Hour " I get an off brand wine that is barley tolerable. Oreana rocks love their tasting room and all their wines! The happy hour food is really good too, lots of options and good portions! Definitely one of the top Happy places I would go to!!

Excellent fried chicken, we have had both crispy regular and spicy ; for our taste the spicy is EXCESSIVELY SALTY and we actually returned it to very understanding staff for our refund . The regular crispy is always SPOT ON ... everyone loves it . Try the chicken tenderloin or strips ; large meaty portions perfectly battered z d crispy perfection and remember their appetizers are the BEST NIBBLES YOU CAN GET  putting bar food to shame .

Long long ago, on a cold winter night, I had one of the weirdest experiences drinking at Gillane's.  The bad memories of that evening mixed with the clowns was enough to drive me away from this place for a good 10 years.

But then a name change and a revamp (plus a long wait at McCloskey's) gave us the opportunity to give it a try.  We went in through the bar and then walked into the restaurant.  As far as I could tell, there was not a specific place for a hostess, so we walked back into the bar with a lost look on our faces and finally someone asked if we needed a seat.  We were sat 10 feet from the bar, which was perfect since the NCAA Final Four was on TV.

The beer list is solid and the prices were not that bad - not that they list them, but I can say after we got the bill, I was actually shocked at how reasonable they were.  

To start, we shared a plate of calamari.  Each piece was exactly the same shape and size, similar to onion rings.  I hesitantly took a bite of the first one and inspected it since I have never seen calamari like this.  In fact, it still kind of terrifies me.  What the heck did we eat? I am not saying it was bad (they weren't amazing either and definitely frozen, not fresh).  I even polled some people throughout the weekend to see if they ever experienced something like this - they hadn't.  I am still confused and slightly concerned.

For the rest of the meal, I had the chicken sandwich with apricot and brie and the fella had a chicken quesadilla.  The quesadilla was lacking in flavor and was kind of cold.  The chicken sandwich was good - but you really have to like brie to order it.  The fries were also cold.  Even if they were hot, not sure I would have loved them since they were skinny and not much to them.

The service was friendly but terrible. We tried to flag the waitress down 3 different times to get another beer and she would walk the other way each time.  I mentioned we were 10 feet from the bar, right?  She would even go to the table behind us and ask how they were doing and then walk away again.  The bartender came out and occasionally helped us too.  He was nice.  Also, there was another waitress that was clearly off the clock since she was drinking at the bar, but helped us with the check too.  

The bar area has been improved, but it still looks like your friend's basement from 1972.  I think I will have to wait another 10 years before going back again.

We came here for a drink. The vibe was very college like, but chill. The beer selection was also interesting. The two we had were pretty good and they came in cool cans. 

If you want to watch a game or just chill for a bit, this is a good place to stop at.

My name is Victor.   I am a JROTC instructor at Lavergne High School. We rented a photo booth from Let's Booth it for our Military Ball hosted this past Saturday on Dec 3rd 2016.  Our kids had a blast of fun dressing up with all the props. They absolutely loved it.  We had a 3 rental with over 200 guests taking pictures and everyone had numerous chances to take photos. The line had a steady flow and no issues.
